## 11.166 Hermitian reciprocal swap and lattice-defect reduction

Section 11.165 identifies the exact reciprocal diagonal null but does not yet
use the conjugate symmetry of the off-diagonal modes.  This section performs
that next algebraic step.  Its scope is the interior Hermitian stationary
main at `xi=T_0`.  It does not supply the discrete Poisson formula, its hard
cutoff terms, or a stationary-phase remainder.

Put

```text
alpha=a^2,                 mu_(k,l)=log(l/k),

e(t)=exp(2pi i t).                                  (11.166.1)
```

The Hermitian kernel, the symmetric square dual window, and the positive
mixed-signature stationary factor imply the swap covariance

```text
A_(l,k)=conj(A_(k,l)),

Z_(k,l)=A_(k,l)e(alpha mu_(k,l)),

Z_(l,k)=conj(Z_(k,l)).                              (11.166.2)
```

This is a statement about the leading interior stationary coefficient.  It
does not identify any endpoint or remainder coefficient.  The differentiated
flow multiplier is `i mu_(k,l)`.  Therefore the two ordered modes in one
off-diagonal pair obey

```text
D_(k,l)+D_(l,k)
 =i mu Z_(k,l)-i mu conj(Z_(k,l))

 =-2mu Im Z_(k,l).                                 (11.166.3)
```

Writing `A_(k,l)=R_(k,l)+iI_(k,l)` gives the fully real form

```text
D_(k,l)+D_(l,k)
 =-2mu{R sin(2pi alpha mu)+I cos(2pi alpha mu)}.
                                                            (11.166.4)
```

The Hermitian family already carries an outer factor `1/2` in (11.164.2).
Thus one unordered pair `k<l` contributes

```text
P_H(k,l)
 =-mu{R sin(2pi alpha mu)+I cos(2pi alpha mu)}.     (11.166.5)
```

Holding the stationary coefficient fixed, the same identity is

```text
D_(k,l)+D_(l,k)
 =(1/(2pi))partial_alpha[Z_(k,l)+conj(Z_(k,l))].   (11.166.6)
```

Since `xi=2pi alpha`, this is exactly the auxiliary-frequency phase
derivative.  On `k=l`, `mu=0`, and (11.166.3) vanishes for the full complex
coefficient, not only for its ideal leading part.

The split in (11.166.5) is important.  The real channel has both the factor
`mu` and a sine zero at integral stationary phase.  The imaginary correction
has `mu` but a cosine.  Consequently integral phase does not kill a general
correction term.

The reciprocal coordinates make the ideal leading channel explicit.  At

```text
n_*=a^2/k,                 m_*=a^2/l,

tau_(k,l)=log(kl/a^2),
```

one has

```text
u_(n_*)-u_(m_*)=-mu_(k,l),

u_(n_*)+u_(m_*)=tau_(k,l).                         (11.166.7)
```

The Hermitian Hessian and leading stationary factor are

```text
Hess(phi_H)=diag(-k^2/a^2,+l^2/a^2),

1/sqrt(|det Hess(phi_H)|)=a^2/(kl).                (11.166.8)
```

Its signature is zero, so there is no extra Maslov phase.  For the ideal
`q=1` kernel `H_0^+=-tau^2/8` and positive real normalized saddle amplitudes
`W_k,W_l`, define

```text
C_(k,l)=a^2 tau_(k,l)^2 W_kW_l/(8kl)>=0.
```

Then `A^0_(k,l)=-C_(k,l)` and (11.166.5) becomes

```text
P_H^0(k,l)
 =C_(k,l)mu_(k,l)
    sin(2pi a^2mu_(k,l)).                          (11.166.9)
```

This leading main has both the reciprocal diagonal zero and an integral-phase
zero.  It still has no pointwise sign.

Pairing now changes the useful summation coordinates.  For `k<l`, write
`l=k+d`, `d>=1`, and put

```text
F_k(d)=alpha log(1+d/k).
```

Then

```text
F_k'(d)=alpha/(k+d),

F_k''(d)=-alpha/(k+d)^2.                           (11.166.10)
```

Thus the ordered two-dimensional square is reduced exactly to a triangular
family of one-dimensional logarithmic offset phases.  No estimate has yet
been applied to those sums.

There is a quantitative reciprocal-lattice gain in the resonant part.  For
`x=d/k>=0`, elementary calculus gives

```text
x-log(1+x)=integral_0^x t/(1+t)dt,

0<=x-log(1+x)<=x^2/2,

0<=log(1+d/k)<=d/k.                                (11.166.11)
```

Let `||y||_Z=dist(y,Z)` and

```text
rho_k=||alpha/k||_Z.
```

Choose an integer `q` with `|alpha/k-q|=rho_k`.  Since `dq` is an integer,
the triangle inequality and (11.166.11) prove

```text
||alpha log(1+d/k)||_Z
 <=d rho_k+alpha d^2/(2k^2).                       (11.166.12)
```

Using `|sin(2pi y)|<=2pi||y||_Z`, the ideal channel therefore satisfies

```text
|P_H^0(k,k+d)|
 <=2pi C_(k,k+d)(d/k)
      [d rho_k+alpha d^2/(2k^2)].                  (11.166.13)
```

For the full coefficient `R+iI`, (11.166.5) gives the honest mixed bound

```text
|P_H(k,k+d)|
 <=2pi|R|(d/k)[d rho_k+alpha d^2/(2k^2)]
    +|I|d/k.                                       (11.166.14)
```

Equation (11.166.14) isolates two different analytic obligations.  Modes
with small `rho_k` expose a pointwise reciprocal-lattice suppression for the
real leading channel.  On the complementary modes, the monotone derivative
in (11.166.10) exposes a one-dimensional exponential-sum problem.  In both
regions the source-specific imaginary coefficient still requires a bound.
This is a resonant/nonresonant route decomposition, not a completed estimate.

The square interior dual window itself creates no unpaired modes.  With

```text
mathcal K={ceil(a^2/B),...,floor(a^2)},
```

the set `mathcal K x mathcal K` is invariant under `(k,l)<->(l,k)`.  Its
`|mathcal K|` diagonal terms vanish and its remaining
`|mathcal K|(|mathcal K|-1)` ordered terms form exactly
`|mathcal K|(|mathcal K|-1)/2` pairs.  This counting does not pair the
one-variable endpoint family, hard-cutoff half-weights, nonstationary modes,
Poisson remainders, or the adjacent terminal recurrence.

Three exact guards prevent overpromotion.  In (11.166.5), choosing
`R=1,I=0,mu=1/4` gives `-1/4` at `alpha=1` and `+1/4` at `alpha=3`, so swap
symmetry has no sign.  Choosing `R=0,I=1,mu=1/2,alpha=2` gives `-1/2` even
though `alpha mu` is integral.  Thus phase resonance kills the real leading
channel but not an arbitrary imaginary correction.  These are algebraic
guards, not asserted Xi configurations.

The `2pi` in (11.166.4)--(11.166.14) has explicit provenance.  Poisson
summation uses `e(t)=exp(2pi i t)`, while `T_0=2pi a^2`.  Therefore

```text
partial_xi e[xi mu/(2pi)]=i mu e[xi mu/(2pi)],
```

and the factor `1/(2pi)` in (11.166.6) is forced.  No circle, polygon, fitted
constant, or new occurrence of `pi` is introduced.

The next theorem must put this pairing inside an endpoint-complete discrete
Poisson or B-process formula with uniform value and first-`x` derivative
remainders.  It must estimate the real offset sums using (11.166.12), bound
the imaginary coefficient in (11.166.14), and retain the endpoint,
transpose, hard-cutoff, and adjacent-recurrence terms before taking absolute
values.  The proof-facing target remains

```text
Psi(T_0)-epsilon integral_0^1
  Psi'(T_0-theta epsilon)dtheta
 <=h^2/400,                                        (11.166.15)
```

preferably with right side `h^2/800`.

## 11.167 Endpoint-complete finite Poisson and stationary transport

Section 11.166 isolates the signed Hermitian reciprocal main but deliberately
does not justify replacing the physical finite sums by that main.  This
section performs the first endpoint-complete Poisson step.  It also records
the exact auxiliary-frequency transport of the stationary main, including
the term caused by motion of the saddle.  The setting is the physical `q=1`,
`L>=50`, fixed-`N` terminal/bulk chart with

```text
B=N-M-1,                 T_0-epsilon<=xi<=T_0.
```

Along this auxiliary segment, hold `sigma`, `t`, the source normalizer, the
terminal jets, and the Section 11.165 observation rows fixed.  Put

```text
e(y)=exp(2pi i y),       alpha=xi/(2pi),

A_j(u)=(log u)^j exp{t(log u)^2/4-sigma log u},

F_(j,xi)(u)=A_j(u)e(alpha log u),

H_j(xi)=sum_(1<=n<=B) F_(j,xi)(n),       0<=j<=5. (11.167.1)
```

The six `H_j` differ from the normalized moments `Ghat_j` only by the fixed
source factor.  If `lambda=log u` and `A_(-1)=0`, then

```text
partial_lambda A_j
 =jA_(j-1)+(t lambda/2-sigma)A_j,

partial_xi F_(j,xi)=iF_(j+1,xi),

H_j'(xi)=iH_(j+1)(xi),                    0<=j<=4. (11.167.2)
```

The occurrence of `pi` here is forced: `2pi alpha=xi`, so
`e(alpha log u)=exp(i xi log u)`.  It is not a fitted constant or a new
geometric assumption.

For the exact Poisson formula, use the endpoint convention in equation (10)
of Vandehey, *Error term improvements for van der Corput transforms*,
`https://arxiv.org/abs/1205.0090`.  A star gives half weight to an integral
endpoint, and the frequency sum is a symmetric limit.  Applied to the smooth
functions in (11.167.1), it gives

```text
sum^*_(1<=n<=B)F_(j,xi)(n)
 =lim_(R->infinity) sum_(r=-R)^R I_(j,r)(xi),

I_(j,r)(xi)
 =integral_1^B A_j(u)e(alpha log u-ru)du.          (11.167.3)
```

The physical bulk sum gives full weight to both endpoints.  Restoring the
missing halves yields the exact endpoint-complete identity

```text
H_j=E_j+lim_(R->infinity)sum_(r=-R)^R I_(j,r),

E_j=(1/2){delta_(j,0)+A_j(B)e(alpha log B)}.       (11.167.4)
```

Indeed `A_0(1)=1` and `A_j(1)=0` for `1<=j<=5`.  Thus the lower hard
endpoint is present only in `H_0`; the upper endpoint is present in all six
moments.  Direct differentiation gives

```text
E_j'=iE_(j+1),       I_(j,r)'=iI_(j+1,r),  0<=j<=4. (11.167.5)
```

Equation (11.167.5) is asserted modewise for the finite integral.  The
identity for `H_j'` follows by applying (11.167.3) separately at orders `j`
and `j+1`; it does not silently differentiate a conditionally convergent
infinite series term by term.

For a positive dual mode `r`, the Poisson phase is

```text
phi_r(u)=alpha log u-ru,

u_r=alpha/r,       phi_r(u_r)=alpha[log(alpha/r)-1],

phi_r''(u_r)=-r^2/alpha.                           (11.167.6)
```

There is one stationary point in `[1,B]` exactly when

```text
alpha/B<=r<=alpha.                                 (11.167.7)
```

Modes `r<=0` have no stationary point there.  Since the curvature in
(11.167.6) is negative, the one-dimensional stationary signature is
`e(-1/8)=exp(-i pi/4)`, and

```text
1/sqrt(|phi_r''(u_r)|)=sqrt(alpha)/r=u_r/sqrt(alpha).
```

Consequently the order-`j` interior stationary main is

```text
M_(j,r)
 =[sqrt(alpha)/r]A_j(u_r)
   e(alpha[log(u_r)-1]-1/8).                       (11.167.8)
```

The `pi/4` in the equivalent exponential is the standard negative-curvature
stationary signature: `e(-1/8)=exp(-i pi/4)`.  Together with the Poisson
normalization in (11.167.1), this accounts for every new occurrence of `pi`
in this section.

The main is not transported by phase differentiation alone because its
saddle and prefactor move with `xi`.  On a fixed dual chart, direct
differentiation of (11.167.8) proves

```text
M_(j,r)'=iM_(j+1,r)+C_(j,r),                       (11.167.9)

C_(j,r)
 =[sqrt(alpha)/r]e(alpha[log(u_r)-1]-1/8)
   /(2pi alpha)
   *{jA_(j-1)(u_r)
      +[1/2-sigma+(t/2)log(u_r)]A_j(u_r)}.         (11.167.10)
```

The first term in (11.167.9) differentiates the oscillatory phase;
`C_(j,r)` is the exact saddle-motion and stationary-prefactor transport.
It cannot be discarded.  For the mode residual

```text
R_(j,r)=I_(j,r)-M_(j,r),
```

(11.167.5) and (11.167.9) give the closed recurrence

```text
R_(j,r)'=iR_(j+1,r)-C_(j,r),       0<=j<=4.        (11.167.11)
```

Thus the first-`xi` remainder through order four needs only the six value
remainders `R_0,...,R_5` and transport amplitudes through `A_4`; no seventh
logarithmic moment is introduced.  This matches the exact Section 11.165
observation algebra: `V,N,A,Q` and their four `xi` derivatives are fixed real
linear forms of `G_0,...,G_5`.  The physical `x` differentiations defining
`N` and `Q` are already encoded in those rows.  Hence the analytic input is
six endpoint-complete value transforms, not eight independently constructed
value/physical-derivative transforms.  Uniformity in all fixed chart
parameters is still required.

To expose the dual endpoint issue, define the sharp stationary proxy

```text
P_j=E_j+sum^*_(alpha/B<=r<=alpha)M_(j,r),

Delta_j=H_j-P_j.                                  (11.167.12)
```

On every open `xi` interval where neither endpoint of (11.167.7) crosses an
integer, (11.167.11) sums to

```text
Delta_j'=iDelta_(j+1)
          -sum^*_(alpha/B<=r<=alpha)C_(j,r),
                                                    0<=j<=4. (11.167.13)
```

The star in (11.167.12) is structural.  As `alpha` increases through an
integer `q`, the upper condition admits mode `q`, so

```text
P_j(alpha+)-P_j(alpha-)=+M_(j,q).                  (11.167.14)
```

As `alpha` increases through `Bq`, the lower condition removes mode `q`, so

```text
P_j(alpha+)-P_j(alpha-)=-M_(j,q).                  (11.167.15)
```

At either crossing the starred value is the midpoint and `Delta_j` has the
opposite jump.  The crossing frequencies are `xi=2pi q` and `xi=2pi Bq`.
The sharp proxy is therefore piecewise smooth, not globally `C1`; the short
length of the auxiliary segment does not by itself exclude a crossing.
A proof must compose these jumps with the physical hard endpoints and the
adjacent terminal recurrence, or use a sourced smooth endpoint transition.

The same source supplies a qualitative weighted B-process theorem, but its
hypotheses have to be localized.  For `f(u)=alpha log u` on `[U,2U]`,

```text
alpha/(4U^2)<=|f''(u)|<=alpha/U^2,

|f'''(u)|<=2alpha/U^3,

|f''''(u)|<=6alpha/U^4.                            (11.167.16)
```

After complex conjugation to match the theorem's curvature sign, Vandehey's
Theorem 1.1 applies on each such block with `M=U` and `T=alpha`.  In the
source's notation it gives a starred stationary transform with qualitative
error

```text
O((V+|g(A)|)
  {M/sqrt(T)+log(f'(A)-f'(D)+2)}),                 (11.167.17)
```

where the implicit constant depends on derivative-comparability constants.
This validates the local transform architecture, not the required numerical
remainder.  On the full interval `[1,B]`, the curvature ratio is `B^2`, so a
single invocation cannot have `B`-independent comparability constants.  A
dyadic or smooth localization is compulsory.  Hard dyadic blocks also create
artificial half-endpoints; those terms must cancel algebraically when blocks
are rejoined, rather than being bounded independently and destroying the
signed structure.

The next quantitative theorem is now precise: choose a smooth localization
or a uniform endpoint transition, derive explicit value-remainder constants
for `H_0,...,H_5` on the full physical chart, rejoin every internal boundary,
and compose the two real hard endpoints with the terminal recurrence.  Insert
those six transforms into the eight observation rows, apply the Section
11.166 Hermitian pairing before absolute values, and prove

```text
Psi(T_0)-epsilon integral_0^1
  Psi'(T_0-theta epsilon)dtheta
 <=h^2/400,                                        (11.167.18)
```

preferably with right side `h^2/800`.

This section proves the endpoint-complete specialization of finite starred
Poisson summation, the six modewise frequency shifts, the negative-curvature
stationary main, five stationary-transport and residual recurrences, the
reduction from eight observations to six value transforms, both sharp dual
cutoff jump laws, and dyadic admissibility for one sourced weighted B-process
theorem.  It proves no explicit uniform Poisson/B-process remainder constant,
smooth endpoint-transition estimate, imaginary Hermitian coefficient bound,
signed offset-sum gain, signed flow estimate, `Phi_B` bound, contact
exclusion, retained aggregate or Xi theorem, `Q209`, cofinal descendant
theorem, `Lambda<=0`, PF-infinity, RH, or prize-level conclusion.

## 11.168 Fixed-roster logarithmic Morse-Fresnel endpoint reduction

Section 11.167 leaves a genuine discontinuity in the sharp stationary proxy:
the upper and lower dual cutoffs jump whenever a saddle crosses a physical
endpoint.  It also leaves the constant in the localized B-process remainder
implicit.  Vandehey, *Error term improvements for van der Corput transforms*,
`https://arxiv.org/abs/1205.0090`, discusses an incomplete-Fresnel endpoint
chart in Section 11, but the relevant displayed error estimates and
Corollary 1.4 still use implicit constants.  This section therefore uses no
numerical constant from that source.  Instead it exploits the exact
logarithmic phase to build one global Morse coordinate and then reassembles
the complementary nonstationary tail before taking absolute values.

Retain all notation and the symmetric Poisson convention of Section 11.167.
For a positive mode `r`, put

```text
u_0=alpha/r,       v=u/u_0,       h(v)=v-1-log v,

phi_r(u)=alpha log u-ru
        =phi_r(u_0)-alpha h(v),

phi_r(u_0)=alpha[log(alpha/r)-1].                 (11.168.1)
```

Since `h(v)>=0`, with equality only at `v=1`, define the signed coordinate

```text
z(v)=sgn(v-1)sqrt(2h(v)),       z(1)=0,

z'(v)=(v-1)/(vz(v))>0,

J(v)=dv/dz=vz(v)/(v-1),         J(1)=1.           (11.168.2)
```

The removable continuation at `v=1` is analytic.  The endpoint limits of
`z` are `-infinity` and `+infinity`, so `z:(0,infinity)->R` is a smooth
increasing bijection.  With `y=sqrt(alpha)z(v)`, (11.168.1) becomes

```text
phi_r(u)=phi_r(u_0)-y^2/2,

du/dy=[sqrt(alpha)/r]J(v).                         (11.168.3)
```

This is an exact quadratic phase identity, not a local asymptotic
replacement.  For `delta=v-1`, the removable chart is fixed by

```text
z=delta-delta^2/3+7delta^3/36+O(delta^4),

J=1+2delta/3-5delta^2/36+O(delta^3).              (11.168.4)
```

The `O` terms in (11.168.4) describe only the local analytic chart; they do
not enter the exact decomposition or any claimed physical remainder bound.
The transformed physical endpoints are

```text
y_1=sqrt(alpha)z(r/alpha),

y_B=sqrt(alpha)z(Br/alpha).                        (11.168.5)
```

Thus `r=alpha` is exactly `y_1=0`, while `r=alpha/B` is exactly `y_B=0`.
Both moving cutoff events now occur inside one continuous coordinate.

Let `alpha_-<=alpha<=alpha_+` be the full auxiliary-frequency segment and
choose the deliberately enlarged, fixed roster

```text
m=max(1,floor(alpha_-/(2B))),

n=ceil(2alpha_+),       T={m,m+1,...,n}.           (11.168.6)
```

Every positive mode satisfying `alpha/B<=r<=alpha` for some point of the
segment belongs to `T`.  If `r<m`, then `q_r(u)=alpha/u-r` is positive and
larger than `alpha_-/(2B)` on `[1,B]`; if `r>n`, then `q_r(u)<-alpha_+`.
Hence all modes outside `T` are uniformly nonstationary throughout the
whole segment.

For `0<=j<=5`, let `v(y)` denote the inverse coordinate and define

```text
b_(j,r)(y)
 =[sqrt(alpha)/r]A_j(u_0v(y))J(v(y)),

b_(j,r)(0)=[sqrt(alpha)/r]A_j(u_0).                (11.168.7)
```

Then every roster integral in (11.167.3), including a mode whose saddle is
just outside `[1,B]`, has the exact form

```text
I_(j,r)
 =e(phi_r(u_0)) integral_(y_1)^(y_B)
    b_(j,r)(y)e(-y^2/2)dy.                         (11.168.8)
```

Put

```text
F(a,b)=integral_a^b e(-y^2/2)dy,

U_(j,r)=b_(j,r)(0)e(phi_r(u_0))F(y_1,y_B),

Q_(j,r)=I_(j,r)-U_(j,r).                           (11.168.9)
```

The standard Fresnel normalization gives

```text
F(-infinity,infinity)=e(-1/8)=exp(-i pi/4),

F(-infinity,0)=F(0,infinity)=e(-1/8)/2.           (11.168.10)
```

Consequently the full stationary main and both starred half-mains in
Section 11.167 are limits of the single continuous function `U_(j,r)`.
There is no separate sharp cutoff rule in the exact roster representation.

For the residual, define the removable quotient

```text
c_(j,r)(y)=[b_(j,r)(y)-b_(j,r)(0)]/y,

c_(j,r)(0)=b_(j,r)'(0).                            (11.168.11)
```

Since `d e(-y^2/2)/dy=-2pi i y e(-y^2/2)`, one exact integration by parts
gives the explicit majorant

```text
|Q_(j,r)|
 <=1/(2pi){|c_(j,r)(y_1)|+|c_(j,r)(y_B)|
             +integral_(y_1)^(y_B)|c_(j,r)'(y)|dy}. (11.168.12)
```

There is no hidden constant.  Regularity at the saddle can be evaluated
without a subtractive quotient by

```text
c(y)=integral_0^1 b'(sy)ds,

c'(y)=integral_0^1 s b''(sy)ds.                   (11.168.13)
```

With `A_(-1)=0`, direct differentiation of (11.168.7) also gives

```text
c_(j,r)(0)
 =r^(-1){jA_(j-1)(u_0)
          +[2/3-sigma+(t/2)log(u_0)]A_j(u_0)}.    (11.168.14)
```

It remains to sum every mode outside `T` without introducing artificial
dyadic endpoints.  Write

```text
kappa=1/(2pi i),       q_r(u)=alpha/u-r,

D_rA=(A/q_r)',         C_rA=((D_rA)/q_r)'.         (11.168.15)
```

Twice integrating by parts gives the exact identity

```text
I_r
 =kappa[e(phi_r)A/q_r]_1^B
  -kappa^2[e(phi_r)(D_rA)/q_r]_1^B
  +kappa^2 integral_1^B e(phi_r)C_rA du.           (11.168.16)
```

Here `q_r'=-alpha/u^2`, `q_r''=2alpha/u^3`, and

```text
C_rA
 =A''/q_r^2-3A'q_r'/q_r^3-Aq_r''/q_r^3
   +3A(q_r')^2/q_r^4.                              (11.168.17)
```

For `x in (m-1,n+1)`, put `a_x=x-m+1` and `b_x=n+1-x`.  The three complete
outside-roster endpoint sums are

```text
S_1(x)=psi(b_x)-psi(a_x),

S_2(x)=zeta(2,a_x)+zeta(2,b_x),

S_3(x)=zeta(3,a_x)-zeta(3,b_x).                   (11.168.18)
```

The first identity uses the same symmetric principal-value convention as
the full Poisson formula.  Equivalently,

```text
S_1(x)=pi cot(pi x)-sum_(r=m)^n 1/(x-r),           (11.168.19)
```

with the removable value used at every integer in `T`.  The occurrence of
`pi` in (11.168.19) is forced by the symmetric partial-fraction expansion of
`pi cot(pi x)`.  Together with `e(x)=exp(2pi i x)` and the Fresnel signature
in (11.168.10), this supplies the analytic provenance of every `pi` in this
section; none is geometrically fitted.

Both physical endpoints `mu in {1,B}` are integers, so `e(-rmu)=1`.  For
`x=alpha/mu`, define the complete outside-roster endpoint functional

```text
calB_j(mu)
 =e(alpha log mu){kappa A_j(mu)S_1(x)
   -kappa^2[A_j'(mu)S_2(x)
      +(alpha/mu^2)A_j(mu)S_3(x)]}.                (11.168.20)
```

Summing (11.168.16) first and only then taking absolute values yields

```text
sum^sym_(r notin T) I_(j,r)
 =calB_j(B)-calB_j(1)
  +kappa^2 sum_(r notin T) integral_1^B
       e(phi_r(u))C_rA_j(u)du.                    (11.168.21)
```

Only `S_1` is conditional.  For `k>=2`, set

```text
Z_k(x)=zeta(k,a_x)+zeta(k,b_x).
```

The last term in (11.168.21) is absolutely convergent and obeys

```text
|kappa^2 sum_(r notin T) integral e(phi_r)C_rA_j du|
 <=1/(4pi^2) integral_1^B {
      |A_j''|Z_2
     +[3|A_j'||q'|+|A_j||q''|]Z_3
     +3|A_j||q'|^2Z_4}du,                         (11.168.22)
```

where `x=alpha/u`, `|q'|=alpha/u^2`, and `|q''|=2alpha/u^3` inside the
integrand.  This removes the artificial internal boundaries and logarithmic
truncation loss of a hard dyadic decomposition.  It does not assert that the
explicit right side is already small enough on the physical chart.

Equations (11.168.8)-(11.168.22) apply separately to `j=0,...,5`.  By
Section 11.167, those six value transforms still supply all eight real flow
observations; no derivative of a moving sharp cutoff and no seventh moment
is required.  The next quantitative stage is to interval-bound the six
roster sums of (11.168.12), evaluate the six tail integrals (11.168.22),
compose `calB_j(B)-calB_j(1)` with the terminal recurrence, preserve the
Hermitian pairings of Section 11.166, and prove

```text
Psi(T_0)-epsilon integral_0^1
  Psi'(T_0-theta epsilon)dtheta
 <=h^2/400,                                        (11.168.23)
```

preferably with right side `h^2/800`.

This section proves the global logarithmic Morse coordinate, one exact
incomplete-Fresnel representation for every mode in a fixed transition
roster, the explicit `1/(2pi)` residual-variation bound, exact twice-
integrated reassembly of the nonstationary tail, stable digamma/Hurwitz-zeta
endpoint sums, and an explicit absolutely convergent tail majorant for all
six moments.  It evaluates no physical remainder constant and proves no
imaginary Hermitian coefficient bound, signed offset-sum gain, signed flow
estimate, `Phi_B` bound, contact exclusion, retained aggregate or Xi theorem,
`Q209`, cofinal descendant theorem, `Lambda<=0`, PF-infinity, RH, or
prize-level conclusion.

## 11.169 Morse-Fresnel aggregate-scaling gate

Section 11.168 gives an exact fixed-roster representation, but an explicit
per-mode majorant is useful only if its aggregate has the physical scale.  This
section performs that scale audit without enumerating the roster.  It proves
that the outside-roster integral remainder can be bounded absolutely at
`O(h^2)`, while the particular termwise transition majorant (11.168.12)
cannot by itself establish an `O(h^2)` theorem.  The latter statement is about
the nonnegative majorant, not the true signed transition residual.

Retain the physical `q=1` chart and the admissible terminal prefix:

```text
L>=50,                 t=1/(2L^2),

a^2=exp(L)+1/(32L^2),  a=N+theta,       0<=theta<=1,

B=N-M-1<a,             h=1/a,

alpha=xi/(2pi)>a^2/2>22,

1/2<sigma<201/400.                              (11.169.1)
```

Here `T_0-epsilon<=xi<=T_0`.  The prefix law `(M+1)^18<=a`, together
with `a>2^25`, gives `B>2>exp(1/10)`.  Hence every mode in

```text
R_alpha={r in Z: ceil(alpha exp(-1/10))<=r<=floor(alpha)}
                                                        (11.169.2)
```

has a saddle `u_0=alpha/r` in `[1,exp(1/10)]`, and so belongs to the fixed
roster of Section 11.168.  At its lower physical endpoint put
`v=r/alpha=exp(-s)`, where `s=log(u_0)` and `0<=s<=1/10`.  The exact Morse
Jacobian gives the two dimensionless functions

```text
P(s)=J(v)^2/v
    =2[exp(s)(s-1)+1]/[exp(s)-1]^2,

Q(s)=J(v) partial_v J(v)
    =[2s exp(2s)-3exp(2s)+4exp(s)-1]/[exp(s)-1]^3
    =[P(s)-P'(s)]/2.                              (11.169.3)
```

Both have removable values at `s=0`, namely `P(0)=1` and `Q(0)=2/3`.
Moreover,

```text
[exp(s)-1]^2-2[exp(s)(s-1)+1]
 =2exp(s)[sinh(s)-s]>=0,

0<P(s)<=1.                                       (11.169.4)
```

There is also a rational lower bound for `Q`.  Define

```text
R(s)=25[2s exp(2s)-3exp(2s)+4exp(s)-1]
      -16[exp(s)-1]^3

    =50s exp(2s)-16exp(3s)-27exp(2s)+52exp(s)-9

    =(2/3)s^3-sum_(n>=4) D_n s^n/n!,

D_n=16*3^n-2^(n-1)(50n-54)-52.                  (11.169.5)
```

Here `D_4=76` and

```text
D_(n+1)-2D_n=16*3^n-50*2^n+52>0       (n>=4).
```

For `0<=s<=1/10`, retain the terms through `n=7` and use
`D_n<16*3^n` afterward.  The remaining tail is at most
`2187/81200000`, while

```text
2/3-19/60-35/600-187/36000-1333/4200000
    -2187/81200000
 =8364091/29232000>0.

Therefore R(s)>=0 and Q(s)>=16/25.                (11.169.6)
```

For `j=0`, direct differentiation of (11.168.7), with
`u=(alpha/r)v`, gives at every point of the lower collar

```text
partial_y b_(0,r)
 ={A_0(u)/r}{Q(v)+P(v)[(t/2)log(u)-sigma]}.       (11.169.7)
```

Writing `lambda=log u`, (11.169.1), (11.169.4), and (11.169.6) imply

```text
A_0(u)=exp(t lambda^2/4-sigma lambda)
       >=1-sigma lambda>=3799/4000,

Q+P[(t/2)lambda-sigma]
       >=16/25-201/400=11/80,

partial_y b_(0,r)>=41789/(320000r)>13/(100r).
                                                        (11.169.8)
```

Since `y_1<=0`, the removable quotient in (11.168.11) is the average of
`partial_y b` on `[y_1,0]`.  Therefore

```text
c_(0,r)(y_1)>=13/(100r),       r in R_alpha.      (11.169.9)
```

The elementary inequality `exp(-1/10)<10/11` and `alpha>=22` give

```text
#R_alpha>alpha/11-1>=alpha/22,

sum_(r in R_alpha)1/r>=1/22.
```

Let `mathfrak M_(0,r)` denote the nonnegative right side of the explicit
majorant (11.168.12).  Keeping only its lower-endpoint term and using the
classical rational inequality `pi<22/7` gives

```text
sum_(r in R_alpha) mathfrak M_(0,r)
 >=1/(2pi) sum_(r in R_alpha)c_(0,r)(y_1)
 >13/100 * 1/22 * 7/44
 =91/96800.                                       (11.169.10)
```

Because `a^2>exp(50)>2^50`, this selected majorant satisfies

```text
[sum_(r in R_alpha) mathfrak M_(0,r)]/h^2
 >(91/96800)2^50>10^12.                           (11.169.11)
```

Thus summing (11.168.12) mode by mode cannot certify a bare-value `h^2`
bound.  Equation (11.169.11) does not lower-bound
`|sum_r Q_(0,r)|`, or even `sum_r|Q_(0,r)|`; a large upper majorant may be
very wasteful.  It rules out only this proposed termwise endpoint-variation
aggregation.  The exact incomplete-Fresnel terms must instead be grouped by
Hermitian pairing, Poisson/Abel summation, or another cancellation-preserving
transform before absolute values.

The outside-roster integral remainder has different scaling.  For
`x=alpha/u`, `a_x=x-m+1`, and `b_x=n+1-x`, the fixed roster (11.168.6)
gives

```text
a_x>=alpha/(2u),             b_x>=alpha.

zeta(k,q)<=q^(-k)+q^(1-k)/(k-1)<=2q^(1-k)
                                      (k>=2, q>=1). (11.169.12)
```

Consequently the absolute sums in (11.168.22) obey

```text
Z_2<=6u/alpha,

Z_3<=10u^2/alpha^2,

Z_4<=18u^3/alpha^3.                           (11.169.13)
```

Set `lambda=log u` and `D=d/dlambda=u d/du`.  Substitution in
(11.168.22), including `du=u dlambda`, gives the exact envelope

```text
Tail_j
 <=1/(4pi^2 alpha) integral_0^(log B)
    {6|(D^2-D)A_j|+30|DA_j|+74|A_j|}dlambda.
                                                        (11.169.14)
```

For `A_j=lambda^j exp(g)` and `g=t lambda^2/4-sigma lambda`, the physical
chart has

```text
g'<=-49/100,       |g'|<=51/100,       g''<=1/10000.
```

It follows that

```text
|A_j|<=lambda^j exp(-49lambda/100),

|DA_j|<={j lambda^(j-1)+(51/100)lambda^j}
          exp(-49lambda/100),

|(D^2-D)A_j|
 <={j(j-1)lambda^(j-2)+(101j/50)lambda^(j-1)
       +(3851/5000)lambda^j}exp(-49lambda/100).
                                                        (11.169.15)
```

Negative powers in (11.169.15) are absent when their polynomial coefficient
vanishes.  The required moments are elementary:

```text
integral_0^infinity lambda^k exp(-49lambda/100)dlambda
 =k!(100/49)^(k+1).                                (11.169.16)
```

Let `C_j` be the resulting integral bound for the braces in
(11.169.14), and let `K_j=ceil(C_j/36)`.  Exact rational arithmetic gives

```text
j    C_j                                  K_j
0    234803/1225                             6
1    1145600/2401                           14
2    232001200/117649                       55
3    69600360000/5764801                   336
4    27840144000000/282475249             2738
5    13920072000000000/13841287201       27936.
                                                        (11.169.17)
```

The factors of `pi` here are inherited, not fitted: `e(x)=exp(2pi i x)`
forces `1/(2pi)` in (11.168.12), its twice-integrated operator gives
`1/(4pi^2)` in (11.169.14), and the rational comparisons use only the
classical analytic bounds `3<pi<22/7`.  No circle or polygon belonging to
the prime data is chosen.

Finally, `pi>3` and `alpha>a^2/2` imply

```text
Tail_j<C_j/(36alpha)<K_j/alpha<=2K_j h^2,

(2K_0,...,2K_5)=(12,28,110,672,5476,55872).
                                                        (11.169.18)
```

This proves physical `h^2` scaling only for the absolutely convergent
integral remainder after the exact endpoint term
`calB_j(B)-calB_j(1)` has been extracted.  It does not bound either endpoint
functional.  The live scalar theorem is now a grouped roster estimate that
keeps the incomplete-Fresnel transition exact and preserves its phase
cancellation, followed by composition with both `calB_j` endpoints, the
physical endpoint `E_j`, `c_xi`, the Hermitian and transpose families, and
the terminal recurrence.  Only after that composition may the six values be
inserted into the eight observations and tested against

```text
Psi(T_0)-epsilon integral_0^1
  Psi'(T_0-theta epsilon)dtheta
 <=h^2/400.                                        (11.169.19)
```

This section proves one scale obstruction for a specified nonnegative
transition majorant and six explicit `O(h^2)` outside-roster integral-tail
bounds.  It proves no grouped roster bound, endpoint-functional bound,
evaluated full physical remainder, signed flow estimate, `Phi_B` bound,
contact exclusion, retained aggregate or Xi theorem, `Q209`, cofinal
descendant theorem, `Lambda<=0`, PF-infinity, RH, or prize-level conclusion.

## 11.170 Endpoint-stationary Abel and coherent-trace gate

Section 11.169 proves that the separated endpoint-plus-variation majorants
cannot be summed at `h^2` scale.  The remaining possibility is cancellation
in the exact roster sum.  This section identifies exactly where the saddle
phase can provide cancellation and where it disappears.  The phase has a
discrete stationary endpoint, so coefficient-blind Abel summation naturally
stops at square-root scale.  More importantly, exact residual integration by
parts makes both physical boundary traces coherent across all integral modes.

Retain the `q=1` chart and lower collar of (11.169.1)-(11.169.2).  Since
`a^2>exp(50)>2^50` and `alpha>a^2/2`,

```text
alpha>2^49>4096,

R=floor(alpha),

R_alpha={ceil(alpha exp(-1/10)),...,R}.            (11.170.1)
```

For integral `r`, adding `r` does not change the exponential phase.  Define

```text
G_alpha(r)=alpha[log(alpha/r)-1]+r,

e(G_alpha(r))=e(phi_r(alpha/r)).                   (11.170.2)
```

The first two forward differences are exact:

```text
Delta G_alpha(r)=1-alpha log(1+1/r),

Delta^2 G_alpha(r)
 =alpha log((r+1)^2/[r(r+2)])
 =alpha log(1+1/[r(r+2)])>0.                      (11.170.3)
```

Thus the first difference is strictly increasing.  The elementary bounds
`x/(1+x)<=log(1+x)<=x`, together with
`exp(1/10)<10/9`, give throughout the collar

```text
1/(2alpha)<=Delta^2G_alpha(r)<=5/(4alpha).         (11.170.4)
```

There is no uniform first-difference gap from the integers: near `r=R`,
`Delta G_alpha(r)` approaches zero.  This is a discrete endpoint stationary
phase, not a nonstationary geometric progression.

Put

```text
H=ceil(sqrt(alpha)),       n_0=R-H,

delta_r=Delta G_alpha(r).                             (11.170.5)
```

On the outer collar `r<=n_0`, the logarithm bounds give

```text
-1/9<delta_r<0,

|delta_(n_0)|>=(H-1)/(alpha-H+1).
```

For `z_r=e(G_alpha(r))` and
`A_r=[e(delta_r)-1]^(-1)`, the difference equation
`z_(r+1)-z_r=[e(delta_r)-1]z_r` gives the exact Abel identity

```text
sum_(r=m)^n z_r
 =A_nz_(n+1)-A_mz_m
   +sum_(r=m+1)^n[A_(r-1)-A_r]z_r.                (11.170.6)
```

For `-1/2<delta<0`,

```text
A(delta)=-1/2-(i/2)cot(pi delta).
```

Its real part is fixed and its imaginary part is monotone, so the total
variation in (11.170.6) telescopes.  Also
`|e(delta)-1|=2sin(pi|delta|)>=4|delta|`.  Hence every outer interval ending
at `n<=n_0` satisfies

```text
|sum_(r=m)^n e(G_alpha(r))|
 <=1/|delta_n|
 <=(alpha-H+1)/(H-1).                              (11.170.7)
```

The remaining terminal core has at most `H` modes.  Since
`H<=sqrt(alpha)+1` and `H-1>=sqrt(alpha)-1`, every contiguous subinterval
`I` of the full collar obeys

```text
|sum_(r in I)e(G_alpha(r))|
 <H+alpha/(H-1)<3sqrt(alpha).                      (11.170.8)
```

No imported exponential-sum constant is used.  A second Abel summation now
gives, for arbitrary complex weights `w_r`,

```text
|sum_(r=m)^n w_r e(G_alpha(r))|
 <3sqrt(alpha){|w_n|+sum_(r=m)^(n-1)|w_(r+1)-w_r|}.
                                                        (11.170.9)
```

Thus a natural discrete bounded-variation norm `C/alpha` supplies only
`3C/sqrt(alpha)`, which is `h` scale because `alpha<=a^2`.  This upper bound
alone does not prove that the actual coefficients attain that scale.  A
physical subblock shows, however, that no uniform `h^2` partial-sum theorem
can follow from the phase and the positive lower coefficient floor alone.

Let

```text
K=floor(sqrt(alpha)/20).
```

For `0<=k<=K`, the block `R-K<=r<=R` lies in `R_alpha`, and

```text
0<=G_alpha(R-k)-G_alpha(R)
 =integral_(R-k)^R(alpha/x-1)dx
 <=k(k+1)/(R-k)<1/300.                            (11.170.10)
```

The last inequality follows from `sqrt(alpha)>=64`: after putting
`A=sqrt(alpha)`, the required cross-multiplied reserve is
`A^2/4-(301/20)A-1`, which is increasing and equals `299/5` at `A=64`.
The angular width is therefore below `pi/150<1/40`, and
`cos(pi/150)>99/100`.  Combining this sector with (11.169.9) yields the
actual partial-sum guard

```text
|sum_(k=0)^K c_(0,R-k)(y_1)e(G_alpha(R-k))|
 >1287/[200000sqrt(alpha)]
 >=1287h/200000.                                  (11.170.11)
```

Since `a>2^25`, the right side of (11.170.11) exceeds `200000h^2`:

```text
[1287h/200000]/h^2>1287*2^25/200000>200000.
                                                        (11.170.12)
```

This is a subblock and Abel-method nonpromotion guard.  Modes outside the
subblock may cancel it, and it is not a lower bound for the complete signed
transition residual.

The stronger structural issue appears when the residual itself is integrated
by parts.  For `s=log(alpha/r)` and

```text
Z(s)=sqrt(2[exp(-s)-1+s]),

c_(j,r)(y_1)
 ={A_j(exp(s))-A_j(1)J(exp(-s))}/[rZ(s)].         (11.170.13)
```

With `kappa=1/(2pi i)`, the exact identity behind (11.168.12) is

```text
Q_(j,r)
 =kappa c_(j,r)(y_1)
  -kappa e(alpha log B)c_(j,r)(y_B)
  +kappa e(phi_r(alpha/r))
     integral_(y_1)^(y_B)c'_(j,r)(y)e(-y^2/2)dy. (11.170.14)
```

Indeed, the Morse identity at the two physical endpoints gives

```text
phi_r(alpha/r)-y_1^2/2=-r,

phi_r(alpha/r)-y_B^2/2=alpha log B-rB.            (11.170.15)
```

Both `r` and `B` are integral.  Therefore every lower trace has phase
`e(-r)=1`, and every upper trace has the common phase `e(alpha log B)`.
The saddle phase has disappeared from the two separated boundary sums.
In particular, (11.169.9) and the analytic harmonic count give the exact
coherent component

```text
|kappa sum_(r in R_alpha)c_(0,r)(y_1)|
 >13/(4400pi)>91/96800.                           (11.170.16)
```

Equation (11.170.16) is not a lower bound for `|sum_r Q_(0,r)|`: the upper
trace and the still-oscillatory `c'` integral in (11.170.14) may cancel it.
It does prove that neither saddle-phase Abel cancellation nor Hermitian
pairing can act on the two boundary traces after they are separated.

The next theorem must therefore reassemble the endpoint package before any
absolute estimate.  For all six values, it must join the physical endpoint
`E_j`, both roster traces in (11.170.14), the extracted functionals
`calB_j(B)-calB_j(1)`, and the terminal recurrence.  Only the remaining
interior term should then be subjected to grouped saddle-phase analysis.
After insertion into the eight observations, the target remains

```text
Psi(T_0)-epsilon integral_0^1
  Psi'(T_0-theta epsilon)dtheta
 <=h^2/400.                                        (11.170.17)
```

Every `pi` here is inherited analytically: `e(x)=exp(2pi i x)` gives the
discrete phases, `kappa=1/(2pi i)` comes from differentiating the Fresnel
oscillation, and the cotangent in (11.170.6) is the exact algebraic identity
`1/[e(delta)-1]=-1/2-(i/2)cot(pi delta)`.  The sector comparison uses only
the classical rational bound `pi<22/7`; no geometric constant is fitted.

This section proves the exact phase differences, an explicit
`O(sqrt(alpha))` phase partial-sum bound, one actual `h`-scale terminal
subblock guard, and exact coherence of both residual endpoint traces.  It
proves no lower bound for the complete signed residual, cancellation of the
coherent endpoint package, bound for either `calB_j`, endpoint-composed or
grouped-roster `h^2` estimate, evaluated full physical remainder, signed flow
estimate, `Phi_B` bound, contact exclusion, retained aggregate or Xi theorem,
`Q209`, cofinal descendant theorem, `Lambda<=0`, PF-infinity, RH, or
prize-level conclusion.

## 11.171 Endpoint-composed six-value carrier and retention gate

Section 11.170 shows that the two residual boundary traces are coherent, so
they cannot be estimated by the saddle phase after being separated.  This
section performs the required exact recombination.  The outcome is not that
the hard endpoints cancel or become small.  They form a retained carrier,
while the still-oscillatory interior `c'` sum becomes the remaining analytic
remainder.

Retain the fixed roster `T={m,...,n}`, `kappa=1/(2pi i)`, and all notation of
Sections 11.167--11.170.  Put `e_B=e(alpha log B)` and define

```text
mathcal F_j=sum_(r in T)U_(j,r),

mathcal J_j=kappa sum_(r in T)e(phi_r(alpha/r))
  integral_(y_1)^(y_B)c'_(j,r)(y)e(-y^2/2)dy,

mathcal T_j=kappa^2 sum_(r notin T)
  integral_1^B e(phi_r(u))C_rA_j(u)du.             (11.171.1)
```

The lower and factored upper endpoint packages are

```text
mathcal L_j
 =delta_(j0)/2-calB_j(1)
   +kappa sum_(r in T)c_(j,r)(y_1),

mathcal U_j
 =A_j(B)/2+e(-alpha log B)calB_j(B)
   -kappa sum_(r in T)c_(j,r)(y_B).                (11.171.2)
```

Substitute the exact residual identity (11.170.14) into the roster part of
finite Poisson summation and substitute (11.168.21) for its complement.
Collecting the two physical endpoint phases gives, with no absolute value,

```text
H_j=mathcal F_j+mathcal L_j+e_B mathcal U_j
      +mathcal J_j+mathcal T_j,       0<=j<=5.     (11.171.3)
```

These are the six endpoint-composed value identities.  They contain no
moving sharp cutoff and are continuous through either saddle crossing.

The packages can be written entirely in the stable endpoint sums of
(11.168.18).  Since

```text
A_j(1)=delta_(j0),

d_j:=A_j'(1)=-sigma delta_(j0)+delta_(j1),         (11.171.4)
```

one has, for `x_B=alpha/B`,

```text
mathcal L_j
 =delta_(j0)/2-kappa delta_(j0)S_1(alpha)
  +kappa^2[d_jS_2(alpha)+alpha delta_(j0)S_3(alpha)]
  +kappa sum_(r in T)c_(j,r)(y_1),

mathcal U_j
 =A_j(B)/2+kappa A_j(B)S_1(x_B)
  -kappa^2[A_j'(B)S_2(x_B)
       +(alpha/B^2)A_j(B)S_3(x_B)]
  -kappa sum_(r in T)c_(j,r)(y_B).                (11.171.5)
```

If `lambda=log B`, the derivative in the second line is explicitly

```text
A_j'(B)
 =B^(-1)exp(t lambda^2/4-sigma lambda)
   {j lambda^(j-1)+(t lambda/2-sigma)lambda^j},   (11.171.6)
```

where the first term is absent at `j=0`.  Formula (11.171.5), rather than a
full cotangent rewrite, is the stable representation: its Hurwitz arguments
remain positive even when `alpha` or `alpha/B` is integral inside `T`.

There is a decisive real-part audit.  Every `S_k`, endpoint `c`, and amplitude
in (11.171.5) is real, while `kappa` is purely imaginary and
`kappa^2=-1/(4pi^2)`.  Therefore

```text
Re mathcal L_j
 =delta_(j0)/2
  -[d_jS_2(alpha)+alpha delta_(j0)S_3(alpha)]/(4pi^2),

Re mathcal U_j
 =A_j(B)/2
  +[A_j'(B)S_2(x_B)
      +(alpha/B^2)A_j(B)S_3(x_B)]/(4pi^2).        (11.171.7)
```

For `j=0`, the bounds from (11.169.13), `sigma<201/400`, and `pi>3` give

```text
|Re mathcal L_0-1/2|
 <=[sigma Z_2(alpha)+alpha Z_3(alpha)]/(4pi^2)
 <2603/(7200alpha)<1/10000,

|mathcal L_0|>4999/10000.                         (11.171.8)
```

The last comparison already follows from `alpha>4096`; the physical chart
has `alpha>2^49`.  Thus the lower coherent package does not cancel its hard
half endpoint.

The same conclusion holds at the upper endpoint for all six values.  Since
`lambda>1/10`, `|t lambda/2-sigma|<=51/100`, and `0<=j<=5`,

```text
|A_j'(B)|/A_j(B)
 <=[j/lambda+51/100]/B,

|Re mathcal U_j-A_j(B)/2|
 <A_j(B)[6(j/lambda+51/100)+10]/(36alpha)
 <=15653A_j(B)/(1800alpha).                       (11.171.9)
```

Consequently

```text
|Re mathcal U_j-A_j(B)/2|<A_j(B)/100,

|mathcal U_j|>49A_j(B)/100,       0<=j<=5.        (11.171.10)
```

The common factor `e_B` may later cancel against other physical terms, but
it does not change this modulus.  Equations (11.171.8) and (11.171.10) do
not lower-bound `H_j`; they prove that endpoint composition retains, rather
than estimates away, the hard endpoints.

For completeness, there is an equivalent but less stable cotangent audit.
At a physical endpoint `mu`, put `q_r(mu)=alpha/mu-r`.  Differentiating the
exact Morse phase gives `q_r=-y dy/du`, and hence

```text
b_(j,r)(y_mu)/y_mu=-A_j(mu)/q_r(mu),

c_(j,r)(y_mu)
 =-A_j(mu)/q_r(mu)-b_(j,r)(0)/y_mu.               (11.171.11)
```

Together with (11.168.19),

```text
S_1(x)+sum_(r in T)1/(x-r)=pi cot(pi x),          (11.171.12)
```

this converts (11.171.5) into a full-cotangent formula.  Its first-order
geometric factors are exactly

```text
1/2-kappa pi cot(pi x)=1/[1-e(x)],

1/2+kappa pi cot(pi x)=1/[1-e(-x)].               (11.171.13)
```

At an integral crossing, the apparent cotangent pole cancels the matching
`b(0)/y` pole in (11.171.11).  Separating those poles would manufacture a
singularity absent from (11.171.5), so (11.171.12)--(11.171.13) are audit
identities and not the form to estimate.

The construction is independent of the particular enlarged roster.  If one
uniformly nonstationary mode is moved from the complement into `T`, its two
exact representations are

```text
I_(j,r)
 =U_(j,r)+kappa c_(j,r)(y_1)-kappa e_Bc_(j,r)(y_B)
  +kappa e(phi_r(alpha/r))integral c'_(j,r)e(-y^2/2)

 =kappa[e(phi_r)A_j/q_r]_1^B
  -kappa^2[e(phi_r)(D_rA_j)/q_r]_1^B
  +kappa^2 integral_1^B e(phi_r)C_rA_jdu.         (11.171.14)
```

This one-mode transfer identity proves that the complete right side of
(11.171.3) is roster-invariant.  The individual packages `mathcal L_j` and
`mathcal U_j` are roster bookkeeping and must not be assigned independent
physical meaning without the other terms.

The correct main/error split is therefore

```text
mathcal P_j^(ec)
 =mathcal F_j+mathcal L_j+e_Bmathcal U_j,

rho_j^(osc)=mathcal J_j+mathcal T_j,

H_j=mathcal P_j^(ec)+rho_j^(osc).                 (11.171.15)
```

This also locates the terminal recurrence correctly.  Write the fixed source
normalizer as `nu`, so `Ghat_j=nu H_j`, and restore the common phase by
`G_j=c_xi Ghat_j`.  Let `p` and `r` be the twelve-real vectors induced by
`nu c_xi mathcal P^(ec)` and `nu c_xi rho^(osc)`, respectively.  Then

```text
y=p+r.                                            (11.171.16)
```

In the exact eight-observation normal form (11.165.8), `M_xi` is symmetric
and `ell_xi=U_1t_T` already contains all fixed terminal coordinates.  Hence

```text
Psi'
 =p^T M_xi p+ell_xi^T p
  +2p^T M_xi r+r^T M_xi r+ell_xi^T r.            (11.171.17)
```

Thus terminal data compose at the observation map, where they belong; no
unproved scalar cancellation between a Poisson endpoint and a terminal
coordinate has been inserted.

The outside piece is already controlled by (11.169.18):

```text
|mathcal T_j|<2K_jh^2,

(K_0,...,K_5)=(6,14,55,336,2738,27936).          (11.171.18)
```

The live analytic remainder is the grouped vector
`(mathcal J_0,...,mathcal J_5)`.  Its required theorem must be
coefficient-aware: after insertion in (11.171.17), it must bound the three
terms involving `r` together with the retained carrier and terminal row.
The target remains

```text
Psi(T_0)-epsilon integral_0^1
  Psi'(T_0-theta epsilon)dtheta
 <=h^2/400,                                        (11.171.19)
```

preferably with right side `h^2/800`.  An `h^2` bound is not required, and
is false as a generic expectation, for the retained endpoint carrier itself.

Every `pi` in this section is inherited analytically.  The character
`e(x)=exp(2pi i x)` gives `kappa=1/(2pi i)`, and `pi cot(pi x)` is the exact
symmetric partial-fraction sum over integral Poisson modes.  No prime-field

## 11.172 Observation-image compression of the oscillatory remainder

Section 11.171 separates the endpoint-complete carrier from the remaining
Morse-Fresnel residual, but its final formula is still written in twelve real
moment coordinates.  The rank-eight factorization of Section 11.165 gives a
strictly smaller exact target.  More strongly, the complete linear residual
interaction is one polynomial-amplitude Morse functional of degree at most
five, not six separately estimated moment remainders.

Retain `y=p+r` from (11.171.16), where `p` is induced by the retained carrier
and `r` by `rho^(osc)`.  Write `M=M_xi`, `ell=ell_xi`, and set

```text
omega=U_0^Tp=(V_p,N_p,A_p,Q_p)^T,

dot(omega)=U_1^Tp
 =(V_(p,xi),N_(p,xi),A_(p,xi),Q_(p,xi))^T,

epsilon=U_0^Tr=(epsilon_V,epsilon_N,epsilon_A,epsilon_Q)^T,

dot(epsilon)=U_1^Tr
 =(epsilon_(V,xi),epsilon_(N,xi),
   epsilon_(A,xi),epsilon_(Q,xi))^T.             (11.172.1)
```

The four-by-four matrix `J` and terminal vector `t_T` are those of
(11.165.7).  Since

```text
M=U_0JU_1^T+U_1JU_0^T,       ell=U_1t_T,
```

the carrier gradient factors exactly as

```text
g_p:=2Mp+ell
 =U_0[2J dot(omega)]+U_1[2Jomega+t_T].           (11.172.2)
```

Therefore the entire carrier/remainder correction in (11.171.17) is

```text
g_p^Tr+r^TMr
 =2omega^TJ dot(epsilon)
  +2dot(omega)^TJepsilon+t_T^Tdot(epsilon)
  +2epsilon^TJdot(epsilon).                      (11.172.3)
```

No component of `r` outside the eight observations in (11.172.1) appears.
Expanding `J` and `t_T` gives the signed scalar identity

```text
g_p^Tr+r^TMr
 =[N_p+A_(T,x)]epsilon_(V,xi)
  +[X_T+V_p]epsilon_(N,xi)
  -[Q_p+X_(T,x)]epsilon_(A,xi)
  -[A_T+A_p]epsilon_(Q,xi)

  +N_(p,xi)epsilon_V+V_(p,xi)epsilon_N
  -Q_(p,xi)epsilon_A-A_(p,xi)epsilon_Q

  +epsilon_Vepsilon_(N,xi)
  +epsilon_Nepsilon_(V,xi)
  -epsilon_Aepsilon_(Q,xi)
  -epsilon_Qepsilon_(A,xi).                      (11.172.4)
```

This formula already retains the hard endpoints and terminal coordinates:
they occur inside the four joined coefficients on its first two lines.

The eight errors have an exact polynomial-amplitude representation.  For a
complex polynomial `P(lambda)=sum_(j=0)^5p_jlambda^j`, define

```text
A_P(u)=P(log u)exp{t(log u)^2/4-sigma log u}.     (11.172.5)
```

Construct `b_(P,r)`, `c_(P,r)`, and `C_rA_P` by the same linear formulas as
in Sections 11.168 and 11.170, and put

```text
mathscr R[P]
 =kappa sum_(r in T)e(phi_r(alpha/r))
    integral_(y_1)^(y_B)c'_(P,r)(y)e(-y^2/2)dy

  +kappa^2 sum_(r notin T)
    integral_1^B e(phi_r(u))C_rA_P(u)du.

Then mathscr R[P]=sum_(j=0)^5p_jrho_j^(osc).      (11.172.6)
```

Linearity here is exact: the Morse coordinate depends on `alpha,r` but not on
the amplitude, and both the removable quotient and the outside differential
operator are linear.

The four coefficient rows of Section 11.160 are the polynomials

```text
P_V(lambda)=C(lambda),          deg P_V<=2,

P_N(lambda)=N(lambda),          deg P_N<=4,

P_A(lambda)=R(lambda)C(lambda), deg P_A<=3,

P_Q(lambda)=Q(lambda),          deg P_Q<=3.       (11.172.7)
```

The coefficient lift (11.165.2) has a particularly simple polynomial form:

```text
dot(P)(lambda)=i(lambda-log a)P(lambda).          (11.172.8)
```

Indeed the coefficient of `lambda^j` is
`i[p_(j-1)-(log a)p_j]`, with the absent endpoint coefficients interpreted
as zero.  Thus the base/lifted degree ceilings are respectively
`(2,4,3,3)` and `(3,5,4,4)`; no seventh moment is introduced.

Let `nu` be the fixed source normalizer and retain the common phase `c_xi`.
For every polynomial `P`, write

```text
mathscr E[P]=nu c_xi mathscr R[P].                (11.172.9)
```

Then, for `X in {V,N,A,Q}`,

```text
epsilon_X=Re mathscr E[P_X],

epsilon_(X,xi)=Re mathscr E[dot(P_X)].           (11.172.10)
```

Because every coefficient in (11.172.4) is real, all eight linear terms
collapse into one polynomial.  Define

```text
P_lin(lambda)
 =N_(p,xi)P_V+V_(p,xi)P_N
  -Q_(p,xi)P_A-A_(p,xi)P_Q

  +i(lambda-log a){
      [N_p+A_(T,x)]P_V+[X_T+V_p]P_N
      -[Q_p+X_(T,x)]P_A-[A_T+A_p]P_Q}.           (11.172.11)
```

Its degree is at most five, and the full linear correction is exactly

```text
g_p^Tr=Re mathscr E[P_lin].                       (11.172.12)
```

Thus the next linear analytic theorem concerns one physical amplitude
`A_(P_lin)`, assembled after the endpoint, terminal, correction, Hermitian,
and transpose coefficient rows are fixed.  Bounding the six
`rho_j^(osc)` separately would discard this composition.

The nonlinear correction is also confined to the observation image:

```text
r^TMr
 =epsilon_Vepsilon_(N,xi)
  +epsilon_Nepsilon_(V,xi)
  -epsilon_Aepsilon_(Q,xi)
  -epsilon_Qepsilon_(A,xi).                      (11.172.13)
```

It is four signed base/lifted pairings, not a twelve-coordinate norm.  In
particular,

```text
U_0^Tr=U_1^Tr=0
  implies g_p^Tr+r^TMr=0                         (11.172.14)
```

regardless of the componentwise size of `r`.  This is an exact
flow-invisible kernel, not evidence that the physical remainder lies in it.

The already proved outside-tail bounds propagate only after polynomial
composition.  If `P(lambda)=sum_(j=0)^5p_jlambda^j`, then

```text
|mathcal T[P]|
 <2h^2 sum_(j=0)^5K_j|p_j|,

(K_0,...,K_5)=(6,14,55,336,2738,27936).          (11.172.15)
```

Equation (11.172.15) is a coefficient-dependent template.  The physical
coefficients of `P_lin` and of the eight base/lifted rows have not yet been
bounded, so the large `K_4,K_5` constants remain visible rather than being
silently absorbed.

Observation compression alone supplies no universal saddle or endpoint zero.
For an exact algebraic guard, take

```text
log a=2,

P_V=1+lambda^2,       P_N=1+lambda^4,
P_A=lambda^3,         P_Q=1+lambda^3,

(N_(p,xi),V_(p,xi),Q_(p,xi),A_(p,xi))=(1,2,3,4),

(N_p+A_(T,x),X_T+V_p,Q_p+X_(T,x),A_T+A_p)
 =(5,6,7,8).                                           (11.172.16)
```

The resulting `P_lin` has leading coefficient `6i`, degree five, and
`P_lin(log a)=-21`.  This witness is not asserted to be a physical Xi state;
it proves only that neither a factor `lambda-log a` nor an endpoint zero can
be inferred from the algebraic compression itself.

The next bounded stage is now precise.  Expand the actual coefficients of
`P_lin` from `C,N,RC,Q` and the retained carrier observations, derive the
exact `c'_(P_lin,r)` Morse amplitude, and audit its discrete mode variation
and saddle behavior before choosing Abel, Poisson, reciprocal-pair, or
interval control.  The four quadratic pairings in (11.172.13) must be treated
at their normalized scale.  The final benchmark remains

```text
Psi(T_0)-epsilon integral_0^1
  Psi'(T_0-theta epsilon)dtheta
 <=h^2/400,                                        (11.172.17)
```

preferably with right side `h^2/800`.

No new `pi` occurs in this section.  All such factors remain those inherited
through `kappa=1/(2pi i)` and the Fourier character used in the underlying
Morse residual.

This section proves exact observation-image compression, degree-five
polynomial-amplitude closure, collapse of the complete linear remainder to
one complex Morse functional, four exact quadratic observation pairings, a
flow-invisible-kernel identity, and one coefficient-dependent tail template.
It does not evaluate the physical `P_lin`, bound its `c'` interior, control
the four quadratic pairings, prove an `h^2` flow error, evaluate the retained
carrier, prove a signed flow or `Phi_B` bound, exclude contact, establish a
retained aggregate or Xi theorem, prove `Q209`, the cofinal descendant
theorem, `Lambda<=0`, PF-infinity, RH, or a prize-level conclusion.

## 11.173 Physical coefficient factorization and Morse interior amplitude

Section 11.172 reduces the complete linear oscillatory remainder to one
polynomial `P_lin` of degree at most five.  This section expands that
polynomial in a chart which preserves the physical terminal cancellation.
It then gives the exact `c'` amplitude that remains to be summed over the
fixed Morse roster.

Put

```text
x=lambda-log a,                 u_N=log(a/N),

s_*'=c+ib,                     s_*''=c_x+ib_x.
```

Since `log N=log a-u_N`, the carrier rates of (11.160.1) become

```text
R=-s_*'x-c u_N,

R_x=-s_*''x-c_xu_N+i b u_(N,x).                  (11.173.1)
```

Thus the apparently large `log N` and `log a` terms cancel exactly before
any norm is taken.  The correction polynomials in the same variable are

```text
C=c_0+c_1x+c_2x^2,             D=d_0+d_1x+d_2x^2,

c_0=1+rho_1log a+rho_2(log a)^2,
c_1=rho_1+2rho_2log a,         c_2=rho_2,

d_0=rho_(1,x)log a+rho_(2,x)(log a)^2,
d_1=rho_(1,x)+2rho_(2,x)log a, d_2=rho_(2,x).    (11.173.2)
```

Define the exact terminal rate defect

```text
delta=chi_N-i b u_N.
```

Then the four physical observation polynomials satisfy

```text
A=RC,             Q=(R+delta)C+D,

mathcal N=RQ+R_xC.                                (11.173.3)
```

The already certified estimate `|delta|<4h^2` is not used in the algebra
below.

For a real coefficient row `f=(f_V,f_N,f_A,f_Q)`, put

```text
F_f=f_VC+f_Nmathcal N+f_AA+f_QQ.                 (11.173.4)
```

The two physical rows in `P_lin` are

```text
alpha=(N_(p,xi),V_(p,xi),-Q_(p,xi),-A_(p,xi)),

beta=(N_p+A_(T,x),X_T+V_p,
      -Q_p-X_(T,x),-A_T-A_p),

P_lin=F_alpha+i x F_beta.                         (11.173.5)
```

Substitution of (11.173.3) factors every row through only `C` and `D`:

```text
F_f=C U_f+D V_f,

V_f=f_NR+f_Q,

U_f=f_N[R(R+delta)+R_x]+f_Q(R+delta)+f_AR+f_V.   (11.173.6)
```

This is an exact two-channel factorization, not a positivity statement.
Write

```text
R=r_0+r_1x,                 R_x=t_0+t_1x,

G_0=r_0(r_0+delta)+t_0,
G_1=r_1(2r_0+delta)+t_1,    G_2=r_1^2.            (11.173.7)
```

If `U_f=u_(f,0)+u_(f,1)x+u_(f,2)x^2` and
`V_f=v_(f,0)+v_(f,1)x`, then

```text
u_(f,0)=f_NG_0+f_Q(r_0+delta)+f_Ar_0+f_V,
u_(f,1)=f_NG_1+(f_Q+f_A)r_1,
u_(f,2)=f_NG_2,

v_(f,0)=f_Nr_0+f_Q,       v_(f,1)=f_Nr_1.        (11.173.8)
```

Define

```text
gamma=(u_(alpha,0),
       u_(alpha,1)+i u_(beta,0),
       u_(alpha,2)+i u_(beta,1),
       i u_(beta,2)),

eta=(v_(alpha,0),
     v_(alpha,1)+i v_(beta,0),
     i v_(beta,1)).                               (11.173.9)
```

Then

```text
P_lin=C sum_(j=0)^3gamma_jx^j
     +D sum_(j=0)^2eta_jx^j
     =sum_(j=0)^5p_jx^j,                          (11.173.10)
```

where all six complex coefficients are

```text
p_0=c_0gamma_0+d_0eta_0,

p_1=c_0gamma_1+c_1gamma_0+d_0eta_1+d_1eta_0,

p_2=c_0gamma_2+c_1gamma_1+c_2gamma_0
    +d_0eta_2+d_1eta_1+d_2eta_0,

p_3=c_0gamma_3+c_1gamma_2+c_2gamma_1
    +d_1eta_2+d_2eta_1,

p_4=c_1gamma_3+c_2gamma_2+d_2eta_2,

p_5=c_2gamma_3.                                  (11.173.11)
```

The top coefficient has the sharper physical factorization

```text
p_5=i rho_2 (X_T+V_p)(s_*')^2.                  (11.173.12)
```

Consequently the degree-five channel vanishes exactly on the total-value
fibre `X_T+V_p=0`.  Corrections can still leave degree four, so this degree
drop is not an error bound or contact exclusion.

The correction-free leading chart is more transparent.  At

```text
C=1,       D=0,       s_*'=-i/2,       s_*''=0,

delta=0,  b=-1/2,
```

one has

```text
R=Q=i x/2,              mathcal N=-x^2/4-i u_(N,x)/2,

A_p=Q_p,  A_(p,xi)=Q_(p,xi),  V_(p,xi)=2A_p.     (11.173.13)
```

The complete leading polynomial is therefore only cubic:

```text
P_lin=N_(p,xi)-i A_pu_(N,x)

 +{i[N_p+A_(T,x)-Q_(p,xi)]
    +(X_T+V_p)u_(N,x)/2}x

 +[A_p+A_T+X_(T,x)]x^2/2
 -i(X_T+V_p)x^3/4.                               (11.173.14)
```

On the simultaneous value/scalar contact fibre

```text
X_T+V_p=0,                 A_T+A_p=0,
```

this further reduces to

```text
P_lin=N_(p,xi)-i A_pu_(N,x)
     +i[N_p+A_(T,x)-Q_(p,xi)]x
     +X_(T,x)x^2/2.                               (11.173.15)
```

Equations (11.173.14)--(11.173.15) are audits of the leading chart.  The
actual `C-1`, `D`, `delta`, `s_*'+i/2`, and `s_*''` terms remain in
(11.173.6)--(11.173.11).

It remains to identify exactly what the Morse interior does to this one
polynomial.  For a polynomial `P`, put

```text
u_0=alpha/r,                    lambda=log(u_0v),

S(lambda)=t lambda^2/4-sigma lambda,

z=sgn(v-1)sqrt(2[v-1-log v]),  J=dv/dz,

W_P(v)=exp(S(lambda))P(lambda)J(v),

y=sqrt(alpha)z.                                    (11.173.16)
```

The exact transformed amplitude and residual quotient are

```text
b_(P,r)(y)=sqrt(alpha)W_P(v)/r,

c_(P,r)(y)=[W_P(v)-W_P(1)]/(r z).                (11.173.17)
```

For `z!=0`, differentiation gives

```text
c'_(P,r)(y)
 ={zJ W_P'(v)-W_P(v)+W_P(1)}/[r sqrt(alpha)z^2]

 ={exp(S(lambda)){zJ^2[P'(lambda)+g(lambda)P(lambda)]/v
                   +[zJJ'-J]P(lambda)}
    +exp(S(lambda_0))P(lambda_0)}
   /[r sqrt(alpha)z^2],                            (11.173.18)

g(lambda)=t lambda/2-sigma,       lambda_0=log(alpha/r).
```

The apparent singularity at the saddle is removable.  Its exact value is

```text
c'_(P,r)(0)
 =exp(S(lambda_0))/[2r sqrt(alpha)]
   {P''+(2g_0+1)P'
     +[g_0^2+g_0+t/2+1/6]P}(lambda_0),            (11.173.19)

g_0=t lambda_0/2-sigma.
```

At fixed `xi`, every Poisson mode samples the same physical `P_lin`; mode
dependence enters through `lambda_0=log(alpha/r)`, the Morse endpoints, and
the common phase.  The grouped interior is therefore one second-order
polynomial operator on the logarithmic mode lattice.  Neither
`P_lin(lambda_0)` nor the operator in (11.173.19) vanishes identically, so
any Abel, reciprocal-pair, or discrete-difference gain must still be proved
from the physical coefficients and their mode coupling.

The next bounded stage is to insert the exact formulas for `rho_1,rho_2`
and their derivatives, obtain interval envelopes for the six centered
coefficients without undoing the terminal cancellation, and apply
(11.173.18)--(11.173.19) to the grouped mode sequence.  The four quadratic
pairings in (11.172.13) remain a separate obligation.  The benchmark is
still

```text
Psi(T_0)-epsilon integral_0^1
  Psi'(T_0-theta epsilon)dtheta
 <=h^2/400,                                        (11.173.20)
```

preferably with right side `h^2/800`.

No new `pi` occurs here.  The factors `sqrt(alpha)` and the Fourier
normalization are inherited from the exact Morse-Poisson chart.

This section proves the exact terminal-centered physical carrier laws, the
`C/D` two-channel factorization, all six centered coefficients of `P_lin`,
the total-value factor in its degree-five coefficient, the correction-free
cubic and contact-quadratic reductions, and exact off-saddle and saddle
Morse `c'` formulas.  It proves no coefficient norm on the physical chart,
grouped `c'` sum, discrete cancellation theorem, quadratic residual bound,
`h^2` flow error, `Phi_B` upper bound, contact exclusion, retained aggregate
or Xi theorem, `Q209`, the cofinal descendant theorem, `Lambda<=0`,
PF-infinity, RH, or a prize-level conclusion.

## 11.174 Physical correction-coefficient envelopes

Section 11.173 gives the exact six coefficients of `P_lin`, but leaves their
physical sizes open.  This section closes the first part of that obligation:
the normalized quadratic correction and all six terminal-centered `C/D`
coefficients.  To avoid colliding with the polynomial variable `x` in Section
11.173, write `X` for the physical height variable in this section and `y` for
the centered logarithmic polynomial variable.

On the complete critical chart, the established geometry gives

```text
L>=50,                    0<tL<=25,        0<t<=1/2,

h=1/a<1/72000000000,     X>a^2=h^(-2),

16892h^2<1.                                      (11.174.1)
```

Write the original first Dirichlet correction as `frak d`, reserving `d_j`
for the centered coefficients of `D`.  For a real logarithmic parameter
`ell`, put

```text
frak d(ell)
 =1/(6s)+alpha'(s){t/4+t^2[alpha(s)-ell]^2/8},

A=log a,              chi=alpha(s)-A,

a_0=1+frak d(0),      B=alpha'(s)t^2/8.          (11.174.2)
```

The normalized correction polynomial is therefore exactly

```text
C(ell)=[1+frak d(ell)]/a_0
      =1+rho_1ell+rho_2ell^2,

rho_2=B/a_0,          rho_1=-2alpha rho_2.        (11.174.3)
```

The source bounds must be kept in two distinct groups.  The normalized
critical-ray calculation in Section 11.150 uses only
`|alpha-ell|<3` in its correction majorant.  At `ell=A`, Sections 11.101 and
11.105 give `|chi|<2`, so the same checked rational chain gives

```text
|alpha'|<h^2,             |alpha''|<h^4,

|chi|<2,

|frak d(A)|<h^2/4,        |frak d_x(A)|<h^4/32.  (11.174.4)
```

The all-carrier estimates, rather than the terminal estimate, control the
normalizer at `ell=0`:

```text
|frak d(0)|<2189/X<2189h^2<1/2,

|frak d_x(0)|<4223/X^2<4223h^4.                  (11.174.5)
```

In particular,

```text
|a_0|>1/2,            |a_0|^(-1)<2,

|a_0|^(-2)<4.                                      (11.174.6)
```

At fixed `t`, one has `s_x=-i/2`.  Hence

```text
B_x=-i alpha''(s)t^2/16,

rho_(2,x)
 =B_x/a_0-B frak d_x(0)/a_0^2.                   (11.174.7)
```

Equations (11.174.1), (11.174.4), and (11.174.6) first give

```text
|B|<h^2/32,                 |B_x|<h^4/64,

|rho_2|<h^2/16.                                      (11.174.8)
```

For the derivative quotient, retain both denominator powers before
rounding:

```text
|rho_(2,x)|
 <h^4/32+(4223/8)h^6
 <h^4/16.                                           (11.174.9)
```

The last strict inequality is exactly
`4223h^2<1/4`, which follows from `16892=4*4223` and (11.174.1).  Thus the
two candidate bounds in Section 11.173 are now theorems on the full critical
chart.

Shift `ell=A+y`.  The value channel has the exact centered coefficients

```text
C(A+y)=c_0+c_1y+c_2y^2,

c_0=[1+frak d(A)]/a_0,

c_1=-2chi rho_2,              c_2=rho_2.          (11.174.10)
```

The ratio form of `c_0` prevents a spurious `(log a)^2` loss.  Equations
(11.174.4)--(11.174.6) give

```text
|c_0-1|
 <2(h^2/4+2189h^2)
 =(8757/2)h^2
 <4379h^2<1/3,

2/3<|c_0|<4/3,

|c_1|<h^2/4,                 |c_2|<h^2/16.        (11.174.11)
```

Here `3*4379<16892` proves the displayed one-third bound using
(11.174.1).

Let `D(ell)=partial_X C(ell)` with `ell` held fixed, as in Sections
11.158--11.160.  Differentiating before shifting gives

```text
D(A+y)=d_0+d_1y+d_2y^2,

d_0=frak d_x(A)/a_0
    -[1+frak d(A)]frak d_x(0)/a_0^2,

d_1=-2alpha_xrho_2-2chi rho_(2,x),

d_2=rho_(2,x),             alpha_x=-i alpha'/2.   (11.174.12)
```

This order of operations matters: `A` is the shift parameter after the
fixed-`ell` derivative, so no artificial `A_x` term is inserted into `D`.
The constant channel obeys

```text
|d_0|
 <h^4/16+4(1+h^2/4)4223h^4

 =[16892+1/16+4223h^2]h^4
 <16893h^4.                                        (11.174.13)
```

Using `|alpha_x|<h^2/2` in the remaining two rows gives

```text
|d_1|<5h^4/16,                 |d_2|<h^4/16.      (11.174.14)
```

Therefore the complete correction-channel coefficient box is

```text
|c_0-1|<4379h^2,  |c_1|<h^2/4,  |c_2|<h^2/16,

|d_0|<16893h^4,   |d_1|<5h^4/16, |d_2|<h^4/16.   (11.174.15)
```

The large visible constant `16893` is retained deliberately.  It is
multiplied by `h^4`, but it must not be hidden when (11.173.11) is propagated
to the six physical coefficients `p_0,...,p_5`.  In particular, the next
stage must combine (11.174.15) with the physical `gamma` and `eta` rows before
taking norms, while preserving

```text
p_5=i rho_2(X_T+V_p)(s_*')^2.                    (11.174.16)
```

No new `pi` is introduced here.  The existing occurrences remain those in
the completed-zeta saddle geometry used to prove the source bounds.

This section proves the exact `rho_2` quotient and derivative identities,
the bounds `|rho_2|<h^2/16` and `|rho_(2,x)|<h^4/16`, and six uniform
terminal-centered `C/D` coefficient envelopes.  It proves no physical
`P_lin` norm, grouped Morse `c'` sum, reciprocal cancellation theorem,
quadratic residual bound, `h^2` flow error, `Phi_B` upper bound, contact
exclusion, retained aggregate or Xi theorem, `Q209`, cofinal descendant
theorem, `Lambda<=0`, PF-infinity, RH, or prize-level conclusion.

## 11.175 Physical carrier-rate and joined-coefficient envelopes

Section 11.174 bounds the centered correction channels `C` and `D`.  The
remaining coefficients in (11.173.11) contain the physical carrier rates and
the two retained observation rows.  This section propagates the rate errors
only after those rows have been assembled.  It does not assign an unproved
numerical size to any retained observation.

Continue on the complete physical chart of (11.174.1), and abbreviate

```text
u_x=u_(N,x)=h^2/(8pi).
```

The source identities are

```text
u_N=-log(1-h theta),       0<=u_N-h theta<h^2,

s_*'=-i/2-it alpha'/4,     s_*''=-t alpha''/8,

|s_*'+i/2|<h^2/6000,       |alpha''|<h^4,

0<t<=1/2,                  |delta|<4h^2.          (11.175.1)
```

Since `0<=theta<=1`, `h<1`, and `pi>3`, these imply

```text
u_N<2h,                    0<u_x<h^2/24,

|c|<h^2/6000,              |c_x|<=|s_*''|<h^4/16,

|b+1/2|<h^2/6000,          |b|<3001/6000.         (11.175.2)
```

Recall from (11.173.1) and (11.173.7) that

```text
r_0=-c u_N,                r_1=-s_*',

t_0=-c_xu_N+i b u_x,       t_1=-s_*'',

G_0=r_0(r_0+delta)+t_0,

G_1=r_1(2r_0+delta)+t_1,   G_2=r_1^2.             (11.175.3)
```

The first rate box is consequently

```text
|r_0|<h^3/3000,

|r_1-i/2|<h^2/6000,        |r_1|<3001/6000,

|t_0|<h^2/16,              |t_1|<h^4/16,

|delta|<4h^2.                                      (11.175.4)
```

For the only slightly nontrivial line,

```text
|t_0|<h^5/8+3001h^2/144000<h^2/16;
```

the final comparison already follows from `h<1/2`.  The ideal rate point is

```text
(r_0,r_1,t_0,t_1,delta)
 =(0,i/2,-i u_x/2,0,0).                            (11.175.5)
```

Keeping this nonzero ideal constant term in `G_0`, rather than bounding
`G_0` from zero, gives

```text
|G_0+i u_x/2|<h^4/15,

|G_1|<17h^2/8,

|G_2+1/4|<h^2/3000.                               (11.175.6)
```

Indeed,

```text
|t_0+i u_x/2|<h^5/8+h^4/144000,

|r_0(r_0+delta)|
 <h^5(1/750+h/9000000),
```

and evaluation at `h=1/2` leaves the rational coefficient

```text
1/16+1/144000+1/1500+1/36000000<1/15.
```

Likewise the coefficient in the `G_1` estimate is bounded by

```text
(3001/6000)(6001/1500)+1/16<17/8,
```

while, for `e=r_1-i/2`,

```text
G_2+1/4=i e+e^2,

1/6000+1/36000000<1/3000.                        (11.175.7)
```

The rate box can now be propagated without replacing the physical rows by
independent constants.  For one real row

```text
f=(f_V,f_N,f_A,f_Q),
```

define the ideal-rate coefficients

```text
bar(u)_(f,0)=f_V-i u_xf_N/2,

bar(u)_(f,1)=i(f_Q+f_A)/2,       bar(u)_(f,2)=-f_N/4,

bar(v)_(f,0)=f_Q,                bar(v)_(f,1)=i f_N/2.  (11.175.8)
```

These are the exact specialization of (11.173.8) at (11.175.5).  Put

```text
e_(u,0)(f)
 =h^4|f_N|/15+(4h^2+h^3/3000)|f_Q|
   +h^3|f_A|/3000,

e_(u,1)(f)
 =17h^2|f_N|/8+h^2(|f_Q|+|f_A|)/6000,

e_(u,2)(f)=h^2|f_N|/3000,

e_(v,0)(f)=h^3|f_N|/3000,

e_(v,1)(f)=h^2|f_N|/6000.                        (11.175.9)
```

Direct subtraction in (11.173.8), followed by (11.175.4)--(11.175.6),
proves

```text
|u_(f,j)-bar(u)_(f,j)|<e_(u,j)(f),      0<=j<=2,

|v_(f,j)-bar(v)_(f,j)|<e_(v,j)(f),      0<=j<=1. (11.175.10)
```

Now use the actual joined rows

```text
alpha=(N_(p,xi),V_(p,xi),-Q_(p,xi),-A_(p,xi)),

beta=(N_p+A_(T,x),X_T+V_p,
      -Q_p-X_(T,x),-A_T-A_p).                    (11.175.11)
```

Their ideal-rate channel coefficients are

```text
bar(gamma)_0=alpha_V-i u_xalpha_N/2,

bar(gamma)_1=i(alpha_Q+alpha_A)/2
             +i beta_V+u_xbeta_N/2,

bar(gamma)_2=-alpha_N/4-(beta_Q+beta_A)/2,

bar(gamma)_3=-i beta_N/4,                         (11.175.12)

bar(eta)_0=alpha_Q,

bar(eta)_1=i(alpha_N/2+beta_Q),

bar(eta)_2=-beta_N/2.                             (11.175.13)
```

At the fully correction-free specialization, the further identities in
(11.173.13) turn (11.175.12) into the cubic coefficients displayed in
(11.173.14).  They are not imposed on the actual rows in (11.175.11).

Compose the row errors before taking the next norms:

```text
E_(gamma,0)=e_(u,0)(alpha),

E_(gamma,1)=e_(u,1)(alpha)+e_(u,0)(beta),

E_(gamma,2)=e_(u,2)(alpha)+e_(u,1)(beta),

E_(gamma,3)=e_(u,2)(beta),                        (11.175.14)

E_(eta,0)=e_(v,0)(alpha),

E_(eta,1)=e_(v,1)(alpha)+e_(v,0)(beta),

E_(eta,2)=e_(v,1)(beta).                          (11.175.15)
```

Thus, with

```text
Gamma_j=|bar(gamma)_j|+E_(gamma,j),

H_j=|bar(eta)_j|+E_(eta,j),                       (11.175.16)
```

one has `|gamma_j|<Gamma_j` and `|eta_j|<H_j`.  In particular, cancellation
inside each physical coefficient in (11.175.12) is retained until its final
modulus.

Combining (11.175.14)--(11.175.16) with the six `C/D` bounds in
(11.174.15), define

```text
Pi_0
 =E_(gamma,0)+4379h^2Gamma_0+16893h^4H_0,

Pi_1
 =E_(gamma,1)+4379h^2Gamma_1+h^2Gamma_0/4
   +16893h^4H_1+5h^4H_0/16,

Pi_2
 =E_(gamma,2)+4379h^2Gamma_2+h^2Gamma_1/4
   +h^2Gamma_0/16+16893h^4H_2
   +5h^4H_1/16+h^4H_0/16,

Pi_3
 =E_(gamma,3)+4379h^2Gamma_3+h^2Gamma_2/4
   +h^2Gamma_1/16+5h^4H_2/16+h^4H_1/16,

Pi_4=h^2Gamma_3/4+h^2Gamma_2/16+h^4H_2/16.       (11.175.17)
```

Termwise propagation through the exact convolution (11.173.11) now gives

```text
|p_j-bar(gamma)_j|<Pi_j,             0<=j<=3,

|p_4|<Pi_4.                                        (11.175.18)
```

The top channel should not be replaced by the generic `Gamma_3` estimate.
Since `gamma_3=i beta_Nr_1^2`, its exact physical form and a sharper bound
are

```text
p_5=i rho_2 beta_N(s_*')^2
   =i rho_2(X_T+V_p)(s_*')^2,

|p_5|
 <(h^2/16)(3001/6000)^2|beta_N|
 <h^2|beta_N|/63.                                 (11.175.19)
```

Thus the physical centered polynomial is an explicit row-sensitive
`O(h^2)` perturbation of its ideal cubic in coefficient space, and both
correction suppression and the total-value fibre remain visible in its two
highest channels.  This statement is relative to the displayed retained
row scales; it does not assert that those rows or the ideal cubic are small.

There is also an essential basis guard.  The `p_j` in (11.175.18)--
(11.175.19) multiply

```text
y=lambda-log(a).
```

The `K_j` outside-tail template in (11.172.15) was stated for powers of
`lambda`.  The centered coefficients may be inserted there only after the
exact binomial basis translation, or after a new centered-weight tail
estimate is proved.  Direct substitution would hide powers of `log(a)` and
is not a valid propagation.

The remaining input is now located precisely.  One may prove a
source-specific joined envelope for the retained quantities
`bar(gamma),Gamma,H`, or leave these rows inside the grouped Morse functional
and prove its cancellation estimate directly.  The existing scalar current
identities, including `Phi_B`, do not by themselves constitute such a
gradient-row norm.

No new `pi` is introduced here.  The sole estimate using it is
`u_x=h^2/(8pi)<h^2/24`, where the constant is inherited from the
completed-zeta/Riemann--Siegel saddle and `pi>3`.

This section proves five carrier-rate bounds, three ideal-rate deviation
bounds, five row-sensitive error envelopes, the joined `gamma/eta`
propagation, four ideal-cubic deviation bounds, one degree-four envelope,
and the exact degree-five total-value factor with its bound.  It proves no

grouped Morse `c'` sum, reciprocal cancellation theorem, quadratic residual
bound, `h^2` flow error, `Phi_B` upper bound, contact exclusion, retained
aggregate or Xi theorem, `Q209`, cofinal descendant theorem, `Lambda<=0`,
PF-infinity, RH, or prize-level conclusion.
