## 11.185 Terminal-bulk phase completion and the pure conditional null

Section 11.184 isolates the first unsuppressed conditional boundary object as

```text
K_BT
 =[S_(1,N)/(2pi)]Im(w_N)mathcal N_(<N,xi).        (11.185.1)
```

Before estimating it arithmetically, one must determine whether the
Hermitian and transpose terms already present in the outer quadratic current
cancel it.  They do not cancel it algebraically.  Instead, (11.185.1) itself
polarizes into exactly those two phase families, and the other outer terms
complete its retained coefficient to the full nonterminal observation.

Write `S=S_(1,N)` and, for `q<N`, put

```text
d_q=-i u_q mathcal N_qw_q.
```

Then `mathcal N_(<N,xi)=sum_(q<N)Re(d_q)`.  For arbitrary complex numbers
`w,d`, direct real-imaginary expansion gives

```text
Im(w)Re(d)
 ={Im(wd)+Im(w conjugate(d))}/2.                 (11.185.2)
```

Since `Im z=Re(-iz)`, insertion of
`d_q=-iu_qmathcal N_qw_q` into (11.185.2) proves the exact split

```text
K_BT
 =sum_(q<N)Re{
     K_H(N,q)w_Nconjugate(w_q)
    +K_T(N,q)w_Nw_q},                            (11.185.3)

K_H(N,q)
 =[S/(4pi)]u_qconjugate(mathcal N_q),

K_T(N,q)
 =-[S/(4pi)]u_qmathcal N_q.                      (11.185.4)
```

In particular,

```text
K_T(N,q)=-conjugate(K_H(N,q)).                   (11.185.5)
```

This anti-conjugacy relates coefficients multiplying different carrier
products; it is not a cancellation.  Under the established physical
factorization

```text
w_q=omega_a A_q exp(-i xi u_q),       A_q>0,
```

the two products are

```text
w_Nconjugate(w_q)
 =|omega_a|^2A_NA_q exp{i xi(u_q-u_N)},

w_Nw_q
 =omega_a^2A_NA_q exp{-i xi(u_N+u_q)}.            (11.185.6)
```

Thus `K_H` is a Hermitian phase-difference family and `K_T` is a transpose
phase-sum family.  They have genuinely different oscillatory coordinates.

The correction-free physical chart makes the distinction explicit.  There

```text
mathcal N_q^0=-u_q^2/4-i u_(N,x)/2,
```

so (11.185.4) becomes

```text
K_H^0(N,q)
 =-S u_q^3/(16pi)+iS u_qu_(N,x)/(8pi),

K_T^0(N,q)
 = S u_q^3/(16pi)+iS u_qu_(N,x)/(8pi).            (11.185.7)
```

Their real parts are opposite, but their imaginary parts agree.  There is
no pointwise sign and no identity forcing their real projections to cancel.
For example, the exact algebraic specialization

```text
u_q=1,       u_(N,x)=0,       w_N=w_q=i
```

gives

```text
Re{K_H^0w_Nconjugate(w_q)+K_T^0w_Nw_q}
 =-S/(8pi)!=0.                                    (11.185.8)
```

This is a noncancellation witness, not an asserted physical Xi state.

We next compose the terminal block with all other outer observations.  Let
`omega_p,dot(omega_p)` be the retained observation vectors of Section
11.172.  Split the real outer residual observation and its frequency lift as

```text
epsilon=a+rho,              dot(epsilon)=dot a+dot rho,
```

where `a` contains only the terminal conditional `S_1` observation and
`rho` contains every other outer observation.  Isolate the carrier/residual
quadratic correction from (11.172.3):

```text
C(epsilon)
 =2omega_p^TJdot(epsilon)
  +2dot(omega_p)^TJepsilon
  +2epsilon^TJdot(epsilon).                       (11.185.9)
```

On the full-support chart of Section 11.181, the external affine row is the
genuine-edge row

```text
t_E:=2Jomega_E
   =(A_(E,x),X_E,-X_(E,x),-A_E)^T.
```

The fixed affine term `t_E^Tdot(epsilon)` is kept separately.  Since the
matrix `J` of (11.165.7) is symmetric, direct expansion of (11.185.9) gives

```text
C(a+rho)
 =C(rho)
  +2(omega_p+rho)^TJdot a
  +2(dot(omega_p)+dot rho)^TJa
  +2a^TJdot a.                                   (11.185.10)
```

Define the complete nonterminal rows

```text
omega_*=omega_p+rho,

dot(omega_*)=dot(omega_p)+dot rho.                (11.185.11)
```

Then every quadratic term involving the terminal conditional endpoint is
the single exact channel

```text
Delta_a
 =2omega_*^TJdot a
  +2dot(omega_*)^TJa
  +2a^TJdot a.                                   (11.185.12)
```

In the order `(V,mathcal N,A,Q)`, (11.185.12) reads

```text
Delta_a
 =V_*dot a_N+N_*dot a_V-A_*dot a_Q-Q_*dot a_A

  +dot V_*a_N+dot N_*a_V-dot A_*a_Q-dot Q_*a_A

  +a_Vdot a_N+a_Ndot a_V-a_Adot a_Q-a_Qdot a_A. (11.185.13)
```

The edge-affine row obeys only the linear split

```text
t_E^Tdot(epsilon)=t_E^Tdot rho+t_E^Tdot a,        (11.185.14)
```

so it is neither hidden in (11.185.12) nor counted twice.  The mixed
coefficient of `a_V` in (11.185.13) is now

```text
dot N_*
 =mathcal N_(p,xi)+rho_(N,xi).                   (11.185.15)
```

Thus the mixed outer terms do not remove the Section 11.184 coefficient.
They complete it from the retained derivative to the complete nonterminal
derivative.  The retained part of `dot N_*a_V`, after the row-relative
terminal reduction of (11.184.14)--(11.184.18), is precisely the live
kernel (11.185.1).  The remaining possible interaction is the pure term
`2a^TJdot a`, which can be resolved exactly.

For `X` in `{V,mathcal N,A,Q}`, let the source-inclusive complex terminal
conditional amplitudes be

```text
Z_X=tau_N P_X(log N),

tau_N=kappa S w_N,             Z_(dot X)=-iu_NZ_X. (11.185.16)
```

The Hermitian and transpose polarizations of the pure terminal real current
are

```text
H_aa
 =Z_Vconjugate(Z_(dot N))+Z_Nconjugate(Z_(dot V))
  -Z_Aconjugate(Z_(dot Q))-Z_Qconjugate(Z_(dot A)),

T_aa
 =Z_VZ_(dot N)+Z_NZ_(dot V)
  -Z_AZ_(dot Q)-Z_QZ_(dot A).                    (11.185.17)
```

Using the common lift in (11.185.16),

```text
H_aa
 =iu_N{Z_Vconjugate(Z_N)+Z_Nconjugate(Z_V)
       -Z_Aconjugate(Z_Q)-Z_Qconjugate(Z_A)},

T_aa=-2iu_N(Z_VZ_N-Z_AZ_Q).                      (11.185.18)
```

The brace in the first line is real.  Therefore

```text
Re(H_aa)=0                                       (11.185.19)
```

exactly.  At the terminal sample, the four carrier polynomials are

```text
P_V=C_N,       P_N=mathcal N_N,
P_A=A_N,       P_Q=Q_N.
```

The source identities `A_N=R_NC_N` and
`mathcal N_N=R_NQ_N+R_(N,x)C_N` give the exact determinant collapse

```text
C_Nmathcal N_N-A_NQ_N=R_(N,x)C_N^2.              (11.185.20)
```

Consequently

```text
T_aa=-2iu_N tau_N^2R_(N,x)C_N^2,                 (11.185.21)

R_aa:=(1/2)Re(H_aa+T_aa)=(1/2)Re(T_aa).          (11.185.22)
```

This is the pure conditional null: its Hermitian real current vanishes, and
only one terminal transpose defect remains.  The rational physical boxes
from Section 11.183 are

```text
u_N<2h,             |R_(N,x)|<h^2/20,

|C_N|<3/2,          |kappa|^2=1/(4pi^2)<1/36,    (11.185.23)
```

where the last strict inequality uses only `pi>3`.  Since
`|tau_N|=|kappa|S|w_N|`, (11.185.21)--(11.185.23) yield

```text
|R_aa|
 <=u_N|tau_N|^2|R_(N,x)||C_N|^2

 <2h (1/36)S^2|w_N|^2 (h^2/20)(9/4)

 =h^3S^2|w_N|^2/160.                             (11.185.24)
```

Hence there is no universal algebraic cancellation of (11.185.1) by the
pure terminal quadratic: its Hermitian projection is exactly zero, and its
transpose projection has the separate determinant form (11.185.21) and the
source-relative envelope (11.185.24).  This does not by itself compare the
complete physical sizes or prove a sign for their sum.

## 11.186 Endpoint-resolved remainder and relative-lift compression

Section 11.185 proves that the terminal conditional block does not cancel
locally and that all mixed outer terms complete its retained coefficient.
The remaining notation `rho` can now be resolved exactly.  The resulting
mixed current does not require eight independently estimated observations:

polynomial functional, each still of degree at most five.

Retain the endpoint functional (11.182.14).  For a complex polynomial `P`
of degree at most five, separate its first and higher endpoint pieces by

```text
mathcal T_mu^[N][P]
 :=e(alpha_Plog mu)kappa A_P(mu)

mathcal U_mu^[N][P]
```

```text
 =mathcal U_N^[N][P]

```

The four terms in (11.186.4) are respectively the terminal `S_2,S_3`

absolute interior.  Their signs are inherited from the difference
`mathcal B_N^[N]-mathcal B_1^[N]`; none has been changed to a modulus.

For `X in {V,mathcal N,A,Q}`, the real remainder observations on a fixed

The full linear outer correction also stays grouped:

Thus (11.186.4) is the promised explicit `rho`; it is not an invitation to

We next identify the lift seen by a terminal cross term.  Set

Section 11.183 gives

## 11.187 Joined lower/interior Abel recombination

Section 11.186 leaves two degree-five relative functionals.  Their lower
`S_1,S_2,S_3` traces contain large logarithms, but those traces arose from
two integrations by parts.  They must first be reversed and joined to the
finite reciprocal band.  This exposes an important distinction: the actual
band-mode sum is not the returned physical carrier.  Their difference is
the finite-cell defect from Section 11.180, and deleting it would apply
Fourier inversion twice.

We first expand the physical terminal coefficients completely.  Retain

```text
Q=(R+delta)C+D,             mathcal N=RQ+R_xC,

A=RC,                       delta=chi_N-i b u_N. (11.187.1)
```

Direct substitution into (11.186.16), including the terminal conjugations,
gives the Hermitian identity

```text
B_(H,N)(lambda)
 =(R-conjugate(R_N))
    {conjugate(C_N)Q-conjugate(Q_N)C}

  +(R_x+conjugate(R_(N,x)))conjugate(C_N)C

 =conjugate(C_N)C{
     (R-conjugate(R_N))^2
    +(R-conjugate(R_N))(delta-conjugate(delta))
    +R_x+conjugate(R_(N,x))}

  +(R-conjugate(R_N))
     {conjugate(C_N)D-conjugate(D_N)C}.           (11.187.2)
```

The transpose identity is

```text
B_(T,N)(lambda)
 =(R-R_N){C_NQ-Q_NC}+(R_x+R_(N,x))C_NC

 =C_NC{(R-R_N)^2+R_x+R_(N,x)}
  +(R-R_N){C_ND-D_NC}.                           (11.187.3)
```

Thus (11.187.2)--(11.187.3) are expressed in the primitive physical rows
`C,D,R,R_x,delta`; no imaginary terminal coefficient has been discarded.
Only now take the correction-free audit

```text
x=lambda-log a,

C=1,               D=delta=0,

R=ix/2,            R_N=-iu_N/2,

R_x=R_(N,x)=-iu_(N,x)/2.                         (11.187.4)
```

Then

```text
B_(H,N)^0=-(x-u_N)^2/4,

B_(T,N)^0=-(x+u_N)^2/4-iu_(N,x).                 (11.187.5)
```

The two relative polynomials are therefore the explicit cubics

```text
P_H^0
 :=i(x+u_N)B_(H,N)^0
  =-i(x+u_N)(x-u_N)^2/4,

P_T^0
 :=i(x-u_N)B_(T,N)^0
  =-i(x-u_N)(x+u_N)^2/4
    +u_(N,x)(x-u_N).                              (11.187.6)
```

At the physical atom `x=-u_q`, these become

```text
P_H^0(log q)
 =i(u_q-u_N)(u_q+u_N)^2/4,

P_T^0(log q)
 =i(u_q+u_N)(u_q-u_N)^2/4
  -u_(N,x)(u_q+u_N).                              (11.187.7)
```

Define `Delta_H=P_H-P_H^0` and `Delta_T=P_T-P_T^0` only after
(11.187.2)--(11.187.3).  Every term in either difference vanishes under the
simultaneous specialization (11.187.4).  The ideal rows are cubic, while
the physical corrections can restore degrees four and five.  No modulus is
taken in this split.

The full lifted lower endpoint can also be written without abbreviations.
Let `g_0=S'(0)`, let `P_0=P(0)`, and consider

```text
P_L(lambda)=i(lambda-L)P(lambda).                 (11.187.8)
```

At `mu=1`, direct differentiation of
`exp(S(lambda))P_L(lambda)` gives

```text
-mathcal T_1^[N][P_L]-mathcal U_1^[N][P_L]
 =i kappa L P_0 S_1^[N](alpha_P)

  +i kappa^2{
     [P_0-L(P'(0)+g_0P_0)]S_2^[N](alpha_P)
     -alpha_P L P_0 S_3^[N](alpha_P)}.           (11.187.9)
```

The Hermitian value is `L=log N`; the transpose value is
`L=log a+u_N`.  Equation (11.187.9) confirms that the logarithms are real
parts of the exact boundary operator.  It does not imply that any one of
the three displayed terms is small enough for the flow reserve.

We now reverse the integrations by parts.  Write
`mathcal T_(mu,r),mathcal U_(mu,r)` for the unsummed mode contributions to
(11.186.1), and let `mathcal I_r[P]` be the corresponding interior in
(11.182.12).  Mode by mode,

```text
I_P(r)
 =mathcal T_(N,r)[P]+mathcal U_(N,r)[P]
  -mathcal T_(1,r)[P]-mathcal U_(1,r)[P]
  +mathcal I_r[P].                                (11.187.10)
```

Consequently

```text
-mathcal T_(1,r)[P]-mathcal U_(1,r)[P]
 +mathcal I_r[P]

 =I_P(r)-mathcal T_(N,r)[P]-mathcal U_(N,r)[P].  (11.187.11)
```

After the joined symmetric outer sum, put

```text
mathcal L_N[P]
 :=-mathcal T_1^[N][P]-mathcal U_1^[N][P]
   +mathcal I_N[P].
```

Then (11.187.11) gives

```text
mathcal L_N[P]
 =mathscr O_N[P]-mathcal T_N^[N][P]
                    -mathcal U_N^[N][P],

mathscr R_N[P]
 =mathscr O_N[P]-mathcal T_N^[N][P].             (11.187.12)
```

Thus the lower logarithms are coordinates of the integrated-by-parts
representation.  They reverse to the original outer-mode integral, but not
to zero.

To identify the exact finite object that must be joined, define

```text
mathscr F_N[P]
 :=sum_(r in mathcal R_N)I_P(r),

mathscr M_N[P]
 :=sum_(q=1)^N omega_N(q)
      e(alpha_Plog q)exp(S(log q))P(log q),

omega_N(1)=omega_N(N)=1/2,
omega_N(q)=1,                    1<q<N,

mathscr D_N[P]
 :=mathscr F_N[P]-mathscr M_N[P].                (11.187.13)
```

Here `mathscr F_N` is the actual reciprocal-band mode sum,
`mathscr M_N` is the starred carrier returned by full finite Poisson
inversion, and `mathscr D_N` is their finite-cell defect.  Full-support
finite Poisson summation gives

```text
mathscr F_N[P]+mathscr O_N[P]=mathscr M_N[P].    (11.187.14)
```

Combining (11.187.12)--(11.187.14) proves the central identities

```text
mathscr R_N[P]
 =-mathscr D_N[P]-mathcal T_N^[N][P],

mathscr F_N[P]+mathscr R_N[P]
 =mathscr M_N[P]-mathcal T_N^[N][P].             (11.187.15)
```

This is also the exact finite-cell/exterior identity.  In the notation of
(11.180.23)--(11.180.25), now on `[1,N]`,

```text
mathscr F_N[P]
 =tau_band[P]+mathscr M_N[P]-E_band[P],

mathscr D_N[P]=tau_band[P]-E_band[P],

mathscr R_N[P]
 =E_band[P]-tau_band[P]-mathcal T_N^[N][P].      (11.187.16)
```

Therefore the defect is the global two-sided exterior and the two band-tie
corrections in another coordinate system.  It is not an independent local
endpoint error.  At a half-open reciprocal tie, `mathscr F_N` gains one
complete mode and `mathscr O_N` loses it.  Hence (11.187.14)--(11.187.16)
remain invariant, with `mathscr D_N` and `mathscr R_N` changing oppositely.

The two relative channels now simplify differently.  Put

```text
P_H=i(lambda-log N)B_(H,N),

P_T=i(lambda-log a-u_N)B_(T,N).                  (11.187.17)
```

Since `P_H(log N)=0`,

```text
mathcal T_N^[N][P_H]=0,

mathscr R_N[P_H]=-mathscr D_N[P_H],

mathscr F_N[P_H]+mathscr R_N[P_H]
 =mathscr M_N[P_H].                              (11.187.18)
```

For the transpose lift, `P_T(log N)=-2iu_NB_(T,N)(log N)`, so

```text
mathcal T_N^[N][P_T]
 =-2iu_Nmathcal T_N^[N][B_(T,N)],

mathscr R_N[P_T]
 =-mathscr D_N[P_T]
   +2iu_Nmathcal T_N^[N][B_(T,N)],

mathscr F_N[P_T]+mathscr R_N[P_T]
 =mathscr M_N[P_T]
   +2iu_Nmathcal T_N^[N][B_(T,N)].               (11.187.19)
```

Equations (11.187.18)--(11.187.19) answer the endpoint-recombination
question.  If the finite object being joined is the actual band-mode sum,
the Hermitian lower/interior package returns the starred physical carrier
exactly, while the transpose package leaves one explicit terminal
conditional term.  If instead the retained object is already the returned
carrier, then the exact joins are

```text
mathscr M_N[P_H]+mathscr R_N[P_H]
 =mathscr M_N[P_H]-mathscr D_N[P_H],

mathscr M_N[P_T]+mathscr R_N[P_T]
 =mathscr M_N[P_T]-mathscr D_N[P_T]
   +2iu_Nmathcal T_N^[N][B_(T,N)].               (11.187.20)
```

Thus replacing `mathscr F_N` by `mathscr M_N` while dropping
`mathscr D_N` is not a cancellation; it applies the Fourier involution a
second time and loses the finite-cell defect.

The starred sums in (11.187.18)--(11.187.20) retain exactly the parent
phase multipliers:

```text
mathscr M_N[P_H]
 =sum_(q<N)^star e(alpha_Plog q)exp(S(log q))
     {-i(u_q-u_N)B_(H,N)(log q)},

mathscr M_N[P_T]
 =sum_(q<=N)^star e(alpha_Plog q)exp(S(log q))
     {-i(u_q+u_N)B_(T,N)(log q)}.                (11.187.21)
```

The `q=N` Hermitian atom vanishes; the transpose atom remains.  The
half-weights at `q=1,N` in (11.187.13) are not silently promoted to full
weights.  The matching hard endpoint halves must be attached in their
existing physical package.

There is now a clean Abel form.  For any finite sequences `a_q,k_q`, put

```text
A_j=sum_(q<=j)a_q.
```

Then

```text
sum_(q=1)^N a_qk_q
 =A_Nk_N+sum_(q=1)^(N-1)A_q(k_q-k_(q+1)).        (11.187.22)
```

Apply (11.187.22) with the starred source amplitude in `a_q` and the full
physical relative kernel in `k_q`.  In the Hermitian channel `k_N=0`, so
the terminal Abel boundary vanishes exactly:

```text
sum_(q=1)^N a_qk_(H,q)
 =sum_(q=1)^(N-1)A_q(k_(H,q)-k_(H,q+1)).         (11.187.23)
```

The transpose boundary generally survives because

```text
k_(T,N)=-2iu_NB_(T,N)(log N).                    (11.187.24)
```

It must be combined with the last term of (11.187.19), the pure terminal
transpose block (11.185.21), and the adjacent terminal recurrence.  The
Hermitian Abel null is useful, but neither (11.187.22) nor (11.187.23)
supplies a partial-sum bound or a sign.

The primary unresolved analytic object has therefore changed.  It is no
longer the three lower traces in isolation.  It is the source-specific
carrier-defect combination

```text
mathscr M_N[P_H]-mathscr D_N[P_H]

and

mathscr M_N[P_T]-mathscr D_N[P_T]
 +2iu_Nmathcal T_N^[N][B_(T,N)],                 (11.187.25)
```

with the ideal cubics (11.187.6) kept intact and `Delta_H,Delta_T` attached
afterward.  The next theorem should derive the global exterior/tie kernel
for `mathscr D_N[P_H],mathscr D_N[P_T]`, rejoin it with the Abel differences
in (11.187.23), and then test reciprocal pairing or the adjacent recurrence.
Only after that signed estimate may the correction perturbations, fixed
affine row, pure terminal transpose term, moved-tail defect, and four
quadratic remainder pairings be reattached.  No `h^2/800` reserve is claimed
at this stage.

Every `pi` in this section is inherited through
`e(x)=exp(2pi i x)`, `kappa=1/(2pi i)`, and
`alpha_P=xi/(2pi)`.  No circle, polygon, fitted constant, or plotted
symmetry is inserted.

This section proves the two full physical terminal-kernel factorizations,
their ideal cubic relative lifts, the complete lifted lower endpoint,

## 11.188 Finite-band Dirichlet kernel and reciprocal-cell block reduction

Section 11.187 identifies the unresolved object as the finite-band defect
`mathscr D_N=mathscr F_N-mathscr M_N`, but its exterior presentation is not
suited to a direct estimate.  This section replaces that presentation by a
finite source integral and then resolves the integral into reciprocal
stationary blocks.  The replacement is exact.  It is not a small-defect or
sign theorem.

Retain the half-open reciprocal roster and put

```text
m_N=floor(alpha_P/(N+1/2))+1,
n_N=floor(2alpha_P),

f_P(u)=e(alpha_P log u)exp(S(log u))P(log u),
K_N(u)=sum_(r=m_N)^(n_N)e(-ru).                  (11.188.1)
```

Thus the roster is the integer interval

```text
mathcal R_N={r in Z_(>0):alpha_P/(N+1/2)<r<=2alpha_P},
```

and finite interchange of sum and integral gives

```text
mathscr F_N[P]
 =sum_(r=m_N)^(n_N)integral_1^N f_P(u)e(-ru)du
 =integral_1^N f_P(u)K_N(u)du.                  (11.188.2)
```

The kernel is one finite geometric sum.  Away from the integers,

```text
K_N(u)
 =e(-(m_N+n_N)u/2)
   sin(pi(n_N-m_N+1)u)/sin(pi u),               (11.188.3)
```

and its removable value at every integer is `n_N-m_N+1`.  Because every
frequency in (11.188.1) is a positive integer,

```text
K_N(u+1)=K_N(u),
K_N(-v)=conjugate(K_N(v)),
integral_(-1/2)^(1/2)K_N(v)dv=0,

H_N:=integral_0^(1/2)K_N(v)dv
   =2kappa sum_(m_N<=r<=n_N, r odd)1/r,
integral_(-1/2)^0K_N(v)dv=-H_N.                 (11.188.4)
```

Here `kappa=1/(2pi i)`, so `H_N` is purely imaginary.  Define the exact
source-coupled cell variation by

```text
V_N[P]
 :=integral_0^(1/2){f_P(1+v)-f_P(1)}K_N(v)dv

   +sum_(q=2)^(N-1)integral_(-1/2)^(1/2)
       {f_P(q+v)-f_P(q)}K_N(v)dv

   +integral_(-1/2)^0{f_P(N+v)-f_P(N)}K_N(v)dv. (11.188.5)
```

The lower and upper half-cells contribute opposite constant terms, while
every centered interior cell has zero kernel mean.  Consequently

```text
mathscr F_N[P]=H_N{f_P(1)-f_P(N)}+V_N[P].        (11.188.6)
```

Combining (11.188.6) with the definition of `mathscr D_N` gives the finite
global defect and the returned-carrier join:

```text
mathscr D_N[P]
 =-mathscr M_N[P]+H_N{f_P(1)-f_P(N)}+V_N[P],

mathscr M_N[P]-mathscr D_N[P]
 =2mathscr M_N[P]-H_N{f_P(1)-f_P(N)}-V_N[P].    (11.188.7)
```

In particular, the carrier-only representation contains two copies of the
starred carrier.  Replacing it by one copy would again identify
`mathscr F_N` with `mathscr M_N` and apply finite Fourier inversion twice.

The centered interior part also has an exact parity split.  If
`K_N=K_(N,R)+iK_(N,I)`, then

```text
V_(N,q)[P]
 =integral_0^(1/2){
    K_(N,R)(v)[f_P(q+v)+f_P(q-v)-2f_P(q)]
   +iK_(N,I)(v)[f_P(q+v)-f_P(q-v)]}dv.          (11.188.8)
```

This identity retains cancellation between the even source difference and
the real kernel, and between the odd source difference and the imaginary
kernel.  Neither term is replaced by its modulus.

For the Hermitian relative polynomial of (11.187.17),
`f_(P_H)(N)=0` and `mathcal T_N^[N][P_H]=0`.  Equations (11.187.15) and
(11.188.7) therefore give

```text
mathscr R_N[P_H]
 =mathscr M_N[P_H]-H_Nf_(P_H)(1)-V_N[P_H],

mathscr M_N[P_H]+mathscr R_N[P_H]
 =2mathscr M_N[P_H]-H_Nf_(P_H)(1)-V_N[P_H].     (11.188.9)
```

For the transpose polynomial,
`f_(P_T)(N)=-2iu_Nf_(B_(T,N))(N)`, and the surviving terminal value from
(11.187.19) remains explicit:

```text
mathscr R_N[P_T]
 =mathscr M_N[P_T]
  -H_N{f_(P_T)(1)-f_(P_T)(N)}-V_N[P_T]
  +2iu_Nmathcal T_N^[N][B_(T,N)],

mathscr M_N[P_T]+mathscr R_N[P_T]
 =2mathscr M_N[P_T]
  -H_N{f_(P_T)(1)-f_(P_T)(N)}-V_N[P_T]
  +2iu_Nmathcal T_N^[N][B_(T,N)].               (11.188.10)
```

The floor functions in (11.188.1) are piecewise constant, not ordinary
differentiable coefficients.  If an upper crossing adds the complete mode
`mathcal I_P(r_*)`, while a lower crossing removes it, then

```text
Delta_upper(mathscr F_N,mathscr D_N,mathscr R_N)
 =(+mathcal I_P(r_*),+mathcal I_P(r_*),-mathcal I_P(r_*)),

Delta_lower(mathscr F_N,mathscr D_N,mathscr R_N)
 =(-mathcal I_P(r_*),-mathcal I_P(r_*),+mathcal I_P(r_*)). (11.188.11)
```

Thus the joined observation is invariant at both half-open transfers.  On a
fixed roster cell, with `P` and `S` held fixed under the auxiliary frequency,

```text
mathscr D_N[i(lambda-c)P]
  =(partial_xi-ic)mathscr D_N[P].                (11.188.12)
```

At a crossing the transferred complete mode and its lifted mode must instead
be included explicitly.  Differentiating the floor functions in the
sine-quotient formula would lose precisely these terms.

The finite integral (11.188.2) now admits a source-adapted two-index
decomposition.  Let `J_q` be the nearest-integer physical `u`-cell truncated
to `[1,N]`, with the inherited half-open convention, and define

```text
C_p={r in Z_(>0):p-1/2<=alpha_P/r<p+1/2},

mathcal B_(q,p)[P]
 :=sum_(r in C_p)integral_(J_q)f_P(u)e(-ru)du.   (11.188.13)
```

The cells `C_p`, `1<=p<=N`, form a disjoint partition of `mathcal R_N`.
Therefore

```text
mathscr F_N[P]
 =sum_(q=1)^N sum_(p=1)^N mathcal B_(q,p)[P].    (11.188.14)
```

For `r in C_p`, write `v=alpha_P/r`.  The scalar phase
`phi_r(u)=alpha_P log u-ru` obeys

```text
phi_r'(u)=alpha_P/u-r
         =alpha_P(v-u)/(uv).                    (11.188.15)
```

Hence the diagonal block `p=q` contains the reciprocal stationary point
`u=v`.  The endpoint diagonals `p=1,N` are truncated.  If `|p-q|>=2`, then
`|v-u|>=|p-q|-1`, while `uv<=(p+1/2)(q+1/2)`, so

```text
|phi_r'(u)|
 >=alpha_P(|p-q|-1)/{(p+1/2)(q+1/2)}.           (11.188.16)
```

This is a uniform nonstationary gap on every separated block.  It has not yet
been summed into a physical remainder estimate.  The adjacent classes
`p=q-1` and `p=q+1` have no positive uniform gap because their cells meet the
diagonal at a shared half-integer boundary.  They must retain opposite
orientations, the tie transfer (11.188.11), and the complex terminal adjacent
recurrence.

Writing `u=q+w` gives the exact local phase identity

```text
phi_r(q+w)-phi_r(q)
 =(alpha_P/q-r)w
  +alpha_P{log(1+w/q)-w/q}.                     (11.188.17)
```

No quadratic truncation is made in (11.188.17).  It keeps the reciprocal
offset and the negative logarithmic curvature in the same block.

Two exact Fourier witnesses delimit what this reduction can prove without
using the physical source.  For `f(u)=e(ku)` with integer `k` in the roster,
orthogonality on `[1,N]` gives

```text
mathscr F_N=N-1=mathscr M_N,
mathscr D_N=0.                                  (11.188.18)
```

For integer `k` outside the roster, including `k=0`, the same test gives

```text
mathscr F_N=0,
mathscr M_N=N-1,
mathscr D_N=-(N-1),
mathscr M_N-mathscr D_N=2(N-1).                 (11.188.19)
```

These nonphysical witnesses rule out a coefficient-blind smallness or sign
theorem for `mathscr D_N`.  They do not decide the physical polynomial
sources.  For those sources,

```text
f_P'(u)
 =u^(-1)e(alpha_P log u)exp(S(log u))
    {P'(log u)+[g(log u)+2pi i alpha_P]P(log u)}. (11.188.20)
```

The `alpha_P` term is large.  An `L1` estimate for `K_N`, or a unit-cell
derivative majorant for (11.188.5), discards the reciprocal stationary
cancellation that (11.188.13)--(11.188.17) expose.

The next signed target is therefore the diagonal plus adjacent composition
for the ideal cubics

```text
P_H^0=-i(x+u_N)(x-u_N)^2/4,

P_T^0=-i(x-u_N)(x+u_N)^2/4
      +u_(N,x)(x-u_N),                          (11.188.21)
```

joined respectively to `2mathscr M_N[P_H^0]` and
`2mathscr M_N[P_T^0]+2iu_Nmathcal T_N^[N][B_(T,N)^0]`.  The separated blocks
must then be controlled using (11.188.16), without taking moduli before the
oriented sum.  Only after that ideal pair has a signed aggregate estimate may
`Delta_H,Delta_T`, the fixed affine row, the remaining terminal packages, and
the quadratic current remainders be attached.

Every `pi` in this section comes from `e(x)=exp(2pi i x)` and
`kappa=1/(2pi i)`.  Equation (11.188.3) is the finite geometric-sum identity;
no circle, polygon, fitted constant, or plotted symmetry is inserted.

This section proves the finite-band kernel, its endpoint harmonic, the exact
cell-variation and parity formulas, both physical relative-channel
reductions, half-open tie transport, the reciprocal block matrix, the exact
phase gradient, and the separated-block gap.  It proves no signed physical
finite-cell defect or completed-current bound, `Phi_B` theorem, contact
exclusion, retained aggregate or Xi theorem, `Q209`, cofinal descendant
theorem, `Lambda<=0`, PF-infinity, RH, or prize-level conclusion.

## 11.189 Reciprocal collar rail transport and finite-moment boundary defect

Section 11.188 proposes joining the diagonal and two adjacent reciprocal
blocks to the returned carriers before estimating the separated blocks.  The
local phase geometry supports that decomposition, but a global structural
test must come first: a fixed-width diagonal collar is not invariant when a
mode crosses an internal reciprocal half-cell.  This section derives its
exact two-rail jump, compresses the far complement before integration by
parts, and identifies the finite endpoint terms omitted by the full-line
first-correction cancellation.

Retain the physical cells `J_q` and reciprocal cells `C_p` from
(11.188.13).  For `r in C_p`, define

```text
I_(q,r)[P]
 :=integral_(J_q)f_P(u)e(-ru)du,

mathcal B_(q,p)[P]
 :=sum_(r in C_p)I_(q,r)[P].                     (11.189.1)
```

For an integer collar radius `0<=L<=N-1`, put

```text
mathcal C_(N,L)[P]
 :=sum_(1<=p,q<=N, |p-q|<=L)mathcal B_(q,p)[P],

mathcal E_(N,L)[P]
 :=sum_(1<=p,q<=N, |p-q|>=L+1)mathcal B_(q,p)[P].
```

Then the block matrix (11.188.14) gives the exact partition

```text
mathscr F_N[P]
 =mathcal C_(N,L)[P]+mathcal E_(N,L)[P].         (11.189.2)
```

The bookmarked diagonal-plus-adjacent object is the radius-one collar

```text
mathcal C_(N,1)[P]
 =sum_(q=1)^N mathcal B_(q,q)[P]
  +sum_(q=1)^(N-1)mathcal B_(q,q+1)[P]
  +sum_(q=2)^N mathcal B_(q,q-1)[P].             (11.189.3)
```

The far complement is not intrinsically a collection of unit-cell errors.
For fixed `p`, its physical cells form at most two contiguous intervals.
Consequently

```text
mathcal E_(N,L)[P]
 =sum_(p=1)^N sum_(r in C_p){

   1_(p>=L+2)integral_1^(p-L-1/2)f_P(u)e(-ru)du

  +1_(p<=N-L-1)integral_(p+L+1/2)^N
       f_P(u)e(-ru)du}.                          (11.189.4)
```

Equation (11.189.4) is the rail-compressed far functional.  It removes the
artificial boundary proliferation that would arise from integrating every
unit cell by parts separately.

Now let an internal reciprocal tie be crossed upward:

```text
alpha_P/r=p+1/2,

r:C_p -> C_(p+1).
```

Before the transfer, the collar contains the physical labels
`p-L,...,p+L`; afterward it contains `p+1-L,...,p+1+L`, truncated to
`[1,N]`.  Therefore its exact jump is

```text
Delta mathcal C_(N,L)[P]
 =1_(p+L+1<=N)I_(p+L+1,r)[P]
  -1_(p-L>=1)I_(p-L,r)[P].                      (11.189.5)
```

The far complement has the opposite jump:

```text
Delta mathcal E_(N,L)[P]
 =-Delta mathcal C_(N,L)[P].                    (11.189.6)
```

Thus (11.189.2) is invariant, as it must be, while no proper fixed-width
collar is coefficientwise invariant.  The radius-one specialization is

```text
Delta mathcal C_(N,1)[P]
 =1_(p+2<=N)I_(p+2,r)[P]
  -1_(p-1>=1)I_(p-1,r)[P].                      (11.189.7)
```

This is a genuine obstruction, not only an indexing possibility.  For the
exact test source `f(u)=u e(ru)`, every complete interior atom equals

```text
I_(q,r)=integral_(q-1/2)^(q+1/2)u du=q.
```

At an interior tie, (11.189.5) is therefore

```text
(p+L+1)-(p-L)=2L+1!=0.                           (11.189.8)
```

The witness is nonphysical and proves only structural nonclosure.  It is
enough to rule out a source-independent theorem that silently treats the
diagonal collar as the globally transported observation.  At the two outer
band ties, the complete mode, including both far rails, must likewise be
transferred to or from the outer remainder.

On a fixed roster-and-cell chart the relative lift remains valid:

```text
mathcal C_(N,L)[i(lambda-c)P]
 = (partial_xi-ic)mathcal C_(N,L)[P],

mathcal E_(N,L)[i(lambda-c)P]
 = (partial_xi-ic)mathcal E_(N,L)[P].            (11.189.9)
```

At a tie, (11.189.5)--(11.189.6) and the two corresponding lifted rail atoms
replace ordinary differentiation.

The exact physical consequence can now be stated.  Since
`mathscr F_N=mathcal C_(N,1)+mathcal E_(N,1)`, the ideal carrier-only joins
of (11.188.9)--(11.188.10) are

```text
mathcal J_H^0
 :=2mathscr M_N[P_H^0]
   -mathcal C_(N,1)[P_H^0]
   -mathcal E_(N,1)[P_H^0],

mathcal J_T^0
 :=2mathscr M_N[P_T^0]
   -mathcal C_(N,1)[P_T^0]
   -mathcal E_(N,1)[P_T^0]
   +2iu_Nmathcal T_N^[N][B_(T,N)^0].             (11.189.10)
```

The collar jump cancels only against the far jump inside (11.189.10).  The
two returned carriers are continuous across an internal reassignment, and
the transpose terminal survivor does not supply either rail atom.  Hence a
uniform sign theorem for `mathcal C_(N,1)` alone would not be a theorem for
the live physical join.

The local geometry remains useful inside a fixed chart.  For a diagonal
mode, put

```text
v=alpha_P/r,             u=v(1+y).
```

Then the exact phase is

```text
phi_r(u)
 =alpha_P(log v-1)
  +alpha_P{log(1+y)-y}.                          (11.189.11)
```

This is the negative Morse chart without a quadratic truncation.  The two
adjacent blocks are stationary boundary corners.  For `p=q+1`, let

```text
c=q+1/2,       u=c-a,       v=c+b,

d=(a+b)/(c+b).
```

Then

```text
phi_r(u)
 =alpha_P(log v-1)
  +alpha_P{log(1-d)+d},

phi_r'(u)=alpha_P(v-u)/(uv)>=0.                  (11.189.12)
```

Equality holds only at the shared corner `a=b=0`.  For `p=q-1`, put

```text
c=q-1/2,       u=c+a,       v=c-b,

d=(a+b)/(c-b).
```

The opposite orientation is

```text
phi_r(u)
 =alpha_P(log v-1)
  +alpha_P{log(1+d)-d},

phi_r'(u)=alpha_P(v-u)/(uv)<=0.                  (11.189.13)
```

Both corner corrections are strictly negative away from contact because

```text
d/dd {log(1-d)+d}=-d/(1-d),

d/dd {log(1+d)-d}=-d/(1+d).                     (11.189.14)
```

Their cubic terms have opposite orientations.  Replacing both by one
unsigned half-Gaussian would erase the rail information in (11.189.7).

For `L>=1`, every far rail is genuinely nonstationary.  On its support,
`|v-u|>=L`; since `1<=u<=N` and `1/2<=v<N+1/2`,

```text
|phi_r'(u)|
 =alpha_P|v-u|/(uv)
 >=alpha_P L/{N(N+1/2)}.                        (11.189.15)
```

Let `q_r(u)=alpha_P/u-r`.  Exact integration by parts on either oriented
far interval gives

```text
integral_a^b A(u)e(phi_r(u))du
 =kappa[Ae(phi_r)/q_r]_a^b

  -kappa integral_a^b e(phi_r)
      {A'/q_r-Aq_r'/q_r^2}du.                   (11.189.16)
```

Because the far cells were compressed first, the internal unit-cell
boundaries telescope.  Only `u=1`, `u=N`, and the two collar rails
`p-L-1/2`, `p+L+1/2` remain.  Equation (11.189.16) does not yet give an
aggregate bound, but it gives the correct boundary count and orientation
for one.

There is a parallel finite-boundary correction to the stationary expansion.
With `kappa=1/(2pi i)`, direct differentiation gives, on finite intervals,

```text
integral_a^b y^2e(-y^2/2)dy
 =kappa integral_a^b e(-y^2/2)dy
  -kappa[y e(-y^2/2)]_a^b,

integral_c^d eta^2e(+eta^2/2)deta
 =-kappa integral_c^d e(+eta^2/2)deta
  +kappa[eta e(+eta^2/2)]_c^d.                  (11.189.17)
```

On the regularized full lines, the displayed boundary terms vanish.  The
first sequential coefficient from Section 11.179 is then

```text
-kappa mathcal D_qA/(2alpha_P)
 +kappa mathcal D_qA/(2alpha_P)=0.               (11.189.18)
```

On finite diagonal and adjacent charts, the four endpoint terms in
(11.189.17) remain.  Equation (11.189.18) therefore survives as a full-line
coefficient identity, but not as a finite-collar remainder theorem.  Those
endpoint terms may cancel only after the two collar rails, physical
endpoints, reciprocal ties, and terminal recurrence have been composed.

The ideal source polynomials themselves retain the exact identities

```text
P_H^0(x)=-i(x+u_N)(x-u_N)^2/4,

P_T^0(x)=-i(x-u_N)(x+u_N)^2/4
          +u_(N,x)(x-u_N),

P_T^0(x)=-P_H^0(-x)+u_(N,x)(x-u_N).             (11.189.19)
```

The last reflection does not produce a cancellation because the physical
logarithmic interval is not reflection symmetric.  At a physical atom
`x=-u_q`,

```text
P_H^0(log q)=i(u_q-u_N)(u_q+u_N)^2/4,

P_T^0(log q)=i(u_q+u_N)(u_q-u_N)^2/4
              -u_(N,x)(u_q+u_N).                (11.189.20)
```

At `q=N`, the Hermitian value is zero and the transpose value is
`-2u_Nu_(N,x)`.  The latter remains joined to the explicit final term of
(11.189.10) and the full complex terminal recurrence; its real trace cannot
replace the imaginary conditional quadrature.

The attempted diagonal-plus-adjacent calculation has therefore produced a
rigorous route correction.  On each fixed cell chart one should evaluate
(11.189.11)--(11.189.14) with the ideal cubics intact, carry the four
finite-moment boundary terms (11.189.17) to the rail interfaces, and combine
them with the rail-compressed far identity (11.189.16).  The first admissible
signed targets are the complete tie-invariant joins (11.189.10), not
`mathcal C_(N,1)` by itself.  Only after that ideal aggregate is controlled
may `Delta_H,Delta_T`, the fixed affine row, pure terminal transpose package,
moved-tail defect, and quadratic current remainders be attached.

Every `pi` in this section comes from `e(x)=exp(2pi i x)` and
`kappa=1/(2pi i)`.  Equation (11.189.17) follows by differentiating the two
fixed Fourier Gaussians.  No circle, polygon, fitted constant, or plotted
symmetry is inserted.

This section proves the exact collar/far partition, general and radius-one
rail jumps, nonclosure of every proper fixed-width collar, fixed-cell lift,

## 11.190 Double-Morse rail flux and moving-endpoint shear

Section 11.189 leaves four finite Gaussian endpoint terms to be matched to
the reciprocal-collar rails.  That match cannot be made by treating the two
Morse variables as a rectangle: the physical endpoints move with the
reciprocal variable.  This section derives the exact two-variable chart,
identifies the resulting shear term, and promotes the paired first
correction from a full-line cancellation to a finite boundary-flux identity.
The calculation is exact, but it is not yet a signed estimate.

Fix a positive continuous reciprocal variable `r` in the `p`-th cell and a
positive physical variable `u`.  Use the lattice-gauged phase

```text
Psi_p(r,u)=alpha_Plog u-r(u-p),

rho=pr/alpha_P,                 v=ur/alpha_P.     (11.190.1)
```

Then

```text
r=alpha_Prho/p,                 u=pv/rho,

Psi_p(r,u)
 =alpha_Plog p
  +alpha_P{rho-1-log rho}
  -alpha_P{v-1-log v}.                          (11.190.2)
```

Retain the signed Morse function and its inverse Jacobian from Section
11.168:

```text
z(w)=sgn(w-1)sqrt(2[w-1-log w]),

J(w)=dw/dz=wz(w)/(w-1),          J(1)=1,

eta=sqrt(alpha_P)z(rho),         y=sqrt(alpha_P)z(v).
```

Equation (11.190.2) becomes the exact separated phase

```text
Psi_p(r,u)=alpha_Plog p+(eta^2-y^2)/2.            (11.190.3)
```

There is no local Taylor approximation in (11.190.3).  Since

```text
det partial(r,u)/partial(rho,v)=alpha_P/rho,
```

the complete coordinate Jacobian is

```text
dr du={J(rho)J(v)/rho}deta dy.                    (11.190.4)
```

Thus, for

```text
A_P(u)=exp(S(log u))P(log u),
```

the transformed two-variable amplitude is

```text
G_P(eta,y)
 =A_P(pv/rho)J(rho)J(v)/rho.                     (11.190.5)
```

The variables remain coupled through `pv/rho`, even though the phase has
separated.  In particular, the physical line `u=p` is exactly

```text
v=rho,                 y=eta,

Psi_p(r,p)=alpha_Plog p.                          (11.190.6)
```

This is the returned-carrier ridge.  It is not an oscillatory error rail.

The continuous reciprocal-cell endpoints are

```text
rho_-=p/(p+1/2),             rho_+=p/(p-1/2),

eta_-=sqrt(alpha_P)z(rho_-),
eta_+=sqrt(alpha_P)z(rho_+).                     (11.190.7)
```

For an internal radius-`L` collar put

```text
U_-=p-L-1/2,                 U_+=p+L+1/2.
```

At a fixed `eta`, with inverse `rho=rho(eta)`, its two physical boundaries
are

```text
y_U(eta)=sqrt(alpha_P)z(Urho(eta)/p),

y_-(eta)=y_(U_-)(eta),       y_+(eta)=y_(U_+)(eta).
```

Consequently the exact Morse image of the collar is

```text
Omega_(p,L)
 ={(eta,y):eta_-<=eta<=eta_+,
             y_-(eta)<=y<=y_+(eta)}.             (11.190.8)
```

It is curvilinear.  Direct differentiation gives the endpoint velocity

```text
y_U'(eta)
 =(U/p)J(rho)/J(Urho/p)
 =vJ(rho)/{rho J(v)}>0.                          (11.190.9)
```

The shear factor `eta y_U'` vanishes at the reciprocal saddle `eta=0`, but
the endpoint velocity itself does not vanish.  At the reciprocal sides, the
inner saddle is

```text
u_0(eta_-)=p+1/2,             u_0(eta_+)=p-1/2.  (11.190.10)
```

For `L=1`, these are the two diagonal/adjacent interfaces, whereas the
outer physical rails are `p+3/2` and `p-3/2`.  They are separated by a full
adjacent cell and cannot be identified pointwise.

The finite first-correction geometry is now transparent.  Put

```text
E(eta,y)=e((eta^2-y^2)/2),       kappa=1/(2pi i).
```

Direct differentiation proves

```text
div_(eta,y)(kappa eta E,-kappa y E)
 =(eta^2+y^2)E.                                  (11.190.11)
```

The cancellation of the two constant terms in the finite moment identities
(11.189.17) is exactly (11.190.11).  On the full regularized plane the
boundary flux vanishes, recovering (11.189.18).  On `Omega_(p,L)`, define

```text
F(eta)=integral_(y_-(eta))^(y_+(eta))
          e(-y^2/2)dy.
```

The divergence theorem gives the exact finite identity

```text
integral_(eta_-)^(eta_+)e(+eta^2/2){
   integral_(y_-)^(y_+)y^2e(-y^2/2)dy
   +eta^2F(eta)}deta

 =kappa[eta e(+eta^2/2)F(eta)]_(eta_-)^(eta_+)

  +kappa integral_(eta_-)^(eta_+)
      e((eta^2-y_-^2)/2){y_-+eta y_-'}deta

  -kappa integral_(eta_-)^(eta_+)
      e((eta^2-y_+^2)/2){y_++eta y_+'}deta.      (11.190.12)
```

The first line on the right is the pair of reciprocal sides.  The next two
lines are the oriented physical rails.  Their terms `eta y_-'` and
`eta y_+'` are the moving-endpoint shear.  They are absent only in an
artificial Cartesian Morse rectangle.

The same fact follows by sequential one-dimensional integration.  Leibniz'
rule gives

```text
F'(eta)
 =y_+'(eta)e(-y_+(eta)^2/2)
  -y_-'(eta)e(-y_-(eta)^2/2).                    (11.190.13)
```

When the positive second-moment identity is applied to `F(eta)`, the term
`-kappa integral eta e(+eta^2/2)F'(eta)deta` supplies exactly the two shear
contributions in (11.190.12).  Therefore the four fixed-limit terms in
(11.189.17), by themselves, are not the physical rail flux.

There is also an exact weighted version.  For any differentiable coefficient
`Gamma(eta,y)`, (11.190.11) becomes

```text
div(Gamma kappa eta E,-Gamma kappa y E)

 =Gamma(eta^2+y^2)E
  +kappa E{eta Gamma_eta-y Gamma_y}.              (11.190.14)
```

Hence

```text
integral_(Omega)Gamma(eta^2+y^2)E

 =kappa integral_(partial Omega)
      Gamma E{eta dy+y deta}

  -kappa integral_(Omega)
      E{eta Gamma_eta-y Gamma_y}deta dy.          (11.190.15)
```

The frozen symbol `Gamma=mathcal D_pA/(2alpha_P)` has only the boundary
flux.  The physical amplitude (11.190.5) is not constant, so its interior
transport in (11.190.15) is compulsory.  The full-line coefficient
cancellation cannot be promoted by substituting the ideal cubic only at
four endpoints.

The diagonal and adjacent physical cells do, however, compose exactly.  For
`L=1`, their original intervals tile

```text
[p-3/2,p-1/2] union [p-1/2,p+1/2]
 union [p+1/2,p+3/2]=[p-3/2,p+3/2].              (11.190.16)
```

The Morse map is increasing, so each internal interface occurs once as an
upper boundary and once as a lower boundary.  Both its ordinary `y_U` flux
and its shear `eta y_U'` cancel with opposite orientations.  Only the two
outer collar rails remain.  This is the correct local role of the adjacent
corner blocks.

At a shared reciprocal boundary the neighboring lattice gauges obey

```text
Psi_(p+1)(r,u)-Psi_p(r,u)=r.                     (11.190.17)
```

When that boundary is an actual integer tie, `e(r)=1`, so the overlapping
complete-mode traces have the same Fourier phase.  The radius-one physical
interval shifts from `[p-3/2,p+3/2]` to `[p-1/2,p+5/2]`; after common
interfaces cancel, the leaving cell is `J_(p-1)` and the entering cell is
`J_(p+2)`.  The ordinary rail flux and the shear move with those complete
cells.  They become invariant only after the far complement is included, in
agreement with (11.189.5)--(11.189.7).

The ideal-cubic values on an arbitrary positive rail `U` are explicit.  Put

```text
u_U=log(a/U).
```

Then (11.189.19) gives

```text
P_H^0(log U)
 =i(u_U-u_N)(u_U+u_N)^2/4,

P_T^0(log U)
 =i(u_U+u_N)(u_U-u_N)^2/4
  -u_(N,x)(u_U+u_N).                             (11.190.18)
```

These formulas apply to the half-integer inner interfaces and outer collar
rails as well as to integer carriers.  At the upper physical endpoint,

```text
P_H^0(log N)=0,

P_T^0(log N)=-2u_Nu_(N,x).                      (11.190.19)
```

Thus the exact Hermitian value term vanishes at `u=N`; the transpose term
still belongs to the conditional terminal quadrature and the full complex
recurrence.  The reflection
`P_T^0(x)=-P_H^0(-x)+u_(N,x)(x-u_N)` does not reflect the physical flux
domain: `[1,N]`, `S(log u)`, reciprocal side traces, and the velocities
(11.190.9) are not reflection symmetric.

The attempted endpoint match has therefore produced a second rigorous route
correction.  The next admissible object is not the four fixed-limit moment
terms.  It is (11.190.15) with the complete transformed amplitudes
`G_(P_H^0),G_(P_T^0)`, joined to the rail-compressed far identity
(11.189.16), the finite-cell tie halves, both returned carriers, and the
transpose terminal survivor.  The remaining interior transport

```text
eta partial_eta G_P-y partial_y G_P              (11.190.20)
```

must then be estimated or rigorously obstructed without blockwise moduli.
Only after that ideal composition closes may `Delta_H,Delta_T` and the
remaining current packages be restored.

Every `pi` in this section comes from `e(x)=exp(2pi i x)` and
`kappa=1/(2pi i)`.  Equations (11.190.11)--(11.190.15) follow by direct
differentiation and the divergence theorem.  No circle, polygon, fitted
constant, or plotted symmetry is inserted.

This section proves the exact double-Morse phase and Jacobian, returned
carrier ridge, reciprocal and physical endpoint maps, endpoint velocity,
curvilinear finite-correction boundary flux, moving-endpoint shear, weighted
interior transport, adjacent-interface cancellation, integer-tie gauge,
ideal-cubic rail values, and terminal values.  It proves no signed weighted
flux, complete ideal join, far aggregate, completed-current or `Phi_B`
theorem, contact exclusion, retained aggregate or Xi theorem, `Q209`,
cofinal descendant theorem, `Lambda<=0`, PF-infinity, RH, or prize-level
conclusion.

## 11.191 Hyperbolic transport and the carrier ridge

Section 11.190 converts the failed rectangular endpoint match into an exact
weighted boundary-flux identity.  Its remaining interior term is
`eta partial_eta G_P-y partial_y G_P`.  This section computes that term in
closed form and then puts the phase in hyperbolic coordinates.  The result
isolates a nonoscillatory carrier ridge and an exact finite transverse
Fourier kernel.  This is a new reduction of the open estimate, not a signed
bound.

For `w>0`, define

```text
h(w)=w-1-log w,

mathfrak R(w)=2h(w)/(w-1),

mathfrak B(w)=2h(w)/(w-1)^2,                     (11.191.1)
```

with the removable values

```text
mathfrak R(1)=0,               mathfrak B(1)=1.
```

The signed Morse function and Jacobian obey

```text
z(w)J(w)=w mathfrak R(w),

z(w)J(w) partial_w log J(w)=1-mathfrak B(w).     (11.191.2)
```

Indeed, `z^2=2h` and

```text
partial_w log J
 =1/w+(w-1)/{2wh(w)}-1/(w-1).
```

The removable saddle series are

```text
mathfrak R(1+d)
 =d-2d^2/3+d^3/2-2d^4/5+O(d^5),

mathfrak B(1+d)
 =1-2d/3+d^2/2-2d^3/5+d^4/3+O(d^5).             (11.191.3)
```

Here the `O` terms record only the analytic local series; they are not used
as an unquantified physical remainder.  Globally, `mathfrak B(w)>0`, while
`mathfrak R(w)` has the sign of `w-1`.

Retain `rho,v,eta,y` and `G_P` from (11.190.1)--(11.190.5).  The transport
vector in the original Morse ratios is

```text
mathcal L
 :=eta partial_eta-y partial_y

 =z(rho)J(rho)partial_rho
  -z(v)J(v)partial_v.                            (11.191.4)
```

Put

```text
x=log(pv/rho),

g(x)=S'(x),

G_P(rho,v)
 =exp(S(x))P(x)J(rho)J(v)/rho.                   (11.191.5)
```

Using (11.191.2), direct differentiation gives the exact division-free
identity

```text
mathcal L G_P
 =exp(S(x))J(rho)J(v)/rho * {

   [mathfrak B(v)-mathfrak B(rho)-mathfrak R(rho)]P(x)

  -[mathfrak R(rho)+mathfrak R(v)]
       [P'(x)+g(x)P(x)]}.                        (11.191.6)
```

No quotient by `P` occurs.  At the double saddle `rho=v=1`, both displayed
coefficients vanish.  If `rho=1+delta_rho` and `v=1+delta_v`, their first
jets are

```text
mathfrak B(v)-mathfrak B(rho)-mathfrak R(rho)
 =-delta_rho/3-2delta_v/3+O(delta^2),

-mathfrak R(rho)-mathfrak R(v)
 =-delta_rho-delta_v+O(delta^2).                 (11.191.7)
```

Thus the weighted transport has one local displacement gain, but not two.
The exact formula (11.191.6), rather than (11.191.7), remains the theorem
input.

On the carrier line `v=rho`, one has `x=log p` and `y=eta`.  Equation
(11.191.6) reduces to

```text
mathcal L G_P(rho,rho)

 =-exp(S(log p))J(rho)^2mathfrak R(rho)/rho *

   {P+2(P'+gP)}(log p).                          (11.191.8)
```

The phase is constant on this line by (11.190.6).  The transport vanishes at
`rho=1`, but it is generally nonzero on either side and reverses orientation
with `mathfrak R(rho)`.  For the exact test source `P=1,S=0`, the ridge value
is `-J(rho)^2mathfrak R(rho)/rho`; this changes sign at `rho=1`.  The witness
is nonphysical and rules out only a coefficient-blind sign theorem.

The correct canonical coordinates are now hyperbolic.  Put

```text
s=(eta+y)/sqrt(2),          d=(eta-y)/sqrt(2),

eta=(s+d)/sqrt(2),          y=(s-d)/sqrt(2).      (11.191.9)
```

The transformation has unit absolute Jacobian and gives

```text
(eta^2-y^2)/2=sd,

mathcal L=d partial_s+s partial_d.                (11.191.10)
```

Thus the double Morse saddle is hyperbolic.  The carrier ridge `y=eta` is
`d=0`, where `e(sd)=1`; `mathcal L` differentiates transversely there as
`s partial_d`.  A two-dimensional modulus would erase the exact direction
in which Fourier inversion returns the carrier.

For any fixed `s!=0` and finite transverse limits `d_-<d_+`, one has the
exact kernel

```text
integral_(d_-)^(d_+)e(sd)dd
 =kappa{e(sd_+)-e(sd_-)}/s,                      (11.191.11)
```

with removable value `d_+-d_-` at `s=0`.  This is a finite Fourier kernel,
not an asymptotic stationary approximation.

For a transformed amplitude `G(s,d)`, subtract its ridge trace:

```text
G(s,d)=G(s,0)+d H(s,d),

H(s,d)={G(s,d)-G(s,0)}/d,
```

with the derivative continuation at `d=0`.  Slice by slice,

```text
integral_(d_-)^(d_+)G(s,d)e(sd)dd

 =G(s,0)kappa{e(sd_+)-e(sd_-)}/s

  +kappa/s[dH(s,d)e(sd)]_(d_-)^(d_+)

  -kappa/s integral_(d_-)^(d_+)
       {H+d partial_dH}e(sd)dd,                  (11.191.12)
```

for `s!=0`.  The removable central chart is kept in its direct integral
form.  In the physical curvilinear domain the transverse limits depend on
`s`; (11.191.12) is applied at fixed `s`, so their boundary traces remain
explicit rather than being differentiated away.

The ideal cubic derivatives required by (11.191.6) are

```text
(P_H^0)'(x)=-i(x-u_N)(3x+u_N)/4,

(P_T^0)'(x)=-i(x+u_N)(3x-u_N)/4+u_(N,x).         (11.191.13)
```

At the terminal logarithmic value `x=-u_N`,

```text
P_H^0=0,                    (P_H^0)'=-iu_N^2,

P_T^0=-2u_Nu_(N,x),

(P_T^0)'+g_NP_T^0
 =u_(N,x)(1-2g_Nu_N).                            (11.191.14)
```

Therefore the exact Hermitian endpoint value null does not delete the
terminal-neighborhood derivative transport.  It deletes the physical value
boundary in the already identified place; the interior term (11.191.6)
remains.  Neither

```text
P_H^0+2{(P_H^0)'+gP_H^0}
```

nor its transpose analogue vanishes identically, so the ridge term
(11.191.8) is live in both channels.

The next admissible analytic split is now precise.  First recompose the ridge
trace in (11.191.12) with both copies of the returned carrier and the
transpose terminal block.  Then keep a central `s` chart around the
removable kernel value, and use the exact `1/s` transverse kernel outside
that chart.  The physical rails, reciprocal sides, tie halves, and
rail-compressed far functional remain joined throughout.  Only after the
ridge coefficient is identified may a modulus be applied to the transverse
residual.

Every `pi` in this section is inherited through
`e(x)=exp(2pi i x)` and `kappa=1/(2pi i)`.  The profiles
`mathfrak R,mathfrak B` come from `w-1-log w` and the exact Morse Jacobian.
No circle, polygon, fitted constant, or plotted symmetry is inserted.

This section proves the removable transport profiles, the closed weighted
transport operator, its saddle zero and carrier-ridge trace, the hyperbolic
phase and boost, the finite transverse kernel, ridge subtraction identity,
and ideal derivative and terminal identities.  It proves no signed
ridge-completed ideal join, transverse residual bound, far aggregate,
completed-current or `Phi_B` theorem, contact exclusion, retained aggregate
or Xi theorem, `Q209`, cofinal descendant theorem, `Lambda<=0`, PF-infinity,
RH, or prize-level conclusion.

## 11.192 Finite ridge inversion and the surviving starred carrier

Section 11.191 left the coefficient of the `d=0` ridge unresolved.  That
coefficient cannot be determined from the local hyperbolic chart alone,
because the finite reciprocal diagonal is not the full Fourier inversion.
This section composes the chart with the exact finite-cell identities of
Section 11.180.  The result fixes the factor of two: one of the two copies in
`2mathscr M_N-mathscr F_N` is used by diagonal inversion, and exactly one
starred carrier remains.  It also gives an exact nonphysical witness showing
that the two-sided exterior cannot be deleted by a coefficient-blind local
argument.

Use full support `[1,N]`.  For each physical reciprocal cell, write

```text
M_q[A]
 :=omega_N(q)A(q)e(alpha_Plog q),

Lambda_q^(alias)[A]
 :=sum_(s!=q)^sym B_(q,s)[A].                    (11.192.1)
```

The endpoint weights are

```text
omega_N(1)=omega_N(N)=1/2,
omega_N(q)=1,                         1<q<N.
```

Equations (11.180.10) and (11.180.21) say exactly

```text
S_q[A]
 =tau_q[A]+B_(q,q)[A]+Lambda_q^(alias)[A],

B_(q,q)[A]=M_q[A]-E_q^(ext)[A].                 (11.192.2)
```

Therefore the local carrier-only join is

```text
2M_q[A]-S_q[A]

 =M_q[A]-tau_q[A]+E_q^(ext)[A]
   -Lambda_q^(alias)[A].                         (11.192.3)
```

This is the exact per-cell coefficient identity.  It leaves one copy of
`M_q`, with its original Dirichlet half-weight when `q=1,N`.  The other copy
has not disappeared by approximation: it is the copy used in
`B_(q,q)=M_q-E_q^(ext)`.  Formula (11.192.3) is not yet a useful cellwise
estimate, because the alias series is symmetrically ordered and the exterior
is two-sided.

The global recomposition removes those cellwise artifacts.  Define

```text
E_band[A]
 :=lim_(R->infinity)sum_(s=-R)^R E_s^(band)[A].
```

On `[1,N]`, (11.180.25) and (11.187.13) give

```text
mathscr F_N[A]
 =tau_band[A]+mathscr M_N[A]-E_band[A],

mathscr D_N[A]
 :=mathscr F_N[A]-mathscr M_N[A]
 =tau_band[A]-E_band[A].                         (11.192.4)
```

Consequently

```text
2mathscr M_N[A]-mathscr F_N[A]

 =mathscr M_N[A]-mathscr D_N[A]

 =mathscr M_N[A]-tau_band[A]+E_band[A].          (11.192.5)
```

At every internal reciprocal boundary, the lower `-I_A/2` correction of one
cell and the upper `+I_A/2` correction of its neighbor cancel.  Thus
`tau_band` in (11.192.4)--(11.192.5) contains only the two outer band
corrections.  The internal aliases and cell exteriors similarly recompose
before estimation into the single global exterior `E_band`.  They must not
be assigned independent absolute budgets.

The ideal joins in (11.189.10) therefore have the exact forms

```text
mathcal J_H^0
 =mathscr M_N[P_H^0]
  -tau_band[P_H^0]+E_band[P_H^0],

mathcal J_T^0
 =mathscr M_N[P_T^0]
  -tau_band[P_T^0]+E_band[P_T^0]
  +2iu_Nmathcal T_N^[N][B_(T,N)^0].              (11.192.6)
```

The `q=N` atom in the first line vanishes through `P_H^0(log N)=0`.  The
transpose carrier retains its starred `q=N` half-atom, while the displayed
terminal conditional term remains separate.  No cancellation between those
two terminal objects is asserted here.

It remains to locate the ridge inside (11.192.2).  The full finite diagonal
rectangle

```text
a_q<=r<=b_q,                     1<=u<=N
```

has the double-Morse image `Omega_q`.  Equations (11.190.3)--(11.190.5) and
(11.191.9) give

```text
B_(q,q)[A]
 =e(alpha_Plog q)
   integral_(Omega_q)G_q(s,d)e(sd)ds dd.         (11.192.7)
```

For a physical boundary `u=U`, the function

```text
eta -> eta+y_U(eta)
```

is strictly increasing because `y_U'>0`.  Hence the intersection of
`Omega_q` with a fixed `s` line is an interval.  The fixed-`s` fibers that
meet the carrier line `d=0` are indexed by

```text
S_q^Delta=[sqrt(2)eta_-,sqrt(2)eta_+].           (11.192.8)
```

For `s` in this interval, denote the actual transverse limits by
`d_-(s)<=0<=d_+(s)`.  This includes one-sided fibers at the physical
endpoints `q=1,N`.  Put

```text
K_q(s)
 :=integral_(d_-(s))^(d_+(s))e(sd)dd

 =kappa{e(sd_+(s))-e(sd_-(s))}/s,       s!=0,

K_q(0)=d_+(0)-d_-(0).                           (11.192.9)
```

The line `d=0` has two-dimensional measure zero.  A ridge contribution is
created only after its trace is lifted across the finite transverse fiber.
On `S_q^Delta`, write

```text
G_q(s,d)=G_q(s,0)+dH_q(s,d)
```

and define

```text
mathscr Z_q[A]
 :=e(alpha_Plog q)
   integral_(S_q^Delta)G_q(s,0)K_q(s)ds,

mathscr V_q[A]
 :=e(alpha_Plog q)
   integral_(S_q^Delta)
     integral_(d_-(s))^(d_+(s))
       dH_q(s,d)e(sd)dd ds.                     (11.192.10)
```

Let `mathscr W_q[A]` be the contribution from the remaining `s` wings.
Then, without approximation,

```text
B_(q,q)[A]
 =mathscr Z_q[A]+mathscr V_q[A]+mathscr W_q[A],

M_q[A]
 =mathscr Z_q[A]+mathscr V_q[A]+mathscr W_q[A]
  +E_q^(ext)[A].                                 (11.192.11)
```

Thus a direct identification `mathscr Z_q=M_q` is equivalent to the
additional cancellation law

```text
mathscr V_q[A]+mathscr W_q[A]+E_q^(ext)[A]=0.    (11.192.12)
```

Neither the local hyperbolic coordinate change nor Fourier inversion proves
(11.192.12).  The finite ridge coefficient is the nonconstant kernel
`K_q(s)`, not the scalar `1`; the central value in (11.192.9) is removable,
not singular.

There is an exact structural witness.  Take `B>=3`, `alpha_P=2`, `q=2`, and
the piecewise-BV test source

```text
F_A(u):=A(u)e(alpha_Plog u)=1_[3/2,5/2](u).      (11.192.13)
```

Since `q=2` is an interior continuity point, full Fourier inversion gives

```text
M_2[A]=F_A(2)=1.
```

On the other hand,

```text
I_A(r)e(2r)
 =integral_(-1/2)^(1/2)e(-rt)dt
 =sin(pi r)/(pi r).                              (11.192.14)
```

The finite reciprocal cell is

```text
[a_2,b_2]=[4/5,4/3],          b_2-a_2=8/15.
```

Therefore

```text
B_(2,2)[A]
 =integral_(4/5)^(4/3) sin(pi r)/(pi r)dr

 ={Si(4pi/3)-Si(4pi/5)}/pi,

|B_(2,2)[A]|<=8/15<1=M_2[A],

|E_2^(ext)[A]|
 =|M_2[A]-B_(2,2)[A]|>=7/15.                    (11.192.15)
```

The bound uses only `|sin(pi r)/(pi r)|<=1`.  The sine-integral notation in
(11.192.15) is an exact antiderivative, not a numerical fit.  The witness is
not a physical ideal-cubic source.  It disproves a universal
coefficient-blind identity equating the finite diagonal to the returned
carrier.  Together with (11.192.11), it shows that a ridge-equals-carrier
claim needs a separate cancellation of the transverse residual, outer wings,
and exterior.  It does not independently disprove such an additional
cancellation special to the physical amplitude.

The route decision is now sharper.  Direct ridge-to-carrier matching is
retired.  Before applying the `1/s` kernel in (11.191.12), the global
exterior in (11.192.5) must be pulled through the full-support
exterior/complement identity (11.187.12)--(11.187.16) and joined to the
negative-, low-positive-, and high-positive-frequency fringes, the outer tie
halves, and the transpose terminal recurrence.  A useful theorem must bound
that complete package rather than repeat the Fourier involution.  Only then
may the central and outer hyperbolic residuals be estimated and the physical
corrections `Delta_H,Delta_T` attached.

Every `pi` in (11.192.9) and (11.192.14)--(11.192.15) comes from the fixed
Fourier character `e(x)=exp(2pi i x)` and
`kappa=1/(2pi i)`.  No circle, polygon, fitted constant, or plotted symmetry
is inserted.

This section proves the per-cell and global one-carrier coefficient,
starred endpoint weighting, internal tie cancellation, exact finite
ridge/transverse/wing decomposition, and a nonzero-exterior obstruction
witness.  It proves no signed ridge-completed ideal join,
exterior/complement bound, completed-current or `Phi_B` theorem, contact
exclusion, retained aggregate or Xi theorem, `Q209`, cofinal descendant
theorem, `Lambda<=0`, PF-infinity, RH, or prize-level conclusion.

## 11.193 Symmetric outer-frequency pairing and the finite near kernel

Section 11.192 identifies the unresolved ideal package as one starred
carrier plus the global exterior/tie combination.  That combination can be
pulled back exactly to the modes outside the reciprocal band.  There is,
however, a convergence constraint that rules out treating the negative and
high-positive infinities as independent tails.  Their endpoint terms are
harmonic and cancel only under the common symmetric cutoff already built
into finite Poisson summation.  This section gives the canonical split and
isolates the remaining finite kernel.

Retain the full-support notation

```text
f_P(u)=e(alpha_Plog u)exp(S(log u))P(log u),

I_P(r)=integral_1^N f_P(u)e(-ru)du,

m_N=floor(alpha_P/(N+1/2))+1,

n_N=floor(2alpha_P),

mathcal R_N={m_N,...,n_N}.                       (11.193.1)
```

In the physical regime the roster is nonempty.  Define its complement with
the same symmetric order as in (11.187.14):

```text
mathscr O_N[P]
 :=lim_(R->infinity)
    sum_(-R<=r<=R, r notin mathcal R_N)I_P(r).
```

Equations (11.187.14), (11.187.16), and (11.192.4) give the exact chain

```text
mathscr O_N[P]
 =mathscr M_N[P]-mathscr F_N[P]
 =E_band[P]-tau_band[P]
 =-mathscr D_N[P].                              (11.193.2)
```

Consequently the ideal joins (11.192.6) are

```text
mathcal J_H^0
 =mathscr M_N[P_H^0]+mathscr O_N[P_H^0],

mathcal J_T^0
 =mathscr M_N[P_T^0]+mathscr O_N[P_T^0]
  +2iu_Nmathcal T_N^[N][B_(T,N)^0].             (11.193.3)
```

These are exterior pullbacks, not estimates.  In particular, (11.193.2)
is the same Fourier involution expressed in three coordinate systems.

For every finite `R>=n_N`, direct partition of the integer roster gives

```text
sum_(-R<=r<=R, r notin mathcal R_N)I_P(r)

 =sum_(r=1)^(m_N-1)I_P(r)+I_P(0)

  +sum_(k=1)^n_N I_P(-k)

  +sum_(k=n_N+1)^R{I_P(-k)+I_P(k)}.             (11.193.4)
```

No infinite series has been rearranged in (11.193.4).  Define the finite
near part and the remote paired part by

```text
mathscr N_N[P]
 :=sum_(r=1)^(m_N-1)I_P(r)+I_P(0)
   +sum_(k=1)^n_N I_P(-k),

mathscr C_N[P]
 :=sum_(k=n_N+1)^infinity{I_P(-k)+I_P(k)}.       (11.193.5)
```

The near part has the exact contiguous Dirichlet kernel

```text
mathscr N_N[P]
 =integral_1^N f_P(u)K_(near,N)(u)du,

K_(near,N)(u)
 :=sum_(j=-(m_N-1))^n_N e(ju).                  (11.193.6)
```

For every integer `ell`, Fourier orthogonality gives

```text
integral_ell^(ell+1)K_(near,N)(u)du=1.          (11.193.7)
```

The value `1` is the coefficient of the unique zero mode.  It is not a
positivity statement: `K_(near,N)` is generally complex, nonsymmetric, and
large pointwise.  Its mean-one component must therefore remain joined to
the returned starred carrier rather than be estimated as an unrelated
error.

The remote pairs are better behaved.  For every positive integer `k`,

```text
I_P(-k)+I_P(k)
 =2integral_1^N f_P(u)cos(2pi ku)du.             (11.193.8)
```

Assume `f_P` is `C^2` on `[1,N]`, as it is for the ideal physical source.
Because `1,N` are integers, the sine endpoint values vanish.  Two exact
integrations by parts yield

```text
I_P(-k)+I_P(k)

 ={2/(2pi k)^2}{

    f_P'(N)-f_P'(1)

   -integral_1^N f_P''(u)cos(2pi ku)du}.         (11.193.9)
```

It follows that the paired series is absolutely convergent and

```text
|mathscr C_N[P]|

 <={|f_P'(N)-f_P'(1)|+||f_P''||_(L^1[1,N])
    /(2pi^2)}
    sum_(k=n_N+1)^infinity 1/k^2

 <={|f_P'(N)-f_P'(1)|+||f_P''||_(L^1[1,N])
    /(2pi^2 n_N)}.                              (11.193.10)
```

Thus (11.193.4) passes to the exact canonical identity

```text
mathscr O_N[P]=mathscr N_N[P]+mathscr C_N[P].   (11.193.11)
```

Equation (11.193.10) is an absolute-convergence theorem, not yet a physical
`h^2` estimate.  Derivatives of `f_P` contain `alpha_P`; those factors can
offset the reciprocal tail scale and must be bounded in the physical
normalization before (11.193.10) can enter the flow reserve.

The need for symmetric pairing is not merely technical.  Put

```text
Delta_P=f_P(N)-f_P(1),

kappa=1/(2pi i).
```

One integration by parts gives

```text
I_P(k)=-kappa Delta_P/k+O(k^(-2)),

I_P(-k)=kappa Delta_P/k+O(k^(-2)).               (11.193.12)
```

If `Delta_P!=0`, each one-sided series has a nonzero harmonic leading term;
only the opposite-mode pair cancels it.  For the ideal Hermitian cubic,
write `x=log(u/a)` and `u_N=log(a/N)`.  Then

```text
P_H^0(x)=-i(x+u_N)(x-u_N)^2/4,

P_H^0(log N)=0,

P_H^0(0)
 =i log N{log(a^2/N)}^2/4.                      (11.193.13)
```

Here `P_H^0(0)` denotes the lower physical endpoint `lambda=log 1=0`, so
`x=-log a`.  Since `S(0)=0` and `e(alpha_Plog 1)=1`, put

```text
c_H:=log N{log(a^2/N)}^2/4>0,

Delta_H=-ic_H                                  (11.193.14)
```

for `a>=N>=2`.  Substitution into (11.193.12) gives

```text
I_H(k)=c_H/(2pi k)+O(k^(-2)),

I_H(-k)=-c_H/(2pi k)+O(k^(-2)).                 (11.193.15)
```

Therefore

```text
sum_(k=n_N+1)^R I_H(k)
 ={c_H/(2pi)}(H_R-H_(n_N))+O(1),

sum_(k=n_N+1)^R I_H(-k)
 =-{c_H/(2pi)}(H_R-H_(n_N))+O(1).               (11.193.16)
```

The two separate outer infinities diverge with opposite real signs.  Their
sum under the common cutoff converges through (11.193.9).  An exact
nonphysical guard makes the same point without asymptotics: for `f(u)=u`
on integer `[1,N]`,

```text
I_f(k)=-kappa(N-1)/k,

I_f(-k)=kappa(N-1)/k                            (11.193.17)
```

for every `k>=1`.  The derivative remainder vanishes exactly.  This witness
does not model the physical coefficient; it rules out assigning separate
absolute budgets to the two conditional half-series.

There is an algebraic symmetry in the ideal cubics,

```text
P_T^0(x)
 =-P_H^0(-x)+u_(N,x)(x-u_N),                    (11.193.18)
```

but it is not a symmetry of the outer operator.  Since `x=log(u/a)`, the
map `x->-x` is

```text
u -> a^2/u,

[1,N] -> [a^2/N,a^2].                           (11.193.19)
```

For `a>=N>=2`, the image lies at or above `N` and is not the original
physical interval.  With `u=a^2/v`, the Fourier phase becomes

```text
alpha_Plog u-ru

 =2alpha_Plog a-alpha_Plog v-r a^2/v.           (11.193.20)
```

Its derivative cannot equal `alpha_P/v-s` for a constant Fourier mode `s`
on an interval: after multiplication by `v^2`, equality would require the
polynomial

```text
s v^2-2alpha_Pv+r a^2
```

to vanish identically, impossible when `alpha_P>0`.  The domain, Jacobian,
and phase therefore obstruct a Hermitian/transpose reflection cancellation.

Conjugation gives a different exact relation.  For real `S`,

```text
conjugate(I_P^(alpha_P)(r))
 =I_(conjugate P)^(-alpha_P)(-r).                (11.193.21)
```

It reverses `alpha_P` as well as `r`.  The physical family has fixed
`alpha_P>0`, so (11.193.21) is not an internal pairing of its negative and
positive modes.  Likewise, the finite Hermitian Abel boundary null from
(11.187.23) does not change `Delta_H` and cannot regularize either
one-sided outer series.

Finally, Fourier algebra alone supplies no sign.  For the nonphysical pure
mode

```text
f_K(u)=e(Ku),                         K in Z,
```

on integer `[1,N]`, one has

```text
I_K(r)=(N-1)1_(r=K),

mathscr M_N[f_K]=N-1.                            (11.193.22)
```

If `K` lies in `mathcal R_N`, then `mathscr O_N=0` and
`mathscr M_N+mathscr O_N=N-1`.  If `K` lies outside the roster, then
`mathscr O_N=N-1` and the same package equals `2(N-1)`.  Negating `f_K`
reverses these values.  Thus the exterior pullback, mode pairing, and finite
Abel identity do not by themselves imply cancellation or a sign.

The exact ideal targets have now become

```text
mathcal J_H^0
 =mathscr M_N[P_H^0]
  +mathscr N_N[P_H^0]+mathscr C_N[P_H^0],

mathcal J_T^0
 =mathscr M_N[P_T^0]
  +mathscr N_N[P_T^0]+mathscr C_N[P_T^0]
  +2iu_Nmathcal T_N^[N][B_(T,N)^0].             (11.193.23)
```

The next admissible theorem target is the finite carrier-plus-near package,
with `K_(near,N)` kept intact and the endpoint half-weights retained.  A
cellwise Euler or Abel composition must prove or obstruct its physical
signed estimate.  The absolutely convergent paired correction may then be
joined through (11.193.10) after its physical derivative numerator is
controlled.  The transpose endpoint atom and conditional terminal block
remain in one terminal package.  The divergent one-sided outer tails are
retired as independent proof objects.

Every `pi` in this section comes from the fixed Fourier character
`e(x)=exp(2pi i x)` and `kappa=1/(2pi i)`.  The factor `2pi k` in
(11.193.8)--(11.193.10) is the derivative of that character with respect to
`u`.  No circle, polygon, fitted constant, or plotted symmetry is inserted.

This section proves the exact exterior pullback, canonical common-cutoff
decomposition, mean-one finite near kernel, absolute convergence of the
remote pairs, the physical ideal-Hermitian endpoint obstruction to separate
one-sided sums, and the reflection and conjugation guards.  It proves no
signed carrier-plus-near or complete ideal join, physical derivative-size
bound, completed-current or `Phi_B` theorem, contact exclusion, retained
aggregate or Xi theorem, `Q209`, cofinal descendant theorem, `Lambda<=0`,
PF-infinity, RH, or prize-level conclusion.

## 11.194 Fixed-root shift tangencies and the finite Hankel obstruction

Lemma 11.22A fixes the coefficient normalization used here:

```text
F(z)=sum_(k>=0)A_k z^k/k!,

J_(d,n)(z)=sum_(j=0)^d binom(d,j)A_(n+j)z^j.    (11.194.1)
```

The first series is the exponential generating function.  This distinction
is essential below; the ordinary series `sum A_kz^k` is not the entire zeta
object.

Direct differentiation and Pascal's identity give

```text
J_(d,n)^(s)(r)
 =d!/(d-s)! sum_(j=0)^(d-s)
    binom(d-s,j)r^jA_(n+s+j),

J_(d+1,n)=J_(d,n)+zJ_(d,n+1).                  (11.194.2)
```

Let `r!=0`.  If `r` has multiplicity at least `m` in `J_(d,n)` and
multiplicity at least `m+1` in `J_(d+1,n)`, then the second identity gives

```text
J_(d,n+1)={J_(d+1,n)-J_(d,n)}/z.
```

The numerator has multiplicity at least `m` at `r`, and division by `z`
does not change that multiplicity because `r!=0`.  Thus the same root
transfers to the next equal-degree shift.  The zero-root channel is excluded:
division by `z` can lower multiplicity there.

The transfer hypothesis is conditional, not automatic.  The polar-contact
lemma proves that a multiplicity-`m` root of the degree-`d` polar derivative
forces multiplicity at least `m+1` in a negative-root hyperbolic
degree-`d+1` extension.  Only under that higher-degree hyperbolicity input may
the preceding identity be iterated.

Now suppose one fixed `r!=0` is a root of multiplicity at least `m` in
`J_(d,n)` for every `n>=0`.  Put

```text
M=m-1,        p=d-m+1,        q=-1/r.
```

Taking `s=m-1` in (11.194.2) gives the exact repeated-root recurrence

```text
epsilon_n
 :=sum_(j=0)^p binom(p,j)r^jA_(M+n+j)=0,

that is, (1+rE)^p A_(M+n)=0.                   (11.194.3)
```

With `B_n=q^(-n)A_(M+n)`, equation (11.194.3) is
`Delta^pB_n=0`.  Hence

```text
A_(M+n)=q^nP(n),       deg P<=p-1=d-m.          (11.194.4)
```

The complete all-shift hypothesis also classifies the finite prefix.  Let
`D=d/dz`.  Coefficient comparison in the exponential generating function
turns every required root jet into

```text
(1+rD)^(d-s)F^(s)=0,       0<=s<m.              (11.194.5)
```

The `s=0` equation first gives `F=e^(qz)Q` with `deg Q<=d-1`.  Since
`1+rq=0`, conjugation by `e^(qz)` gives

```text
e^(-qz)(1+rD)e^(qz)=rD.
```

The `s=m-1` equation is therefore
`D^p(D+q)^(m-1)Q=0`.  Because `q!=0`, the operator `D+q` preserves the degree
of every nonzero polynomial, and consequently

```text
F(z)=e^(qz)Q(z),       deg Q<=d-m.              (11.194.6)
```

Conversely, (11.194.6) makes every equation in (11.194.5) vanish, because
`d-s>=p` for `s<m`.  Thus (11.194.6) is the exact fixed-root
classification, not merely a necessary tail condition.

This corrects an ordinary-generating-function shortcut.  The exact positive
witness

```text
A_n=(33n^2+3n+4)/(4*10^n),       r=-10          (11.194.7)
```

has

```text
sum_(n>=0)A_nz^n
 ={1+7z/10+17z^2/200}/{(1-z/10)^3},

sum_(n>=0)A_nz^n/n!
 ={1+9z/10+33z^2/400}e^(z/10).                 (11.194.8)
```

The ordinary series has an uncancelled triple pole at `z=10`, while the
zeta-normalized exponential series is entire and has exactly the form
(11.194.6).  OGF entireness therefore cannot exclude the chain.  The
exponential-polynomial classification is the valid obstruction target.

There is also a finite obstruction, which is stronger than waiting for an
infinite chain.  Define

```text
c_p(r)=(binom(p,0),binom(p,1)r,...,r^p)^T,

mathcal H_(p+1,M+n)
 =[A_(M+n+i+j)]_(i,j=0)^p.                     (11.194.9)
```

The vector of `p+1` consecutive recurrence defects is exactly

```text
(epsilon_n,...,epsilon_(n+p))^T
 =mathcal H_(p+1,M+n)c_p(r).                    (11.194.10)
```

Since the first component of `c_p(r)` is one, `p+1` exact consecutive
recurrences force

```text
det mathcal H_(p+1,M+n)=0.                      (11.194.11)
```

This gives a finite first-boundary theorem.  Suppose `J_(d,n)` has one
nonzero root of multiplicity at least `m`, and suppose the `p=d-m+1`
consecutive upper windows

```text
J_(d+1,n),...,J_(d+1,n+p-1)
```

are negative-root hyperbolic.  Polar lifting and (11.194.2) propagate the
same multiplicity-`m` root through `J_(d,n),...,J_(d,n+p)`.  Equation
(11.194.11) then forces

```text
det mathcal H_(p+1,m-1+n)=0.
```

Consequently a nonzero determinant rules out that collision.  In
particular, at a first loss of global Jensen hyperbolicity, every fixed
higher-degree window remains hyperbolic at the boundary by closure of the
real-rooted cone.  A nonvanishing determinant of the indicated order then
excludes the degree-`d`, multiplicity-`m` first collision.  This reduction is
finite; it does not assume or require an infinite shift chain.

For quartic double roots, `d=4,m=2,p=3,M=1`.  Four consecutive quartic
tangencies at one fixed nonzero double root therefore force

```text
det[A_(n+1+i+j)]_(i,j=0)^3=H_(4,n+1)=0.
```

The certified order-four entry theorem gives `H_(4,k)(-100)>0` for every
`k>=0`, and the certified forward-invariance theorem strengthens this to

```text
H_(4,k)(lambda)>0
for every k>=0 and every lambda in [-100,0].
```

Hence no such four-shift fixed-root chain exists anywhere on that heat
interval.  Conditionally, at any fixed `lambda` in `[-100,0]`, if one
quartic double tangency at shift `n` has negative-root hyperbolic quintic
extensions at shifts `n,n+1,n+2`, polar lifting and equal-degree transfer
create the four forbidden quartic tangencies.  The starting tangency and
all three quintic hypotheses therefore cannot coexist there.

The same matrix gives a quantitative near-rigidity statement.  Without
setting `epsilon_n` to zero, normalization gives

```text
Delta^pB_n=(-1)^p q^(-n)epsilon_n.
```

If

```text
P_(p-1)(k)=sum_(s=0)^(p-1)binom(k,s)Delta^sB_0,
```

then exact Newton summation yields

```text
B_k-P_(p-1)(k)
 =sum_(j=0)^(k-p)binom(k-1-j,p-1)Delta^pB_j,

|B_k-P_(p-1)(k)|
 <=binom(k,p)max_(0<=j<=k-p)|q|^(-j)|epsilon_j|.
                                                               (11.194.12)
```

For quartic double roots the amplification is `binom(k,3)`.  Moreover,
(11.194.10) and the singular values of `mathcal H=mathcal H_(p+1,M+n)`
give

```text
max_(0<=i<=p)|epsilon_(n+i)|
 >=sigma_min(mathcal H)||c_p(r)||_2/sqrt(p+1)

 >=|det mathcal H| ||c_p(r)||_2
   /{sqrt(p+1)||mathcal H||_2^p}.                (11.194.13)
```

Thus a determinant-and-norm margin forces at least one quantitative
tangency defect in every block.

The remaining zeta-specific gap is root drift.  If row `i` is exact at
`r_i` but is tested at one reference root `r_*`, its residual is

```text
sum_(j=1)^p binom(p,j)(r_*^j-r_i^j)A_(M+n+i+j).
                                                               (11.194.14)
```

On `|r_i|,|r_*|<=R`, the elementary bound
`|r_*^j-r_i^j|<=jR^(j-1)|r_*-r_i|` converts root drift into an explicit
row error.  To turn (11.194.13)--(11.194.14) into collision exclusion on a
heat interval, one still needs a heat-uniform determinant/norm or singular
value margin, a compact root annulus excluding zero and infinity, and a
bound on adjacent-root drift.  None of those three inputs is proved here.
