## 11.195 Eventual-Hankel escape at an attained finite first boundary

Section 11.194 used an immediately available Hankel determinant.  At a true
global first boundary there is a stronger option: the common root can be
propagated arbitrarily far in the shift index before the determinant is
tested.

Retain the normalization

```text
mathcal H_(k,l)=[A_(l+i+j)]_(i,j=0)^(k-1),
H_(k,l)=det mathcal H_(k,l),
Q_(k,l)=(-1)^binom(k,2) H_(k,l).
```

The graded-kernel tail theorem has the exact quantifier order

```text
for every fixed k there exists N_k such that
Q_(k,l)(lambda)>0
for every l>=N_k and every lambda in [-100,0].       (11.195.1)
```

The threshold may depend arbitrarily on `k`.  No uniform threshold is used
in the following fixed-collision theorem.

Fix `lambda in [-100,0]`, integers `d>=2`, `n>=0`, and `2<=m<=d`.
Suppose that `J_(d,n)` has a nonzero root `r` of multiplicity at least `m`
and that

```text
J_(d+1,s) is negative-root hyperbolic for every s>=n. (11.195.2)
```

These hypotheses are inconsistent.  Indeed, polar contact lifts the
multiplicity at `r` from `J_(d,s)` to at least `m+1` in `J_(d+1,s)`.  The
identity

```text
J_(d+1,s)=J_(d,s)+zJ_(d,s+1)
```

then transfers the same multiplicity-`m` root to `J_(d,s+1)`.  Division by
`z` is harmless because `r!=0`.  Induction therefore puts that same root in
every `J_(d,s)` with `s>=n`.

Set

```text
M=m-1,       p=d-m+1,       k=p+1=d-m+2.
```

The `(m-1)`st root jet at shift `s` is the recurrence defect

```text
epsilon_s
 =sum_(j=0)^p binom(p,j)r^j A_(M+s+j)=0.             (11.195.3)
```

Choose `k` first, then its threshold `N_k`, and finally choose

```text
s_0>=max(n,N_k-M).
```

The propagated chain supplies (11.195.3) for
`s=s_0,...,s_0+p`.  By (11.194.10),

```text
mathcal H_(k,M+s_0)c_p(r)=0,
c_p(r)=(binom(p,0),binom(p,1)r,...,r^p)^T.           (11.195.4)
```

Since the first component of `c_p(r)` is one,
`H_(k,M+s_0)=0`.  But `M+s_0>=N_k`, so (11.195.1) makes the same determinant
nonzero.  This contradiction proves the fixed-collision escape theorem.
The valid quantifier sequence is

```text
fix d,m; set k=d-m+2; choose N_k; then move the shift. (11.195.5)
```

There is no exchange of `forall k` with a single uniform `N`.

Now let `lambda_*` be an attained boundary value approached from a side on
which every shifted Jensen polynomial is negative-root hyperbolic.  For each
fixed degree and shift, coefficient continuity and closure of the
real-rooted cone preserve hyperbolicity at `lambda_*`.  If a fixed
`J_(d,n)(lambda_*)` had a multiple root, its positive constant coefficient
would exclude zero, and all the upper windows required by (11.195.2) would
be available.  The fixed-collision theorem gives a contradiction.  Thus an
attained global boundary cannot be witnessed by any fixed finite-degree,
finite-shift collision.

This conclusion does not supply the missing attainment or compactness.  A
loss may still escape through unbounded degree, unbounded shift, or another
non-attained limiting regime.  The independent polar degree-axis cascade
reaches the same warning in a different direction: a fixed finite collision
under all higher-degree hyperbolicity forces an exponential-polynomial
source, so a non-exponential-polynomial boundary can only be approached by
failing degrees that escape to infinity.

The effective determinant inventory should not be confused with this
unlimited-shift theorem.  In the degree-20 indexing audit there are `190`
degree/multiplicity pairs.  If only the immediate block from Section 11.194
is allowed, `139` rows have effective all-shift determinant coverage, `6`
have coverage only after a finite shift floor, and `45` have no effective
immediate-block theorem.  With unlimited first-boundary shift propagation,
all `190` rows are covered by (11.195.1), and the symbolic proof applies to
every fixed finite degree.

Order ten illustrates why the distinction matters.  The certified signs

```text
Q_(10,l)(-100)<0<Q_(10,l)(0),       l=0,1,2,3,
```

force four low determinant sensors to vanish somewhere in the interval.
A Hankel determinant zero is not by itself a Jensen collision.  At an
attained first boundary, an actual common-root chain can be moved beyond
`N_10`, where the determinant is nonzero.  Order twelve likewise remains
open for the effective all-shift signed-Hankel programme, but its completion
is not required for this non-effective fixed-order escape implication.

The prize-level successor is therefore not another isolated fixed-order
determinant calculation.  It is a cofinal compactness or scaled-limit
theorem showing that any putative loss relevant to `Lambda<=0` must produce
one attained finite collision, or otherwise excluding every possible
degree/shift escape.  The thresholds `N_k` may diverge arbitrarily fast, and
the present argument gives no control when `k` itself tends to infinity.

This section introduces no `pi`.  Its inputs are binomial identities,
polar multiplicity, Hankel rank, continuity, and quantifier order.

This section proves the fixed-order eventual-Hankel escape theorem and
excludes attained finite-degree, finite-shift first collisions under the

## 11.196 Arbitrary-multiplicity cofinal Jensen boundary layer

The preceding section identifies fixed finite collisions.  A hypothetical
positive Newman boundary has a different, already-attained source.  The
positive-boundary compactness theorem gives

```text
Lambda>0
 => H_Lambda has a finite real zero c of multiplicity m>=2. (11.196.1)
```

Here `c!=0` because `H_Lambda(0)>0`.  Under the coefficient coordinate

```text
F_(0,t)(s)=sum_(j>=0)A_j(t)s^j/j!=2H_t(i sqrt(s)),
```

the zero becomes

```text
rho=-c^2<0,
F_(0,Lambda)(s)=(s-rho)^m U(s),       U(rho)!=0.   (11.196.2)
```

Thus the prize-relevant Jensen sequence can be kept at the single shift
`n=0`.  The limiting issue is degree, not shift.

For a general fixed shift `n`, write

```text
F_(n,lambda)(z)=sum_(j>=0)A_(n+j)(lambda)z^j/j!,

P_(D,n,lambda)(z)
 =J_(D,n,lambda)(z/D)
 =sum_(j=0)^D (D)_j/D^j A_(n+j)(lambda)z^j/j!.
                                                               (11.196.3)
```

The scaled Jensen map has the exact differential-operator form

```text
P_(D,n,lambda)(z)
 =[(1+(z/D)partial_x)^D F_(n,lambda)(x)]_(x=0).
                                                               (11.196.4)
```

Translate the evaluation point from zero to `z`.  Since all operators have
constant coefficients,

```text
e^(-z partial_x)(1+(z/D)partial_x)^D
 =exp(
    -z^2 partial_x^2/(2D)
    +sum_(r>=3)(-1)^(r+1)z^r partial_x^r/(rD^(r-1))
   ).                                                          (11.196.5)
```

Put

```text
lambda=lambda_*+tau/D,
z=rho+eta/sqrt(D).
```

On this scale, `partial_z=sqrt(D)partial_eta`.  The quadratic term in
(11.196.5) tends to `-(rho^2/2)partial_eta^2`, while its term of order
`r>=3` is `O(D^(1-r/2))` and vanishes on compact `eta` sets.  The exact
coefficient heat equation

```text
partial_lambda F_n
 =(4n+2)partial_z F_n+4z partial_z^2 F_n             (11.196.6)
```

similarly tends to `4rho tau partial_eta^2`; its shift-dependent drift is
only `O(D^(-1/2))`.  Taylor truncation on a larger compact disk and Cauchy
bounds justify both operator limits.  Their constant-coefficient leading
operators commute.

Consequently, if

```text
F_(n,lambda_*)(z)=(z-rho)^m U(z),       U(rho)!=0,
```

then locally uniformly in `eta`,

```text
D^(m/2)
 J_(D,n,lambda_*+tau/D)((rho+eta/sqrt(D))/D)/U(rho)
 -> K_(m,a)(eta),

a=4rho tau-rho^2/2,

K_(m,a)(eta)
 =exp(a partial_eta^2)eta^m
 =m! sum_(q=0)^floor(m/2)
      a^q eta^(m-2q)/[q!(m-2q)!].                  (11.196.7)
```

This is the arbitrary-multiplicity cofinal Jensen layer.  For
`a=-sigma^2/2<0`,

```text
K_(m,a)(eta)=sigma^m He_m(eta/sigma),              (11.196.8)
```

so the local cluster has `m` simple real roots.  For `a=beta^2/2>0`,

```text
K_(m,a)(eta)=(i beta)^m He_m(eta/(i beta)),         (11.196.9)
```

so every `m>=2` has a nonreal conjugate pair; when `m` is odd, only the
central root remains real.

The transition occurs at

```text
a=0 iff tau=rho/8.                                 (11.196.10)
```

Indeed, for any `epsilon>0`, the limits at
`tau_+=rho/8+epsilon` and `tau_-=rho/8-epsilon` have respectively simple
real and nonreal local root patterns because `rho<0`.  Uniform Rouche
counting isolates exactly `m` finite roots in the scaled cluster.  Continuous
dependence on the real heat parameter then forces a multiple real root
between the two values.  A diagonal choice `epsilon->0` gives degrees
`D_j->infinity`, collision parameters `lambda_j`, and collision roots `w_j`
such that

```text
D_j(lambda_j-lambda_*) -> rho/8,
D_j^(3/2)(w_j-rho/D_j) -> 0.                       (11.196.11)
```

Equivalently,

```text
lambda_j=lambda_*+rho/(8D_j)+o(D_j^(-1)),
w_j=rho/D_j+o(D_j^(-3/2)).                          (11.196.12)
```

The explicit `D^(-2)` parameter correction and `D^(-2)` root-center
coefficient in the earlier scaled double-zero gate remain specific to its
nondegenerate quadratic calculation.  They are not imported here.

Applying (11.196.11) to (11.196.2) gives the conditional Newman theorem

```text
Lambda>0
 => there exist D_j->infinity and unshifted Jensen collisions with

t_j=Lambda-c^2/(8D_j)+o(D_j^(-1)),
D_j^(3/2)(w_j+c^2/D_j) -> 0.                       (11.196.13)
```

This removes two avoidable assumptions from the cofinal route: the boundary
zero need not be double, and the Jensen shift need not escape.  It also
explains why bounded-degree results do not close the problem.  The uniform
positive-time sector theorem through degree `361` is exact, but every
sequence in (11.196.13) eventually lies above that cutoff.

Nor can the fixed-order Hankel tail from Section 11.195 be promoted here.
Its certified interval is `[-100,0]`, while a hypothetical positive Newman
boundary lies in `(0,1/5]`.  Even a positive-time extension proved
separately for every fixed order would leave the following quantifier
obstruction.  If a finite collision in the isolated cluster has multiplicity
`mu_j`, then
`2<=mu_j<=m`, and its Section 11.194 determinant order is

```text
k_j=D_j-mu_j+2 -> infinity.                        (11.196.14)
```

The quantifiers have changed: one now needs control uniform in growing
determinant or Jensen degree.  Choosing one threshold `N_k` after fixing one
finite `k` does not address (11.196.14).

The live Jensen-side theorem is therefore an Xi-specific estimate uniform in
degree throughout the layer (11.196.13), strong enough to exclude the local
nonreal-to-real transition.  The independent first-jet boundary-winding
programme remains an alternative that attacks the entire-function contact
directly.

For `m=2`, equation (11.196.7) is

```text
eta^2+8rho tau-rho^2,
```

exactly reproducing the earlier double-zero layer.  The machine companion
checks the coefficient and Hermite identities through multiplicity `16` and

Those finite audits check the algebra; arbitrary `m` follows from the
operator limit and the closed sum in (11.196.7).

This section introduces no `pi`.  The identity `rho=-c^2` is the algebraic
map `s=-z^2`; separate Xi kernel estimates carry their own `pi`

This section proves the arbitrary-multiplicity local layer and, conditional

## 11.197 Secondary cubic layer at a multiple Jensen contact

Section 11.196 locates the first cofinal collision scale, but its limiting
polynomial is `eta^m` at the critical value `tau=rho/8`.  For `m>=3` that
root is too degenerate for an ordinary first-order perturbation.  The next
scale is fractional and remains universal.

Put

```text
h=D^(-1/2),
F_(n,lambda_*)(rho+h eta)=h^m U(rho)[eta^m+O(h eta^(m+1))].
                                                               (11.197.1)
```

In the `eta` coordinate, the scaled radial heat generator is

```text
L_n
 =h^(-2) A_0+h^(-1) A_1,

A_0=4rho partial_eta^2,
A_1=4eta partial_eta^2+(4n+2)partial_eta.          (11.197.2)
```

The first Duhamel correction to `exp(tau A_0)` is

```text
integral_0^tau exp(-sA_0)A_1exp(sA_0) ds
 =4tau eta partial_eta^2+(4n+2)tau partial_eta
  -16rho tau^2 partial_eta^3.                      (11.197.3)
```

Indeed,
`exp(-sA_0) eta exp(sA_0)=eta-8rho s partial_eta`.
The order-`h` part of the translated finite-Jensen logarithm from
(11.196.5) is

```text
-rho eta partial_eta^2+(rho^3/3)partial_eta^3.     (11.197.4)
```

At `tau_0=rho/8`, the leading heat operator
`exp((rho^2/2)partial_eta^2)` cancels the leading finite-Jensen operator
`exp(-(rho^2/2)partial_eta^2)`.  Combining (11.197.3) and (11.197.4), the
remaining order-`h` operator is

```text
B_1
 =-(rho/2)eta partial_eta^2
  +[rho(2n+1)/4]partial_eta
  +(rho^3/12)partial_eta^3.                        (11.197.5)
```

The cubic coefficient is therefore

```text
rho^3/3-rho^3/4=rho^3/12.                         (11.197.6)
```

This coefficient is not a truncation artifact.  Set

```text
epsilon=D^(-1/6),

lambda
 =lambda_*+rho epsilon^6/8+(rho q/4)epsilon^8,

z=rho+rho y epsilon^4.                             (11.197.7)
```

Equivalently, `h=epsilon^3`, `eta=rho epsilon y`, and the Jensen
polynomial is evaluated at `z/D`.  On this scale,

```text
4rho(tau-tau_0)partial_eta^2 -> q partial_y^2,

h(rho^3/12)partial_eta^3 -> (1/12)partial_y^3.     (11.197.8)
```

Every power of the cubic derivative has the same graded size and must be
exponentiated.  The other two terms in (11.197.5), the fourth and higher
finite-Jensen logarithmic terms, and the next variable-coefficient heat
commutators have positive graded weight and vanish in the present limit.
Taylor truncation on a larger compact disk and Cauchy bounds give local
uniformity exactly as in Section 11.196.  Hence, for every `m>=3`,

```text
epsilon^(-4m)
 J_(D,n,lambda)((rho+rho y epsilon^4)/D)
 /[rho^m U(rho)]

 -> P_m(y,q)
 :=exp(q partial_y^2+partial_y^3/12)y^m.            (11.197.9)
```

The polynomial is explicit:

```text
P_m(y,q)
 =m! sum_(2r+3s<=m)
   q^r y^(m-2r-3s)
   /[r!s!12^s(m-2r-3s)!].                         (11.197.10)
```

Neither the fixed shift `n` nor a logarithmic derivative of the local unit
`U` occurs in (11.197.9).  This is the secondary cubic Jensen layer.

Its real-root transition is itself one-dimensional.  Since the derivative
operators commute,

```text
P_m(y,q-s)=exp(-s partial_y^2)P_m(y,q),   s>=0.     (11.197.11)
```

The operator `exp(-s partial_y^2)` preserves real-rooted polynomials.  A
self-contained finite-degree proof follows from

```text
exp(-s partial_y^2)
 =lim_(N->infinity)(1-s partial_y^2/N)^N
 =lim_(N->infinity)
   [(1-sqrt(s/N)partial_y)(1+sqrt(s/N)partial_y)]^N.
                                                               (11.197.12)
```

For a real-rooted polynomial, its derivative interlaces it, so each real
first-order operator `1+a partial_y` preserves real-rootedness.  Apply this
to every finite product in (11.197.12) and pass to the coefficientwise
limit.

The hyperbolicity set is nonempty.  If `q=-R`, set
`y=sqrt(2R)x`; after monic normalization,

```text
(2R)^(-m/2)P_m(sqrt(2R)x,-R)
 -> exp(-partial_x^2/2)x^m=He_m(x)                 (11.197.13)
```

as `R->infinity`.  The Hermite roots are simple and real, so root
continuity makes `P_m(.,-R)` hyperbolic for all sufficiently large `R`.

The value `q=0` is not hyperbolic.  In `P_m(y,0)`, the coefficients of
`y^(m-1)` and `y^(m-2)` vanish, while

```text
[y^(m-3)]P_m(y,0)=m!/[12(m-3)!]!=0.               (11.197.14)
```

If all roots were real, the first two vanishing elementary symmetric sums
would give `sum_j r_j=0`, `sum_(i<j)r_i r_j=0`, and therefore
`sum_j r_j^2=0`.  Every root would be zero, contradicting (11.197.14).

Closedness, (11.197.11), (11.197.13), and (11.197.14) therefore prove that
there is a finite constant

```text
q_m<0 such that

P_m(.,q) is hyperbolic iff q<=q_m.                 (11.197.15)
```

At `q=q_m`, the polynomial has a real multiple root `y_m`; otherwise its
simple real roots would persist for slightly larger `q`.  Local-uniform
root continuity on two sides of `q_m`, followed by the same diagonal
argument as in Section 11.196, now refines the finite collision sequence:

```text
lambda_D
 =lambda_*+rho/(8D)+(rho q_m/4)D^(-4/3)
  +o(D^(-4/3)),

w_D
 =rho/D+rho y_m D^(-5/3)+o(D^(-5/3)).              (11.197.16)
```

Here and below `D` denotes a selected cofinal degree sequence, not every
sufficiently large degree.  Since `rho<0` and `q_m<0`, the new parameter
coefficient `rho q_m/4` is positive.  Under `Lambda>0` and `rho=-c^2`, the
secondary correction therefore moves the finite collision toward `Lambda`
relative to the primary approximation `Lambda-c^2/(8D)`; it does not cross
or contradict the boundary.

For multiplicity three the threshold is exact:

```text
P_3(y,q)=y^3+6qy+1/2,

Disc_y P_3=-(27/4)(128q^3+1),

q_3=-2^(-7/3),
y_3=2^(-2/3),

(rho q_3/4)D^(-4/3)
 =-rho 2^(-13/3)D^(-4/3).                         (11.197.17)
```

Multiplicity two is genuinely different: `partial_y^3 y^2=0`, so the
secondary cubic layer disappears.  Its first external-field correction is
the existing `D^(-2)` term from the scaled double-zero gate.

The graded bookkeeping also locates where source-specific information can
first enter:

```text
secondary cubic and q diffusion:       epsilon^0,
shift drift and fourth-order operators: epsilon^2=D^(-1/3),
local unit U'(rho)/U(rho):              epsilon^4=D^(-2/3).
                                                               (11.197.18)
```

Thus the attempted first refinement supplies no Xi-specific sign.  The
`D^(-1/3)` correction should be calculated next, but it may still be
universal; the first local Xi jet is delayed until `D^(-2/3)`.  Even that
jet would need a degree-uniform remainder estimate before it could exclude
(11.197.16).

The first-jet winding theorem is compatible with this result but does not
close it.  Every entire-function contact has positive local index
`floor(m/2)`, whereas (11.197.9) resolves the associated finite-Jensen root
cluster.  A global contradiction still requires zero boundary winding for
the Xi first jet, or an independent degree-uniform coefficient estimate.

The exact companion checks `200` symbolic coefficients through multiplicity

This section introduces no `pi`.  The number `1/12` is the rational cubic
operator difference in (11.197.6), not a circle normalization.

threshold `q_m`, the refined cofinal collision scales, and the exact

## 11.198 Tertiary universal transport and the first Xi-jet entry

The scale in Section 11.197 can be continued by one graded step.  Retain
`m>=3`, put `epsilon=D^(-1/6)`, and set

```text
lambda
 =lambda_*+rho epsilon^6/8
  +(rho q/4)epsilon^8+(rho r/4)epsilon^10,

z=rho+rho y epsilon^4.                              (11.198.1)
```

As before, the Jensen polynomial is evaluated at `z/D`.  Define its
normalized local cluster by

```text
mathcal J_D(y;q,r)
 =epsilon^(-4m)
  J_(D,n,lambda)((rho+rho y epsilon^4)/D)
  /[rho^m U(rho)].                                  (11.198.2)
```

Expanding the exact translated Jensen operator (11.196.5) and the exact
radial heat equation (11.196.6) two graded powers beyond (11.197.9) gives,
locally uniformly for bounded `y`, `q`, and `r`,

```text
mathcal J_D(y;q,r)
 =P_m(y,q)+epsilon^2 Q_(m,n)(y,q,r)+O(epsilon^4),   (11.198.3)

Q_(m,n)
 =[(r-y/2)partial_y^2+(2n+1)partial_y/4]P_m.
                                                               (11.198.4)
```

Here `Q_(m,n)` is the local tertiary correction in this section; it is not
the signed Hankel minor denoted by `Q` in Sections 11.46--11.195.

For completeness, (11.198.4) can be verified without formal operator
shorthand.  In each term of (11.197.10), put `k=m-2a-3b`.  Direct
coefficient extraction from the falling-factorial Jensen multiplier and
the radial heat exponential gives

```text
Q_(m,n)(y,q,r)
 =m! sum_(2a+3b<=m)
   q^a/[a!b!12^b k!]
   {
     r k(k-1)y^(k-2)
     +k[(2n+1)/4-(k-1)/2]y^(k-1)
   },

k=m-2a-3b,                                         (11.198.5)
```

with terms containing a negative power of `y` omitted because their
falling coefficient is zero.  Applying `partial_y` and `partial_y^2` to
(11.197.10) turns (11.198.5) exactly into (11.198.4), proving the identity
for every fixed `m`.

The three pieces in (11.198.4) have separate origins.  The next heat
parameter in (11.198.1) contributes `r partial_y^2`.  Under
`h=epsilon^3` and `eta=rho epsilon y`, the first two terms of (11.197.5)
become

```text
epsilon^2[-(y/2)partial_y^2+(2n+1)partial_y/4].     (11.198.6)
```

The cubic term in (11.197.5) has already been exponentiated into `P_m`.
Normal ordering the fourth-order Jensen term and the second heat-commutator
terms against that cubic exponential produces the finite sum (11.198.5):
their apparent independent `partial_y^4` contributions cancel or recombine,
and no `partial_y^4 P_m` term remains.  Taylor truncation on a larger disk
and Cauchy bounds, as in Sections 11.196--11.197, control the
`O(epsilon^4)` remainder for each fixed `m`.  This is not a bound uniform in
the Jensen degree.

The universal family also obeys the two Appell identities

```text
partial_q P_m=partial_y^2 P_m,
partial_y P_(m+1)=(m+1)P_m.                        (11.198.7)
```

The first follows by differentiating the heat exponential, and the second
by commuting `partial_y` through both constant-coefficient exponentials.

Now suppose that the threshold polynomial `P_m(.,q_m)` has a
nondegenerate double root `y_m`:

```text
P_m(y_m,q_m)=partial_y P_m(y_m,q_m)=0,
partial_y^2 P_m(y_m,q_m)!=0.                       (11.198.8)
```

This condition is not asserted for every `m`.  Seek the next collision at
`r=r_m` and `y=y_m+s_m epsilon^2+o(epsilon^2)`.  The value equation at
order `epsilon^2` is

```text
0=Q_(m,n)(y_m,q_m,r_m)
  =(r_m-y_m/2)partial_y^2 P_m(y_m,q_m),             (11.198.9)
```

so `r_m=y_m/2`.  Differentiating (11.198.3), the corresponding derivative
equation is

```text
0=s_m partial_y^2 P_m+partial_y Q_(m,n)
  =[s_m+(2n-1)/4]partial_y^2 P_m,                  (11.198.10)
```

all quantities being evaluated at `(y_m,q_m,r_m)`.  Therefore

```text
r_m=y_m/2,
s_m=(1-2n)/4.                                      (11.198.11)
```

For `m=3`, (11.197.17) gives a nondegenerate contact and hence

```text
q_3=-2^(-7/3),       y_3=2^(-2/3),
r_3=2^(-5/3),        s_3=(1-2n)/4.                 (11.198.12)
```

Along the selected cofinal collision sequence this yields

```text
lambda_D
 =lambda_*+rho/(8D)
  -rho 2^(-13/3)D^(-4/3)
  +rho 2^(-11/3)D^(-5/3)+o(D^(-5/3)),

w_D
 =rho/D+rho 2^(-2/3)D^(-5/3)
  +rho(1-2n)D^(-2)/4+o(D^(-2)).                   (11.198.13)
```

The coefficient `rho(1-2n)/4` exactly matches the root-center correction
from the independent double-zero calculation, although the earlier
fractional scales differ.  At the Newman shift `n=0`, with `rho=-c^2`,
(11.198.13) becomes

```text
t_D
 =Lambda-c^2/(8D)
  +c^2 2^(-13/3)D^(-4/3)
  -c^2 2^(-11/3)D^(-5/3)+o(D^(-5/3)).             (11.198.14)
```

The calculation also locates the first source-specific term.  Write

```text
U(rho+u)/U(rho)=1+u_1 u+O(u^2),
u_1=U'(rho)/U(rho).
```

The coefficient of `u_1 epsilon^4` in the normalized cluster is exactly

```text
[u_1 epsilon^4] mathcal J_D
 =rho P_(m+1)(y,q).                                (11.198.15)
```

Thus the local unit is absent from (11.198.4), while its first linear
contribution is
`rho[U'(rho)/U(rho)]P_(m+1)(y,q)` at relative order
`epsilon^4=D^(-2/3)`.  Equation (11.198.15) is only the Xi-dependent piece
of that order.  The same order also contains a universal background, the
next heat parameter, and the next root displacement.  Until their complete

The exact companion constructs `P_m` and (11.198.4) for multiplicities

No `pi` enters this calculation.  The constants in (11.198.12)--(11.198.14)
are rational powers of two from the exact cubic discriminant; `rho`, `q_m`,
and `y_m` are the displayed algebraic local data, not circle
normalizations.

## 11.199 Complete first-Xi-jet layer and its local sign obstruction

The first source-dependent term identified in (11.198.15) occurs together
with a universal correction of the same size.  Both can be calculated
without truncating the cubic Appell exponential.  Extend (11.198.1) to

```text
lambda
 =lambda_*+rho epsilon^6/8
  +(rho q/4)epsilon^8+(rho r/4)epsilon^10
  +(rho v/4)epsilon^12,

epsilon=D^(-1/6),       z=rho+rho y epsilon^4.      (11.199.1)
```

Let

```text
E=exp(q partial_y^2+partial_y^3/12),
P_m=E y^m,

A_(n,r)
 =(r-y/2)partial_y^2+(2n+1)partial_y/4,

ell=rho U'(rho)/U(rho).                            (11.199.2)
```

For the normalized cluster `mathcal J_D` from (11.198.2), exact graded
coefficient extraction gives, locally uniformly for fixed `m` and bounded
parameters,

```text
mathcal J_D
 =P_m+epsilon^2 A_(n,r)P_m
  +epsilon^4{R_(n,q,r,v)P_m+ell P_(m+1)}
  +O(epsilon^6),                                   (11.199.3)
```

where `A^2` below means operator composition and

```text
R P
 =v P''+(A^2 P)/2
  +[q(2n+1)/2]P'
  +[q y+(2n+1)/8]P''
  +(q^2+r/2)P'''
  +(q/4)P''''
  +(1/80)P'''''.                                   (11.199.4)
```

There are two useful checks on (11.199.4).  First, remove the next heat
term `vP''`, the exponential contribution `A^2P/2`, and the local unit.
Conjugating the remaining universal operator back through `E` gives the
finite monomial-frame identity

```text
E^(-1){R P_m-vP_m''-(A^2P_m)/2}
 =[
    q(2n+1)partial_y/2
    +(q y+(2n+1)/8)partial_y^2
    +(r/2-q^2)partial_y^3
    +partial_y^5/80
  ]y^m.                                             (11.199.5)
```

Second,

```text
E y E^(-1)=y+2q partial_y+partial_y^2/4.             (11.199.6)
```

Substitution of (11.199.6) into (11.199.5) changes the cubic coefficient
from `r/2-q^2` to `r/2+q^2`, creates the `q partial_y^4/4` term, and gives
(11.199.4).  Thus the rational `1/80` is the surviving fifth-order
normal-order coefficient; it is not numerical fitting.

The source-specific term follows separately.  Write

```text
F_(n,lambda_*)(rho+u)
 =U(rho)[u^m+u_1 u^(m+1)+O(u^(m+2))],

u_1=U'(rho)/U(rho).
```

The additional power of `u` costs exactly `rho epsilon^4` on the local
scale, while its leading Appell image is `P_(m+1)`.  This proves the term
`ell P_(m+1)` in (11.199.3).  Terms involving `U''` occur later.  The
remaining contributions in (11.199.3) depend only on the universal heat
and Jensen operators.

For multiplicity three, continue the exact contact from Sections
11.197--11.198.  Put

```text
q_3=-2^(-7/3),       y_3=2^(-2/3),
r_3=2^(-5/3),        s_3=(1-2n)/4,

y=y_3+s_3 epsilon^2+t_3 epsilon^4+o(epsilon^4).
                                                               (11.199.7)
```

At order `epsilon^4`, the value and derivative equations are

```text
0=(s_3^2/2)P_3''+s_3(A P_3)'
  +R P_3+ell P_4,

0=t_3P_3''+(s_3^2/2)P_3'''
  +s_3(A P_3)''+(R P_3+ell P_4)'.                  (11.199.8)
```

Every quantity in (11.199.8) is evaluated at `(y_3,q_3,r_3)`.  Since
`P_3''(y_3,q_3)!=0`, the equations solve uniquely:

```text
v_3=-(2ell+3n+2)/8,
t_3=2^(-7/3)(2ell+n+4).                            (11.199.9)
```

Consequently the selected cofinal collision sequence has

```text
lambda_D
 =lambda_*+rho/(8D)
  -rho 2^(-13/3)D^(-4/3)
  +rho 2^(-11/3)D^(-5/3)
  -rho(2ell+3n+2)D^(-2)/32+o(D^(-2)),

w_D
 =rho/D+rho 2^(-2/3)D^(-5/3)
  +rho(1-2n)D^(-2)/4
  +rho 2^(-7/3)(2ell+n+4)D^(-7/3)
  +o(D^(-7/3)).                                   (11.199.10)
```

At the unshifted Newman specialization `n=0`, `rho=-c^2`, this gives

```text
t_D
 =Lambda-c^2/(8D)
  +c^2 2^(-13/3)D^(-4/3)
  -c^2 2^(-11/3)D^(-5/3)
  +c^2(ell+1)D^(-2)/16+o(D^(-2)).                 (11.199.11)
```

Equation (11.199.11) is the first source-dependent refinement, but it is
not a contradiction.  Its coefficient is a regular zero field.  Indeed,
at an all-real boundary the `s`-coordinate function has order `1/2` and a
genus-zero product.  If its distinct zeros are `rho_j<0` with
multiplicities `mu_j`, then at a multiplicity-`m` zero `rho_k`,

```text
U'(rho_k)/U(rho_k)
 =F^(m+1)(rho_k)/[(m+1)F^(m)(rho_k)]
 =sum_(j!=k) mu_j/(rho_k-rho_j),

ell_k
 =rho_k sum_(j!=k) mu_j/(rho_k-rho_j).             (11.199.12)
```

Terms from zeros on opposite sides of `rho_k` have opposite signs.  This
is not merely a logical possibility.  At `rho=-1`, both

```text
F_-(s)=(s+1)^3(s+4),       ell=-1/3,
F_+(s)=(s+1)^3(s+1/4),     ell=4/3                 (11.199.13)
```

have only negative zeros and strictly positive coefficients.  Thus local
Laguerre--Polya geometry, negative-rootedness, and coefficient positivity
do not determine the sign of `ell` at an interior multiple root.  Moving a
neighboring simple zero arbitrarily close on either side also makes the
corresponding sign arbitrarily large in magnitude.

The exact companion verifies (11.199.4) at shifts zero and three through
multiplicity `16`.  It then evolves `12` finite polynomial sources with
free `rho,q,r,v,u_1` under the exact radial heat generator and exact
falling-factorial Jensen map.  An independent checker uses separate
rational data, computes every model both with and without the local unit,
and recovers the complete background and `ell P_(m+1)` separately.  It
also reconstructs (11.199.9) and both sign countermodels.

The next local obligation is no longer an unspecified Taylor coefficient.
It is an Xi-specific bound on the regular field (11.199.12), using the
location and dynamics of the hypothetical boundary zero relative to all
other Xi zeros.  Even such a bound must be paired with an analytic
remainder uniform along the selected degree sequence.  The independent
zero-boundary-winding theorem remains the alternative global route.

No `pi` enters this local operator calculation.  In particular, `1/80`
comes from exact fifth-order Jensen/heat normal ordering.  Pi appears only
in the separate Fourier normalization of the Xi kernel.

This section proves the complete fixed-m first-Xi-jet layer, the exact
multiplicity-three source-dependent collision displacement, the
genus-zero regular-field identity, and the local sign countermodels.  It
proves no bound on the actual Xi field `ell`, no degree-uniform remainder,
no Xi-specific collision exclusion, all-degree Jensen hyperbolicity,
PF-infinity, `Lambda<=0`, RH, or prize-level conclusion.

## 11.200 First-loss dynamics does not constrain the regular zero field

Section 11.199 reduced the first source-dependent Jensen correction to

```text
ell=rho U'(rho)/U(rho).                              (11.200.1)
```

The two sign examples there leave open a sharper possibility: perhaps the
fact that the source is attained at a first heat-flow loss restricts `ell`,
even though static Laguerre--Polya geometry does not.  The answer is no for
every local condition shared by the following exact models.

Fix an arbitrary real number `ell`, a height `c>0`, and an integer `m>=2`.
Set

```text
A=ell^2+2,
B=ell^2-ell+2=(ell-1/2)^2+7/4,

alpha=1-1/A,
beta =1+1/B.                                        (11.200.2)
```

Then `A>1`, `B>0`, and

```text
0<alpha<1<beta.                                     (11.200.3)
```

Define the finite genus-zero product

```text
F_(m,ell,c)(s)
 =(s+c^2)^m(s+alpha c^2)(s+beta c^2).               (11.200.4)
```

All its zeros are negative and every coefficient is strictly positive.  At
the multiplicity-`m` zero `rho=-c^2`, write

```text
F_(m,ell,c)(s)=(s-rho)^m U(s).
```

The simple zero between `rho` and zero contributes `A` to the regular
field, while the simple zero below `rho` contributes `-B`:

```text
rho/[rho-(-alpha c^2)]= A,
rho/[rho-(-beta  c^2)]=-B.
```

Consequently,

```text
rho U'(rho)/U(rho)=A-B=ell.                         (11.200.5)
```

Thus every finite real value, rather than merely both signs, occurs in an
all-negative-root positive-coefficient product.

The construction also has an exact first-loss heat interpretation.  Lift
it to the even real-rooted polynomial

```text
H_(m,ell,c)(x)=F_(m,ell,c)(-x^2),
H_tau=exp(-tau partial_x^2)H_(m,ell,c).              (11.200.6)
```

The points `+c` and `-c` are both roots of multiplicity `m`.  For every
`tau>=0`, Section 11.197's factorization gives

```text
exp(-tau partial_x^2)
 =lim_(N->infinity)
  [(1-sqrt(tau/N)partial_x)(1+sqrt(tau/N)partial_x)]^N.
                                                               (11.200.7)
```

Each real first-order factor preserves real-rootedness, and the degree and
leading coefficient remain fixed in the coefficientwise limit.  Hence
`H_tau` is real-rooted for every `tau>=0`.

To inspect the other side, factor locally

```text
H_(m,ell,c)(x)=(x-c)^m V(x),       V(c)!=0,
B_c=V'(c)/V(c).
```

The change `s=-x^2` and (11.200.5) give the exact conversion

```text
B_c=m/(2c)-2c U'(rho)/U(rho)
   =(m+4ell)/(2c).                                  (11.200.8)
```

For positive time, put `x=c+sqrt(tau)z`.  Locally uniformly on bounded
`z`-sets,

```text
tau^(-m/2)H_tau(c+sqrt(tau)z)/V(c)
 =P_m^-(z)+sqrt(tau)B_c P_(m+1)^-(z)+O(tau),

P_m^-(z)=exp(-partial_z^2)z^m
        =2^(m/2)He_m(z/sqrt(2)).                    (11.200.9)
```

The `m` roots `h_j` of `P_m^-` are simple and real.  The exact recurrence

```text
P_(m+1)^-=zP_m^--2(P_m^-)'                          (11.200.10)
```

shows that the first perturbation of every root is the same.  Therefore

```text
x_j(tau)
 =c+sqrt(tau)h_j+2B_c tau+O(tau^(3/2)).             (11.200.11)
```

The arbitrary regular field changes the common cluster drift, but not the
real-rooted side of the contact.  In the multiplicity-three case relevant
to Section 11.199,

```text
B_c=(3+4ell)/(2c).                                  (11.200.12)
```

For negative time write `tau=-sigma`, `sigma>0`.  The opposite parabolic
limit is

```text
sigma^(-m/2)H_(-sigma)(c+sqrt(sigma)z)/V(c)
 ->P_m^+(z)=exp(partial_z^2)z^m
   =sum_(k=0)^floor(m/2)
      m! z^(m-2k)/[k!(m-2k)!].                     (11.200.13)
```

If `m` is even, (11.200.13) is a strictly positive polynomial in `z^2`
and has no real zero.  If `m` is odd, it is `z` times a strictly positive
polynomial in `z^2` and has only the real zero zero.  Equivalently it is an
imaginary rescaling of `He_m`, so all its roots are simple.  Root continuity
therefore gives a nonreal pair in `H_(-sigma)` for every sufficiently small
positive `sigma`.

This is the exact first boundary, not merely a one-sided local example.  If
`H_tau` were real-rooted at some `tau_0<0`, applying the preserver
(11.200.7) from `tau_0` would make it real-rooted at every later time,
contradicting the negative-time local split.  Thus

```text
H_tau is real-rooted iff tau>=0.                    (11.200.14)
```

Equations (11.200.2)--(11.200.14) prove a local nonclosure theorem.  Evenness,
finite genus-zero negative-root geometry, positive `s`-coefficients,
backward-heat evolution, and attainment at an exact Newman-style first loss
impose no sign, finite interval, or one-sided bound on `ell`.  In particular,
first-loss dynamics cannot turn the Section 11.199 coefficient into a
collision contradiction.  It only changes the collision displacement, as
the common drift (11.200.11) already predicts.

This theorem does not make the actual Xi field arbitrary.  A useful bound
must use structure absent from (11.200.4): the theta/Fourier source, global
Xi zero placement, or zero first-jet winding on the cofinal half-rectangles.
The Jensen route independently still needs a Cauchy or Xi-integral remainder
uniform along its selected degree sequence.  These are now the two live
obligations; another purely local heat-jet inequality cannot close them.

The exact companion checks ten rational prescribed fields, including zero
and both signs, and positive coefficients, negative roots, signed-field
conversion, and ten fully evolved positive-time polynomials.  An independent
checker reconstructs those models.  Both programs separately verify the
forward Hermite and backward nonreal root counts for every multiplicity from
`2` through `16`; the closed formulas above prove arbitrary fixed `m`.

No `pi` enters this construction.  The two auxiliary root locations are
rational functions of `ell`; pi remains confined to the separate Xi
Fourier/theta normalization where it actually originates.

This section proves the arbitrary-field exact first-loss countermodel family,
the all-multiplicity field-to-drift formula, and the resulting local
nonclosure theorem.  It proves no bound on the actual Xi field, no
degree-uniform Jensen remainder, no Xi-specific collision exclusion,
all-degree Jensen hyperbolicity, PF-infinity, `Lambda<=0`, RH, or prize-level
conclusion.

## 11.201 Fourier and score coordinates do not close the regular field

Section 11.200 shows that generic local first-loss dynamics does not bound
the regular field.  The next question is whether positivity of the Fourier
kernel, or even strong shape control of that kernel, closes the gap.  First
put the actual Xi field into exact Fourier coordinates.  In the convention
of the parent score bridge, write

```text
f_t(u)=exp(tu^2)Phi(u),
H_t(x)=integral_0^infinity f_t(u)cos(xu)du.          (11.201.1)
```

For `k>=0`, define the complex half-line moments

```text
M_k(c,t)
 =integral_0^infinity u^k f_t(u)exp(icu)du.
```

The super-exponential tail of `Phi` justifies every differentiation used
below, and gives

```text
H_t^(k)(c)=Re[i^k M_k(c,t)].                        (11.201.2)
```

Suppose `c>0` is a zero of exact multiplicity `m>=2`, and factor

```text
H_t(x)=(x-c)^m V(x),             V(c)!=0.
```

Then (11.201.2) gives the contact equations and the regular logarithmic
derivative without any division by a vanishing lower jet:

```text
Re[i^jM_j]=0,                         0<=j<m,
Re[i^mM_m]!=0,

B_c:=V'(c)/V(c)
 =Re[i^(m+1)M_(m+1)]
    /[(m+1)Re[i^mM_m]].                           (11.201.3)
```

Writing

```text
C_k=integral_0^infinity u^k f_t(u)cos(cu)du,
S_k=integral_0^infinity u^k f_t(u)sin(cu)du,
```

the real projection in (11.201.3) gives the parity-correct split

```text
m even: B_c=-S_(m+1)/[(m+1)C_m],
m odd:  B_c= C_(m+1)/[(m+1)S_m].                  (11.201.4)
```

In particular, an absolute-value moment estimate is not a substitute for
the signed ratio.  The conversion from Section 11.200 is

```text
ell=(2cB_c-m)/4.                                  (11.201.5)
```

There is an equivalent positive-probability formulation.  Where the
one-sided score bridge applies, set

```text
dnu_t(u)=-f_t'(u)du/f_t(0),
mathcal S_t(x)=E_nu[sin(xU)],
H_t(x)=f_t(0)mathcal S_t(x)/x,       x>0.          (11.201.6)
```

The factor `1/x` is nonzero at `c`, so the multiplicity of the zero transfers
unchanged.  Direct differentiation of a local jet
`mathcal S_t(x)=(x-c)^m(a_0+a_1(x-c)+...)` gives

```text
B_c=mathcal S_t^(m+1)(c)
       /[(m+1)mathcal S_t^(m)(c)]-1/c,

ell=c mathcal S_t^(m+1)(c)
       /[2(m+1)mathcal S_t^(m)(c)]-(m+2)/4.        (11.201.7)
```

If `Cnu_k=E[U^k cos(cU)]` and `Snu_k=E[U^k sin(cU)]`, then

```text
m even: B_c= Cnu_(m+1)/[(m+1)Snu_m]-1/c,
m odd:  B_c=-Snu_(m+1)/[(m+1)Cnu_m]-1/c.          (11.201.8)
```

Equations (11.201.3)--(11.201.8) identify the exact Xi-specific target:
one adjacent signed moment ratio subject to all lower contact equations.
Positivity of the underlying measure alone does not determine it.

To prove the last assertion sharply, let `sinc(z)=sin(z)/z`, with
`sinc(0)=1`, fix `pi<y<2pi`, and define

```text
H_(m,y,c)(x)
 =sinc(pi x/c)^m sinc(y x/c).                      (11.201.9)
```

This is the characteristic function of the convolution of `m` copies of
`Uniform[-pi/c,pi/c]` and one copy of `Uniform[-y/c,y/c]`.  Its frequency
density is even, nonnegative, compactly supported, and log-concave by
closure of log-concavity under convolution.

At `x=c`, the first factor has a simple zero.  Removing its `m` powers,
the regular logarithmic derivatives of the first and last factors are
`-1/c` and `(y cot y-1)/c`, respectively.  Therefore

```text
B_c=(y cot(y)-m-1)/c,
ell=(2y cot(y)-3m-2)/4.                            (11.201.10)
```

Moreover,

```text
d/dy[y cot(y)]
 =[sin(y)cos(y)-y]/sin(y)^2<0,       pi<y<2pi.     (11.201.11)
```

The left and right endpoint limits are `+infinity` and `-infinity`.
Hence (11.201.10) realizes every real `ell`, uniquely, inside positive
compact log-concave Fourier kernels.

The countermodel is also an exact all-time heat family.  If `p` is its
compact frequency density, define

```text
H_tau(x)
 =integral_R p(u)exp(tau u^2)exp(ixu)du
 =exp(-tau partial_x^2)H_0(x).                     (11.201.12)
```

For `tau>=0`, compact support permits passage to the locally uniform limit

```text
exp(-tau partial_x^2)
 =lim_(N->infinity)
  [(1-sqrt(tau/N)partial_x)
   (1+sqrt(tau/N)partial_x)]^N.                    (11.201.13)
```

Each finite first-order factor preserves the Laguerre--Polya class, so
`H_tau` has only real zeros.  On the other side of the contact, with
`tau=-sigma<0`,

```text
sigma^(-m/2)H_(-sigma)(c+sqrt(sigma)z)/V(c)
 ->exp(partial_z^2)z^m.                            (11.201.14)
```

The limit is an imaginary rescaling of a Hermite polynomial and has a
nonreal pair for every `m>=2`.  Root continuity gives a nonreal pair for
all sufficiently small `sigma>0`; if an earlier negative time were
real-rooted, (11.201.13) would preserve real-rootedness up to that small
negative time, a contradiction.  Thus

```text
H_tau has only real zeros iff tau>=0.               (11.201.15)
```

Even positive Fourier representation, compact log-concavity, and attainment
at an exact first loss therefore leave `ell` arbitrary.

The compact spline density can be made smooth and uniformly strongly
log-concave without restoring a field bound.  Multiply (11.201.9) by
`exp(-q x^2/2)`.  In frequency space this replaces the compact variable
`Y` by `X=Y+Z`, where `Z` is independent `N(0,q)`.  Since

```text
|Y|<=R=(m pi+y)/c,
q=((m+2)^2 pi^2+1)/c^2>R^2,                        (11.201.16)
```

Gaussian posterior differentiation gives the exact curvature identity

```text
(log p_q)''(u)
 =Var(Y|X=u)/q^2-1/q
 <=-(q-R^2)/q^2<0.                                (11.201.17)
```

The density `p_q` is consequently smooth, positive, even, strictly
decreasing for `u>0`, and uniformly strongly log-concave.  Its one-sided
score law has a continuous positive density on `(0,infinity)`.  The
Gaussian factor changes `B_c` by `-qc`, and hence

```text
ell=[2y cot(y)-3m-2-2qc^2]/4.                      (11.201.18)
```

For the fixed `q` in (11.201.16), the phase map in (11.201.11) again makes
(11.201.18) surjective onto the real line.

The role of `pi` in (11.201.9) is completely explicit.  It is the first
positive zero of the sine in the characteristic function of
`Uniform[-pi/c,pi/c]`: `sin(pi)=0` places the contact at `x=c`.  No pi is
inserted into (11.201.2)--(11.201.8), and no polygon or unstated circle
normalization is being used.

This closes another generic route.  Positive Fourier representation,
compact log-concavity, a continuous positive score law, uniform strong
log-concavity, and exact local first-loss dynamics do not bound the first
Xi-jet field.  The smooth model has Gaussian rather than Xi theta-derived
double-exponential tails.  The separate weighted theta-tail countermodel
blocks promotion from shape plus tail estimates, but does not itself realize
this exact multiple contact; the two models are not being silently merged.

A surviving local theorem must therefore use the simultaneous Xi
theta/modular source and the multiple-contact moment equations, not generic
positivity or curvature in isolation.  The alternative global route remains
zero first-jet winding.  Independently, the cofinal Jensen programme still
needs a remainder uniform in degree.

The exact companion verifies the direct Fourier and score identities for
multiplicities `2` through `16`, fifteen exact sinc contacts, five
Gaussian-smoothed curvature models, and all forward/backward Hermite counts
through multiplicity `16`.  The closed formulas prove arbitrary fixed `m`.

This section proves no bound for the actual Xi moment ratio, no simultaneous
theta-contact theorem, no degree-uniform Jensen remainder, no Xi collision
exclusion, all-degree Jensen hyperbolicity, PF-infinity, `Lambda<=0`, RH, or
prize-level conclusion.

## 11.202 Modular-primitive reflection still does not constrain the field

Section 11.201 leaves open whether the theta primitive and its modular
endpoint cancellation restrict the adjacent signed moment ratio.  These
coordinates can first be written for every contact order.  Recall

```text
R''-R=8Phi,                         R'(0)=-1/2,
C_t(x)=integral_0^infinity exp(tu^2)R(u)cos(xu)du,
A_t=D_t[C_t]=8H_t-1/2,                            (11.202.1)

D_t=-4t^2 partial_x^2+4tx partial_x+(2t-1-x^2).
```

If `c>0` is a zero of `H_t` of exact multiplicity `m>=2`, multiplication
by eight and subtraction of the constant give

```text
A_t(c)=-1/2,
A_t^(j)(c)=0,                         1<=j<m,
A_t^(m)(c)!=0.                                   (11.202.2)
```

The regular factor is unchanged, so

```text
B_c=A_t^(m+1)(c)/[(m+1)A_t^(m)(c)],
ell=(2cB_c-m)/4.                                 (11.202.3)
```

Differentiating the explicit second-order operator gives, for every
`j>=0`,

```text
A_t^(j)
 =-4t^2 C_t^(j+2)+4tx C_t^(j+1)
  +(4tj+2t-1-x^2)C_t^(j)
  -2jx C_t^(j-1)-j(j-1)C_t^(j-2),               (11.202.4)
```

where terms with negative derivative order are omitted.  Thus a
multiplicity-`m` theta contact is a completely explicit finite jet system
for `C_t`, but (11.202.4) itself has no sign.  In the actual theta
decomposition it says

```text
sum_n A_(n,t)(c)=-1/2,
sum_n A_(n,t)^(j)(c)=0,               1<=j<m,     (11.202.5)
```

followed by the adjacent ratio of the two infinite sums.  Section 11.12's
finite-block obstruction forbids replacing these coupled cancellations by
termwise positivity.

There is a sharper structural test.  For `a>0`, let

```text
z_a(u)=2 exp(-a cosh(4u))/K_0(a),
G_a(x)=K_(ix/4)(a)/K_0(a).                       (11.202.6)
```

The first expression is a normalized probability density on the real
line.  It is smooth, positive, even, and uniformly strongly log-concave,
because

```text
(log z_a)''(u)=-16a cosh(4u)<=-16a.               (11.202.7)
```

Its tails have exactly the double-exponential scale used in the theta-tail
guards.  The characteristic transform in (11.202.6) belongs to the
Laguerre--Polya class.  This is a published theorem for `K_(iz)(a)`; a
square-integral proof is given in
`https://arxiv.org/abs/0801.2996`.

The Bessel factor can be kept nonzero at any prescribed contact.  If `Z`
has density `z_a` and `V(u)=a cosh(4u)`, integration by parts gives

```text
E[Z V'(Z)]=1.
```

Since `z sinh(4z)>=4z^2`,

```text
E[Z^2]<=1/(16a).
```

The elementary inequality `cos w>=1-w^2/2` then yields

```text
G_a(c)=E[cos(cZ)]
      >=1-c^2/(32a)>0,               a>c^2/32.    (11.202.8)
```

Fix such an `a`, choose `pi<y<2pi`, and define

```text
P_(m,y,c,a)(x)
 =sinc(pi x/c)^m sinc(y x/c)G_a(x).               (11.202.9)
```

This is the characteristic function of the convolution of `m` copies of
`Uniform[-pi/c,pi/c]`, one copy of `Uniform[-y/c,y/c]`, and `Z`.  The
frequency density is smooth, positive, even, and log-concave by the
Prekopa convolution theorem.  If

```text
R_0=(m pi+y)/c,
```

then for `u>R_0` its density lies between the corresponding translates
`z_a(u+R_0)` and `z_a(u-R_0)`.  It therefore retains two-sided
double-exponential theta-style decay.

The point `x=c` is an exact multiplicity-`m` zero by (11.202.8).  Removing
the vanishing sinc powers gives

```text
B_c=(y cot y-m-1)/c+G_a'(c)/G_a(c),

ell=[2y cot y-3m-2+2cG_a'(c)/G_a(c)]/4.           (11.202.10)
```

The Bessel correction is a fixed finite number.  As proved in Section
11.201, `y cot y` is a decreasing bijection from `(pi,2pi)` onto the real
line.  Thus (11.202.10) realizes every prescribed real `ell`, uniquely in
the phase `y`.

Every factor in (11.202.9) is Laguerre--Polya.  The double-exponential tail
makes

```text
P_tau(x)=integral_R p(u)exp(tau u^2)exp(ixu)du     (11.202.11)
```

entire for every real `tau`.  For `tau>=0`, it is
`exp(-tau partial_x^2)P_0` and remains Laguerre--Polya.  For negative time,
the multiplicity-`m` contact has the local limit

```text
exp(partial_z^2)z^m,
```

which has a nonreal pair.  Forward heat preservation then excludes
real-rootedness at every earlier time.  Hence the exact Newman-style
threshold of (11.202.11) is zero for every value in (11.202.10).

The contact can now be embedded at any prescribed positive boundary time
`t_*`.  Define

```text
Phi_*(u)=kappa exp(-t_*u^2)p(u),                   (11.202.12)
```

where the unique positive scale `kappa` is chosen so that

```text
integral_0^infinity cosh(u)Phi_*(u)du=1/16.        (11.202.13)
```

At time `t_*`, the transform of (11.202.12) is a positive multiple of
(11.202.9), so its zero, field, and first-loss geometry are unchanged.
For `u>=0`, put

```text
R_*(u)=8 integral_u^infinity sinh(v-u)Phi_*(v)dv. (11.202.14)
```

Differentiation under the super-exponentially convergent integral gives

```text
R_*''-R_*=8Phi_*,                 R_*'(0)=-1/2,
R_*>0,                            R_*'<0,
R_*''=R_*+8Phi_*>0.                              (11.202.15)
```

Extend the primitive to the negative half-line by

```text
R_*(-u)-R_*(u)=sinh(u),              u>=0.        (11.202.16)
```

This is the exact reflection equation of the Jacobi-theta primitive.
Evenness of `Phi_*`, (11.202.15), and `R_*'(0)=-1/2` imply recursively
that every odd endpoint jet of `R_*` is `-1/2`; hence (11.202.16) is
`C^infinity` and satisfies the same differential identity on both sides.

The positive curvature also supplies the same triangular probability
package used in Section 11.12A:

```text
dmu_*(v)=2R_*''(v)dv,
integral dmu_*=2(R_*'(infinity)-R_*'(0))=1,

R_*(u)=(1/2)integral_[0,infinity)(v-u)_+dmu_*(v). (11.202.17)
```

Equations (11.202.9)--(11.202.17) prove a modular-primitive nonclosure
theorem.  The endpoint normalization, reflection equation, positive
decreasing convex primitive, triangular probability representation,
theta-style double-exponential tail, positive log-concave Fourier kernel,
and exact positive first-loss contact can coexist with every real regular
field at every fixed multiplicity.

The construction deliberately does not reproduce the discrete
Jacobi-theta summand roster.  That is now the surviving local distinction:
the arithmetic translate law

```text
phi_n(u)=n^(-1/2)phi_1(u+(log n)/2),               (11.202.18)
```

its fixed component weights, and the coupled infinite cancellations in
(11.202.5).  Any useful Xi field inequality must use that discrete data,
not merely the modular reflection consequence.  The global first-jet
winding route and the degree-uniform cofinal Jensen remainder remain
independent obligations.

The exact companion verifies 17 operator jets, all contact multiplicities
from `2` through `16`, fifteen sinc--Bessel field models, three independent
Bessel nonvanishing diagnostics, eight modular odd endpoint jets, and the
forward/backward Hermite root counts through multiplicity `16`.

This section proves no bound on the actual Xi field, no discrete
theta-summand inequality, no degree-uniform Jensen remainder, no Xi
collision exclusion, all-degree Jensen hyperbolicity, PF-infinity,
`Lambda<=0`, RH, or prize-level conclusion.

## 11.203 Free discrete theta shifts do not by themselves close the field

Section 11.202 isolates the exact shifted theta roster as the remaining
local distinction.  The shift locations and the arithmetic coefficients
must be separated before either is promoted.  For every real `a>=1`, set

```text
phi_a(u)
 =(2*pi^2*a^4*exp(9u)-3*pi*a^2*exp(5u))
  *exp(-pi*a^2*exp(4u)),

M_(a,t)=integral_0^infinity exp(tu^2)phi_a(u)du,
h_(a,t)^(j)(x)
 =M_(a,t)^(-1) integral_0^infinity
   exp(tu^2)phi_a(u)partial_x^j cos(xu)du.          (11.203.1)
```

The translate identity remains exact for continuous `a`:

```text
phi_a(u)=a^(-1/2)phi_1(u+(log a)/2).               (11.203.2)
```

Consider a finite nonnegative mixture with normalized weights `p_a`.
At a multiplicity-two contact `c>0`, its normalized transform satisfies

```text
sum_a p_a h_a(c)=0,
sum_a p_a h_a'(c)=0,
sum_a p_a=1.                                      (11.203.3)
```

If the second derivative does not vanish, its first Xi-jet field is

```text
ell=c sum_a p_a h_a'''(c)/(6 sum_a p_a h_a''(c))-1/2.  (11.203.4)
```

No division is needed to test a prescribed value `ell_0`.  Add the linear
equation

```text
c sum_a p_a h_a'''(c)
 -6(ell_0+1/2)sum_a p_a h_a''(c)=0.               (11.203.5)
```

Equations (11.203.3)--(11.203.5) give an exact convex-hull reduction.
Every vertex of the contact slice has support at most three.  By the
finite-dimensional Caratheodory theorem, every feasible prescribed-field
point has a witness with support at most four.  A pole of (11.203.4) occurs
when a segment in the contact slice crosses `sum p_a h_a''=0` while the
third-derivative sum remains nonzero.  These facts are algebraic and do not
use a numerical grid.

The companion scout applies this reduction to four rosters on
`0<=t<=1/5`: a continuous log mesh, a geometric square-root-of-two lattice,
the integer indices `1<=a<=8`, and the integer indices `1<=a<=12`.  The
tested field set is

```text
{-20,-5,-1,0,1,5,20}.                              (11.203.6)
```

The continuous and geometric rosters realize all seven values on the main
grid and have sampled adjacent-ratio poles.  The coarse integer grid first
realizes five values.  Targeted refinement then finds strictly positive
four-component integer witnesses for the two apparent gaps:

```text
ell=-1: t=0.0075, c=48.975, support {1,2,4,5},
ell=20: t=0.02,   c=79.4,   support {1,2,3,12}.     (11.203.7)
```

An independent 80-decimal-place checker recomputes every component
integral and resolves the four linear equations afresh.  It validates
twenty-four main-grid prescribed-field witnesses, the two refined integer
witnesses, and the two main-grid pole witnesses.  The largest recomputed
field error is below `1e-76`; the smallest recomputed positive weight is
above `7.9e-11`.  Explicit analytic envelopes cover the omitted `u>2`
integrals and the fixed-mixture index tail, while the point quadrature and
finite parameter grids remain diagnostics rather than interval
certificates.

Thus the current evidence rejects the shift locations alone as the source
of a field restriction: even the true integer locations support all seven
widely separated test values once their mixture weights are freed.  This is
not a theorem that every real field is attainable on the integer roster.
It also does not alter the actual Xi coefficients.  In the normalized
coordinate (11.203.1), the genuine unit-coefficient theta sum has the
specific time-dependent weights

```text
p_(n,t)=M_(n,t)/sum_(k>=1)M_(k,t).                 (11.203.8)
```

The next local theorem must therefore use (11.203.8), equivalently the unit
coefficients before normalization, together with the complete infinite
contact cancellation.  Any separator or signed-minor proposal that is
valid for arbitrary positive weights is contradicted by the stored
witnesses.  The global zero-trajectory and degree-uniform Jensen-remainder
routes remain independent.

This section proves the exact division-free convex-hull reduction.  It
records high-precision finite diagnostics, not an interval-certified
free-weight countermodel theorem.  It proves no fixed-weight Xi contact
exclusion, no actual Xi field bound, no degree-uniform Jensen remainder,
no `Lambda<=0`, RH, or prize-level conclusion.

with a finite L1 KKT slack above `6.92`.  The relative discrepancy from the

## 11.205 The drifting contact is a rigorous interval branch

Section 11.204 leaves the tracked fourth-summand contact as a numerical
mechanism.  It can be promoted on its stated local domain without replacing
the oscillatory integrals by floating-point point samples.  Write

```text
G_lambda(t,x)=(F_lambda(t,x),partial_x F_lambda(t,x)),
F_lambda=H_1+H_2+H_3+lambda H_4.                 (11.205.1)
```

For a transform derivative of order `q`, every mixed derivative at a fixed
center `(t_0,x_0)` has the exact integral representation

```text
partial_t^a partial_x^b H_n^(q)(t_0,x_0)
 =Re[i^(q+b) integral_0^infinity
   u^(q+2a+b) exp(t_0 u^2)phi_n(u)exp(i x_0 u)du]. (11.205.2)
```

This identity is important at `x` near `136`.  Direct interval substitution
of a whole `(t,x)` box destroys the oscillatory cancellation and produces an
enclosure many orders of magnitude wider than `F_xx`, which is of order
`10^(-21)`.  Instead, the companion evaluates the point integrals in
(11.205.2) by rigorous ACB quadrature and uses a bivariate Taylor enclosure of
order ten in `t` and order twenty-eight in `x`.

The remainder is bounded without cancellation.  First expand in time through
order `A=10`, uniformly in `x`, and then expand each retained time coefficient
in frequency through order `B=28`.  If

```text
phi_n(u)/phi_5(u)
 <= 2(n/5)^4 exp(-pi*(n^2-25)*exp(4u))
 <  2(n/5)^4 exp(-3*(n^2-25))=:b_n.              (11.209.3)
```

The last inequality uses only `pi>3` and `exp(4u)>=1`.  For `n>=6`,

```text

 <= (7/6)^4 exp(-3(2n+1))
 < 2*2^(-39)=2^(-38),                            (11.209.4)
```

`b_6<5*2^(-33)`.  Therefore

```text
sum_(n>=6) b_n
 < (5*2^(-33))/(1-2^(-38))
 < 6*2^(-33)
 < 10^(-9),                                      (11.209.5)
```

the final decimal conversion being the exact integer inequality
`6*10^9<2^33`.  Equations (11.209.3)--(11.209.5) prove the pointwise bound

```text
sum_(n>=6) phi_n(u) < 10^(-9) phi_5(u)
for every u>=0.                                  (11.209.6)
```

```text
       u^j exp((9/20)u^2)phi_5(u)du.              (11.209.7)
```

At 288-bit precision and absolute quadrature tolerance `10^(-44)`, the raw

Retain

## 11.214 Anchor disks are signed tangent disks

Section 11.213 exposes two negative raw anchor centres, but its transpose
handoff estimates `R_T` and `Q_T` separately.  The exact reciprocal-cell
identities show that those two terms should be recombined before any
modulus.  They also reveal a geometric constraint: an anchor disk is tangent
to the origin, so entering it is necessarily a signed statement about the
complete ideal join.  This section makes both facts exact and proves that a
separated termwise absolute budget cannot close either disk on the fixed
`q=1` chart.

Put

```text
W_H:=R_H,

W_T:=R_T+Q_T.                                    (11.214.1)
```

The identities (11.213.15) and (11.213.19) give

```text
W_H=A_H+mathcal J_H^0,

W_T=A_T+mathcal J_T^0.                           (11.214.2)
```

Thus the transpose correction belongs inside one combined residual.  In
particular, the sufficient handoff

```text
|R_T+Q_T|<=A_T-delta
  implies |mathcal J_T^0|>=delta                 (11.214.3)
```

is weaker, and therefore sharper, than the separated condition in
(11.213.21).  No cancellation between `R_T` and `Q_T` is asserted; equation
(11.214.3) merely postpones their separation until after their exact sum is
formed.

The reciprocal-stationary content of (11.214.2) is also exact.  For one
physical reciprocal cell, retain the notation of Section 11.192:

```text
S_q=tau_q+M_q-E_q^(ext)+Lambda_q^(alias).
```

Then

```text
2M_q-S_q
 =M_q-tau_q+E_q^(ext)-Lambda_q^(alias).          (11.214.4)
```

After the internal tie halves, aliases, and cell exteriors are recomposed,
(11.192.5)--(11.192.6) give

```text
mathcal J_H^0
 =mathscr M_N[P_H^0]-tau_band[P_H^0]
   +E_band[P_H^0],

mathcal J_T^0
 =mathscr M_N[P_T^0]-tau_band[P_T^0]
   +E_band[P_T^0]
   +2iu_Nmathcal T_N^[N][B_(T,N)^0].            (11.214.5)
```

Equations (11.214.2) and (11.214.5) are the requested anchored reciprocal-
stationary decomposition.  It is invariant under internal roster transfer.
No proper fixed-width collar, one-sided exterior, or detached terminal atom
has been frozen.

The disk geometry is elementary but decisive.  For `A>0` and `J` complex,

```text
|A+J|^2-A^2=|J|^2+2A Re J.                      (11.214.6)
```

Consequently, for `0<delta<=A`,

```text
|A+J|<=A-delta

iff |J|^2+2A Re J<=-2A delta+delta^2.            (11.214.7)
```

The reverse triangle inequality then gives `|J|>=delta`.  More
importantly, every nonzero point in the uncontracted disk satisfies

```text
Re J<=-|J|^2/(2A)<0.                             (11.214.8)
```

Thus the anchor disk does not convert the signed stationary problem into a
magnitude-only estimate.  It is the disk of radius `A` centred at `-A`,
tangent to zero.  A successful raw-disk proof must put the complete join in
its negative tangent half-plane.  As in (11.213.22), that raw half-plane is
not automatically the physical-current half-plane after the terminal phase
is restored.

There is a source-specific obstruction to the most direct absolute route.
For `C=H,T`, define the fully termwise carrier budget

```text
B_C:=2 sum_(r=1)^N omega_N(r)
           |f_(P_C^0)(r)|.                      (11.214.9)
```

This is the exact right side obtained by applying the triangle inequality
to the two copies of the starred carrier before any cancellation.  Consider

```text
I_N={r:ceil(N/64)<=r<=floor(N/32)}.              (11.214.10)
```

On `L>=50`, one has `N>4160`, so `#I_N>=N/65`.  For `r` in this block,

```text
u_r-u_N=log(N/r)>=log 32>3,

u_r+u_N>=u_r-u_N.                               (11.214.11)
```

The first strict inequality follows already from `e<3`, hence
`e^3<27<32`.  The physical exponent obeys

```text
sigma<1/2+1/(8L),

log a<(L+1)/2.
```

Since

```text
(L+1)/(16L)<=51/800<1/10<log(10/9),
```

where `log(1+x)>x/(1+x)` is used at `x=1/9`, it follows that

```text
exp(S(log r))
 >=r^(-sigma)
 >9/(10sqrt(r))
 >9/(2sqrt(N)).                                  (11.214.12)
```

At the same atoms, (11.189.20) gives

```text
|P_H^0(log r)|>27/4.
```

The imaginary cubic part of `P_T^0` has the same lower bound, while its

```text
|P_T^0(log r)|>27/4.                             (11.214.13)
```

All weights in (11.214.10) are full interior weights.  Equations
(11.214.9)--(11.214.13) therefore prove, for both channels,

```text
B_C>(243/260)sqrt(N)
   >(243/520)exp(L/4).                            (11.214.14)
```

The anchors have only polynomial upper growth.  Indeed,

```text
m_N>alpha_P/(N+1/2),          n_N<=2alpha_P,
```

and comparison with the complete harmonic sum gives

```text
D_N
 <=sum_(r=m_N)^n_N 1/r
 <1+log(n_N/m_N)
 <1+log(2N+1)
 <(L+7)/2.                                       (11.214.15)
```

Also

```text
b<(L+1)/2,                    d<(L+3)/2.
```

The second inequality uses `u_N=log(a/N)<log 2<1`.  Since `pi>3`, both
anchors satisfy

```text
A_H<U(L),             A_T<U(L),

U(L):={(L+7)(L+1)(L+3)^2}/192.                  (11.214.16)
```

The exponential lower bound in (11.214.14) already wins at the left
endpoint.  Positivity of the exponential series gives the exact rational
check

```text
(243/520)sum_(k=0)^40 (25/2)^k/k! >125396,

U(50)<42531.                                     (11.214.17)
```

Moreover,

```text
d/dL log U(L)
 =1/(L+7)+1/(L+1)+2/(L+3)
 <4/(L+1)<=4/51<1/4.                            (11.214.18)
```

Hence the ratio between the lower bound in (11.214.14) and `U(L)` is
strictly increasing.  We have proved

```text
B_H>A_H,                  B_T>A_T,
                                  L>=50, q=1.    (11.214.19)
```

Equation (11.214.19) is a route obstruction, not a lower bound for the
signed carriers.  It says that an estimate which first uses
`|2mathscr M_N|<=B_C` and then adds any nonnegative separate budget for
`V_N`, the exterior, or the aliases already has a right side larger than
the anchor.  Such an estimate cannot prove either disk inclusion.  The
actual oscillatory carrier may be much smaller; proving that requires the
signed reciprocal recomposition in (11.214.4)--(11.214.5).

The next admissible target is therefore not `|R_H|` or `|R_T|+|Q_T|` by
separated triangle inequalities.  One must either prove the signed tangent-
disk inequality (11.214.7) for a complete tie-invariant join, or bypass the
raw disk with a phase-weighted Hermitian/transpose inequality for the
physical current.  The terminal multiplier, symmetric exterior, outer tie
halves, and transpose survivor must all be composed before moduli.

Every `pi` in this section is inherited from `e(x)=exp(2pi i x)`,
`kappa=1/(2pi i)`, and the anchors of Section 11.213.  The new comparison
uses only rational interval counting, logarithms, and the positive
exponential series.  No circle, polygon, or fitted constant is introduced.

This section proves the exact combined anchor residuals, the improved
transpose disk handoff, the complete reciprocal-cell form of those
residuals, tangent-disk geometry, and the source-specific failure of every
separated termwise absolute carrier/variation budget on the fixed `q=1`
chart.  It proves no signed reciprocal join, disk inclusion, physical-
current sign, all-`q` transport, contact-box exclusion, `Q209`, cofinal
successor, `Lambda<=0`, RH, or prize-level conclusion.

## 11.215 The terminal phase winds; the surviving current target is covariant

The anchor disks in Section 11.214 are phase-free modulus statements, but
their use in the mixed physical current is not.  Section 11.213 leaves open
whether the terminal phase might remain in a favourable sector on a fixed
cutoff cell.  On the physical `q=1` chart it does the opposite: it traverses
the full unit circle many times inside every complete fixed-`N` cell.  This
section proves that fact without sampling and replaces the informal
"phase-weighted" alternative by an exact two-channel matrix criterion.

Retain the physical identities of Section 11.162:

```text
a(L)^2=exp(L)+1/(32L^2),

T_0(L)=2pi a(L)^2,

Omega(L)=T_0(L)-epsilon(L),

0<epsilon(L)<7/{8L^2x(L)},

x(L)=4pi exp(L),                         L>=50.  (11.215.1)
```

The cutoff is strictly increasing, since

```text
d/dL a(L)^2=exp(L)-1/(16L^3)>0.                 (11.215.2)
```

It is also continuous and unbounded.  Hence, for every integer
`N>=ceil(a(50))`, there are unique endpoints `L_N,L_(N+1)` such that

```text
a(L_N)=N,                 a(L_(N+1))=N+1.       (11.215.3)
```

The interval `[L_N,L_(N+1)]` is a complete fixed-`N` cutoff cell.  The
possibly incomplete cell meeting `L=50` is not used.

At the physical frequency `xi=Omega`, the terminal carrier in
(11.213.12) has positive modulus and phase

```text
E_N=|E_N|exp(i phi_N),

phi_N(L)=Omega(L)log N.                          (11.215.4)
```

Evaluating (11.215.4) at the two cell endpoints gives the exact unwrapped
increment

```text
Delta phi_N
 ={2pi(2N+1)+epsilon(L_N)-epsilon(L_(N+1))}
    log N.                                       (11.215.5)
```

On `L>=50`, equation (11.215.1) gives `epsilon<1`.  Since the left endpoint
correction is positive,

```text
Delta phi_N
 >{2pi(2N+1)-1}log N
 >4pi N log N
 >2pi.                                           (11.215.6)
```

The middle inequality uses `2pi-1>0`.  For the last one, `N>=2` and
`log N>=log 2>1/2`, the latter following directly from
`integral_1^2 du/u>1/2`.  Thus (11.215.6) is very conservative; the actual
number of turns grows at least on the scale `N log N`.

There is a useful exact consequence of the unwrapped inequality.  If a
continuous real phase has endpoint increment greater than `2pi`, then for
every angle `theta` one may choose

```text
k=floor{(phi_N(L_N)-theta)/(2pi)}+1.
```

The representative obeys

```text
phi_N(L_N)<theta+2pi k
 <=phi_N(L_N)+2pi<phi_N(L_(N+1)).
```

The intermediate value theorem therefore supplies an interior `L` at which
`phi_N(L)=theta+2pi k`.  In particular, this statement is independent of
which half-open cutoff convention owns either integer tie.  Thus

```text
{exp(i phi_N(L)):L_N<=L<=L_(N+1)}
 = {z in C:|z|=1}.                               (11.215.7)
```

In particular, `sin(phi_N)` takes both signs and vanishes on every complete
cell.  The raw centre projections in (11.213.22) consequently take both
signs.  No fixed proper terminal phase sector can turn either negative raw
centre into a cell-uniform physical-current sign.  This does not rule out an
adaptive phase partition or a cancellation correlated with the complete
reciprocal residual.

The Hermitian and transpose channels should now be composed at the source
level.  Retain (11.186.15), (11.186.17), and the complete ideal joins of
Section 11.214, and put

```text
h:=Re{conjugate(tau_0)mathcal J_H^0},

t:=tau_0 mathcal J_T^0,

z:=nu c_xi.                                      (11.215.8)
```

Since `|c_xi|=1`, the source-weighted ideal mixed block is exactly

```text
R_id(z)=(1/2){|z|^2 h+Re(z^2t)}.                 (11.215.9)
```

Write `z=X+iY` and `t=U+iV`.  Then (11.215.9) is the real quadratic form

```text
R_id(z)=[X Y] Q(h,t) [X Y]^T,

Q(h,t)=(1/2)[[h+U, -V],
             [-V,  h-U]].                       (11.215.10)
```

Its trace, determinant, and eigenvalues are

```text
tr Q=h,

det Q=(h^2-|t|^2)/4,

lambda_-(Q)=(h-|t|)/2,

lambda_+(Q)=(h+|t|)/2.                          (11.215.11)
```

Equations (11.215.9)--(11.215.11) give two precise theorem targets.  If
`z=r exp(i gamma)`, negativity at the actual physical source phase is
equivalent to

```text
h+Re{exp(2i gamma)t}<0.                          (11.215.12)
```

Negativity for every nonzero source phase is equivalent to negative
definiteness of `Q`, hence to the single phase-invariant inequality

```text
h+|t|<0.                                         (11.215.13)
```

The nonpositive version is obtained by replacing `<` with `<=`.  Condition
(11.215.13) is stronger than the physical theorem at one known source
phase, but it is the exact robust alternative; estimating the two channels
independently is not equivalent to it.

The bare centres do not satisfy the robust criterion throughout a complete
cell.  Write

```text
tau_0=rho exp{i(phi_N-pi/2)},          rho>0.
```

For `mathcal J_H^0=-A_H` and `mathcal J_T^0=-A_T`, equations (11.215.8)
give

```text
h_0=-rho A_H sin(phi_N),

|t_0|=rho A_T.                                  (11.215.14)
```

By (11.215.7), every complete cell contains a point with
`phi_N=3pi/2 mod 2pi`.  There

```text
h_0+|t_0|=rho(A_H+A_T)>0.                        (11.215.15)
```

Thus static negative centres cannot prove a source-phase-uniform current
theorem.  Equation (11.215.15) is a route obstruction, not a disproof of the
complete current: the signed reciprocal residuals, physical correction
polynomials, fixed affine row, and moved-tail defect can change both `h` and
`t` and have not been estimated here.

The next admissible target is now explicit.  Form the complete physical pair
`(h,t)` only after the tie-invariant reciprocal join, transpose survivor,
correction rows, affine row, and moved-tail defect are composed.  Then prove
the actual-phase inequality (11.215.12) with the contact-box reserve, or
prove the stronger invariant inequality (11.215.13).  A pair of independent
raw anchor-disk bounds does not address the phase winding in (11.215.7).

Every `pi` in this section has recorded provenance.  The factor `2pi` in
`T_0=2pi a^2` and `alpha_P=xi/(2pi)` comes from the completed-zeta saddle
and the Fourier convention `e(y)=exp(2pi i y)`.  The threshold `2pi` in
(11.215.6) is one period of `exp(i phi_N)`.  Elementary rational bounds on
`pi` are used only to audit the deliberately coarse full-turn comparison;
no circle, polygon, or fitted plotting constant is inserted into the
physical model.

This section proves complete-cell winding of the physical `q=1` terminal
phase, failure of every fixed proper terminal phase sector on such a cell,
the exact source-phase-covariant Hermitian/transpose matrix, its invariant
eigenvalues, and the centre-only obstruction to source-phase-uniform
negativity.  It proves no signed reciprocal residual estimate, actual-source-
phase current inequality, correction-row bound, all-`q` transport, contact-
box exclusion, `Q209`, cofinal successor, `Lambda<=0`, RH, or prize-level
conclusion.
