## 11.216 The actual source has one reverse saddle turn and an exact centre symmetry

Section 11.215 leaves the physical source angle as `gamma_phys`.  It is not
free.  The absolute first-coefficient anchor of Section 11.104 and the
physical `q=1` normalization of Section 11.162 give

```text
nu=eta/S_a=omega_c/(B_0T_0),

omega_c=(-1)^Neta,

eta=phi_t(1+d_1)/|1+d_1|,

|nu|=(B_0T_0)^(-1).                              (11.216.1)
```

At the physical frequency `xi=Omega`, `c_xi=1`.  Consequently

```text
exp(2i gamma_phys)=eta^2.                         (11.216.2)
```

The cutoff parity is constant on a fixed-`N` cell and disappears from the
transpose square.  Thus (11.216.2) identifies the actual source phase rather
than adding a new phase assumption.

Choose continuous arguments on one complete physical `q=1` cell:

```text
phi_t=exp(i beta_t),

delta_1=arg(1+d_1),

theta_eta=beta_t+delta_1,

chi_N=phi_N+theta_eta.                            (11.216.3)
```

This lift exists because the explicit `M_t` never vanishes on the chart and
`|d_1|<1/2`.  The phase `chi_N` is the phase of the source-inclusive
absolute terminal carrier `eta exp(i phi_N)`.

The reciprocal normalizer lock of Section 11.119 evaluates this phase
without differentiating an arbitrary branch.  For

```text
Q(v)=exp{i[v log(v/(2pi))-v-pi/4]},

gamma_t=conjugate(M_t)/M_t=exp(-2i beta_t),

psi=arg{Q(Omega)/gamma_t},              |psi|<1/x,       (11.216.4)
```

take the continuous lift inherited from `t=0`.  Then

```text
arg Q(Omega)+2beta_t=psi.                         (11.216.5)
```

Put

```text
K_N=2pi N^2,

F_N(v)=v[1+log(K_N/v)].                           (11.216.6)
```

Since `phi_N=Omega log N`, equations (11.216.3)--(11.216.6) give the exact
unwrapped identity

```text
2chi_N=F_N(Omega)+pi/4+psi+2delta_1.              (11.216.7)
```

This is the cancellation hidden by treating the terminal and source phases
independently.  The terminal phase itself makes order `N log N` turns per
cell, but its sum with the normalizer phase has a finite limiting turn.

First ignore the one-sided frequency defect `epsilon`.  At the two ideal
cell endpoints `Omega=2pi N^2` and `Omega=2pi(N+1)^2`, equation (11.216.7)
has main increment

```text
2pi G_N,

G_N=(N+1)^2[1-2log(1+1/N)]-N^2.                 (11.216.8)
```

Let `u=1/N<=1/2`.  The alternating logarithm estimate

```text
log(1+u)>=u-u^2/2+u^3/3-u^4/4                   (11.216.9)
```

gives, after multiplication by `(1+u)^2` and division by `u^2`,

```text
G_N
 <=-2-(2/3)u+(1/6)u^2+(1/3)u^3+(1/2)u^4
 <=-2-(7/16)u.                                  (11.216.10)
```

For the last inequality, the three positive terms are at most
`u/12+u/12+u/16=11u/48`, while `2/3-11/48=7/16`.
Thus the ideal main obeys

```text
Delta(2chi_N)_ideal
 <=-4pi-7pi/(8N).                                (11.216.11)
```

The physical corrections are smaller than the strict `N^(-1)` reserve.
At either cell endpoint write `a=m`, where `m=N` or `N+1`.  Since
`a^2=exp(L)+1/(32L^2)`, `pi>3`, and `m>=2`,

```text
x=4pi[m^2-1/(32L^2)]>9m^2.                      (11.216.12)
```

Moreover `N>=ceil(a(50))>2^25`, because `a(50)>e^25` and `e>2`.  From
(11.162.3),

```text
0<epsilon<1/x<1/(9m^2).                          (11.216.13)
```

As `F_N'(v)=log(K_N/v)`, the left endpoint perturbation is below
`2epsilon^2/K_N`, and the right endpoint perturbation is below
`2epsilon log(1+1/N)`.  Equations (11.216.12)--(11.216.13) therefore give

```text
|Delta F_N-Delta F_N,ideal|<1/N^2.               (11.216.14)
```

The phase-lock error contributes

```text
|Delta psi|<2/(9N^2).                            (11.216.15)
```

Finally, `|d_1|<2189/x<1/2` and the convergent logarithm series give

```text
|delta_1|<=|Log(1+d_1)|
            <|d_1|/(1-|d_1|)
            <4378/x.
```

Hence

```text
2|Delta delta_1|<17512/(9N^2).                   (11.216.16)
```

Combining (11.216.14)--(11.216.16), the complete perturbation of
`Delta(2chi_N)` is less than

```text
[1+2/9+17512/9]/N^2=1947/N^2.                   (11.216.17)
```

Since `N>2^25` and `pi>3`,

```text
1947/N^2<7pi/(8N).                               (11.216.18)
```

Equations (11.216.11) and (11.216.17)--(11.216.18) prove

```text
Delta chi_N<-2pi                                (11.216.19)
```

on every complete physical `q=1` cutoff cell.  The bounds in
(11.216.9)--(11.216.17) also show

```text
Delta chi_N -> -2pi       as N->infinity.         (11.216.20)
```

Thus the normalizer cancels the macroscopic terminal winding down to just
over one reverse turn; it does not freeze the absolute terminal phase.  The
same intermediate-value argument as in Section 11.215 gives

```text
{eta(L)exp(i phi_N(L)):L_N<=L<=L_(N+1)}
 ={z in C:|z|=1}.                                (11.216.21)
```

There are two immediate phase-inventory corollaries.  Since
`Delta phi_N>2pi`,

```text
Delta theta_eta=Delta chi_N-Delta phi_N<-4pi,

Delta(phi_N+2theta_eta)
 =2Delta chi_N-Delta phi_N<-6pi.                 (11.216.22)
```

The physical source phase and the transpose phase therefore also cover the
unit circle.  Marginal winding of these phases is no longer the open
question; their joint correlation is.

That correlation has an exact raw-centre symmetry.  Retain

```text
b=log N,                 u_N=log(a/N),

d=log(a^2/N)=b+2u_N,

A_H=D_N b d^2/(4pi),

A_T=D_N d b^2/(4pi).                             (11.216.23)
```

Then

```text
A_H/A_T=1+2u_N/b,

A_H-A_T=D_N b d u_N/(2pi)>=0.                    (11.216.24)
```

Write `tau_0=rho exp{i(phi_N-pi/2)}`, `rho>0`.  Inserting the actual source
phase (11.216.2) into (11.215.9) gives the bare-centre current

```text
R_center
 =-(rho|nu|^2/2)
    [A_H sin(phi_N)+A_T sin(phi_N+2theta_eta)].   (11.216.25)
```

Using (11.216.24) and the sum-of-sines identity, this factors exactly as

```text
R_center
 =-rho|nu|^2 A_T
   [cos(theta_eta)sin(phi_N+theta_eta)
      +(u_N/b)sin(phi_N)].                       (11.216.26)
```

The first term is the product of the source phase and the source-inclusive
absolute terminal phase from (11.216.21).  The second is precisely the
Hermitian/transpose anchor mismatch.  A branch-free parity-invariant form is

```text
R_center
 =-rho|nu|^2 A_T
  [Re(eta)Im{eta exp(i phi_N)}
     +(u_N/b)Im{exp(i phi_N)}].                  (11.216.27)
```

Replacing `eta` by `omega_c=(-1)^Neta` changes both factors in the product
and leaves it invariant.

The mismatch is uniformly tiny:

```text
0<=u_N<=log(1+1/N)<1/N,

0<=u_N/b<2/N.                                    (11.216.28)
```

It cannot yet be discarded.  At zeros of either factor in the leading
product, an arbitrarily small mismatch can determine the sign.  Nor is the
raw centre tie invariant: `D_N` changes at internal odd-roster crossings,
while the complete reciprocal residual changes with it.

The next exact target is therefore local and falsifiable.  On roster
interiors, use the scale separation between the rapidly winding terminal
phase and the one-turn locked phase to decide whether

```text
Re(eta)Im{eta exp(i phi_N)}                       (11.216.29)
```

must take both signs with a quantitative reserve exceeding `2/N`, or whether
the actual Xi path has a one-sided correlation unavailable to arbitrary
phases.  In either case the result must then be recomposed with the
tie-invariant reciprocal residual, terminal survivor, correction rows,
fixed affine row, and moved-tail defect before a physical-current sign can
be claimed.

Every `pi` in this section has inherited provenance.  The phase
`Q(v)=exp{i[v log(v/(2pi))-v-pi/4]}` is the completed-zeta reciprocal
stationary phase, with `pi/4` its negative-curvature signature.  The factor
`2pi` in `K_N=2pi N^2` is the same saddle/Fourier normalization as
`T_0=2pi a^2`.  The threshold `2pi` is one period of `exp(i chi_N)`.
Only `pi>3` is used in the deliberately coarse error comparison.

This section proves the exact actual-source normalization, a reverse full
turn of the source-inclusive terminal carrier on every complete physical
`q=1` cell, the source/transpose winding inventory, and the exact
parity-invariant bare-centre symmetry with its `O(u_N/log N)` mismatch.  It
proves no sign for (11.216.29), raw-centre sign theorem, signed reciprocal
residual estimate, complete physical-current inequality, correction-row
bound, tie-spliced theorem, all-`q` transport, contact-box exclusion, `Q209`,
cofinal successor, `Lambda<=0`, PF-infinity, RH, or prize-level conclusion.

## 11.217 The actual-source raw centre takes both signs on every complete cell

Section 11.216 reduces the bare physical centre to

```text
R_center=-rho|nu|^2A_T B,

B=cos(theta_eta)sin(chi_N)+(u_N/log N)sin(phi_N),

chi_N=phi_N+theta_eta.                            (11.217.1)
```

The marginal winding statements in (11.216.21)--(11.216.22) do not alone
determine the sign of `B`.  The exact normalizer lock supplies the missing
scale separation and in fact proves that `B` takes both signs with a fixed
reserve.

Retain

```text
K_N=2pi N^2,

F_N(v)=v[1+log(K_N/v)],

chi_0=(1/2)F_N(Omega)+pi/8,

r=psi/2+delta_1.                                 (11.217.2)
```

Then (11.216.7) is exactly

```text
chi_N=chi_0+r.                                    (11.217.3)
```

The physical frequency is strictly increasing.  Indeed,

```text
T_0=2pi a^2
```

is strictly increasing by (11.215.2), while both positive summands in

```text
epsilon
 =atan(1/x)/(8L^2)+3x/[4L^2(1+x^2)]              (11.217.4)
```

are strictly decreasing for `L>=50`: `x` increases, `atan(1/x)` decreases,
and `x/(1+x^2)` decreases for `x>1`.  Therefore

```text
Omega=T_0-epsilon
```

is strictly increasing.  The cell starts below `K_N` and ends above it, so
there is one point at which `Omega=K_N`.

From that point to the right endpoint, (11.216.10) and the right-frequency
part of (11.216.14) give

```text
F_N(Omega_right)-F_N(K_N)
 <=-4pi-7pi/(8N)+2/(9N^3)
 <-4pi.                                           (11.217.5)
```

Thus `chi_0` is strictly decreasing there and loses more than `2pi`.  Its
derivatives in the physical terminal phase coordinate are exact:

```text
d chi_0/dOmega=(1/2)log(K_N/Omega),

phi_N=Omega log N,

|d chi_0/d phi_N|
 =log(Omega/K_N)/(2log N)
 <log(1+1/N)/log N
 <2/N.                                            (11.217.6)
```

The middle inequality uses
`Omega<2pi(N+1)^2`; the last uses `log(1+1/N)<1/N` and
`log N>1/2`.

Consider the periodic safe set

```text
S={y in R:sin y>=1/2}.                            (11.217.7)
```

In each period its connected component has width `2pi/3`.  Any real phase
interval of length greater than `2pi` either contains one such component or
splits one occurrence between its two ends.  In the split case one piece has
width at least `pi/3`.  Hence the decreasing image of `chi_0` contains a
connected subinterval `J` on which

```text
sin(chi_0)>=1/2,

|Delta_J chi_0|=pi/3.                            (11.217.8)
```

Equation (11.217.6) now forces

```text
Delta_J phi_N>pi N/6.                            (11.217.9)
```

Put `theta_0=chi_0-phi_N`.  Both terms decrease on `J`, so

```text
Delta_J theta_0
 <-pi N/6-pi/3
 <-2pi.                                           (11.217.10)
```

The last inequality is overwhelmingly strict because `N>2^25`.  The
continuous phase `theta_0` therefore assumes one representative with
`cos(theta_0)=1` and another with `cos(theta_0)=-1` while
`sin(chi_0)>=1/2`.

The true phase and anchor errors cannot change the resulting signs.  From
(11.216.12), (11.216.15), and (11.216.16), uniformly through the cell,

```text
|r|
 <1/(2x)+4378/x
 <487/N^2
 <1/1000.                                         (11.217.11)
```

Also, by (11.216.28),

```text
0<=e_N:=u_N/log N<2/N<1/1000.                    (11.217.12)
```

At the point with `theta_0=0 mod 2pi`, equations
(11.217.3), (11.217.8), and (11.217.11) imply

```text
cos(theta_eta)=cos(theta_0+r)>999/1000,

sin(chi_N)>499/1000.
```

Consequently

```text
B
 >(999/1000)(499/1000)-1/1000
 =497501/1000000
 >49/100.                                         (11.217.13)
```

At the point with `theta_0=pi mod 2pi`, the same estimates give

```text
B<-497501/1000000<-49/100.                       (11.217.14)
```

The finite set of internal roster ties causes no loophole.  The inequalities
in (11.217.13)--(11.217.14) are strict and continuous in the phase bracket,
so either witness can be moved slightly into a roster interior while
retaining the weaker `49/100` reserve.  The positive common factor `A_T`
may jump, but it cannot change the centre sign.

Since the prefactor in (11.217.1) is strictly negative, every complete
physical `q=1` cell therefore contains two roster-interior points satisfying

```text
R_center<-(49/100)rho|nu|^2A_T,

R_center> +(49/100)rho|nu|^2A_T,                 (11.217.15)
```

respectively.  This closes the joint-phase question posed in (11.216.29):
the actual Xi source phase does not give the raw Hermitian/transpose centre
a one-sided sign.  The obstruction is much stronger than a marginal
full-circle statement because the two witnesses survive the exact unequal-
anchor correction with a fixed normalized reserve.

The required residual compensation can now be stated exactly.  Put

```text
W_H=R_H,

W_T=R_T+Q_T,

mathcal J_H^0=-A_H+W_H,

mathcal J_T^0=-A_T+W_T.                          (11.217.16)
```

For the actual-source scalar in (11.215.12), define

```text
Sigma_id
 :=Re{conjugate(tau_0)mathcal J_H^0}
    +Re{eta^2tau_0mathcal J_T^0}.
```

Equations (11.216.25)--(11.216.26) give the exact decomposition

```text
Sigma_id=-2rho A_TB+E_W,

E_W
 =Re{conjugate(tau_0)W_H}
   +Re{eta^2tau_0W_T},

R_id=(|nu|^2/2)Sigma_id.                         (11.217.17)
```

At the witness where `B<-49/100`, a negative complete ideal current would
therefore require

```text
E_W<-(98/100)rho A_T.                            (11.217.18)
```

In particular, since `|tau_0|=rho`, the necessary modulus condition is

```text
|W_H|+|W_T|>(98/100)A_T.                         (11.217.19)
```

Thus the surviving residual is not a perturbative cleanup: it must be
macroscopic and correctly signed on every positive-centre witness arc.  This
may come either from a cell-uniform negative bias or from a phase-correlated
response; the necessary condition alone does not distinguish them.  The
fixed affine, correction, moved-tail, and quadratic rows can be included by
adding their exact actual-source scalar to `E_W`; the same `98/100` total
compensation threshold remains.

Equation (11.217.15) is still not a counterexample to the complete current.
The reciprocal-stationary residuals `R_H` and `R_T+Q_T`, the physical
correction polynomials, fixed affine row, and moved-tail defect were removed

their signed, tie-invariant composition supplies an `O(A_T)` compensation on

The `pi/3` in this section is not an inserted model constant.  It is half the

## 11.218 Complete actual-source compensation ledger and the two proof mechanisms

Section 11.217 proves that the bare centre has both signs.  Its compensation
condition must now be stated in one normalization before any further estimate
is attempted.  Retain

```text
B=cos(theta_eta)sin(chi_N)+(u_N/log N)sin(phi_N),

R_full=(|nu|^2/2)Sigma_full,

Sigma_full=-2rho A_TB+E_tot.                    (11.218.1)
```

Here `E_tot` is, by definition, the sum of every non-centre contribution to
the actual-source retained current in the scalar units of (11.217.17).  The
elementary sum-of-sines identity gives a useful exact phase audit:

```text
B=(1/2)sin(phi_N+2theta_eta)
   +(1/2+u_N/log N)sin(phi_N).                   (11.218.2)
```

Thus the centre contains two inherited terminal-frequency tones.  Equation
(11.218.2) is only a rewrite; it supplies no cancellation theorem.

The ideal reciprocal residual can be partitioned without separating either
one-sided outer infinity.  Write `M_C,N_C,C_C` for
`mathscr M_N[P_C^0],mathscr N_N[P_C^0],mathscr C_N[P_C^0]`, respectively,
and put

```text
W_H^F=A_H+M_H+N_H,             W_H^R=C_H,

W_T^F=A_T+M_T+N_T,             W_T^R=C_T,

W_T^term=2iu_Nmathcal T_N^[N][B_(T,N)^0].       (11.218.3)
```

Equations (11.193.23) and (11.214.2) give exactly

```text
W_H=W_H^F+W_H^R,

W_T=W_T^F+W_T^R+W_T^term.                       (11.218.4)
```

The superscripts mean finite carrier-plus-near, symmetrically paired remote,
and ideal transpose terminal survivor.  In particular, `W_H^R,W_T^R` are
common-cutoff paired series; they are not differences of two separately
convergent tails.  Define their actual-source projections by

```text
E_F=Re{conjugate(tau_0)W_H^F}
      +Re{eta^2tau_0W_T^F},

E_R=Re{conjugate(tau_0)W_H^R}
      +Re{eta^2tau_0W_T^R},

E_term=Re{eta^2tau_0W_T^term}.                   (11.218.5)
```

Then `E_W=E_F+E_R+E_term` exactly.  This is the first no-double-counting rule:
the transpose terminal survivor belongs to `E_term` and is not included again
as a remote endpoint.

The physical coefficient perturbation is linear only after the exact
terminal factorizations.  Write

```text
P_H=P_H^0+Delta_H,        P_T=P_T^0+Delta_T,

B_(T,N)=B_(T,N)^0+Delta B_(T,N),

L_H[P]=mathscr M_N[P]+mathscr N_N[P]+mathscr C_N[P],

L_T[P,B]=mathscr M_N[P]+mathscr N_N[P]+mathscr C_N[P]
          +2iu_Nmathcal T_N^[N][B].              (11.218.6)
```

By linearity, the correction scalar is

```text
E_Delta
 =Re{conjugate(tau_0)L_H[Delta_H]}
  +Re{eta^2tau_0 L_T[Delta_T,Delta B_(T,N)]}.    (11.218.7)
```

No coefficient modulus has been taken in (11.218.7).  The remaining real
packages are the fixed affine row `R_aff`, the pure terminal transpose row
`R_aa`, the moving-tail defect `R_move`, and the four nonterminal quadratic
observation pairings `R_quad`.  Put

```text
E_X=2R_X/|nu|^2,       X in {aff,aa,move,quad}.

E_tot=E_F+E_R+E_term+E_Delta
      +E_aff+E_aa+E_move+E_quad.                 (11.218.8)
```

Equation (11.218.8) uses the split convention of (11.185.10): terminal-
nonterminal terms are in (11.218.6)--(11.218.7), the pure terminal term is
`E_aa`, and `E_quad` contains only the four remaining nonterminal pairings.
If the unsplit `epsilon^T J dot(epsilon)` formula is used instead, `E_aa`
must not be added separately.  The moving-tail defect is likewise attached
once, at the observation level, as required by (11.182.25).

The complete sign target is now the single pointwise inequality

```text
Sigma_full<0       iff       E_tot<2rho A_TB.    (11.218.9)
```

At the adverse roster-interior witness of Section 11.217, where
`B<-49/100`, (11.218.9) necessarily gives

```text
E_tot<-(98/100)rho A_T.                          (11.218.10)
```

Conversely, if at that witness

```text
E_tot>=-(98/100)rho A_T,                         (11.218.11)
```

then `Sigma_full>0`.  Thus (11.218.11) at one adverse witness would prove a
sign change of the complete retained current and retire this current-sign
route.  The sharp reserve inherited from the centre is `98/100`; the
`49/100` sufficient estimate mentioned at the end of Section 11.217 is
valid but unnecessarily stronger.

There is a useful conditional budget lemma.  Split

```text
E_tot=E_F+E_sec.
```

If, on an adverse witness, `|E_sec|<=delta rho A_T` with
`0<=delta<98/100`, then (11.218.10) forces

```text
E_F<-(98/100-delta)rho A_T.                      (11.218.12)
```

On the other hand, if `E_F>=-alpha rho A_T` and
`|E_sec|<=beta rho A_T`, where `alpha+beta<=98/100`, then
(11.218.11) holds and the complete current is positive at that adverse
witness.  This lemma is exact triangle arithmetic applied only after the
signed finite package has been isolated.

The existing estimates do not yet provide a positive `delta` for
(11.218.12) in the common normalization:

* `E_F` has no signed anchor-relative bound, and the separated carrier
  modulus budget already exceeds the anchor.
* `E_R` is absolutely convergent, but its physical derivative numerator has
  not been bounded relative to `rho A_T`.
* `E_term` and `E_aa` have explicit terminal `h` mechanisms, but no completed
  common-unit comparison with `rho A_T` has been proved.
* `E_Delta` has `O(h^2)` and `O(h^4)` coefficient envelopes, but the retained
  observation rows multiplying those coefficients have no proved relative
  norm.
* `E_move` has an atomic `h^3K` phase-displacement estimate, but the joined
  bulk observation factors in the complete defect remain unbounded.
* `E_aff` and `E_quad` have exact linear and four-pairing formulas but no
  anchor-relative estimates.

The logical gap in the coefficient-only arguments is real.  For arbitrary
positive `varepsilon,A`, the product

```text
varepsilon*(A/varepsilon)=A.                     (11.218.13)
```

Hence a small coefficient or phase displacement alone cannot make its
current contribution perturbative without a bound for the multiplying row.
Equation (11.218.13) is a nonpromotion guard, not a physical counterexample.

There are therefore two admissible proof mechanisms.  One may prove a
cell-uniform negative bias strong enough to satisfy (11.218.9), or prove a
pointwise phase-correlated estimate tracking `2B`.  The necessary condition
(11.218.10) does not choose between them.  A complementary obstruction route
is to prove a lower bound such as (11.218.11), possibly from a cell average,
half-turn comparison, or slow-variation theorem for the secondary package.

Every `pi` in this section is inherited from the Fourier character,
completed-zeta saddle, and earlier anchor formulas.  Equation (11.218.2) is
the elementary angle-addition identity; (11.218.10)--(11.218.13) use only
rational arithmetic.

This section proves the common scalar normalization, exact finite/remote/
terminal residual partition, correction linearization, package ownership
guards, sharp adverse-witness threshold, conditional budget lemma, and the
uniform-bias/phase-correlation proof alternatives.  It proves no secondary
package budget, signed finite carrier-near estimate, complete-current sign,
all-`q` transport, contact-box exclusion, `Q209`, cofinal successor,
`Lambda<=0`, PF-infinity, RH, or prize-level conclusion.

## 11.219 The two terminal secondary packages are perturbative in anchor units

Section 11.218 places the ideal transpose survivor `E_term` and the pure
terminal transpose row `E_aa` in the same scalar normalization as the anchor.
Their earlier powers of `h` can now be converted into a common-unit budget.

Retain `b=log N` and

```text
E_N=e(alpha_Plog N)exp(S(b)),

S(b)=tb^2/4-sigma b,

rho=|tau_0|=|kappa|S_(1,N)|E_N|.                (11.219.1)
```

On the physical `q=1` chart, `t=1/(2L^2)`, `sigma>1/2`,
`b<(L+1)/2`, and `b>L/2-1`.  Hence, for `L>=50`,

```text
tb^2/4<(L+1)^2/(32L^2)<1/8,

sigma b>b/2>L/4-1/2>=12,

S(b)<0,                    |E_N|<1.             (11.219.2)
```

The relevant terminal kernel is the logarithmic upper-end kernel from
(11.184.11), not the lower-end kernel in (11.186.23).  Since
`N+1<=a+1<2a`, `log a<(L+1)/2`, and `log 36<4`, (11.184.11) and `pi>3`
give

```text
0<S_(1,N)
 <log{8(N+1)^2+4}+4
 <log(36a^2)+4
 <L+9,

|kappa|<1/6,                rho<(L+9)/6.          (11.219.3)
```

The extra factor needed below is still tiny.  Indeed `h<exp(-L/2)`, and
the logarithmic derivative of `(L+9)exp(-3L/2)` is
`1/(L+9)-3/2<0`.  At `L=50`, the rational estimate
`h<1/72000000000` gives `59h^3<1`.  Thus

```text
(L+9)h^3<1                 for every L>=50.
```

First consider the ideal transpose survivor.  Equation (11.213.18) is

```text
W_T^term=-iE_Nu_Nu_(N,x)S_(1,N)/pi.
```

Since `S_(1,N)|E_N|/pi=2rho`, its actual-source projection obeys

```text
|E_term|
 <=rho|W_T^term|
 =2rho^2u_Nu_(N,x).                              (11.219.4)
```

Using `u_N<2h`, `u_(N,x)<h^2/24`, (11.219.3), the preceding decreasing
majorant, and the anchor floor `A_T>14300`, one obtains

```text
|E_term|/(rho A_T)
 <2{(L+9)/6}(2h)(h^2/24)/14300
 =(L+9)h^3/514800
 <1/68640.                                       (11.219.5)
```

The pure terminal row is normalized just as explicitly.  At `xi=Omega`,
the source-inclusive terminal carrier satisfies

```text
w_N=nu E_N,

S_(1,N)|E_N|=2pi rho.                            (11.219.6)
```

Substitution into the proved envelope (11.185.24) gives

```text
|R_aa|
 <h^3S_(1,N)^2|w_N|^2/160
 =h^3|nu|^2pi^2rho^2/40.
```

Therefore, with the scalar normalization `E_aa=2R_aa/|nu|^2`,

```text
|E_aa|<h^3pi^2rho^2/20.                          (11.219.7)
```

Now use `pi^2<10`, (11.219.3), the same decreasing majorant, and
`A_T>14300`:

```text
|E_aa|/(rho A_T)
 <10h^3{(L+9)/6}/(20*14300)
 =(L+9)h^3/171600
 <1/22880.                                       (11.219.8)
```

Combining (11.219.5) and (11.219.8) proves the common-unit terminal budget

```text
|E_term+E_aa|
 <{1/68640+1/22880}rho A_T
 =rho A_T/17160.                                 (11.219.9)
```

This estimate preserves the ownership distinction: `E_term` is the ideal
terminal/nonterminal transpose survivor, whereas `E_aa` is the pure terminal
quadratic row.  They are bounded together only after each has been included
once.

Let

```text
E_sec^*=E_R+E_Delta+E_aff+E_move+E_quad.         (11.219.10)
```

At an adverse witness, if `|E_sec^*|<=delta_*rho A_T`, the budget lemma
(11.218.12) and (11.219.9) force

```text
E_F<-[98/100-delta_*-1/17160]rho A_T.            (11.219.11)
```

Thus two of the seven secondary packages are now closed in anchor units.
The remaining five are exactly the paired remote, physical correction,
fixed affine, moving-tail, and nonterminal quadratic packages.  No estimate
for their sum is inferred from (11.219.9).

Every `pi` in this section is inherited through `kappa=1/(2pi i)`, the
terminal carrier, and the already proved anchor.  The displayed budget uses
only `pi>3`, `pi^2<10`, and exact rational arithmetic.

This section proves a common-unit `1/17160` bound for the two terminal

## 11.220 Full-phase pairing makes the ideal remote package anchor-small

The cosine estimate (11.193.10) differentiates the oscillatory factor
`e(alpha_Plog u)` as part of its amplitude and therefore exposes powers of
`alpha_P`.  For the genuinely remote modes this is avoidable.  Keeping the
full phases `alpha_Plog u-ku` and `alpha_Plog u+ku` through the two
integrations by parts gives a common-cutoff estimate in which the first
endpoint denominators cancel to order `k^(-2)`.

Write `alpha=alpha_P`, `n=n_N=floor(2alpha)`, and

```text
A(u)=exp(S(log u))P(log u),

q_-(u)=alpha/u-k,              q_+(u)=alpha/u+k,

k>n.                                             (11.220.1)
```

Then `k>2alpha`, so, for `1<=u<=N`,

```text
|q_-|>k/2,                    q_+>k.
```

The first endpoint denominators pair exactly:

```text
1/q_-+1/q_+
 =2(alpha/u)/{(alpha/u)^2-k^2},

|1/q_-+1/q_+|
 <=8alpha/(3u k^2).                              (11.220.2)
```

Since `alpha>2`, one has `n>3alpha/2`, and integral comparison gives

```text
sum_(k=n+1)^infinity 1/k^2<1/n,

alpha/n<2/3.                                     (11.220.3)
```

Using `|kappa|<1/6`, the paired first-boundary contribution at both integer
endpoints is consequently bounded by

```text
(8/27){|A(1)|+|A(N)|}.                           (11.220.4)
```

It remains to bound the second boundary and interior without restoring the
large oscillatory derivative.  The exact formula (11.182.12)--(11.182.13)
uses derivatives of `A`, not of `e(alpha log u)A`.  Put

```text
R=(L+3)/2.
```

For `P=P_H^0` or `P_T^0`, the physical inequalities
`|log(u/a)|< (L+1)/2`, `u_N<1`, and `u_(N,x)<1/24` give

```text
|P|<R^3/2,              |P'|<R^2,

|P''|<2R.                                       (11.220.5)
```

On the same interval, `S<=0` and `|S'|<1`.  Direct logarithmic
differentiation therefore gives the convenient uniform bounds

```text
|A(u)|<R^3/2,

|A'(u)|<R^3/u,

|A''(u)|<2R^3/u^2.                               (11.220.6)
```

For completeness, the last line follows from

```text
A''(u)=exp(S)/u^2{
 P''+(2g-1)P'+(g^2-g+t/2)P},       g=S'(log u),
```

using `|2g-1|<3`, `|g^2-g+t/2|<9/4`, and `R>26`.

In the second endpoint of (11.182.12), the two denominator bounds give

```text
sum_(signs)|(D_(sign k)A)/q_(sign k)|
 <=k^(-2){5|A'|+(9/2)|A|/u^2}.                  (11.220.7)
```

For the interior operator, use `|q'|=alpha/u^2`,
`|q''|=2alpha/u^3`, and `alpha/k<1/2`.  The paired integrand is bounded by

```text
k^(-2){
 5|A''|+(27/2)|A'|/u
 +(9/u^3+51/(4u^4))|A|}.                         (11.220.8)
```

Equations (11.220.6)--(11.220.8), integrated on `[1,N]`, give constants

```text
second boundaries <(29/2)R^3,

interior <(223/8)R^3.
```

After multiplication by `|kappa|^2<1/36` and summation using (11.220.3),
the total second-boundary-plus-interior remainder for one polynomial is

```text
<339R^3/(288alpha).                              (11.220.9)
```

For both ideal polynomials together it is below
`339R^3/(144alpha)`.  The physical chart has `alpha>a^2/2` and
`a^2>exp L>2^L`.  Moreover `R^3 2^(-L)` decreases for `L>=50`, because
`3/(L+3)<1/2<log 2`; at `L=50`, `R<27` and `27^3<2^15`.  Hence

```text
339R^3/(144alpha)
 <339R^3h^2/72
 <5/2^35
 <1.                                             (11.220.10)
```

We now compare the first boundary with the transpose anchor.  Put

```text
c_H=b d^2/4,             c_T=d b^2/4,

A_T=D_Nc_T/pi.
```

The ideal endpoint values give

```text
|A_(P_H^0)(1)|=c_H,                 A_(P_H^0)(N)=0,

|A_(P_T^0)(1)|<=c_T+u_(N,x)d,

|A_(P_T^0)(N)|<=2u_Nu_(N,x).                   (11.220.11)
```

Here `A_(P_H^0)` and `A_(P_T^0)` are the amplitudes associated with the two
ideal coefficient polynomials.  Since `b>24`, `d>25`,
`u_(N,x)<1/24`, and `u_N<2h<2`,

```text
u_(N,x)d+2u_Nu_(N,x)<c_T/1000.                  (11.220.12)
```

Also

```text
c_H/c_T=d/b=1+2u_N/b<7/6,

pi/D_N<4pi/L<44/175.                            (11.220.13)
```

Substitution of (11.220.11)--(11.220.13) into (11.220.4) shows that the
sum of the two first-boundary budgets, divided by `A_T`, is below

```text
(8/27)(6503/3000)(44/175).                      (11.220.14)
```

The exact rational comparison

```text
(8/27)(6503/3000)(44/175)+1/14300<1/6           (11.220.15)
```

combines (11.220.10), `A_T>14300`, and the first boundary.  Therefore the
two common-cutoff ideal remote tails satisfy

```text
|mathscr C_N[P_H^0]|+|mathscr C_N[P_T^0]|
 <A_T/6.                                         (11.220.16)
```

The actual-source projection now costs only `|tau_0|=rho` and
`|eta^2|=1`, so

```text
|E_R|<rho A_T/6.                                 (11.220.17)
```

This estimate does not split either one-sided remote series.  The
`k^(-1)` endpoint terms cancel in (11.220.2) under the same common cutoff
that defines `mathscr C_N`.

Combining (11.220.17) with the terminal budget (11.219.9), put

```text
E_four=E_Delta+E_aff+E_move+E_quad.
```

If `|E_four|<=delta_4rho A_T`, adverse-witness negativity forces

## 11.221 Contiguous-kernel control makes the physical correction anchor-small

Section 11.220 leaves `E_Delta` open because the coefficient-relative tail
estimate of Section 11.176 contains an uncontrolled retained row norm.  The
later terminal factorization permits a different route.  The correction
polynomials `Delta_H,Delta_T` depend only on the explicit physical coefficient
fields, and their complete finite-plus-outer functionals can be returned to a
finite contiguous Fourier roster before taking a modulus.

Work on the fixed physical `q=1` chart.  Put

```text
ell=log a,        b=log N,        u=u_N=ell-b,

x=lambda-ell,    R_*=(L+3)/2,

K=(L+70)^2,      J=(L+130)^2,     epsilon=h^2K. (11.221.1)
```

For `0<=lambda<=b`, one has `|x|<L`, `u<2h<1`, and `R_*>53/2`.
The coefficient envelopes (11.174.15) and rate envelopes
(11.175.4)--(11.175.6) give

```text
|C-1|<epsilon,                  |C_N-1|<epsilon,

|D|,|D_N|<epsilon/1000,

|R-ix/2|,|R_N+iu/2|<epsilon/6000,

|R_x+iu_(N,x)/2|,
|R_(N,x)+iu_(N,x)/2|<epsilon/1000,

|delta-conjugate(delta)|<epsilon/1000,

epsilon<1/1000.                                  (11.221.2)
```

Here `C_N,D_N,R_N,R_(N,x)` are the terminal evaluations.  For example,

```text
|C-1|<h^2{4379+L/4+L^2/16}<h^2K,

|D|<h^4{16893+5L/16+L^2/16}<h^4J,

|R-ix/2|<h^2(L+2)/6000.
```

Since `J<3K`, `h<1/72000000000`, and `K>=14400`, these imply all of
(11.221.2).  In particular, no retained observation-row norm occurs.

The two exact terminal factorizations can be treated simultaneously.  In
the transpose channel set

```text
G=C_NC,                  z=R-R_N,

w=R_x+R_(N,x),          d=0,

H=C_ND-D_NC,
```

and in the Hermitian channel set

```text
G=conjugate(C_N)C,       z=R-conjugate(R_N),

w=R_x+conjugate(R_(N,x)),

d=delta-conjugate(delta),

H=conjugate(C_N)D-conjugate(D_N)C.
```

Equations (11.187.2)--(11.187.3) then have the common form

```text
B=G(z^2+zd+w)+zH.                                (11.221.3)
```

For the transpose channel the ideal values are

```text
z_0=i(x+u)/2,        w_0=-iu_(N,x),       d_0=H_0=0,
```

whereas for the Hermitian channel they are

```text
z_0=i(x-u)/2,        w_0=d_0=H_0=0.
```

Thus `B^0=z_0^2+w_0`.  The boxes (11.221.2) imply

```text
|z_0|<R_*-1,              |z|<R_*,

|G-1|<(2001/1000)epsilon, |G|<1003/1000,

|z-z_0|<epsilon/3000,     |w-w_0|<epsilon/500,

|d|<epsilon/1000,         |H|<3epsilon/1000.     (11.221.4)
```

Subtracting the ideal form in (11.221.3), before estimating either channel
separately, gives

```text
|B-B^0|/(epsilon R_*^2)

 <2001/1000
  +(1003/1000){1/(1500R_*)+1/(1000R_*)
                         +1/(500R_*^2)}
  +3/(1000R_*)

 <=8431968331/4213500000
 <3.                                               (11.221.5)
```

The middle `1/(1000R_*)` term is absent in the transpose channel, but
retaining it gives one valid common bound.  Consequently

```text
|Delta B_H|,|Delta B_T|<3epsilon R_*^2,

|Delta_H|,|Delta_T|<6epsilon R_*^3=:P_*,          (11.221.6)
```

because the two relative lifts have modulus below `2R_*` on `[0,b]`.
The same estimate gives

```text
|Delta B_(T,N)|<3epsilon R_*^2.                  (11.221.7)
```

It remains to estimate the complete linear functionals without using the
large pointwise height of the reciprocal Dirichlet kernel.  For any one of
the correction polynomials, (11.193.2) gives the exact identity

```text
mathscr M_N[P]+mathscr O_N[P]
 =2mathscr M_N[P]-mathscr F_N[P].                (11.221.8)
```

Let `m` be the number of consecutive frequencies in `mathcal R_N`.  Up to a
unit phase, its kernel on one unit interval is

```text
K_m(v)=sum_(j=0)^(m-1)e(jv),

|K_m(v)|=|sin(pi m v)|/|sin(pi v)|.
```

For `0<=v<=1/2`, concavity gives `sin(pi v)>=2v`, and hence

```text
|K_m(v)|<=min(m,1/(2v)).
```

Splitting at `v=1/(2m)` and using symmetry proves the exact unit-period
Lebesgue bound

```text
integral_0^1|K_m(v)|dv<=1+log m.                 (11.221.9)
```

This is the decisive gain: the cost is logarithmic in the roster length,
not its height.  Since

```text
m<=2alpha_P<=2a^2,       N<=a=h^(-1),

1+log m<2+2L<3L,
```

and `S(lambda)<=0` on the `q=1` interval, (11.221.9) gives

```text
|mathscr M_N[P]|<P_*/h,

|mathscr F_N[P]|<3LP_*/h.                       (11.221.10)
```

Applying (11.221.8) to both correction channels therefore yields

```text
2{|mathscr M_N[Delta_H]|+|mathscr M_N[Delta_T]|}
 +|mathscr F_N[Delta_H]|+|mathscr F_N[Delta_T]|

 <(4+6L)P_*/h
 =6hK R_*^3(4+6L)

 <=8485989/1250000
 <679/100.                                        (11.221.11)
```

For completeness, the right side decreases for `L>=50`: after replacing
`h` by `exp(-L/2)`, its logarithmic derivative is

```text
-1/2+2/(L+70)+3/(L+3)+6/(4+6L)<0.
```

The rational value in (11.221.11) is the endpoint evaluation at `L=50`
using `h<1/72000000000`.

The transpose terminal correction is smaller still.  By the definition of
`rho` and (11.221.7),

```text
|mathcal T_N^[N][Delta B_(T,N)]|
 =rho|Delta B_(T,N)|.
```

Using `u<2h` and the corrected logarithmic estimate
`rho<(L+9)/6` from (11.219.3) gives

```text
2u|mathcal T_N^[N][Delta B_(T,N)]|
 <2(L+9)h^3K R_*^2
 <1/1000.                                         (11.221.12)
```

The corresponding exponential majorant also decreases from `L=50`: its
logarithmic derivative is

```text
1/(L+9)-3/2+2/(L+70)+2/(L+3)<0,
```

and the endpoint test uses `h<1/72000000000`, `K=120^2`, and
`R_*=53/2`.
Combining (11.221.8)--(11.221.12) with the exact definition (11.218.7)
proves

```text
|E_Delta|<7rho.
```

Finally `A_T>14300` and `7/14300<1/2000`, so the physical correction has
the common-unit budget

```text
|E_Delta|<rho A_T/2000.                          (11.221.13)
```

This estimate does not use the optional row norm `R` of Section 11.176.
It first bounds the explicit terminal coefficient perturbation and then
uses the complete contiguous Fourier roster.  It therefore does not promote
coefficient smallness without controlling its multiplying functional.

Put

```text
E_three=E_aff+E_move+E_quad.
```

If `|E_three|<=delta_3rho A_T`, the adverse-witness finite-package target is

```text
E_F<-[98/100-delta_3-1/6-1/17160-1/2000]rho A_T

   =-[697361/858000-delta_3]rho A_T.             (11.221.14)
```

Thus only the fixed affine, moving-tail, and nonterminal quadratic packages

The `pi` in (11.221.9) is not inserted geometrically.  It comes from the
already fixed Fourier character `e(v)=exp(2pi i v)` through the finite
geometric-sum identity.  All other `pi` factors remain inherited through

This section proves a common-unit `rho A_T/2000` bound for the complete

## 11.222 Edge-only affine ownership and signed-main reclassification

The full-support transfer in Section 11.181 changes the ownership of the
external linear row.  This must be propagated through Sections 11.185--11.186
before estimating the package called `E_aff`.  The complete frozen terminal
row decomposes as

```text
t_T=2Jomega_T
   =2Jomega_E+2Jomega_C(Omega)
   =t_E+t_C.                                      (11.222.1)
```

But `omega_C` is already part of the moving all-carrier moment vector `Y` in
(11.181.9)--(11.181.10).  Using `t_T` again as the external row would add
`t_C^Tdot(epsilon)` a second time.  Therefore the unique full-support affine
owner is

```text
t_E=2Jomega_E
   =(mathcal N_E,V_E,-Q_E,-A_E)^T
```

when it is read as a coefficient row acting on
`dot(epsilon)=(dot epsilon_V,dot epsilon_mathcal N,
dot epsilon_A,dot epsilon_Q)^T`.  This is the corrected ownership used in
(11.185.14).

The row has one exact polynomial compression.  Put

```text
beta_E=(mathcal N_E,V_E,-Q_E,-A_E),

P_E(lambda)=i(lambda-log a)F_(beta_E)(lambda).    (11.222.2)
```

Linearity of the full-support complement and (11.186.5) give

```text
R_aff:=t_E^Tdot(epsilon)
 =Re{nu c_xi mathscr O_N[P_E]}.                   (11.222.3)
```

Thus this package is already contained once in the `beta_E` part of
`P_lin^[N]`.  If it is displayed separately, the remaining linear polynomial
must use `beta_p=beta_N-beta_E`; `P_E` must not also remain inside that
remainder.

At the physical frequency `c_xi=1`, the common scalar normalization of
Section 11.218 and the actual-source identity
`nu=omega_c/(B_0T_0)`, `|omega_c|=1`, give

```text
E_aff=2R_aff/|nu|^2
     =2Re{mathscr O_N[P_E]/conjugate(nu)}
     =2B_0T_0 Re{omega_c mathscr O_N[P_E]}.       (11.222.4)
```

Equation (11.222.4) fixes the source phase and scale; there is no free affine
phase.  The full-support identity also fixes its arithmetic support:

```text
mathscr O_N[P_E]
 =mathscr N_N[P_E]+mathscr C_N[P_E]
 =mathscr M_N[P_E]-mathscr F_N[P_E].              (11.222.5)
```

In particular, the factor `u_N` in the terminal trace (11.182.20) suppresses
that endpoint only.  It is not a factor of the near component or of the
complete polynomial functional.

The correction-free polynomial shows why an absolute-smallness
classification cannot be made from the affine coefficient alone.  Write
`x=lambda-log a` and `u_x=u_(N,x)`.  On the ideal chart,

```text
C^0=1,                A^0=Q^0=ix/2,

mathcal N^0=-x^2/4-iu_x/2.
```

Substitution into (11.222.2) gives the exact cubic

```text
P_E^0(x)
 =-iV_E x^3/4+(A_E+Q_E)x^2/2
   +(V_Eu_x/2+i mathcal N_E)x.                   (11.222.6)
```

The cubic coefficient is present on an actual recurring source fibre.  At
the half-integer saddle `p=0`, evenness gives `C_0'''(0)=0`, so
`H_a(0)=C_0(0)`.  With `tau=1+i/T_0`,

```text
V_E=Re{tau H_a(0)},

C_0(0)=sqrt(2-sqrt 2)/4
       +i{sqrt(2+sqrt 2)/4-sqrt 2/2}.
```

The imaginary part is negative, while
`sqrt(2-sqrt 2)/4>3/16`; hence

```text
V_E>3/16,          |[x^3]P_E^0|>3/64             (11.222.7)
```

on every such physical midpoint.  This does not prove that the complete
functional is large, because its near and paired-remote pieces can cancel.
It does prove that `E_aff` is not certified perturbative by an `h^2`
coefficient envelope.  Its leading polynomial is on the same cubic scale as
the two ideal carrier polynomials and must initially remain signed.

Accordingly define the signed finite-affine package

```text
E_FA:=E_F+E_aff.                                  (11.222.8)
```

The already closed secondary packages satisfy

```text
|E_R+E_term+E_aa+E_Delta|
 <=(1/6+1/17160+1/2000)rho A_T
 =143479rho A_T/858000.                           (11.222.9)
```

If the two still unbounded absolute-secondary packages obey

```text
|E_move+E_quad|<=delta_2rho A_T,
```

then adverse-witness negativity necessarily requires

```text
E_FA<-[697361/858000-delta_2]rho A_T.             (11.222.10)
```

This is a reclassification, not a bound for `E_aff`.  The next admissible
stage is to split (11.222.5) with common cutoff ownership, compose its near
part with `E_F`, and test whether the paired-remote affine part is
anchor-small after the exact source factor in (11.222.4).  Only then should
one decide whether any remainder of `E_aff` can return to an absolute budget.

Every `pi` in this section is inherited through the completed-zeta endpoint,
`e(v)=exp(2pi i v)`, `kappa=1/(2pi i)`, and the already fixed source
normalizer.  No geometric constant is introduced.

This section proves edge-only affine ownership, one exact full-support
polynomial compression, its physical source normalization, the ideal cubic
and a recurring non-suppression witness, and the signed finite-affine target.
It proves no absolute affine, moving-tail, or quadratic budget, no signed
finite-affine inequality, complete-current sign, all-`q` transport,
contact exclusion, `Q209`, cofinal successor, `Lambda<=0`, PF-infinity, RH,
or prize-level conclusion.

## 11.223 Source-normalized affine paired-remote budget

Section 11.222 deliberately kept the whole affine package signed because its
ideal cubic has an unsuppressed coefficient.  That classification can now be
sharpened without taking a modulus across the near/remote composition.  Keep
the symmetric cutoff in (11.222.5) and define

```text
E_aff^N=2B_0T_0 Re{omega_c mathscr N_N[P_E]},

E_aff^C=2B_0T_0 Re{omega_c mathscr C_N[P_E]}.
```

Then

```text
E_aff=E_aff^N+E_aff^C.                           (11.223.1)
```

The first point is that the physical source factor in (11.223.1) has a
uniform bound in terminal-anchor units.  From the definitions of `B_0` and
`beta`, the corrected Riemann--Siegel normalizer floor, and `|f_1|>1/2`,

```text
B_0T_0
 <8sqrt(pi)
   exp{tpi^2/64-pi T_0/4+pi X/8}
   (T_0/X)^(3/2)X^(-1/4).                       (11.223.2)
```

On the physical `q=1` chart,

```text
t=1/(2L^2),             T_0=X/2+pi/(16L^2),

tpi^2/64-pi T_0/4+pi X/8=-pi^2/(128L^2)<0.
```

The established elementary bounds

```text
sqrt(pi)<9/5,       (T_0/X)^(3/2)<3/8,

X^(-1/4)<(5/9)exp(-L/4)
```

therefore give

```text
B_0T_0<3exp(-L/4).                               (11.223.3)
```

In the opposite direction, (11.184.11) and the physical terminal exponent
give

```text
S_(1,N)>L-3>=(47/50)L,

|E_N|>(2/3)exp(-L/4).
```

Since `rho=S_(1,N)|E_N|/(2pi)` and `1/(2pi)>7/44`,

```text
rho>(329/3300)L exp(-L/4).                       (11.223.4)
```

Combining (11.223.3)--(11.223.4), with `L>=50`, proves the exact source
comparison

```text
B_0T_0/rho<198/329<61/100.                       (11.223.5)
```

We next bound the genuine edge row, with the moved terminal carrier still
excluded as required by Section 11.222.  Retain `tau=1+i/T_0`,
`J=H_x+mu H`, and the radial coefficient `alpha_c` from (11.149.18).  The
endpoint-only formulas are

```text
V_E=Re(tau H),

Q_E=Re(tau_xH+tau H_x),

A_E=Re(tau J)-alpha_cV_E,

mathcal N_E=Re(tau_xJ+tau J_x)
            -alpha_(c,x)V_E-alpha_cQ_E.          (11.223.6)
```

Substitution of the certified endpoint source and jet bounds

```text
|H-F|<86h,                       |H_x|<3h,

|J+hF'/(4pi)|<236h^2,

|J_x-h^2F''/(16pi^2)|<810h^3,

|mu|<h^2,                        |mu_x|<h^4,

|Re(s_*')|<h^2/20000,            |s_*''|<h^4/40000
```

into (11.223.6), using `h<1/72000000000`, yields

```text
|V_E|<3/5,       |A_E|<4h,       |Q_E|<4h,

|mathcal N_E|<4h^2.                              (11.223.7)
```

Put `x=lambda-log a` and `R_*=(L+3)/2`.  For the ideal observation fields,
the polynomial (11.222.6) and (11.223.7) imply, throughout

```text
|P_E^0|<R_*^3/6,

|(P_E^0)'|<R_*^2/2,

|(P_E^0)''|<R_*.                                 (11.223.8)
```

For example, after division by the indicated powers of `R_*`, the three
left sides are bounded by

```text
3/20+4h/R_*+(321/80)h^2/R_*^2,

9/20+8h/R_*+(321/80)h^2/R_*^2,

9/10+8h/R_*,
```

which are respectively below `1/6`, `1/2`, and `1` at `L>=50`.

Remove only the full oscillatory phase and set

```text
A_E^0(u)=exp(S(log u))P_E^0(log u).
```

As in Section 11.220, `S<=0`, `|S'|<1`, and direct logarithmic

```text
|A_E^0(u)|<R_*^3/6,
```

The second derivative here is the exact identity

```text
 =exp(S)/u^2{P''+(2g-1)P'+(g^2-g+t/2)P},

g=S'(log u),
```

not a differentiation of the large phase `alpha log u` into the amplitude.

Apply the full-phase paired integrations by parts of Section 11.220 to this

```text
8R_*^3/81.                                       (11.223.10)
```

The two second boundaries cost at most `7R_*^3/2`, while the paired interior

```text
7R_*^3/2+799R_*^3/120=1219R_*^3/120.
```

After `|kappa|^2<1/36` and the common-cutoff `k^(-2)` summation, this is

```text
<1219R_*^3/(4320alpha)<1.                        (11.223.11)
```

The final inequality follows from `alpha>a^2/2`, `a^2>exp L`, and the same

```text
A_T>(7/2816)L^2(L-2)^2,
```

```text
 -(L+3)^3/81-1
```

```text
|mathscr C_N[P_E^0]|<13A_T/100.                 (11.223.12)
```

```text
epsilon=h^2(L+70)^2
```

and write `P_E=P_E^0+Delta_E`.  The boxes of (11.221.2), restricted to the

```text
|Delta_E|<epsilon R_*^3/6=:P_*.                 (11.223.14)
```

```text
|mathscr M_N[Delta_E]|<P_*/h,

|mathscr F_N[Delta_E]|<3LP_*/h,

|mathscr N_N[Delta_E]|<3LP_*/h.
```

Because `mathscr C_N=mathscr M_N-mathscr F_N-mathscr N_N`,

```text
 <(1+6L)epsilon R_*^3/(6h)<1/5.                 (11.223.15)
```

At `L=50`, the middle expression is at most

```text
44811977/240000000<1/5,
```

using `h<1/72000000000`; its logarithmic derivative is bounded by

Now (11.223.5) and the exact source normalization in (11.223.1) give the

```text
|E_aff^C|
 <2(61/100)(131/1000)rho A_T
 =(7991/50000)rho A_T
 <(4/25)rho A_T.                                (11.223.17)
```

The affine near term is not bounded by (11.223.17).  Define instead the
common-cutoff signed package

```text
E_FAN=E_F+E_aff^N.                               (11.223.18)
```

The five now-closed absolute secondary packages satisfy

```text
|E_R+E_term+E_aa+E_Delta+E_aff^C|
 <(1/6+1/17160+1/2000+4/25)rho A_T
 =(280759/858000)rho A_T.                       (11.223.19)
```

Consequently, if the two remaining absolute packages obey

```text
|E_move+E_quad|<=delta_2rho A_T,
```

then adverse-witness negativity necessarily requires

```text
E_FAN<-[560081/858000-delta_2]rho A_T.           (11.223.20)
```

Thus the unsuppressed affine cubic has not been declared small.  Only its
common-cutoff paired-remote image has returned to the absolute budget; its
near image stays composed with `E_F` before any modulus is taken.

Every `pi` in this section is inherited from the completed-zeta endpoint,
the Fourier character `e(v)=exp(2pi i v)`, `kappa=1/(2pi i)`, and the fixed
source normalizer.  The rational surrogates for `pi` only certify displayed
inequalities; no geometric constant is inserted.

This section proves the fixed-`q=1` source-scale comparison, the genuine-edge
coefficient box, the common-cutoff affine paired-remote budget
`|E_aff^C|<4rho A_T/25`, and the resulting signed near-affine target.  It

## 11.224 Source-free observation envelopes make the moving tail perturbative

Section 11.181 identified the complete moving-tail defect but correctly did
not infer a current bound from the motion of one terminal atom.  The missing
input is now available: all four physical observation fields can be bounded
before they are summed, while the actual source scale is kept visible.  This
gives a deliberately loose common-unit estimate with a large safety margin.

Write

```text
varepsilon=T_0-Omega,       xi_theta=T_0-theta varepsilon,

Delta omega_C(xi)=omega_C(xi)-omega_C(Omega).
```

Retaining the observation order and matrix in (11.181.1), define

```text
D_move(xi)
 =2Delta omega_C(xi)^T J dot(omega_B)(xi)

  +2[omega_E+omega_B(xi)+omega_C(xi)]^T
       J dot(omega_C)(xi).                         (11.224.1)
```

This is exactly `tilde(Psi)'-Psi_B'` from (11.181.8).  Comparing the two
physical transfer identities therefore fixes the package, including its
sign:

```text
R_move=-varepsilon integral_0^1D_move(xi_theta)dtheta,

E_move=2R_move/|nu|^2.                             (11.224.2)
```

The later relative-lift and quadratic decompositions explicitly leave
(11.224.1) outside their packages.  Thus (11.224.2) is inserted once at the
observation level; it repeats neither the pure terminal row nor any of the
four nonterminal quadratic pairings.

We first derive a source-free carrier envelope.  For

```text
q_n=exp{t(log n)^2/4-sigma log n},
```

the physical `q=1` chart gives `sigma>1/2`,
`t=1/(2L^2)`, and `log n<log a<(L+1)/2`.  Hence
`t(log n)^2/4<1/8`.  Since
`log(8/7)=-log(1-1/8)>1/8`,

```text
q_n<(8/7)n^(-1/2).                                 (11.224.3)
```

Put `R_*=(L+3)/2` and use `epsilon_c=h^2(L+70)^2` for the coefficient error,
reserving `varepsilon` for the physical frequency gap.  Equations
(11.221.2), (11.223.13), and `|delta|<4h^2` give, on
`0<=lambda<=log N`,

```text
|C|<1001/1000,             |R|<R_*/2,

|A|,|Q|<3R_*/5,            |mathcal N|<R_*^2/2.
                                                        (11.224.4)
```

For completeness, `|lambda-log a|<R_*-1` and
`|R-i(lambda-log a)/2|<epsilon_c/6000` prove the second bound.  Also
`|delta|,|D|<epsilon_c/1000` and

```text
|R_x|<h^2/48+epsilon_c/1000<1/500000.
```

Substitution into the exact identities
`A=RC`, `Q=(R+delta)C+D`, and
`mathcal N=RQ+R_xC` gives the last two bounds in (11.224.4).  The endpoint
checks are strict already at `R_*=53/2`.  Since the value field is `V=C`,
all four carrier observation polynomials obey

```text
|P_X(lambda)|<P_*:=R_*^2/2,
             X in {V,mathcal N,A,Q}.              (11.224.5)
```

Let

```text
S_0=sum_(n<=N)q_n,             S_1=sum_(n<=N)u_nq_n.
```

The elementary integral bound
`sum_(n<=N)n^(-1/2)<2sqrt(N)`, together with `N<a=h^(-1)` and
`0<=u_n<=log a<R_*`, yields

```text
S_0<(16/7)h^(-1/2),

S_1<(16/7)R_*h^(-1/2).                          (11.224.6)
```

For the terminal block put

```text
T_1=sum_(B<n<=N)u_nq_n,             K=M+1.
```

The growing-prefix condition is `K^18<=a`.  Since `K>=2`, it implies
`2K<=a`.  As `B=N-K` and `a=N+theta`, every terminal carrier has
`n>=a-K>=a/2`.  Equations (11.181.22) and (11.224.3) then give

```text
q_n<2h^(1/2),        u_n<2hK,

T_1<4h^(3/2)K^2.                                  (11.224.7)
```

The auxiliary rotation changes only the carrier phase.  Each real
observation coordinate is the real part of the common source `nu`, a unit
phase, `q_n`, and one polynomial from (11.224.5).  Consequently, uniformly
on the physical auxiliary segment,

```text
||omega_B+omega_C||_infinity <=|nu|P_*S_0,

||dot(omega_B)||_infinity    <=|nu|P_*S_1,

||dot(omega_C)||_infinity    <=|nu|P_*T_1,

||Delta omega_C||_infinity
             <=varepsilon|nu|P_*T_1.              (11.224.8)
```

The last line follows either by integrating `dot(omega_C)` or directly from
`|exp(iv)-1|<=|v|`.  The genuine edge estimate (11.223.7) also gives
`||omega_E||_infinity<3/5`.

For the fixed matrix `J`, direct expansion gives

```text
|2x^TJy|<=4||x||_infinity||y||_infinity.          (11.224.9)
```

Applying (11.224.8)--(11.224.9) to the two terms in (11.224.1) proves the
pointwise estimate

```text
|D_move|
 <4varepsilon|nu|^2P_*^2T_1S_1
  +4|nu|^2P_*^2S_0T_1
  +(12/5)|nu|P_*T_1.                              (11.224.10)
```

Now integrate (11.224.10), use (11.224.2), and insert
`1/|nu|=B_0T_0`:

```text
|E_move|
 <8varepsilon P_*^2(varepsilon T_1S_1+S_0T_1)
  +(24/5)varepsilon P_*(B_0T_0)T_1.               (11.224.11)
```

With `varepsilon<7h^2/(8L^2)`, (11.224.6)--(11.224.7), and
`P_*=R_*^2/2`, this becomes

```text
|E_move|
 <16h^3R_*^4K^2/L^2
  +14h^5R_*^5K^2/L^4
  +(42/5)(B_0T_0)h^(7/2)R_*^2K^2/L^2.            (11.224.12)
```

The prefix condition gives `K^2<=h^(-1/9)`.  For the first two terms use

```text
rho>(329/3300)Lexp(-L/4),       A_T>14300,

exp(L/4)<h^(-1/2),
```

and for the edge term use `B_0T_0/rho<61/100`.  After division by
`rho A_T`, the three respective ratios are strictly below

```text
[52800/(329*14300)] h^(43/18)R_*^4/L^3,

[46200/(329*14300)] h^(79/18)R_*^5/L^5,

[2562/(500*14300)] h^(61/18)R_*^2/L^2.           (11.224.13)
```

Replacing `h` by `exp(-L/2)`, their logarithmic derivatives are

```text
-43/36+4/(L+3)-3/L,

-79/36+5/(L+3)-5/L,

-61/36+2/(L+3)-2/L.                              (11.224.14)
```

All three are negative for `L>=50`.  At the endpoint, the positive Taylor
floor

```text
sum_(j=0)^60 25^j/j!>72000000000
```

proves `exp(-25)<1/72000000000`.  Since
`43/18>2`, `79/18>4`, and `61/18>3`, the endpoint sum is bounded by the exact
rational expression

```text
[52800/(329*14300)](1/72000000000)^2(53/2)^4/50^3

+[46200/(329*14300)](1/72000000000)^4(53/2)^5/50^5

+[2562/(500*14300)](1/72000000000)^3(53/2)^2/50^2

 <1/1000000.                                      (11.224.15)
```

Thus the complete observation-level moving-tail package has the common-unit
budget

```text
|E_move|<rho A_T/1000000.                         (11.224.16)
```

Combining (11.224.16) with (11.223.19) closes six absolute secondary
packages:

```text
|E_R+E_term+E_aa+E_Delta+E_aff^C+E_move|

 <(280759/858000+1/1000000)rho A_T

 =(140379929/429000000)rho A_T.                  (11.224.17)
```

Only `E_quad` remains in the absolute-secondary frontier.  If

```text
|E_quad|<=delta_1rho A_T,
```

then the adverse-witness target is

```text
E_FAN<-[280040071/429000000-delta_1]rho A_T.      (11.224.18)
```

No new geometric `pi` is introduced.  The only `pi`-dependent rate used in
the observation box is `u_(N,x)=h^2/(8pi)`, inherited from the completed-zeta
and Riemann--Siegel saddle coordinate; `pi>3` merely gives a rational upper
bound.

This section proves the fixed-`q=1` source-free observation envelope and the
common-unit moving-tail budget `|E_move|<rho A_T/1000000`.  It proves no
nonterminal quadratic budget, signed finite-near-affine inequality,
complete-current sign, all-`q` transport, contact exclusion, `Q209`, cofinal
successor, `Lambda<=0`, PF-infinity, RH, or prize-level conclusion.

## 11.225 Current/transfer ownership correction and the quadratic determinant primitive

Section 11.224 proves a valid small bound for the moving-tail contribution to
the **integrated transfer**.  The compensation ledger in Section 11.218,
however, is a **pointwise frequency-current** ledger.  Those two objects were
given the same name there.  This section separates them, repairs the
pointwise budget, and then identifies the four nonterminal quadratic
pairings as one exact determinant derivative.

Retain the pointwise moving-tail derivative defect from (11.181.8):

```text
D_move(xi)
 =tilde(Psi)'(xi)-Psi_B'(xi)

 =2Delta omega_C(xi)^TJdot(omega_B)(xi)

  +2[omega_E+omega_B(xi)+omega_C(xi)]^T
       Jdot(omega_C)(xi).                         (11.225.1)
```

For `varepsilon=T_0-Omega` and
`xi_theta=T_0-theta varepsilon`, define two differently typed packages:

```text
R_move^cur:=D_move(Omega),

R_move^tr:=-varepsilon integral_0^1
                  D_move(xi_theta)dtheta,

E_move^cur:=2R_move^cur/|nu|^2,

E_move^tr:=2R_move^tr/|nu|^2.                    (11.225.2)
```

The theorem (11.224.16) remains valid, with its package now written
unambiguously as

```text
|E_move^tr|<rho A_T/1000000.                     (11.225.3)
```

It does not bound `E_move^cur`.  In particular, the use of (11.224.16) in
the pointwise current sum (11.224.17)--(11.224.18) is superseded by the
calculation below.  No mathematical content of the integrated-transfer
estimate is discarded.

At the physical point `xi=Omega`, one has
`Delta omega_C(Omega)=0`.  Hence (11.225.1) reduces exactly to

```text
R_move^cur
 =2[omega_E+omega_B(Omega)+omega_C(Omega)]^T
      Jdot(omega_C)(Omega).                       (11.225.4)
```

Use the source-free envelopes (11.224.5)--(11.224.9):

```text
P_*=R_*^2/2,                 R_*=(L+3)/2,

S_0<(16/7)h^(-1/2),         T_1<4h^(3/2)K^2,

||omega_B+omega_C||_infinity<=|nu|P_*S_0,

||dot(omega_C)||_infinity<=|nu|P_*T_1,

||omega_E||_infinity<3/5.
```

The fixed `J` bilinear therefore gives

```text
|E_move^cur|
 <8P_*^2S_0T_1+(24/5)(B_0T_0)P_*T_1

 <(128/7)hR_*^4K^2
   +(48/5)(B_0T_0)h^(3/2)R_*^2K^2.               (11.225.5)
```

There is no transfer factor `varepsilon` in (11.225.5).  This is the
pointwise current bound required by (11.218.8).

Now use

```text
K^2<=h^(-1/9),

rho>(329/3300)Lexp(-L/4),

exp(L/4)<h^(-1/2),

B_0T_0/rho<61/100,             A_T>14300.
```

After division by `rho A_T`, the two terms in (11.225.5) are strictly below

```text
[422400/(7*329*14300)]h^(7/18)R_*^4/L,

[2928/(5*100*14300)]h^(25/18)R_*^2.              (11.225.6)
```

Replacing `h` by `exp(-L/2)`, their logarithmic derivatives are

```text
-7/36+4/(L+3)-1/L,

-25/36+2/(L+3),                                  (11.225.7)
```

both negative for `L>=50`.  At the left endpoint, the established Taylor
floor gives `h<1/72000000000`.  The exact integer comparison

```text
(72000000000)^7>13000^18
```

implies `h^(7/18)<1/13000`, while
`h^(25/18)<h`.  Substitution of `R_*=53/2` and `L=50` into (11.225.6) gives

```text
[422400/(7*329*14300)](53/2)^4/(50*13000)

 +[2928/(5*100*14300)](53/2)^2/72000000000

 <1/100.                                          (11.225.8)
```

Thus the corrected pointwise moving-current budget is

```text
|E_move^cur|<rho A_T/100.                         (11.225.9)
```

Combining (11.225.9) with the five-package pointwise budget (11.223.19)
gives

```text
|E_R+E_term+E_aa+E_Delta+E_aff^C+E_move^cur|

 <(280759/858000+1/100)rho A_T

 =(289339/858000)rho A_T.                        (11.225.10)
```

We next resolve the remaining quadratic ownership.  To avoid collision with
the positive anchor `rho=|tau_0|`, rename the nonterminal real observation
remainder in the split `epsilon=a+rho` of (11.185.9) as

```text
e=(e_V,e_mathcalN,e_A,e_Q)^T,

dot e=(e_(V,xi),e_(mathcalN,xi),
       e_(A,xi),e_(Q,xi))^T.                      (11.225.11)
```

All physical coefficient rows remain fixed on the auxiliary `xi` segment,
so (11.165.1)--(11.165.5) give `dot e=partial_xi e`.  The four constituents
of the normalized nonterminal quadratic current are therefore

```text
E_quad^cur
 =(2/|nu|^2){
      e_Ve_(mathcalN,xi)+e_mathcalNe_(V,xi)
     -e_Ae_(Q,xi)-e_Qe_(A,xi)}.                  (11.225.12)
```

Define the normalized determinant primitive

```text
Q_quad(xi)
 :=(2/|nu|^2){e_Ve_mathcalN-e_Ae_Q}
   =(2/|nu|^2)e^TJe.                              (11.225.13)
```

Direct differentiation, with no estimate, gives

```text
partial_xi Q_quad=E_quad^cur.                     (11.225.14)
```

Thus the four pairings are not four independent errors.  They are one exact
frequency derivative.

The phase content is equally explicit.  Let `Z_X` be the source-free
complex nonterminal amplitude for observation `X`, after the terminal
conditional amplitude has been removed, and put

```text
U_X=(nu c_xi/|nu|)Z_X.
```

Then `e_X=|nu|Re(U_X)`, and the elementary real-product polarization yields

```text
Q_quad
 =Re{
      U_Vconjugate(U_mathcalN)-U_Aconjugate(U_Q)
     +U_VU_mathcalN-U_AU_Q}.                     (11.225.15)
```

Differentiating (11.225.15) reproduces the Hermitian phase-difference and
transpose phase-sum currents.  The common source phase cancels in the first
family and is squared in the second.  Neither family, nor any imaginary
coefficient, has been discarded.

The integrated transfer now telescopes exactly:

```text
-varepsilon integral_0^1
    E_quad^cur(T_0-theta varepsilon)dtheta

 =Q_quad(Omega)-Q_quad(T_0).                     (11.225.16)
```

Equation (11.225.16) is an ownership reduction, not an endpoint bound.  A
transfer proof must join this determinant difference to
`tilde(Psi)(T_0)` before taking a modulus.  A pointwise-current proof must
instead retain `E_quad^cur` with the signed finite/near package.

The no-double-counting rule is now complete.  The vector `e` contains no
terminal conditional factor `a`.  The `a-a` block is `E_aa`; the mixed
terminal/nonterminal block supplies `E_F,E_R,E_term,E_Delta`; `E_aff` is
linear; and `E_move^cur` is the terminal-motion current defect.  None occurs
in (11.225.12).

For the pointwise route, define

```text
E_main^cur:=E_FAN+E_quad^cur.                     (11.225.17)
```

At an adverse witness, (11.218.10) and (11.225.10) show that negativity
necessarily requires

```text
E_main^cur<-(551501/858000)rho A_T.               (11.225.18)
```

Conversely, the stronger inequality

```text
E_main^cur<-(1130179/858000)rho A_T               (11.225.19)
```

is sufficient independently of the signs of the six bounded packages.
The different constants in (11.225.18)--(11.225.19) are respectively the
necessary and triangle-safe sufficient thresholds; they must not be
interchanged.

The next theorem therefore has two coherent forms.  One may prove or falsify
the signed pointwise inequality for `E_FAN+E_quad^cur` on every adverse
actual-source witness arc.  Alternatively, one may return to the exact
transfer (11.181.23), use (11.225.16), and bound the endpoint determinant
difference jointly with `tilde(Psi)(T_0)`.  A detached absolute
`|E_quad|` budget is no longer assumed.

No new `pi` is introduced.  Every `pi` remains inherited from the
completed-zeta saddle, `e(x)=exp(2pi i x)`, `kappa=1/(2pi i)`, and the
existing source/anchor normalization.

This section separates the pointwise current from the integrated moving-tail
transfer, preserves the valid millionth-scale transfer theorem, proves the
corrected pointwise moving-current budget `rho A_T/100`, repairs the common
pointwise reserve, identifies all four nonterminal quadratic constituents,
proves their determinant primitive and complex polarization, and gives the
two exact next-route formulations.  It proves no signed main inequality,
endpoint determinant bound, complete-current sign, all-`q` transport,
contact exclusion, `Q209`, cofinal successor, `Lambda<=0`, PF-infinity, RH,
or prize-level conclusion.

## 11.226 Quadratic residual closure in the two-carrier kernel

Section 11.225 identifies the four nonterminal quadratic pairings as the
derivative of one determinant.  We now expand that determinant through its
actual complex remainder functional.  The result is not a new phase model:
it closes exactly in the Hermitian and transpose two-carrier families already
present in Sections 11.160 and 11.164.

Work on one fixed reciprocal-roster cell, with all physical coefficient rows
held fixed along the auxiliary `xi` segment.  The terminal conditional
`mathcal T_N` block has already been removed as in Section 11.186.  Put

```text
x_lambda=lambda-log a,

mathcal L_xi[P]
 :=(nu c_xi/|nu|)mathscr R_N[P].                 (11.226.1)
```

For the four physical coefficient polynomials

```text
P_V=C,                 P_mathcalN=mathcal N,

P_A=A,                 P_Q=Q,
```

define `U_X=mathcal L_xi[P_X]`.  Equations (11.186.5) and (11.172.8)
give, exactly,

```text
e_X=|nu|Re(U_X),

partial_xi mathcal L_xi[P]
 =mathcal L_xi[i x_lambda P].                   (11.226.2)
```

The coefficient rows retain the physical identities

```text
A(lambda)=R(lambda)C(lambda),

Q(lambda)=[R(lambda)+delta(lambda)]C(lambda)+D(lambda),

mathcal N(lambda)
 =R(lambda)Q(lambda)+R_(lambda,x)C(lambda).       (11.226.3)
```

No estimate on `delta`, `C-1`, or `D` is used below.

For two logarithmic carrier variables `lambda,mu`, define the symmetric
transpose kernel

```text
K_T(lambda,mu)
 :=C_lambda mathcal N_mu+mathcal N_lambda C_mu
   -A_lambda Q_mu-Q_lambda A_mu.
```

Substitution of (11.226.3), before any real projection, gives

```text
K_T(lambda,mu)
 =[R_mu-R_lambda][C_lambda Q_mu-C_muQ_lambda]

  +[R_(lambda,x)+R_(mu,x)]C_lambda C_mu,          (11.226.4)
```

where the coefficient wedge is

```text
C_lambda Q_mu-C_muQ_lambda
 =C_lambda C_mu{
      [R_mu-R_lambda]+[delta_mu-delta_lambda]}

  +C_lambda D_mu-C_muD_lambda.                   (11.226.5)
```

Thus every correction remains inside an antisymmetric physical difference.
The corresponding symmetric Hermitian kernel is

```text
K_H(lambda,mu)
 :=C_lambda conjugate(mathcal N_mu)
   +mathcal N_lambda conjugate(C_mu)
   -A_lambda conjugate(Q_mu)
   -Q_lambda conjugate(A_mu)

 =[conjugate(R_mu)-R_lambda]
     [C_lambda conjugate(Q_mu)
       -Q_lambda conjugate(C_mu)]

  +[R_(lambda,x)+conjugate(R_(mu,x))]
       C_lambda conjugate(C_mu).                 (11.226.6)
```

Let `mathcal L_xi tensor conjugate(mathcal L_xi)` mean that the first
functional acts in `lambda` and the conjugate functional acts in `mu`; define
`mathcal L_xi tensor mathcal L_xi` similarly.  The polarization in
(11.225.15) is then the exact double-functional identity

```text
Q_quad
 =(1/2)Re{
    [mathcal L_xi tensor conjugate(mathcal L_xi)][K_H]

   +[mathcal L_xi tensor mathcal L_xi][K_T]}.     (11.226.7)
```

The factor `1/2` is forced by
`2Re(z)Re(w)=Re[z conjugate(w)+zw]`; it is not a normalization choice.
Differentiating (11.226.7) with (11.226.2) gives

```text
E_quad^cur
 =(1/2)Re{
    [mathcal L_xi tensor conjugate(mathcal L_xi)]
       [i(lambda-mu)K_H]

   +[mathcal L_xi tensor mathcal L_xi]
       [i(lambda+mu-2log a)K_T]}.                (11.226.8)
```

The first multiplier is a phase difference; the second is a phase sum.
Consequently

```text
i(lambda-mu)=0,                 lambda=mu,

i(lambda+mu-2log a)=2i(lambda-log a),
                                  lambda=mu.      (11.226.9)
```

The Hermitian current diagonal therefore vanishes identically.  The
transpose current diagonal does not vanish structurally and must not be
deleted.

There is an exact check against the earlier physical kernel.  In the
correction-free specialization of Section 11.173,

```text
C=1,               D=delta=0,

R_lambda=i x_lambda/2,

R_(lambda,x)=-i u_x/2,          u_x=u_(N,x),      (11.226.10)
```

equations (11.226.4) and (11.226.6) reduce to

```text
K_H^0(lambda,mu)=-(x_lambda+x_mu)^2/4,

K_T^0(lambda,mu)=-(x_mu-x_lambda)^2/4-i u_x.      (11.226.11)
```

On a retained physical atom `lambda=log n`, one has
`x_lambda=-u_n`.  Hence the half-normalized kernels appearing in
(11.226.7) are

```text
K_H^0/2=-(u_n+u_m)^2/8,

K_T^0/2=-(u_n-u_m)^2/8-i u_x/2.                  (11.226.12)
```

These are exactly (11.160.13).  Moreover,
`i(lambda-mu)=-i(u_n-u_m)` and
`i(lambda+mu-2log a)=-i(u_n+u_m)`, exactly the auxiliary-flow multipliers
in (11.164.3).  Thus `E_quad^cur` introduces neither a third phase family nor
a new diagonal mechanism.  It is the residual-residual portion of the same
two-carrier flow.

The source grouping remains essential.  Section 11.186 gives

```text
mathscr R_N[P]
 =mathcal U_N[P]-mathcal T_1[P]-mathcal U_1[P]
   +mathcal I_N[P].                              (11.226.13)
```

This is one nonterminal functional after the terminal conditional
`mathcal T_N` block has been removed.  Expanding its tensor square before
forming `K_H` and `K_T` creates sixteen endpoint/interior coordinate terms,
but those terms are not sixteen independent errors.  Such an expansion would
discard the fixed-cell tie invariance and the cancellations certified in
Sections 11.186--11.188.  The kernels must be formed first and only then
subjected to a joined arithmetic decomposition.

For the pointwise route, the remaining sufficient target can now be written
without an unnamed quadratic package:

```text
E_FAN
 +(1/2)Re{
    [mathcal L_xi tensor conjugate(mathcal L_xi)]
       [i(lambda-mu)K_H]

   +[mathcal L_xi tensor mathcal L_xi]
       [i(lambda+mu-2log a)K_T]}

 <-(1130179/858000)rho A_T.                     (11.226.14)
```

This must be proved or falsified on every adverse actual-source witness cell,
with the finite/near term `E_FAN` and both residual kernels kept joined before
absolute values.  The weaker necessary threshold remains
`551501/858000` from (11.225.18).  Alternatively, the transfer route retains
the endpoint determinant difference (11.225.16).  Neither route has yet been
closed.

No new `pi` is introduced.  The `u_x=h^2/(8pi)` term in (11.226.11) is the
completed-zeta/Riemann--Siegel saddle term whose provenance was recorded in
Section 11.160.

This section proves the exact residual-residual transpose and Hermitian
factorizations, the double-functional normalization, both frequency
multipliers, the diagonal classification, and exact agreement with the prior
two-carrier kernel.  It proves no signed Type-I/II, Vaughan, reciprocal-pair,
or endpoint determinant estimate, complete-current sign, contact exclusion,
`Lambda<=0`, PF-infinity, RH, or prize-level conclusion.

## 11.227 Nonterminal determinant completion and compensation-ledger correction

Sections 11.225--11.226 correctly identify and factor the nonterminal
quadratic current.  The proposed join with `E_FAN`, however, is not the
derivative of the completed nonterminal determinant.  Returning to the
original observation-image formula exposes one retained/nonterminal linear
cross that was present in `P_lin^[N]` but omitted from the eight-package
ledger (11.218.8).  This section restores that package.  All previously
proved component identities and absolute budgets remain valid.

Work on one fixed reciprocal-roster cell at the physical point, after the
moving-tail current has been assigned separately.  Retain the symmetric
matrix `J` from (11.181.1).  Let

```text
p       = retained real observation vector,

a       = terminal conditional S_1 observation,

e       = every other nonterminal outer observation,

dot p, dot a, dot e
        = their auxiliary-frequency derivatives.       (11.227.1)
```

Thus `e` is the observation called `rho` in (11.185.9) and renamed in
(11.225.11).  The observation residual current before the separately owned
moving defect is

```text
R_raw
 =2p^TJ dot(a+e)+2dot(p)^TJ(a+e)
  +2(a+e)^TJ dot(a+e)+t_E^T dot(a+e).             (11.227.2)
```

Direct expansion, using `J^T=J`, gives five disjoint blocks:

```text
R_nr
 :=2p^TJdot(e)+2dot(p)^TJe,

R_quad
 :=2e^TJdot(e),

R_(a*)
 :=2(p+e)^TJdot(a)+2[dot(p)+dot(e)]^TJa,

R_aa
 :=2a^TJdot(a),

R_aff
 :=t_E^T[dot(a)+dot(e)],                          (11.227.3)

R_raw=R_nr+R_quad+R_(a*)+R_aa+R_aff.             (11.227.4)
```

The ownership of the last four terms was already certified.  The
finite/near, paired-remote, terminal-survivor, and physical-correction
channels partition the terminal mixed block `R_(a*)`; `E_aa` owns the pure
terminal block; `E_aff` owns the genuine-edge row; and `E_quad^cur` owns
only `R_quad`.  Consequently the residual sector represented in
(11.218.8) differs from (11.227.2) by exactly `R_nr`.  The separately owned
`E_move^cur` neither creates nor removes this fixed-point algebraic term.

The same defect is visible before taking real observation coordinates.
Retain (11.181.11) and split the full-support beta row as in (11.182.18):

```text
alpha_p:=alpha_N
 =(mathcal N_(p,xi),V_(p,xi),-Q_(p,xi),-A_(p,xi)),

beta_p:=beta_N-beta_E
 =(mathcal N_p,V_p,-Q_p,-A_p),

beta_E
 =(mathcal N_E,V_E,-Q_E,-A_E).                  (11.227.5)
```

Define

```text
P_nr(lambda)
 :=F_(alpha_p)(lambda)
   +i(lambda-log a)F_(beta_p)(lambda),

P_E(lambda)
 :=i(lambda-log a)F_(beta_E)(lambda).            (11.227.6)
```

Both have degree at most five, and the original full-support polynomial
satisfies

```text
P_lin^[N]=P_nr+P_E.                              (11.227.7)
```

Now use the exact outer split (11.186.3):

```text
mathscr O_N[P_lin^[N]]
 =mathcal T_N^[N][P_nr]
  +mathscr R_N[P_nr]
  +mathscr O_N[P_E].                             (11.227.8)
```

The first term is the retained/terminal part already contained in the
terminal mixed channel.  The last term is the separately displayed affine
package.  The middle term has no owner in (11.218.8).  Since

```text
alpha_p=2Jdot(p),              beta_p=2Jp,

e_X=Re{nu c_xi mathscr R_N[P_X]},

dot(e)_X
 =Re{nu c_xi
      mathscr R_N[i(lambda-log a)P_X]},           (11.227.9)
```

linearity gives the exact source-functional identity

```text
R_nr
 =Re{nu c_xi mathscr R_N[P_nr]}.                 (11.227.10)
```

Thus this is not a new model term.  It is the nonterminal projection of the
linear polynomial already present in (11.181.12).

There is a useful primitive.  On a fixed cell,

```text
R_nr=partial_xi(2p^TJe),                         (11.227.11)

R_nr+R_quad
 =2{(p+e)^TJ[dot(p)+dot(e)]-p^TJdot(p)}

 =partial_xi{
      (p+e)^TJ(p+e)-p^TJp}.                     (11.227.12)
```

Normalize the missing package and completed primitive by

```text
E_nr:=2R_nr/|nu|^2,

Q_nt
 :=(2/|nu|^2){(p+e)^TJ(p+e)-p^TJp}.             (11.227.13)
```

Equations (11.225.12)--(11.225.14) and (11.227.12) then give

```text
partial_xi Q_nt=E_nr+E_quad^cur.                 (11.227.14)
```

This is the completed nonterminal determinant-current difference.  The
exact partner of `E_quad^cur` is therefore `E_nr`, not `E_FAN`.

An independent exact-rational audit makes the failed proposed identity
visible without numerical tolerance.  For one assignment of independent
real observation rows it gives

```text
R_nr=-3410569/60843510,

R_quad=-120401707/334639305,

R_nr+R_quad=-278319673/669278610.                (11.227.15)
```

Setting the terminal and edge rows to zero leaves the old represented
sector equal to `R_quad`, whereas the completed nonterminal determinant
current is the last value in (11.227.15).  This is an algebraic
specialization disproving a universal bookkeeping identity; it is not
asserted to be a physical Xi state.  A separate physical cancellation could
still occur, but it would require a theorem and cannot be installed as an
identity.

The pointwise compensation ledger (11.218.8) is therefore superseded by

```text
E_tot^corr
 =E_F+E_R+E_term+E_Delta
  +E_aff+E_aa+E_move^cur+E_nr+E_quad^cur.        (11.227.16)
```

This has nine packages.  It does not change the six-package absolute bound
from (11.225.10).  With

```text
E_FAN=E_F+E_aff^N,

E_main^corr:=E_FAN+E_nr+E_quad^cur,

E_sec^cur
 :=E_R+E_term+E_aa+E_Delta+E_aff^C+E_move^cur,   (11.227.17)
```

one has

```text
|E_sec^cur|<(289339/858000)rho A_T.              (11.227.18)
```

The arithmetic thresholds in (11.225.18)--(11.225.19) remain numerically
unchanged, but their left side is corrected.  At an adverse witness,
negativity necessarily requires

```text
E_main^corr<-(551501/858000)rho A_T,             (11.227.19)
```

while the stronger inequality

```text
E_main^corr<-(1130179/858000)rho A_T             (11.227.20)
```

is sufficient independently of the signs of the six bounded packages.
The constants remain unchanged because `E_nr` is restored to the unbounded
signed main; no absolute allowance for it has been invented.  Equations
(11.225.17)--(11.225.19) and (11.226.14) are superseded only in replacing
their signed-main left side by (11.227.17).  Their budget arithmetic and all
quadratic kernel identities remain valid.

The transfer form also completes.  If
`xi_theta=T_0-theta varepsilon` stays inside a fixed roster cell, then

```text
-varepsilon integral_0^1
  [E_nr+E_quad^cur](xi_theta)dtheta

 =Q_nt(Omega)-Q_nt(T_0).                         (11.227.21)
```

Across a reciprocal tie this formula must be applied cell by cell with the
complete mode transfer from (11.186.10); no complement is differentiated
alone.

The next target is now precise: decompose the completed nonterminal current
`E_nr+E_quad^cur` through the retained finite, near, and common-cutoff
paired-remote functionals, and test its endpoint transfer or source-correlated
sign before taking moduli.  `E_FAN` remains a separate terminal/edge-near
signed channel and is joined only after that exact decomposition.

No new `pi` is introduced.  The correction uses only the symmetric matrix
`J`, linearity, and the already normalized full-support functionals.

This section proves the omitted linear package, its source polynomial,
the corrected five-block residual split, the completed determinant
primitive, the nine-package pointwise ledger, and the corrected signed-main
thresholds.  It proves no estimate or sign for `E_nr`, `E_quad`, their
completed determinant current, `E_FAN`, or the complete current; no all-`q`
transport, contact exclusion, `Lambda<=0`, PF-infinity, RH, or prize-level
conclusion.
