## 11.228 Complete outer-determinant recombination and finite-cell chart

Section 11.227 restored the omitted retained/nonterminal linear current.  The
restored block can be joined further with the terminal and genuine-edge
blocks.  This produces one exact geometric determinant current and leaves
only the separately owned moving-roster current outside it.

Continue on one fixed reciprocal-roster cell and use the real observation
vectors from (11.227.1).  Put

```text
o:=a+e,                 b:=omega_E+p,

Q(x):=x^TJx.                                      (11.228.1)
```

Here `o` is the observation of the complete outer functional
`mathscr O_N`, while `omega_E` is fixed on the auxiliary-frequency segment.
Direct differentiation and `J^T=J` give

```text
partial_xi{Q(p+o)-Q(p)}
 =2p^TJdot(o)+2dot(p)^TJo+2o^TJdot(o)

 =R_nr+R_quad+R_(a*)+R_aa.                       (11.228.2)
```

The terminal mixed package certified earlier is

```text
E_(a*)=E_F+E_R+E_term+E_Delta,                   (11.228.3)
```

and `E_aa` is the pure terminal block.  Thus (11.228.2) joins the
nonterminal completion from Section 11.227 to the complete terminal
observation without estimating either one separately.

The genuine-edge row has `t_E=2Jomega_E`.  Since `omega_E` is fixed on the
cell,

```text
R_aff=t_E^Tdot(o)=2omega_E^TJdot(o).              (11.228.4)
```

Adding (11.228.4) shifts the determinant base from `p` to `b`:

```text
R_geom
 :=R_nr+R_quad+R_(a*)+R_aa+R_aff

 =partial_xi{Q(b+o)-Q(b)}.                       (11.228.5)
```

Normalize this completed primitive by

```text
Q_geom
 :=(2/|nu|^2){Q(omega_E+p+o)-Q(omega_E+p)},

E_geom^cur:=partial_xi Q_geom.                   (11.228.6)
```

Equations (11.227.3), (11.228.3), and (11.228.4) now give the exact
eight-package collapse

```text
E_geom^cur
 =E_F+E_R+E_term+E_Delta
  +E_aa+E_nr+E_quad^cur+E_aff.                   (11.228.7)
```

Consequently the corrected nine-package pointwise ledger (11.227.16) is
equivalently the two-package ledger

```text
E_tot^corr=E_geom^cur+E_move^cur.                 (11.228.8)
```

This identity does not discard the previously proved component budgets.
They remain valid fallback estimates, but they are not spent when the joined
determinant formulation is used.

There are two equivalent arithmetic charts for `Q_geom`.  For the canonical
outer split, write

```text
o=n+c,

n_X:=Re{nu c_xi mathscr N_N[P_X]},

c_X:=Re{nu c_xi mathscr C_N[P_X]},               (11.228.9)
```

where `mathscr N_N` is the finite mean-one near functional and
`mathscr C_N` is defined only as a common-cutoff paired-remote functional.
Define

```text
Q_near
 :=(2/|nu|^2){Q(b+n)-Q(b)},

Q_remote
 :=(2/|nu|^2){Q(b+n+c)-Q(b+n)}.                 (11.228.10)
```

Then

```text
Q_geom=Q_near+Q_remote.                          (11.228.11)
```

The near-first order is canonical because the certified outer construction
composes the finite near kernel first and attaches the paired remote tail
afterward.  It assigns the near/remote cross to `Q_remote`.  Reversing the
order changes that ownership but not the total in (11.228.11).  In
particular, the old linear bound for `E_R` cannot be reused as a bound for
`partial_xi Q_remote`: the latter also contains the near/remote cross and the
remote self-determinant.

The second chart is purely finite.  Let

```text
d_X:=Re{nu c_xi mathscr D_N[P_X]},

f_X:=Re{nu c_xi mathscr F_N[P_X]}.               (11.228.12)
```

The exact functional identities

```text
mathscr O_N=-mathscr D_N,

mathscr D_N=mathscr F_N-mathscr M_N             (11.228.13)
```

give `o=-d`, `d=f-p`, and hence

```text
Q_geom
 =(2/|nu|^2){Q(omega_E+p-d)-Q(omega_E+p)}

 =(2/|nu|^2){Q(omega_E+2p-f)-Q(omega_E+p)}.      (11.228.14)
```

On a fixed Dirichlet cell the defect itself is the finite expression

```text
mathscr D_N[P]
 =-mathscr M_N[P]
  +H_N{f_P(1)-f_P(N)}+V_N[P].                   (11.228.15)
```

Thus (11.228.14) eliminates the conditionally convergent outer series
exactly.  It does not imply that the finite defect is small or has a useful
sign.

At a reciprocal boundary, (11.228.14) is interpreted using the certified
half-open jump laws: transfer the complete mode and its lift between
`mathscr F_N` and `mathscr O_N`.  The full observation and `Q_geom` are tie
invariant.  Differentiating `m_N` or `n_N` as floor functions is forbidden.

The signed target can now be calibrated without the older component budget.
The complete current is

```text
Sigma_full
 =-2rho A_T B+E_geom^cur+E_move^cur.             (11.228.16)
```

Inside each continuous roster-interior arc carrying the two certified values
`B>49/100` and `B<-49/100`, the intermediate-value theorem supplies a point
with

```text
B=-49/100.                                       (11.228.17)
```

At this calibrated adverse level, the pointwise theorem
`|E_move^cur|<rho A_T/100` shows that negativity necessarily requires

```text
E_geom^cur<-(97/100)rho A_T,                     (11.228.18)
```

whereas

```text
E_geom^cur<-(99/100)rho A_T                      (11.228.19)
```

is sufficient independently of the moving-current sign.  The level condition
(11.228.17) is essential for the stated sufficient constant; merely assuming
`B<-49/100` would not provide an upper bound for the positive centre term.

The live arithmetic theorem is therefore sharper but still open.  One may
insert (11.228.15) into the finite determinant (11.228.14) and derive its
reciprocal-stationary decomposition.  Alternatively, one may compose the
mean-one near observation with the retained carrier and then estimate the
paired-remote cross and self-determinant in (11.228.10).  Physical coefficient
rows should be tested in both charts before selecting Type-I/II, Vaughan,
adjacent-recurrence, or reciprocal-pair machinery.

No new `pi` is introduced.  The determinant recombination uses only `J` and
linearity.  The `pi` in the finite and paired-remote representations is
inherited from `e(x)=exp(2pi i x)`, `kappa=1/(2pi i)`, and the finite Dirichlet
kernel.

This section proves exact package recombination, edge completion, the
canonical near/paired-remote split, the finite-cell determinant chart, tie
ownership, and the calibrated threshold arithmetic.  It proves no sign or
bound for `E_geom^cur`, `Q_near`, `Q_remote`, the finite-cell determinant, or
the complete current; no all-`q` transport, contact exclusion, `Lambda<=0`,
PF-infinity, RH, or prize-level conclusion.

## 11.229 Determinant symmetry and reciprocal-block telescope

The finite chart (11.228.14) has a determinant symmetry not visible in the
component ledger.  For a real observation vector
`x=(x_V,x_mathcalN,x_A,x_Q)^T`, define

```text
M(x):=[[x_V,x_A],[x_Q,x_mathcalN]].               (11.229.1)
```

Then

```text
det M(x)=x_Vx_mathcalN-x_Ax_Q=x^TJx=Q(x).        (11.229.2)
```

At the physical anchor put

```text
b:=omega_E+p,               d:=f-p,

B_mat:=M(b),                D_mat:=M(d).          (11.229.3)
```

The full-support anchor (11.181.6) and the finite determinant (11.228.14)
become

```text
det(B_mat)=Q(omega_E+p)=h^2P_ret,

Q_geom
 =(2/|nu|^2){det(B_mat-D_mat)-det(B_mat)}.        (11.229.4)
```

For arbitrary `2 x 2` matrices the determinant difference has the
division-free form

```text
det(B-D)-det B
 =det D-tr(adj(B)D)

 =d^TJd-2b^TJd.                                  (11.229.5)
```

No inverse and no assumption `P_ret!=0` occurs in (11.229.5).

There is a genuine left-right symmetry.  If real matrices `L,R` satisfy

```text
det(L)det(R)=1,                                  (11.229.6)
```

then the simultaneous action

```text
M(x) mapsto L M(x) R                             (11.229.7)
```

preserves `Q(x)` and every determinant increment.  The subgroup with
`det L=det R=1` is `SL(2,R) x SL(2,R)`; (11.229.6) also includes the
component where both determinants are `-1`.  Consequently a raw Euclidean
norm of the four observation coordinates is not intrinsic to the target.
The invariant scalar objects are the determinant and adjugate pairings in
(11.229.5), together with their tangent analogues.

The symmetry supplies conditional pointwise normal forms.  Suppose first
that

```text
Delta:=det B>0,             s:=sqrt(Delta).
```

Then

```text
L=sB^(-1),       R=I,       det L det R=1,

LBR=sI.                                             (11.229.8)
```

If `D'=LDR`, direct expansion gives

```text
det(B-D)-det B
 =det D'-s(D'_(11)+D'_(22)).                    (11.229.9)
```

If instead `Delta<0`, put `s=sqrt(-Delta)` and take

```text
L=sB^(-1),       R=diag(1,-1),

det L=det R=-1,  LBR=diag(s,-s).                (11.229.10)
```

Then

```text
det(B-D)-det B
 =det D'-s(-D'_(11)+D'_(22)).                  (11.229.11)
```

For a pointwise current, the chosen `L,R` are frozen at that point and the
base, defect, and tangent matrices are all transformed by the same fixed
maps.  Differentiating a moving gauge would introduce spurious connection
terms.

The null cone is a separate branch.  If `det B=0`, equations
(11.229.8)--(11.229.11) are unavailable.  Rank-zero and rank-one bases remain
covered by (11.229.5).  A proof using the canonical gauges must therefore
either certify

```text
P_ret!=0                                           (11.229.12)
```

at every selected calibrated witness or treat the singular strata directly.
No such nonsingularity theorem is currently claimed.

The finite reciprocal band now has a canonical arithmetic partition.  Use
the block notation of Section 11.228 and write

```text
f=f^(0)+f^(1)+f^(2),                             (11.229.13)
```

where `f^(0)` is the real observation of all diagonal blocks `p_rec=q`,
`f^(1)` is the observation of the two adjacent classes
`|p_rec-q|=1`, and `f^(2)` is the observation of the far blocks
`|p_rec-q|>=2`.  Define

```text
d_0:=f^(0)-p,             d_1:=f^(1),

d_2:=f^(2),               d=d_0+d_1+d_2.        (11.229.14)
```

The diagonal sector contains the reciprocal stationary point and the two
incomplete endpoint diagonals, so `d_0` retains the carrier cancellation.
The adjacent sectors meet the diagonal cells at half-integer boundaries and
have no positive uniform phase-gradient gap.  Only the far sector has the
certified gap

```text
|alpha_P/u-r|
 >=alpha_P(|p_rec-q|-1)/
   {(p_rec+1/2)(q+1/2)},       |p_rec-q|>=2.     (11.229.15)
```

Set

```text
b_0:=b,             b_1:=b-d_0,

b_2:=b-d_0-d_1,

Delta_j:=Q(b_j-d_j)-Q(b_j),       0<=j<=2.       (11.229.16)
```

Then the finite primitive telescopes exactly:

```text
Q(b-d)-Q(b)=Delta_0+Delta_1+Delta_2.             (11.229.17)
```

This diagonal-first order is not cosmetic.  If every block increment were
formed against the original base `b`, the result would omit

```text
2d_0^TJd_1+2d_0^TJd_2+2d_1^TJd_2.              (11.229.18)
```

Equation (11.229.17) assigns the diagonal/adjacent cross to `Delta_1` and all
crosses involving the far sector to `Delta_2`.

The current has the same ownership.  For a base `B` and defect `D`, define

```text
I(B,D)
 :=partial_xi{Q(B-D)-Q(B)}

 =-2B^TJdot(D)-2dot(B)^TJD+2D^TJdot(D).         (11.229.19)
```

With the derivatives of `b_0,b_1,b_2` inherited from (11.229.16),

```text
E_geom^cur
 =(2/|nu|^2){I(b_0,d_0)+I(b_1,d_1)+I(b_2,d_2)}. (11.229.20)
```

## 11.231 Fixed-cell low-N determinant evaluator contract

Section 11.230 supplies physical phase rows but also rules out using a direct
carrier or reciprocal-block enumeration at their scale.  Before introducing
any compression, the finite functional and determinant interfaces need an
executable reconstruction oracle.  This section gives that oracle at low
`N`.  It validates the complete bookkeeping, not a physical sign.

Fix a point strictly inside one roster-and-reciprocal-cell chart.  For a
polynomial

```text
P(lambda)=sum_(k=0)^5 c_k lambda^k,

f_P(u)=exp{2pi i alpha_Plog u+S(log u)}P(log u),

S(lambda)=t lambda^2/4-sigma lambda.             (11.231.1)
```

The evaluator tabulates every linear functional first on the monomial basis
`1,lambda,...,lambda^6`.  The extra degree is compulsory because the exact
fixed-cell tangent lift is

```text
P(lambda) mapsto i(lambda-log a)P(lambda).       (11.231.2)
```

Thus arbitrary physical coefficient rows can later be inserted by one matrix
projection without rerunning the scalar functional engine.

Retain the starred carrier

```text
mathscr M_N[P]
 ={f_P(1)+f_P(N)}/2+sum_(q=2)^(N-1)f_P(q).      (11.231.3)
```

For

```text
J_q=[max(1,q-1/2),min(N,q+1/2)],

C_p={r in Z_(>0):p-1/2<=alpha_P/r<p+1/2},       (11.231.4)
```

the finite block table is evaluated as

```text
mathcal B_(q,p)[P]
 =sum_(r in C_p)integral_(J_q)f_P(u)e(-ru)du.   (11.231.5)
```

The three stored sectors are

```text
mathscr F_N^(0)=sum_(p=q)mathcal B_(q,p),

mathscr F_N^(1)=sum_(|p-q|=1)mathcal B_(q,p),

mathscr F_N^(2)=sum_(|p-q|>=2)mathcal B_(q,p).  (11.231.6)
```

Every roster mode is assigned once by the half-open rule in (11.231.4).
The resulting sum is checked against two separately evaluated forms:

```text
mathscr F_N[P]
 =integral_1^N f_P(u)sum_(r=m_N)^n_N e(-ru)du,

mathscr F_N[P]
 =H_N{f_P(1)-f_P(N)}+V_N[P].                   (11.231.7)
```

The first uses the complete finite Dirichlet kernel.  The second uses the
endpoint harmonic and centered cell variations of (11.188.4)--(11.188.6).
Consequently a wrong endpoint half, reciprocal orientation, or cell owner is
tested in a different arithmetic chart.

The near/remote cross-check is also finite.  Put

```text
mathscr N_N[P]
 =integral_1^N f_P(u)
    sum_(j=-(m_N-1))^n_N e(ju)du.               (11.231.8)
```

For the common-cutoff paired remote tail define

```text
T_n=pi^2/6-sum_(k=1)^n 1/k^2,

K_(tail,n)(u)
 =pi^2 B_2({u})-sum_(k=1)^n cos(2pi ku)/k^2,

B_2(x)=x^2-x+1/6.                               (11.231.9)
```

The Fourier identity

```text
sum_(k=1)^infinity cos(2pi ku)/k^2=pi^2B_2({u})
```

and the twice-integrated pair formula (11.193.9) give the exact finite
representation

```text
mathscr C_N[P]
 ={[f_P'(N)-f_P'(1)]T_(n_N)
    -integral_1^N f_P''(u)K_(tail,n_N)(u)du}
   /(2pi^2).                                     (11.231.10)
```

No infinite numerical truncation or rearrangement of the two conditional
one-sided tails occurs in (11.231.10).  The evaluator checks

```text
mathscr M_N[P]-mathscr F_N[P]
 =mathscr N_N[P]+mathscr C_N[P]                 (11.231.11)
```

on every stored monomial.

To exercise the observation chart, choose four fixed complex coefficient
rows and one unit common phase `z=nu c_xi`.  For any scalar functional
`mathcal L`, put

```text
x_X=Re{z mathcal L[P_X]},

dot x_X=Re{z mathcal L[i(lambda-log a)P_X]},

x=(x_V,x_mathcalN,x_A,x_Q)^T.                   (11.231.12)
```

The common phase is differentiated as
`partial_xi z=-i log(a)z`, while `S` and the polynomial coefficients remain
fixed.  This is precisely the fixed-chart lift of (11.188.12).

Let `p` be (11.231.12) for the carrier and let `f^(j)` be its three block
observations.  For a fixed real edge row `omega_E`, define

```text
b=omega_E+p,

d_0=f^(0)-p,       d_1=f^(1),       d_2=f^(2),

d=d_0+d_1+d_2.                                  (11.231.13)
```

The implementation evaluates both the direct primitive/current

```text
Delta=Q(b-d)-Q(b),

dot Delta
 =-2b^TJdot d-2dot b^TJd+2d^TJdot d             (11.231.14)
```

and the diagonal-first telescopes (11.229.17), (11.229.20).  It then changes
`alpha_P` by `+/-delta`, rotates `z` by
`exp(-/+2pi i delta log a)`, verifies that every half-open mode label is
unchanged, and checks

```text
dot Delta
 ={Delta(alpha_P+delta)-Delta(alpha_P-delta)}
   /(4pi delta).                                 (11.231.15)
```

The denominator is `4pi delta` because `xi=2pi alpha_P`.

Three fixtures were run:

```text
(N,a,alpha_P)=(4,4.25,17.8),

(N,a,alpha_P)=(5,5.4,28.9),

(N,a,alpha_P)=(7,7.35,53.6).                    (11.231.16)
```

Each satisfies


and remains at least `0.1` in `alpha_P` from every roster or internal

```text
block sum versus direct kernel        <5.12*10^(-12),

block sum versus cell variation       <3.04*10^(-12),

outer versus near plus paired remote  <3.34*10^(-12),

primitive/current finite difference   <6.57*10^(-10). (11.231.17)
```

An independent checker replaces the builder's mode-by-mode fixed Gauss

## 11.232 Exact physical-observation polynomial compiler

Section 11.231 deliberately uses synthetic coefficient rows.  This section
closes the convention gap between that functional interface and the actual
four observation polynomials of Sections 11.159--11.173.  It does not yet
supply their physical numerical scalar inputs.

Use the monomial variable and centered coordinate

```text
ell=log n,                 x=ell-log a,

L_N=log N,                 u_N=log a-L_N.          (11.232.1)
```

The compiler stores coefficients in ascending powers.  Its explicit scalar
inputs are

```text
L_N, log a, rho_1, rho_2, rho_(1,x), rho_(2,x),

c,b,c_x,b_x, chi_rate, u_(N,x),

s_*'=c+ib,                 s_*''=c_x+ib_x.         (11.232.2)
```

Here `chi_rate` means the complex bulk rate denoted `chi_N` in
(11.157.5c), (11.159.4), and (11.160.1).  This executable name is
intentional: a later part of the corpus also prints `chi_N` for a phase
angle.  The two quantities are not identified.

First construct the five moment vectors

```text
v_0=(1,rho_1,rho_2,0,0),

v_1=(L_N,L_Nrho_1-1,L_Nrho_2-rho_1,-rho_2,0),

v_2=(L_N^2,L_N^2rho_1-2L_N,
     L_N^2rho_2-2L_Nrho_1+1,rho_1-2L_Nrho_2,rho_2),

e_0=(0,rho_(1,x),rho_(2,x),0,0),

e_1=(0,L_Nrho_(1,x),L_Nrho_(2,x)-rho_(1,x),
     -rho_(2,x),0).                               (11.232.3)
```

Then put

```text
q_0=chi_rate v_0+s_*'v_1+e_0,

q_1=chi_rate v_1+s_*'v_2+e_1,

a_0=s_*'v_1+i b u_Nv_0,

n_0=s_*''v_1+s_*'q_1
    +i(b_xu_N+b u_(N,x))v_0+i b u_Nq_0.          (11.232.4)
```

In observation order `(V,mathcal N,A,Q)`, the resulting coefficient rows are

```text
(P_V,P_N,P_A,P_Q)=(v_0,n_0,a_0,q_0).             (11.232.5)
```

There is a second construction which does not use (11.232.3)--(11.232.4).
Define directly

```text
C=1+rho_1ell+rho_2ell^2,

D=rho_(1,x)ell+rho_(2,x)ell^2,

R=s_*'(L_N-ell)+i b u_N,

R_x=s_*''(L_N-ell)+i(b_xu_N+b u_(N,x)),

Q=[chi_rate+s_*'(L_N-ell)]C+D,

mathcal N=RQ+R_xC.                                (11.232.6)
```

The polynomial construction gives

```text
(P_V,P_N,P_A,P_Q)=(C,mathcal N,RC,Q).             (11.232.7)
```

Expanding (11.232.6) in ascending powers of `ell` gives exactly the twenty
entries of (11.232.5).  Thus the moment-vector and carrier-law derivations
agree coefficient by coefficient, rather than merely after evaluation on one
moment vector.

Translation to the centered chart gives

```text
C=c_0+c_1x+c_2x^2,          D=d_0+d_1x+d_2x^2,

R=-s_*'x-c u_N,

R_x=-s_*''x-c_xu_N+i b u_(N,x),

delta=chi_rate-i b u_N,

Q=(R+delta)C+D,             mathcal N=RQ+R_xC.    (11.232.8)
```

The binomial translation of every coefficient in (11.232.5) agrees exactly
with the direct centered construction (11.232.8).  In particular the large
`L_N` and `log a` terms cancel before a norm is taken.  The useful radial-rate
cancellation is retained as the polynomial identity

```text
P_A-P_Q=(i b u_N-chi_rate)C-D.                    (11.232.9)
```

For an ascending row `p=(p_0,...,p_d)`, define its fixed-chart tangent by

```text
dot P(ell)=i(ell-log a)P(ell),

dot p_j=i[p_(j-1)-(log a)p_j],                   (11.232.10)
```

with absent endpoint coefficients zero.  The four base degree ceilings

```text
(2,4,3,3)
```

therefore lift exactly to

```text
(3,5,4,4).                                       (11.232.11)
```

No moment above degree five enters the physical joined polynomial.  The
degree-six storage of Section 11.231 remains a regression margin rather than
a hidden seventh physical moment.

For a real row `f=(f_V,f_N,f_A,f_Q)`, retain

```text
F_f=f_VP_V+f_NP_N+f_AP_A+f_QP_Q.                 (11.232.12)
```

The actual linear ownership rows are

```text
alpha=(mathcal N_(p,xi),V_(p,xi),-Q_(p,xi),-A_(p,xi)),

beta_p=(mathcal N_p,V_p,-Q_p,-A_p),

beta_E=(mathcal N_E,V_E,-Q_E,-A_E).              (11.232.13)
```

Consequently

```text
P_lin=F_alpha+i(ell-log a)F_(beta_p+beta_E)

     ={F_alpha+i(ell-log a)F_(beta_p)}
       +i(ell-log a)F_(beta_E).                  (11.232.14)
```

Equation (11.232.14) is an exact additive ownership identity.  The genuine
edge enters once, through `beta_E`; it is not inserted into `alpha` and is not
repeated after the terminal carriers have moved into `p`.  At `ell=log a`,
the complete lifted channel vanishes and

```text
P_lin(log a)=F_alpha(log a).                     (11.232.15)
```

This endpoint value does not imply that the full polynomial has a universal
factor `ell-log a`.

An exact rational-complex fixture exercises every scalar input and all twelve

```text
rho_1,rho_2,rho_(1,x),rho_(2,x),c,b,c_x,b_x,

chi_rate,u_(N,x), omega_E, alpha, beta_p,          (11.232.16)
```

including the common normalization and retained carrier observations.  The

## 11.233 Physical scalar and genuine-edge adapter at the calibrated roots

Section 11.232 leaves twelve scalar inputs and the genuine endpoint row to be
evaluated before the retained arithmetic observations are attached.  This
section closes that pointwise interface at the three immutable roots of
Section 11.230.  The evaluation convention is essential: the root value of
`L` selects the physical state, but every subscript `x` below is the source
derivative at fixed heat time `t` and fixed cutoff `N`.  It is not a
derivative along the `q=1` root curve.

Put

```text
t=1/(2L^2),                 x=4pi exp(L),

s=(1-ix)/2,                 a^2=x/(4pi)+t/16,

h=1/a,                      theta=a-N,

p=1-2theta,                 T_0=2pi a^2.          (11.233.1)
```

For the normalized first correction, retain

```text
B=alpha'(s)t^2/8,           a_0=1+d_1,

rho_2=B/a_0,                rho_1=-2alpha rho_2,

B_x=-i alpha''(s)t^2/16,

rho_(2,x)=B_x/a_0-B d_(1,x)/a_0^2,

rho_(1,x)=-2alpha_xrho_2-2alpha rho_(2,x),

alpha_x=-i alpha'(s)/2.                         (11.233.2)
```

These are quotient identities, not asymptotic replacements of `a_0`.  The
remaining elementary rates are

```text
s_*'=-i/2-it alpha'/4,       s_*''=-t alpha''/8,

u_(N,x)=h^2/(8pi).                              (11.233.3)
```

The small centered bulk rate is vulnerable to loss of digits if it is formed


## 11.234 Shifted-Hardy diagnostic bridge for the retained carrier

The finite reciprocal decomposition does not remove the retained carrier.
The exact ridge identity of Section 11.190 has the form

```text
2 mathscr M_N[P]-mathscr F_N[P]
 =mathscr M_N[P]-tau_band[P]+E_band[P],             (11.234.1)
```

so one starred `mathscr M_N` remains.  The diagonal-plus-adjacent collar is
locally exact on a fixed roster chart, but the current identities do not turn
that carrier into an `O(polylog N)` evaluator at `N` near `7.2*10^10`.
This is a structural obstruction to the proposed local-compression algorithm,
not a proof that no other fast carrier algorithm can exist.

For the physical carrier put

```text
T=T_0=2pi a^2=Omega,

W(lambda)=exp[t lambda^2/4-(sigma-1/2)lambda],

omega_c=(-1)^N eta.                                (11.234.2)
```

The equality `T_0=Omega` in (11.234.2) is essential.  Replacing this height by
the unshifted `x/2` changes the endpoint phase and does not represent the
carrier in Sections 11.231--11.233.

For real shifts `delta_j`, define the Riemann--Siegel main sum and its complex
kernel by

```text
H_main(T+delta_j)
 =2 Re{exp[-i theta_RS(T+delta_j)]
       sum_(n<=N)n^(-1/2+i(T+delta_j))},

K_j(lambda)
 =2 exp[-i theta_RS(T+delta_j)]exp(i delta_j lambda).
                                                        (11.234.3)
```

If real coefficients `c_j` satisfy

```text
g_P(lambda)=omega_c W(lambda)P(lambda)
            approximately sum_j c_j K_j(lambda),       (11.234.4)
```

then linearity gives the exact conditional reconstruction identity

```text
sum_j c_j H_main(T+delta_j)
 =Re sum_(n<=N)n^(-1/2+iT)
      {sum_j c_jK_j(log n)}.                            (11.234.5)
```

Thus the difference between the two sides after replacing the braces by
`g_P(log n)` is solely the fitted-kernel error.  The starred carrier has half
weight at `n=1,N`, while (11.234.3) has full endpoint weight.  Its value is
therefore recovered by subtracting one half of the two fitted endpoint terms.
No terminal band is silently removed.

At the three calibrated roots, high-precision evaluation gives

```text
omega_c/exp[-i theta_RS(T_0)]
 =-1-4.84*10^(-17)i,  +1,  -1-4.84*10^(-17)i,          (11.234.6)
```

in cutoff order.  Equation (11.234.6) is recorded as a numerical phase-lock
check at double-output precision, not as a new interval theorem.  It explains
why the stationary endpoint does not lose a quadrature at the actual carrier
height.

The diagnostic uses the fixed upstream grid

```text
delta_j=0.01j,              -7<=j<=7.                   (11.234.7)
```

For each of the four physical rows and four tangent rows in Section 11.233,
the real coefficients in (11.234.4) were fitted on the full interval
`0<=lambda<=log N` and checked on a disjoint union of midpoint and
endpoint-clustered grids.  Across three roots and twenty-four kernels, the

## 11.235 Resumable Hardy evaluator and exact restart equivalence

Section 11.234 left a concrete software obligation before any bounded
physical-height diagnostic could be considered.  The pinned upstream checkout
remains unchanged.  A GPL-3.0 RH-owned derivative retains the accepted
fifteen-point grid

```text
delta_j=0.01j,                    -7<=j<=7,             (11.235.1)
```

and adds a deterministic state machine.  Stage zero unit `k` means that the
direct block and Gaussian blocks through `k` are complete.  Stage one unit `r`
means that disjoint Riemann--Siegel tail rounds through `r` are complete.
Stage two unit zero is the corrected final output.  The restart state is

```text
(stage,unit,t,et,numbercalc,nchalf,totblock,
 rn1,mt,mto,aenums,mmax,NC,N_MAX,
 zsum[15],rszsumtot[15],rszsum[15]).                  (11.235.2)
```

The source format, a mandatory 64-hex run identifier, MPI size, tail chunk
size, height, tolerance, roster dimensions, stage range, finiteness, and three
weighted array checksums are checked before (11.235.2) is accepted.  The run
identifier hashes the container image, binary, module, derivative source,
input, rank roster, and chunk policy.  A mismatched executable or policy
therefore fails closed rather than silently continuing a foreign state.

After every completed atomic unit, rank zero performs

```text
write temporary snapshot -> flush -> fsync -> atomic rename -> fsync,
append JSONL audit state -> fsync.                             (11.235.3)
```

Only after (11.235.3) may a runtime limit, deterministic stage/unit request,
or stop file park the job.  All fifteen arrays in (11.235.2) use the sign-safe
format `ES49.40E4`, carrying 41 significand digits.  The initial executable
test found that `ES48.40E4` overflowed to asterisks on the first negative
partial sums; widening by one character and adding a source regression guard
closed that defect before fixture promotion.

The fixture tail chunk is deliberately reduced to `257` terms to expose
multiple restart points without changing the mathematical sum.  The exact
results are

```text
T=10^10:  36 Gaussian + 3 tail + 1 final = 40 states,
           4 parked invocations and 2 fail-closed bad resumes;

T=10^12:  47 Gaussian + 8 tail + 1 final = 56 states,
           2 parked invocations.                              (11.235.4)
```

For each height, an uninterrupted journal and a multiply interrupted journal
agree as arbitrary-precision decimal objects at every stage and unit.  Thus
`2(40+56)=192` full states are compared.  The final snapshots agree field by
field, all fifteen displayed outputs agree exactly, and both paths reproduce
the accepted ten-decimal fixtures with maximum displayed absolute difference
zero.  Bad run-identifier and bad-chunk resumes exit with status two without
changing either checkpoint artifact.

No new `pi` occurs in this implementation gate.  The `pi` already present in
the evaluator remains inherited from the completed-zeta and Riemann--Siegel
normalizations described in Section 11.234.

This section proves deterministic finite stop/resume equivalence and
fail-closed provenance for the tested one-rank evaluator at `10^10` and
`10^12`.  It does not validate the upstream asymptotic error constant,
establish correlated-error cancellation among shifted samples, produce a
physical-height value, or provide interval arithmetic.  Hence it proves no
retained `alpha` or `beta_p` row, determinant sign or bound, complete-current
inequality, all-`q` transport, contact exclusion, `Lambda<=0`, PF-infinity,
RH, or prize-level conclusion.  The next admissible step is a joint
correlated-error ledger; a physical-height run remains behind that gate.

## 11.236 Joint shifted-Hardy error modes and the scalar-extrapolation obstruction

Restart equivalence does not control the error of the external evaluator.  On
the accepted shift grid, define the two saved calibration residual vectors by

```text
epsilon_T(j)=H_fast,main(T+0.01j)-H_direct,main(T+0.01j),

                         -7<=j<=7,  T in {10^10,10^12}.       (11.236.1)
```

Let `q_0,...,q_14` be the discrete orthonormal polynomial basis obtained by
orthonormalizing degrees zero through fourteen on `j/7`.  Then every saved
physical coefficient vector `c` has the exact finite ledger identity

```text
sum_j c_j epsilon_T(j)
 =sum_(k=0)^14 <c,q_k><epsilon_T,q_k>.                       (11.236.2)
```

Equation (11.236.2) loses no sign or correlation.  It separates common mode,
slope, curvature, cubic, quartic/quintic, and the degree-six-through-fourteen
remainder before any norm is applied.

The residual vectors are numerically smooth.  Their measured data are

```text
                         T=10^10                 T=10^12

max_j |epsilon_T(j)|     0.00724738923861        0.00288990976752

energy above degree 3    1.11353863066e-6        1.43084915836e-5

energy above degree 5    2.74694241496e-9        8.59346550533e-9.
                                                               (11.236.3)
```

The two profiles have cosine similarity `0.927285625844`, but the best scalar
multiple of the `10^10` vector leaves `0.374354602087` of the `10^12` L2 norm.
Thus smoothness does not make the profiles scalar copies.

For the twenty-four physical base/tangent kernel rows of Section 11.234,
twenty-one coefficient vectors annihilate a constant additive sample error to
relative sensitivity below `10^(-12)`.  This explains why the independent
worst-case L1 bound is excessively pessimistic: at `10^10` the observed
cancellation factors range from `7.0262` to `1.77172*10^6`, and at `10^12`
from `11.1023` to `4.16509*10^5`.  These are finite observations, not
certified persistence bounds.

The decisive falsification is that the raw maximum in (11.236.3) decreases by
the factor

```text
0.00288990976752/0.00724738923861=0.398751836334,             (11.236.4)
```

while twenty-one of the twenty-four absolute physical projections in
(11.236.2) increase.  The largest increase factor is
`3.48540571632`.  The maximum projected magnitudes are
`0.00945336322404` and `0.0160347031382` at the two heights.  Consequently a
single scalar decay inferred from the pointwise envelope cannot control the
actual physical coefficient combinations, even across these two calibration
heights.

This conclusion is not an artifact of one pseudoinverse cutoff.  The physical
kernel matrices have condition number near `2.5*10^16`, so the fits were
recomputed with least-squares cutoffs

```text
10^(-8),10^(-10),10^(-12),10^(-14),10^(-15),10^(-16).
                                                               (11.236.5)
```

The largest coefficient L1 norm ranges from `2.23078*10^5` to
`1.05731*10^7`, while every choice in (11.236.5) still has exactly twenty-one
increasing projections.  The maximum projected-error ranges are only

```text
T=10^10: [0.00937479208,0.00946191152],

T=10^12: [0.0159334513,0.0160643188].                         (11.236.6)
```

The admissible upgrade is therefore modewise.  One needs explicit functions
`A_k(T)` and `R_6(T)` such that, at physical height,

```text
|<epsilon_T,q_k>|<=A_k(T),                    0<=k<=5,

||(I-P_5)epsilon_T||_2<=R_6(T),

|sum_j c_j epsilon_T(j)|
 <=sum_(k=0)^5 |<c,q_k>|A_k(T)+||c||_2 R_6(T).                (11.236.7)
```

The first two rows of (11.236.7) must come from a proved expansion or interval

No new `pi` is introduced here.  The only height and phase normalizations are

## 11.237 Published remainder audit and an exact derivative-to-mode handoff

Section 11.236 identifies the required mode bounds but does not say which
external theorem would imply them.  This section makes that handoff exact.
For the fixed fifteen-value batch, put

```text
delta_j=j/100,  -7<=j<=7,

I_T=[T-7/100,T+7/100],

D_r(T)=sup_(u in I_T)|epsilon^(r)(u)|,  0<=r<=6.             (11.237.1)
```

Here `epsilon` is the absolute fast-main-minus-direct-main error for one
fixed combinatorial branch of the batched evaluator.  The assumption in
(11.237.1) is conditional: this corpus does not yet prove that the required
derivatives exist on the physical interval or that the branch remains
admissible there.

Let `p_0,...,p_5` be the primitive integer Gram polynomials obtained by exact
rational Gram--Schmidt on the fifteen grid points, and put
`q_k=p_k/||p_k||_2`.  Thus

```text
<q_k,delta^r>=0,  0<=r<k<=5.                                (11.237.2)
```

Taylor's theorem at the central height gives

```text
epsilon(T+delta_j)
 =sum_(r=0)^5 epsilon^(r)(T) delta_j^r/r!+rho_j,

|rho_j|<=D_6(T)|delta_j|^6/6!.                              (11.237.3)
```

Combining (11.237.2)--(11.237.3), without fitting any decay in `T`, yields
the six exact conditional bounds

```text
|<epsilon_T,q_k>|
 <=sum_(r=k)^5 |<q_k,delta^r>|D_r(T)/r!
   +[sum_j |q_k(j)||delta_j|^6/6!]D_6(T)
 =:A_k(T),                                      0<=k<=5.    (11.237.4)
```

Every coefficient in (11.237.4) is stored exactly as a rational number
divided by the square root of an integer.  Since the Taylor polynomial has
degree at most five and orthogonal projection is an L2 contraction,

```text
||(I-P_5)epsilon_T||_2
 <=[sqrt(sum_j |delta_j|^12)/6!]D_6(T)
 =C_tail D_6(T),                                            (11.237.5)

C_tail^2
 =4069880729/64800000000000000000000000000,

C_tail=2.50612851572812981556*10^(-10).                     (11.237.6)
```

Equations (11.237.4)--(11.237.5) supply exactly the `A_k(T)` and `R_6(T)`
inputs of (11.236.7).  A stronger but potentially cleaner sufficient input
is one complex-neighborhood estimate.  If the fixed-branch error is
holomorphic on `|z-T|<=rho`, where `rho>7/100`, and

```text
sup_(|z-T|<=rho)|epsilon(z)|<=M_rho(T),                      (11.237.7)
```

then Cauchy's estimate gives

```text
D_r(T)<=r! M_rho(T)/rho^r,  0<=r<=6.                        (11.237.8)
```

The primary-source audit explains why neither route may currently be treated
as supplied.  Lewis and Brereton, arXiv:2607.15310v1, equations (120)--(123),
reduce the recursive MGS error to a multiple of the largest local iteration
error.  On pages 41--42 the paper says that a precise upper bound requires an
estimate for that local term and does not pursue such a bound for the
higher-order sums.  Page 44 separately records that the hybrid Hardy
representation is not exact and has both representation and Gaussian-sum
errors.  Its final error study is sample evidence; the relative-error
statistics omit `|Z(t)|<=1/2`, and the surrounding discussion says that an
adverse combination of constituent cubic-sum errors is not ruled out by a
theorem.

The pinned fifteen-value source is nevertheless structurally favourable: it
uses one central hierarchy and varies the nearby heights and phases on the
`0.01` grid.  That makes a joint fixed-branch expansion more plausible than
fifteen unrelated pointwise bounds.  But the source comment behind
`numbercalc<=8` itself says there is no hard-and-fast rule for the error as
the shifts move away from the centre.  It supplies no derivative remainder
contract.

There is one mandatory transition guard.  If a combinatorial or analytic
transition crosses the physical interval, (11.237.1) cannot be asserted
globally.  The interval must then be partitioned, with each jump or truncated
power entered as an additional explicit fifteen-vector before the mode
contraction.  Smooth residuals at `10^10` and `10^12` do not prove that this
guard is inactive at physical height.

No new `pi` is introduced in this section.  The shift scale is the source
code's literal decimal grid, and every constant in (11.237.4)--(11.237.6)
comes from exact finite-grid Taylor algebra.

This section proves the conditional implications (11.237.4)--(11.237.8) and
identifies the exact source gap.  It proves no evaluator derivative bound,
complex-disk bound, transition exclusion, external absolute error constant,
physical carrier value, interval enclosure, retained observation,
determinant sign or bound, complete-current inequality, all-`q` transport,
contact exclusion, `Lambda<=0`, PF-infinity, RH, or prize-level conclusion.

## 11.239 Local MGS defects: source anatomy and an exact-shell bypass

Section 11.237 reduces the shifted evaluator problem to real derivative
bounds or one complex-disk bound, but leaves the external MGS error as a
black box.  The primary source permits a sharper decomposition.  Lewis and
Brereton state that the Euler--Maclaurin/Fourier reduction is exact through
equation (69).  Approximation begins only when the finite integrals in (69)
are replaced by the contour and saddle formulas (71)--(78).

For one hierarchy level, write the exact finite generalized sum as `S_l`,
the transformed child as `S_(l+1)`, the recurrence multiplier as `a_l`, and
the assembled endpoint correction as `q_l`.  The paper's equation (120)
defines the local defect exactly by

```text
epsilon_l=S_l-[a_l S_(l+1)+q_l].                           (11.239.1)
```

This identity is independent of how the terms in `q_l` are approximated.
It therefore gives two possible certification strategies: bound every
analytic component of `q_l`, or enclose the finite difference (11.239.1)
directly after specifying exactly what the transformed child represents.

The source-to-paper map in the pinned evaluator is

```text
paper component             Fortran component

W1, equation (81)           t5
W2, equation (89)           t2
W3 or W4, (93) or (94)      t4
W5, equation (97)           t1
endpoint half-sum in (96)   t3
assembled recurrence        qq, then csum=c1*csum+qq.
                                                               (11.239.2)
```

Thus the difficult source term is `t5`, not `t1`.  It contains the two
endpoint loops controlled by `ip`, together with the digamma base.  The
executable fixes

```text
ip=3,                                                        (11.239.3)
```

while the comment in the same routine says that `ip` near twenty was found
adequate and that deciding the best value is not obvious.  This discrepancy
does not prove that the computed values are inaccurate.  It proves that the
cutoff is empirical and requires a tail theorem before it can enter a
rigorous evaluator bound.

The full local obligation has thirteen separately owned components.  Within
MGS these are the omitted higher phase on the diagonal saddle contour, the
two vertical-leg phase and exponential remainders, the two endpoint-index
tails beyond `ip`, saddle-location error, digamma error, complex-error-function
error, the remaining `W2`--`W4` contour approximations, hierarchy coefficient
truncation, the transformed kernel model, and floating-point accumulation.
Outside the local MGS defect lie the outer hybrid Hardy representation
remainder, the shared multi-shift approximation, and all floor, rounding,
sign, and special-function selector transitions.

The implementation audit makes several of those obligations concrete.  The
complex error function is called with six retained terms; `PSI` uses finite
series or a finite asymptotic expansion; higher-order saddle solves use a
Newton tolerance of `10^(-7)`; a `psi(2,z)` correction present in a Maple
version is explicitly omitted; and the commented `ecor` correction is set
to zero.  Quad precision controls elementary roundoff but does not, by
itself, bound any of these analytic remainders.

There is an exact accumulation identity that avoids treating the largest
local defect as an indivisible global error.  If `e_l` is the error in the
computed level-`l` sum and the terminal level `r` is exact, then

```text
e_l=epsilon_l+a_l e_(l+1),

e_0=sum_(k=0)^r [product_(j=0)^(k-1) a_j] epsilon_k.        (11.239.4)
```

The empty product in (11.239.4) is one.  The companion checker verifies the
recursive and expanded forms over an exact rational-complex fixture, so no
floating tolerance is involved.

Equation (11.239.4) exposes an algorithmic bypass.  If an intermediate level
`m` is evaluated directly and recurrence begins from that exact value, then

```text
e_0=sum_(k=0)^(m-1)
       [product_(j=0)^(k-1) a_j] epsilon_k.                 (11.239.5)
```

Every descendant defect `epsilon_m,...,epsilon_r` is absent.  In particular,
direct evaluation of the first parent above the kernel removes the defect
which the paper says is usually the largest.  This implication is exact,
but no cost saving is asserted: the parent length must first be recorded on
the physical chain roster.  The source's denominator-weighted kernel and
raised-order coefficients must also be identified with a precise finite
transformed target before direct defects or shells can be certified.

The next executable step is therefore a read-only chain telemetry scout on
an already accepted low-height fixture.  At every hierarchy level it must
record `L`, `m1`, all retained coefficients, `x`, `fracL`, `ip`, the five
correction components, the mathematical finite level value, and the direct
defect at an increasing precision ladder.  The same saved chain must compare
three routes:

```text
1. termwise W1 contour and endpoint-tail bounds;
2. direct interval enclosure of (11.239.1);
3. direct evaluation of one parent shell.                         (11.239.6)
```

A low-height replay is only a route selector.  The selected route must still
be made uniform on the physical real interval or on a fixed complex disk.
For the latter route, the object to continue holomorphically is a mathematical
fixed-branch surrogate using analytic `erf` and `psi`, with source evaluation
error enclosed separately.  The raw program's `ABS`, floor, rounding, and
piecewise selectors are not themselves a holomorphic function.  Any selector
or combinatorial transition must be excluded by strict interval margins or
partitioned with an explicit jump-mode vector.

The factors `2*pi` in this section are inherited from the paper and source
definition `e(f)=exp(2*pi*i*f)`, namely the Fourier phase normalization.  No
new circle, polygon, or geometric use of `pi` is introduced.

This section proves the source map (11.239.2), the exact defect and
accumulation identities (11.239.1), (11.239.4), and the conditional
exact-shell implication (11.239.5).  It proves no `W1` tail or contour bound,
special-function enclosure, transformed-level adapter, evaluator `C^6` or
disk theorem, transition exclusion, outer Hardy representation bound,
physical carrier value, interval kernel approximation, determinant sign or
bound, complete-current inequality, all-`q` transport, contact exclusion,
`Lambda<=0`, PF-infinity, RH, or prize-level conclusion.

## 11.241 The exact first-level parity adapter and its binary phase budget

The first item in (11.240.10) can be closed at level one.  Let the original
generalized-sum phase be

```text
A(k)=sum_(j=1)^m a_j k^j,
```

and write the source's quadratic split as

```text
2a_2=ix+xr,  ix=nint(2a_2),  |xr|<=1/2.                    (11.241.1)
```

Before the source's orientation branch, put `b_2=xr/2` and `b_j=a_j` for
`j>=3`.  If `ix` is even, put `b_1=a_1`.  If `ix` is odd, put

```text
b_1=a_1-sigma/2,

sigma=1  when a_1>=0,
sigma=-1 when a_1<0.                                      (11.241.2)
```

For `B(k)=sum b_j k^j`, direct subtraction gives

```text
A(k)-B(k)=ix k^2/2,                         ix even,
A(k)-B(k)=(ix k^2+sigma k)/2,               ix odd.       (11.241.3)
```

Both expressions are integers for integer `k`.  The even case is immediate.
In the odd case, `ix` is odd and `k^2+k` and `k^2-k` are even.  Therefore

```text
exp(2*pi*i*A(k))=exp(2*pi*i*B(k))                         (11.241.4)
```

for mathematical `pi`.

The remaining source orientation also preserves the mathematical sum.  If
`xr>0`, the source stores `B` and conjugates its internally negative-phase
sum.  If `xr<=0`, it stores `-B` and does not conjugate.  In both cases the
adapted output is the positive-phase sum associated with `B`.  Equations
(11.241.3)--(11.241.4) consequently prove that the adapted level-one finite
sum equals the original generalized Gauss sum exactly.

This is not merely a reading of comments.  The exact-bit telemetry now records
the original coefficients passed into `computarrs`.  On all sixty-four saved
chains, exact dyadic arithmetic reproduces every source level-one coefficient
and orientation decision.  The checker verifies (11.241.3) for all 105
indices on every chain, giving 6,720 exact saved checks.  Thirty-six additional
rational fixtures cover

```text
ix=-4,-3,...,4,
both signs of a_1,
both signs of xr,
65 indices per fixture.                                  (11.241.5)
```

All parity differences in (11.241.5) are exact integers.

There is, however, a separate implementation budget.  The executable does
not multiply by mathematical `2*pi`; it uses the binary128 number
`tpp_hat=-tpm`.  A 160-digit Arb comparison gives

```text
Delta=tpp_hat-2*pi
     =-1.73436202602475620495940880520867039...e-34.
                                                               (11.241.6)
```

If `nu_k=A(k)-B(k)` is the integer in (11.241.3), then the elementary
inequality `|exp(iu)-exp(iv)|<=|u-v|` and exact `2*pi` periodicity give

```text
|G_hat(A)-G_hat(B)|
   <= |Delta| sum_(k=0)^N |nu_k|.                         (11.241.7)
```

Thus mathematical periodicity alone is not a bit-level source bound when
`ix` is nonzero.  The physical chain roster must record or bound both `ix`
and `N`, and (11.241.7) must be included in the numerical adapter budget.

For the present fixture, every row has `ix=0`.  Hence `A(k)=B(k)` exactly,
all `nu_k` vanish, and the right side of (11.241.7) is zero even with the
binary source constant.  The saved level-one adapter is therefore exact
without a phase-normalization loss.  This special simplification must not be
extrapolated to unmeasured physical chains.

This section proves the mathematical coefficient/parity adapter, both source
orientation branches, and the exact saved `ix=0` source case.  It also isolates
the nonzero-`ix` binary phase budget (11.241.7).  It does not prove the
level-one-to-level-two transformed-child adapter, analytic `W1`--`W5` or
special-function bounds, a real-cell or disk enclosure, transition exclusion,
outer Hardy representation control, physical-height complexity, a carrier
value, `Lambda<=0`, PF-infinity, RH, or prize-level conclusion.

## 11.242 The cubic transformed-child Legendre adapter

The next source transformation can also be made explicit.  Let the level-one
cubic phase be

```text
F(x)=a_1 x+a_2 x^2+a_3 x^3,  y=2a_2,
```

and introduce the stationary coordinate

```text
u=F'(x)-a_1=yx+3a_3x^2.                                  (11.242.1)
```

On the branch `X(0)=0`, define the Legendre dual

```text
H(u)=uX(u)-a_2X(u)^2-a_3X(u)^3,

X(u)=2u/[y(1+sqrt(1+12a_3u/y^2))].                       (11.242.2)
```

The stable expression for `X` in (11.242.2) also covers `a_3=0`.  Formal
inversion of (11.242.1), or differentiation of `H`, gives

```text
H(u)=u^2/(2y)-a_3u^3/y^3
       +9a_3^2u^4/(2y^5)+O(u^5).                         (11.242.3)
```

This identifies the source routines exactly.  In `scheme`, `see(1)` and
`see(2)` are the two displayed coefficients of

```text
H_3(u)=u^2/(2y)-a_3u^3/y^3,                              (11.242.4)
```

while `small` is the first omitted coefficient `9a_3^2/(2y^5)`.  In

translation

```text
H_3(k-a_1)=r_0+r_1k+r_2k^2+r_3k^3,                       (11.242.5)

r_0=s_1x^2+s_2x^3,       r_1=2s_1x+3s_2x^2,
r_2=s_1+3s_2x,           r_3=s_2,

x=-a_1,  s_1=1/(2y),  s_2=-a_3/y^3.                     (11.242.6)
```

The subsequent source normalization is another exact integer-phase adapter.
Let `n_1=anint(r_1)`, split `2r_2=ix+xr`, and apply the odd-`ix` half-linear
shift from Section 11.241.  Before orientation, the raw and normalized phases
differ by

```text
n_1k+ix k^2/2,                             ix even,
n_1k+(ix k^2+sigma k)/2,                   ix odd.        (11.242.7)
```

Equation (11.242.7) is integer-valued for integer `k`.  If `xr>0`, the source
stores the normalized phase and conjugates its internally negative-phase
child.  If `xr<=0`, it negates the nonconstant coefficients and does not
conjugate.  Both branches therefore recover the same positive mathematical
phase.  The constant `r_0` is not negated; it is carried by

```text
exp(i*tpp*r_0)/(EPI4 sqrt(|xr_parent|))                   (11.242.8)
```

in the recurrence multiplier.  Here `tpp` has the explicit provenance in

The kernel amplitude denominator has a similarly useful centered form.  Put

```text
h_1=3a_3/y^2,
h_2=a_4/y^3  (zero on the saved cubic rows),
v=k-a_1.
```

Direct expansion of the source's `denn`, `rminorcor`, and `rminorcor2`
expressions gives the exact identity

```text
D(k)=denn+k(rminorcor-k rminorcor2)
    =1+h_1v+(6h_2-3h_1^2/2)v^2.                          (11.242.9)
```

Thus the denominator weighting is not an unexplained numerical adjustment.
Equation (11.242.9) also covers the first raised-order coefficient `a_4`.

The exact-bit audit applies (11.242.3)--(11.242.9) to all sixty-four saved
chains.  Every chain has `MIT=2` and degree pair `3 -> 3`; its level-one sum

not the same expression with `L(0)`.  The maximum saved value of (11.242.10)

```text
8.41734599123692218030548417635...e-6 < 0.001.           (11.242.11)
```

This explains why the saved chains do not raise degree.  The threshold

## 11.256 The displayed `ecor` phase is already present in `gc`

One source comment suggests the phase coefficient


For the cubic block-20 parents put

```text

c_src=a/x-3b a^2/x^3.                                  (11.256.2)
```

The accepted source does not insert (11.256.1) separately.  It evaluates the
full cubic Legendre phase `g(c)=a c-x c^2/2-b c^3` at (11.256.2).  Exact
symbolic expansion gives

```text
g(c_src)=a^2/(2x)-b a^3/x^3+9b^2a^4/(2x^5)
         -27b^3a^5/x^7+27b^4a^6/x^9.                  (11.256.3)
```

After multiplication by the source Fourier phase `2*pi`, substitution
`x=2phi2` makes the `b^2a^4` coefficient in (11.256.3) exactly

```text
9*pi/(32*phi2^5),                                      (11.256.4)
```

which is (11.256.1).  The source has only two executable occurrences of
`ecor`: its declaration and `ecor=0`.  It is never used in the phase
expression.  Adding `exp(i*ecor*a^4)` to the current full-`gc` path would
therefore double the leading quartic cubic-saddle correction rather than
restore a missing term.

This exact algebra removes the displayed `ecor` coefficient from the live
candidate list for this accepted source.  It does not reconstruct the
unavailable Maple implementation, prove the saddle approximation exact, or

## 11.262 Cubic obstruction to the stated vertical nonsaddle contours

The remaining contour obligation is structural.  Put

```text
F(z)=Phi1*z+Phi2*z^2+Phi3*z^3,  xi=F'(N).
```

For the equation-(82) phase `g_n(z)=n*z-F(z)`, exact expansion gives

```text
Im g_n(x+iR)=R*(n-F'(x))+Phi3*R^3.                    (11.262.1)
```

The bound printed below equation (82) retains only the linear term.  If
`Phi3<0`, then at `x=N`, `n=ceil(xi)`, the imaginary part becomes negative
once

```text
R^2>(ceil(xi)-xi)/|Phi3|.                              (11.262.2)
```

Hence the modulus `exp(-2*pi*Im g_n)` grows super-exponentially and the
vertical integrand in equation (83) does not tend to zero.

For the (67c) phase `h_n(z)=n*z+F(z)`, similarly

```text
Im h_n(x+iR)=R*(n+F'(x))-Phi3*R^3.                    (11.262.3)
```

If `Phi3>0`, then `x=0,n=1` makes the imaginary part negative once

```text
R^2>(1+Phi1)/Phi3.                                     (11.262.4)
```

The exact block-20 roster has 187 negative and 187 positive cubic
coefficients, with no zero.  Thus the stated (67b) vertical contour fails on
187 calls and the stated (67c) vertical contour fails on the other 187; no
saved cubic admits both printed infinite vertical contours.  The exact
crossover radii lie between `3.040175195895e2` and
`1.145273628477e4`.  At the certified witness `R=2R_cross`, both cases obey

```text
Im phase=-3*(positive linear factor)*R<0,              (11.262.5)
```

with 90/150-digit overlap on every call and maximum identity gap below
`1.63e-145`.

This is a gap in the stated infinite-contour justification, not a proof that
the local W2--W4 expressions cannot be recovered.  For the failing signs,
the ray `z=z0+r*exp(i*pi/6)` lies in a cubic decay sector because
`sin(3*pi/6)=1`, while its linear imaginary part has the required sign.  The
next theorem must construct a vertical-to-`pi/6` homotopy, prove that no
saddle or Stokes contribution is crossed, bound the connector and far tail
uniformly in the summation index, and only then sum the repaired (67b)--(67c)
aggregate.  Nothing in this section proves a uniform recurrence, the outer
Hardy remainder, `Lambda<=0`, PF-infinity, RH, or a prize-level result.

## 11.263 Sign-aware cubic sector-contour repair

The obstruction in Section 11.262 can be repaired without crossing a
singularity.  The useful rays are determined by the signs of the linear,
quadratic, and cubic imaginary parts together, not by the cubic part alone:

```text
                         Phi3 < 0       Phi3 > 0
(67b), g_n=nz-F(z)         5*pi/6          pi/2
(67c), h_n=nz+F(z)           pi/2          pi/6.       (11.263.1)
```

Indeed, exact cubic Taylor expansion at any `x in [0,N]` gives, in the two
slanted cases,

```text
Im[g_n(x+r*exp(5*pi*i/6))-g_n(x)]
 = (n-F'(x))*r/2 + sqrt(3)*F''(x)*r^2/4 + |Phi3|*r^3,
                                                        Phi3<0, (11.263.2)

Im[h_n(x+r*exp(pi*i/6))-h_n(x)]
 = (n+F'(x))*r/2 + sqrt(3)*F''(x)*r^2/4 + Phi3*r^3,
                                                        Phi3>0. (11.263.3)
```

For the retained vertical cases the corresponding identities are

```text
Im[g_n(x+ir)-g_n(x)]=(n-F'(x))*r+Phi3*r^3,  Phi3>0,
Im[h_n(x+ir)-h_n(x)]=(n+F'(x))*r+|Phi3|*r^3, Phi3<0.   (11.263.4)
```

The paper assumes `F''>0` on `[0,N]`.  Exact binary128 reconstruction proves
this on all 374 saved calls.  Since `F'` is then increasing,

```text
n-F'(x) >= ceil(xi)-xi > 0       in (67b),
n+F'(x) >= 1+Phi1 > 0            in (67c).             (11.263.5)
```

Consequently every coefficient in (11.263.2)--(11.263.4) is positive.  The
weakest roster-wide certified values are

```text
min F''                         > 1.1851070466517283e-2,
min 67b ray linear coefficient > 7.3178358782875733e-4,
min 67c ray linear coefficient > 2.5484104722318731e-1,
min |Phi3|                     > 1.0981527437305080e-8,
min slanted quadratic term     > 5.1316640430217331e-3. (11.263.6)
```

Let `A_n(z)` denote either polynomial amplitude times its corresponding
Fourier exponential, and close the finite parallelogram whose translated
edge is `x+R exp(i theta)`, `0<=x<=N`, with `theta` from (11.263.1).  Equations
(11.263.2)--(11.263.4) imply

```text
|A_n(x+R exp(i theta))|
 <= C*(1+R+R^2)*exp(-2*pi*|Phi3|*R^3),                (11.263.7)
```

where `C` is finite on each saved call and the omitted linear and quadratic
factors only improve decay.  Thus the translated edge tends to zero.  The
phase and amplitude are entire, so Cauchy's theorem gives the two endpoint
rays with no residue.  A saddle is not a singularity; Stokes switching can
affect a later asymptotic decomposition but contributes nothing to this exact
finite contour identity.

The slanted rays also preserve the paper's quadratic endpoint integrals.  In
the `(67b)` wedge `pi/2<=theta<=5*pi/6`, a quadratic phase `a*u-B*u^2` obeys

```text
Im(a*R*exp(i theta)-B*R^2*exp(2i theta))
 =a*R*sin(theta)-B*R^2*sin(2theta) >= a*R/2.          (11.263.8)
```

In the `(67c)` wedge `pi/6<=theta<=pi/2`, the sign is instead `a*u+B*u^2`
and both sine terms are nonnegative, again giving at least `aR/2`.  The large
rotation arcs therefore vanish, so the slanted quadratic models equal their
vertical error-function evaluations.

Finally, the outer `1/n` sums may be interchanged with the repaired rays for
each saved call.  After absolute values, their only origin singularity is
controlled by

```text
sum_{n>=1} exp(-pi*n*r)/n=-log(1-exp(-pi*r))
                         =O(1+|log r|),               (11.263.9)
```

which is integrable at zero; (11.263.7) controls infinity.  This proves exact
contour existence, connector decay, quadratic-ray rotation, and termwise
summability for the complete finite roster.

It does not yet bound the difference between the full cubic endpoint rays
and the rotated quadratic models.  In particular, the exact endpoint
quadratic coefficient `F''(N)/2=Phi2+3Phi3*N`, the cubic exponential, and the
polynomial-amplitude terms must be retained in the next enclosure before
W2--W4 can be certified.  No height-uniform recurrence, outer Hardy bound,
`Lambda<=0`, PF-infinity, RH, or prize-level conclusion follows here.

## 11.264 Logarithmic endpoint-ray reduction of the nonsaddle sums

The repaired rays allow the infinite `1/n` sums to be performed before
quadrature.  For `Im u>0` and integer `m>=1`, set

```text
K_m(u)=sum_{n=m}^infinity exp(2*pi*i*n*u)/n
      =-Log(1-exp(2*pi*i*u))
       -sum_{n=1}^{m-1} exp(2*pi*i*n*u)/n.             (11.264.1)
```

Because `|exp(2*pi*i*u)|<1`, the principal logarithm in (11.264.1) is
single-valued and analytic on every admitted ray.  At the origin,

```text
K_m(u)=-Log(-2*pi*i*u)+O(1),                           (11.264.2)
```

so the singularity is logarithmic and integrable.

Write `E_-(z)=exp(-2*pi*i*F(z))`, `E_+(z)=exp(2*pi*i*F(z))` and define

```text
J^-_m(x;theta)=integral_0^infinity
 F'(x+r*e^(i theta))*E_-(x+r*e^(i theta))*K_m(r*e^(i theta))*e^(i theta) dr,

J^+_m(x;theta)=the same integral with E_+ in place of E_-. (11.264.3)
```

Let `L=floor(xi)`, `m=L+1`, and choose `theta_b,theta_c` from (11.263.1).
Absolute interchange from Section 11.263 and integer `N` give the exact
source-oriented tail identities

```text
B^-=J^-_m(0;theta_b)-J^-_m(N;theta_b),
C^-=conj(J^+_1(N;theta_c)-J^+_1(0;theta_c)).           (11.264.4)
```

Here `B^-` is the conjugate of (67b), while `C^-` is the conjugate of
(67c), including its leading minus sign.  The equality
`K_m(N+u)=K_m(u)` uses `N in Z`; it is not a periodicity assumption on
`F`.

The remaining endpoint term follows directly from (67a).  With
`g_n(y)=ny-F(y)` and `H_L=sum_{n=1}^L 1/n`, use
`F'(y)=n-g_n'(y)` to obtain

```text
sum_{n=1}^L (1/n) integral_0^N F'(y)e^(2*pi*i*g_n(y))dy
=sum_{n=1}^L integral_0^N e^(2*pi*i*g_n(y))dy
 +i*(E_-(N)-1)*H_L/(2*pi).                            (11.264.5)
```

Let

```text
P^-=sum_{k=0}^N E_-(k),
I69^-=sum_{n=j0}^L integral_0^N exp(2*pi*i*(ny-F(y)))dy,
j0=ceil(Phi1) in {0,1}.                               (11.264.6)
```

When `Phi1<0`, the `n=0` integral is already in `I69^-`; when `Phi1>0`
it remains the exact zero-mode represented approximately by W4.  Combining
(11.264.4)--(11.264.6) yields

```text
P^-=I69^-+Q_exact^-,

Q_exact^-=(1+E_-(N))/2+i*(E_-(N)-1)*H_L/(2*pi)
          +B^-+C^-
          +1_(Phi1>0)*integral_0^N E_-(y)dy.          (11.264.7)
```

Thus the exact nonsaddle target is four logarithmic endpoint-ray integrals,
one optional finite zero-mode integral, and explicit endpoint terms.  There
is no infinite numerical `n` truncation in (11.264.7).

The exact selector audit has 369 calls with `L=1` and five with `L=2`; the
four `(sign Phi1,sign Phi3)` counts are `91,74,96,113`.  As an orientation
guard only, 50-digit mpmath quadrature on chains `1,2,3,36` compares the

The absolute gaps are respectively below `2.05e-20`, `5.1e-49`, `2.75e-34`,
and `7.01e-32`.  These four quadratures are non-rigorous diagnostics and do

Sections 11.265--11.266 discharge the finite singularity-subtracted Arb

## 11.267 Exact endpoint-linearization error architecture

At endpoint `x in {0,N}`, put `A_x=F'(x)` and

```text
F(x+u)=F(x)+A_x*u+B_x*u^2+Phi3*u^3,
B_x=Phi2+3*Phi3*x.                                    (11.267.1)
```

The generic approximation in equations (84), (88), (90), and (92) is linear
at the endpoint.  W2 and W3 replace one poorly separated generic mode by its
quadratic error-function model; W4 supplies the corresponding positive-Phi1
zero-mode model.  Thus replacing every logarithmic ray by one quadratic ray
does not represent the published approximation.

The generic linear rays can be summed exactly.  For the `(67b)` tail starting
at `m=L+1` and the `(67c)` tail starting at one,

```text
J_b,lin(x)=i*E_-(x)/(2*pi)*[psi(m)-psi(m-A_x)],
J_c,lin(x)=i*E_+(x)/(2*pi)*[psi(1+A_x)-psi(1)].        (11.267.2)
```

Let

```text
R_b=[J_b(0)-J_b,lin(0)]-[J_b(N)-J_b,lin(N)],
R_c=conj([J_c(N)-J_c,lin(N)]-[J_c(0)-J_c,lin(0)]).
                                                               (11.267.3)
```

The digamma recurrence and `H_L=psi(L+1)+gamma` give the exact generic
identity

```text
endpoint_half+a_endpoint+B_linear+C_linear
 =paper_endpoint_half+W5.                              (11.267.4)
```

Consequently the full endpoint error has the exact architecture

```text
Q_exact-Q_paper=R_b+R_c+zero_mode-W2-(W3 or W4).       (11.267.5)
```

A 70/110-digit Arb pilot on chains `1,2,3,36` covers all four sign branches.
Equation (11.267.4) has maximum gap below `1.824e-106`, while (11.267.5)
has maximum gap below `4.994e-14`.  This validates the decomposition but does
not yet make it uniform in height.

## 11.270 Singularity-free exceptional-mode recombination

Let `m=ceil(F'(N))`, `delta=m-F'(N)`, and `eta=1+Phi1`.  The
exceptional quadratic modes in W2--W4 use the paper's global coefficient
`Phi2`, not the exact endpoint Taylor coefficient
`Phi2+3*Phi3*x`.  If `M_b` and `M_c` denote one endpoint-ray Fourier mode,
direct evaluation of equations (89), (93), and (94) gives

```text
W2=M_b,lin(N)-M_b,quad(N),
W3=conj(M_c,lin(0)-M_c,quad(0)),
W4=Z_quad(0)+i*exp(-2*pi*i*F(N))/(2*pi*F'(N)).       (11.270.1)
```

Remove the exceptional mode from each generic remainder and call the
remaining sums `G_b,G_c`.  Then

```text
R_b-W2=G_b-[M_b,exact(N)-M_b,quad(N)],               (11.270.2)
R_c-W3=G_c-conj[M_c,exact(0)-M_c,quad(0)].           (11.270.3)
```

Neither right side contains `1/delta` or `1/eta`.  On the W4 branch the
corresponding lower pair is

```text
[zero_mode-Z_quad(0)]
 +[R_c-i*exp(-2*pi*i*F(N))/(2*pi*F'(N))].            (11.270.4)
```

The exact modes in (11.270.2)--(11.270.3) were integrated directly on the
certified cubic rays, with explicit tail balls, at 70 and 110 decimal digits.
All identities overlap on chains `1,2,3,36`, and then on all 374 calls.  The
all-call audit contains 165 W3 and 209 W4 branches.  Its maximum paper-model
identity gap is below `1.857e-106`, its maximum complete recombination gap is
below `5.237e-14`, and its maximum exceptional-mode tail is below
`5.861e-31`.

The four singularity-free pieces may still have a triangle/correction ratio
as large as `6483.649`; thus (11.270.2)--(11.270.4) remove false poles but do
not license separate absolute bounds for every endpoint family.

## 11.271 Gap-uniform shared-contour majorants for W2 and W3

After (11.270.1), integration by parts cancels the common reciprocal boundary
term before estimation.  For the upper exceptional mode, interpolate between
the paper quadratic phase and the exact endpoint cubic phase:

```text
H_t(u)=delta*u-(Phi2+3*t*Phi3*N)*u^2-t*Phi3*u^3,
0<=t<=1.                                             (11.271.1)
```

If `Phi3>=0`, deform every member of the homotopy to
`arg(u)=7*pi/12`; if `Phi3<0`, use `arg(u)=3*pi/4`.  The integrands are
entire and the closing arcs vanish in these common decay sectors.  Put

```text
B_*=min(Phi2,Phi2+3*Phi3*N),
sigma_b=1/2  for Phi3>=0,   sigma_b=1 for Phi3<0,
a_b=2*pi*B_*sigma_b.                                 (11.271.2)
```

The quadratic decay along the whole homotopy is at least
`a_b*r^2`, while differentiation in `t` contributes at most
`2*pi*|Phi3|*(3*N*r^2+r^3)`.  Dropping the nonnegative linear and cubic
decay and evaluating the Gaussian moments proves the gap-uniform theorem

```text
|M_b,exact-M_b,quad|
 <=2*pi*|Phi3|*[3*N*sqrt(pi)/(4*a_b^(3/2))+1/(2*a_b^2)].
                                                               (11.271.3)
```

For W3 use the homotopy
`eta*u+Phi2*u^2+t*Phi3*u^3`.  The common ray is `pi/6` for
`Phi3>=0` and `5*pi/12` for `Phi3<0`; in both cases
`sin(2*arg(u))>=1/2`.  The same argument gives

```text
|M_c,exact-M_c,quad| <= pi*|Phi3|/(pi*Phi2)^2.        (11.271.4)
```

Crucially, (11.271.3) contains no `delta` and (11.271.4) contains no `eta`.
They remain finite at the hypothetical exact-gap boundaries.  Pi is inherited
from the Fourier phase `exp(2*pi*i*n*u)`; it is not a fitted constant.

Arb applies (11.271.3) to all 374 saved W2 modes and (11.271.4) to all 165
W3 modes with positive interval slack.  The largest bounds are respectively
below `3.8600e-3` and `9.939e-5`.  The worst bound/actual ratios are about
`2.03e4` and `3.39e5`, so these are conservative analytic majorants rather
than fitted approximations.

This is the first gap-uniform exceptional-mode bound in the block-20 route.
It does not yet cover the W4 zero-mode pair, the coupled generic endpoint
tails, recurrence propagation, outer Hardy control, `Lambda<=0`, PF-infinity,
RH, or a prize-level conclusion.

## 11.272 W4 contour identity and complete endpoint Hurwitz majorant

Assume `Phi1>0`.  Let `H_exact(x,0)` be the lower half-ray integral of
`exp(-2*pi*i*F)` starting at `x`.  For `Phi3>=0` use angle `-pi/6`; for
`Phi3<0` use `-5*pi/12`.  Strict positivity of `F'` and of the endpoint
quadratic coefficient makes the closing connector vanish.  Cauchy's theorem
then gives

```text
zero_mode=H_exact(0,0)-H_exact(N,0).                  (11.272.1)
```

The first W4 term is the global-`Phi2` quadratic half-ray
`H_quad(0,0)`.  Its endpoint term is exactly the negative of the linear
zero-mode half-ray at `N`:

```text
H_linear(N,0)=-i*exp(-2*pi*i*F(N))/(2*pi*F'(N)),
zero_mode-W4
 =[H_exact(0,0)-H_quad(0,0)]
  -[H_exact(N,0)-H_linear(N,0)].                     (11.272.2)
```

Thus W4 also belongs to the exact-minus-model endpoint architecture; its
explicit boundary is not a separate approximation error.  Direct 70/110-
digit Arb half-ray integration verifies (11.272.1)--(11.272.2) on all 209
positive-`Phi1` calls.  The maximum identity gap is below `5.901e-41` and
the maximum explicit half-ray tail below `3.530e-41`.

It remains to sum the generic exact-minus-linear modes.  On the same
sign-aware common rays, let `q>0` be the first linear phase gap, `B>0` the
local quadratic coefficient, and `C=|Phi3|`.  Interpolation from the linear
phase to the full cubic phase, while retaining only
`pi*(q+k)r` of the positive decay, gives

```text
sum_(k>=0)|D_(q+k)|
 <=4*B*zeta(3,q)/pi^2+12*C*zeta(4,q)/pi^3.           (11.272.3)
```

The two terms are the exact moments
`integral r^2 exp(-a r)dr=2/a^3` and
`integral r^3 exp(-a r)dr=6/a^4`, summed over the modes.  The admissible
Hurwitz arguments are

```text
upper at 0: m-Phi1,       upper at N: m+1-xi,
W3 at 0:    2+Phi1,       W3 at N:    1+xi,
W4 at 0:    1+Phi1,       W4 at N:    xi.             (11.272.4)
```

Pairing the exceptional modes first is essential: every argument in
(11.272.4) stays positive as `delta=m-xi` or `eta=1+Phi1` tends to zero.
Adding (11.271.3) or (11.271.4) to the appropriate generic sums therefore
proves a symbolic selector-gap-uniform bound for both complete endpoint
families and hence for `|Q_exact-Q_paper|`.

Arb validates the theorem on all 374 calls with positive interval slack.
Roster-wide bounds are

```text
max upper-family majorant   <8.507e-3,
max lower-family majorant   <4.550e-3,
max complete local majorant <1.069e-2.                (11.272.5)
```

The worst complete-majorant/correction ratio is below `2784.243`, at chain
260.  This is a conservative local-error contract, not a fitted correction.
The next obligation is to propagate it through the actual recursive and
direct weights and then combine it with coefficient transport, Legendre
tails, cross-block scaling, and the outer Hardy remainder.  Section 11.272
does not establish any of those global budgets, `Lambda<=0`, PF-infinity,
RH, or a prize-level conclusion.

## 11.274 Retained-decay endpoint majorant

The Hurwitz estimate (11.272.3) integrates the homotopy only after dropping
its positive quadratic and cubic decay.  Keep that decay instead.  On one of
the sign-aware common rays put

```text
alpha=2*pi*sin(theta),
beta =2*pi*B*|sin(2*theta)|,
gamma=2*pi*C*|sin(3*theta)|,
varphi(x)=(1-exp(-x))/x,  varphi(0)=1.                (11.274.1)
```

For the exact-minus-linear modes starting at gap `q>0`, integrate the
linear-to-cubic homotopy parameter before taking the outer absolute value and
sum the modes geometrically.  This proves

```text
sum_(k>=0)|D_(q+k)| <= S(B,C,q),

S(B,C,q)=2*pi*integral_0^infinity
 (B*r^2+C*r^3) exp(-alpha*q*r)
 varphi(beta*r^2+gamma*r^3)/(1-exp(-alpha*r)) dr.     (11.274.2)
```

The origin is removable: its integrand is `O(r)`.  Since
`0<varphi(x)<=1`, (11.274.2) is no larger than the corresponding
linear-moment estimate, while retaining all decay shared by the homotopy.

The exceptional modes already have their reciprocal boundaries cancelled.
Their positive linear selector-gap decay may also be retained:

```text
E_b=2*pi*C*integral_0^infinity (3*N*r^2+r^3)
       exp(-alpha_b*delta*r-a_b*r^2) dr,

E_c=2*pi*C*integral_0^infinity r^3
       exp(-alpha_c*kappa*r-a_c*r^2) dr,              (11.274.3)
```

where `kappa=1+Phi1` on W3 rows and `kappa=Phi1` on W4 rows.  Both formulas
remain finite at `delta=0` or `kappa=0`; no selector reciprocal has been
reintroduced.  The W3/W4 distinction in `kappa` is essential because W4
replaces the zero mode.

Arb evaluates (11.274.2)--(11.274.3) at 60 and 90 decimal digits for all 374
recursive calls.  The compact interval is `[10^-12,64]`.  An explicit
`O(epsilon^2)` bound covers the omitted origin, exact exponential moments
bound generic infinity, and exact Gaussian moments bound exceptional
infinity.  Both precision levels overlap on every call, and every sharpened
upper, lower, and complete majorant dominates the independently enclosed
exact endpoint family.

Transport through the exact weights of Section 11.273 gives

```text
max_i B_endpoint,retained
 <2.189214921476639e-3,
max_i B_endpoint,retained/0.005
 <0.437842984295328,
outputs below 0.005: 15/15.                           (11.274.4)
```

Equation (11.274.4) closes the finite block-20 **endpoint-model portion** of
the nominal local budget without using the observed signed cancellation.  It
does not bound coefficient neighborhoods, arithmetic outside the admitted
local models, the complete Legendre tail, other blocks, the outer Hardy

## 11.276 Complete saved-point cubic Legendre-tail transport

The source raise-order test in Section 11.242 records only the first omitted
coefficient.  For a cubic parent the whole omitted transformed-child series
can instead be recovered from the exact stationary radical.  Put

```text
u=k-a1,  y=2a2,  z=12a3*u/y^2,
X=2u/[y(1+sqrt(1+z))].                                  (11.276.1)
```

Then the exact and source-truncated Legendre phases are

```text
H(u)=uX-(y/2)X^2-a3X^3,
H3(u)=u^2/(2y)-a3u^3/y^3.                               (11.276.2)
```

There is also an amplitude remainder.  Direct substitution into
`F''(X)=y+6a3X` gives

```text
F''(X)=y sqrt(1+z),
A(z)=(1+z)^(1/4),
D2(z)=1+z/4-3z^2/32.                                    (11.276.3)
```

Here `1/A` is the exact normalized stationary amplitude and `1/D2` is the
source's quadratic denominator approximation.  Thus at one saved child index

```text
|exp(i*tpm*H)/A-exp(i*tpm*H3)/D2|
 <= |1/A-1/D2|+|tpm| |H-H3|/D2.                         (11.276.4)
```

The implementation evaluates the direct left side and verifies (11.276.4).
It adds `H-H3` only after the fixed child integer, parity, and orientation
normalization.  Consequently `tpm` is the saved binary source constant and no
exact-`2*pi` periodicity shortcut is used.  The child termwise majorant is
multiplied by the saved recurrence-multiplier magnitude and then by the exact
Section 11.273 output weights.

## 11.277 Coefficient-cell transport of the complete cubic Legendre tail

Direct interval subtraction of `H-H3` would discard the smallness proved at
the centers.  The exact radical in Section 11.276 has a cancellation-preserving
factorization.  With `s=sqrt(1+z)`, first write

```text
H/(u^2/y)=2(1+2s)/[3(1+s)^2],
H3/(u^2/y)=(7-s^2)/12.                                  (11.277.1)
```

Exact subtraction and `z=s^2-1` give

```text
H-H3=(u^2/y)(s-1)^2(s^2+4s+1)/[12(1+s)^2]
     =(u^2/y)z^2(s^2+4s+1)/[12(1+s)^4].                 (11.277.2)
```

Equation (11.277.2) is nonnegative whenever `y>0` and `1+z>0`.  It exposes the
quadratic small factor `z^2` explicitly and therefore remains sharp under Arb
evaluation of a whole selector box.

There is a second useful cancellation.  If `theta` is the fixed normalized
child phase, then one exact-versus-source term is

```text
exp(i*tpm*theta){
 exp(i*tpm*(H-H3))/(1+z)^(1/4)
 -1/(1+z/4-3z^2/32)}.                                   (11.277.3)
```

The prefactor has modulus one.  It is removed before estimation rather than
enclosing two broad oscillatory terms separately.  The remaining magnitude in
braces is evaluated directly and checked against the elementary amplitude-plus-
phase bound from (11.276.4).  The source-anchored multiplier enclosure from
Section 11.275 is applied after summing the child-term bounds.

## 11.278 Correlated exact-W1 recurrence identity on coefficient cells

The separate parent, child, multiplier, and equation-(69) columns in Section
11.275 are not independent once W1 is defined by the exact equation-(69)
remainder.  Let `P` be the exact finite parent sum, `I69` the sum of the fixed
equation-(69) mode integrals, and `Q_exact` the endpoint-complete finite Poisson
complement.  Section 11.264 gives


```text

```

If `Q_paper` is the W2--W5 endpoint model, then the corrected recurrence is


This cancellation is exact.  In particular, arbitrary perturbations of `C`


## 11.295 Fail-closed outer-Hardy representation ledger

For each real target height `t_j=10^10+(j-8)/100`, `1<=j<=15`, fix the
exact mathematical targets

```text
Z(t_j)=exp(i theta(t_j)) zeta(1/2+i t_j),
theta(t)=Im log Gamma(1/4+i t/2)-t log(pi)/2,             (11.295.1)

Xi(t_j)=-((t_j^2+1/4)/2)
          |pi^(-s_j/2) Gamma(s_j/2)| Z(t_j),
s_j=1/2+i t_j.                                           (11.295.2)
```

Equation (11.295.2) uses the convention
`xi(s)=s(s-1)pi^(-s/2)Gamma(s/2)zeta(s)/2`.  These
normalizations and critical-line conjugation are exact.  The `pi` in
(11.295.1)--(11.295.2) is the standard circle constant.  In the legacy
source its binary128 approximation is generated visibly as `p=4*atan(1)`;
that source operation is not silently substituted for an exact interval.

The source-equivalent observer fixes the complete fifteen-value binary128
output vector and all 50880 weight rows for blocks 20--35.  Section 11.294
then supplies one enclosed internal corrected-model column,

```text
max B_20--35,internal < 1.185343683305326e-3.             (11.295.3)
```

The reverse dependency audit does not identify (11.295.3) with
`|Z_source-Z|`.  The paper's equations (126)--(127) contain relative
`O(epsilon_t)` and `O(Lambda_alpha^-1)` factors, and the paper explicitly
states that the hybrid representation is not exact.  No constant-bearing
outer theorem covering those factors is imported by the executable.
Consequently the source input `et=0.005` is a requested accuracy parameter,
not a proved Hardy-error bound.

The fail-closed ledger has four exact rows, one enclosed internal row, and
thirteen open rows.  The open rows are:

```text
central PARI-to-binary128 phase/scale propagation;
the fourteen shifted-theta and shifted-a Taylor remainders;
the hybrid (126)--(127) representation and H(t) normalization;
lower-alpha Euler--Maclaurin and exponential tails;
block-zero transition quadrature and direct terms;
cubic blocks 1--19;
the upper-alpha/portcullis cutoff;
the n<=621 lower Riemann--Siegel source arithmetic;
higher Riemann--Siegel corrections and its final remainder;
uncovered source accumulation rounding;
the assembled outer Hardy remainder.                         (11.295.4)
```

Thus all fifteen rows have `hardy_z_certified=false` and
`xi_certified=false`.  This is useful progress: it locates the present wall
upstream of the corrected recurrence rather than inside it.

The next finite gate is an independent Arb enclosure of the exact Hardy
targets at the same fifteen heights, used only to falsify or calibrate the
saved estimator.  The proof route is distinct: begin with an exact classical
Riemann--Siegel or exact Hardy identity, partition it exactly, and attach a

corrected cubic machinery.  Finite calibration is not evidence for RH by

## 11.297 Exact lower-RS versus hybrid-upper residual split

Use the last stage-1 checkpoint to recover the source upper value `P_j`
before the Riemann--Siegel addition, and the stage-2 checkpoint to recover
the source lower contribution `R_j` and final rounded value `S_j` separately.
Define with exact Arb phases

```text
L_j=2 sum_(n=1)^621 cos(theta(t_j)-t_j log n)/sqrt(n)+C_0(t_j),
U_j=Z(t_j)-L_j,                                           (11.297.1)
```

where `C_0` is the leading endpoint formula visibly used by the source.
Then the total residual has the exact decomposition

```text
S_j-Z(t_j)=(R_j-L_j)+(P_j-U_j)+(S_j-P_j-R_j).             (11.297.2)
```

The three terms in (11.297.2) respectively measure the lower source
arithmetic, the hybrid-upper approximation, and the final binary128
addition.  Arb enclosures at 70 and 110 decimal digits overlap for all
fifteen values of `L_j`, `U_j`, and `Z(t_j)`.  A 130-digit independent
checker overlaps every saved component and verifies that all fifteen
reconstructed identity residuals contain zero.

The lower component is not the observed wall.  Across all outputs,

```text
max |R_j-L_j|
 < 4.861491844763081e-9,

max |S_j-P_j-R_j|
 < 7.000000000000001e-41.                                (11.297.3)
```

In contrast, the hybrid-upper discrepancy satisfies

```text
min |P_j-U_j|
 > 0.006636315886290539,

max |P_j-U_j|
 < 0.007247383052486167,

min |P_j-U_j| / max |R_j-L_j|
```

The block-zero source uses the same circle constant as the paper: in the
