```text
a=sqrt(8t/pi).                                             (11.300.1)
```

Thus `pi` here is not an inserted geometric parameter or a selectable
polygon; it is the usual circumference-to-diameter constant represented by
the source's `4 atan(1)` identity.  At the central height `t=10^10`, the
source chooses `M2=159577` and tests the transition variables



For an odd alpha in block zero put

```text
b(b-s)+log(s+b)+1
    =(log(pc)+1/pc+1)/2.                                  (11.300.4)
```

For (11.300.4), `(s+b)(s-b)=1` and
`log(pc)=2log(s+b)` because `s+b>0`.  Consequently the normalized source
`ter` expression is algebraically identical to the left-hand alpha summand

introduce no further approximation.

The gate reconstructs all 101 odd-alpha summands from `159577` through
`159777` at each output.  The resulting 1,515 independent summand evaluations
differ from the saved binary128 block-zero checkpoints by at most

```text
2.681024869518533e-23.                                    (11.300.5)
```

The source also uses an unsuffixed default-real literal `0.01` in the shifted
block-zero parameters.  Replacing that rounded literal by exact decimal


This is a real implementation detail, but it is over ten billion times too

The terminal value `alpha=159777` is itself an odd pole of the contour
integrand in paper equation (8).  It cannot literally be used as a real-axis
circle intercept.  The paper accordingly permits a slight radius adjustment
whenever the circle would cross a pole.  Write

```text
L=t/pi-R,       U=t/pi+R=2t/pi-L                         (11.302.1)
```

for the left and right real intercepts.  At each of the fifteen saved heights,
the gate constructs two explicit selectors `L_s,L_c` in the same open pole
gap

```text
159777 < L_s < L_c < 159779.                              (11.302.2)
```

The first lies between `159777` and `alpha(37945;t)` and induces classical
tail start `37946`.  The second lies between `alpha(37941;t)` and
`alpha(37940;t)` and induces tail start `37941`.  At the central output,

```text
L_s=159777.0875851615063299...,
L_c=159778.1247714375689283....                           (11.302.3)
```

The opposite intercepts satisfy

```text
6366037945 < U_c < U_s < 6366037947                     (11.302.4)
```

at every output.  Thus no far-side odd pole is crossed.  Both radii are also
strictly smaller than the radial distance from the centre `t/pi` to the branch
point `z=+a`; `z=-a` is farther away.  The annulus between the two circles
therefore contains neither an odd pole nor a denominator branch point.  The
two contours enclose exactly the same alpha residues.

Appendix-B equation (B9) has lower integration limit

```text
u_0(R)=t/(pi R),                                          (11.302.5)
```

and equation (B15a) places its `N`-saddle at

```text
u_sad(N)=1/(1-1/N-2pi N/t).                              (11.302.6)
```

Combining (11.302.6) with equation (124) gives the exact identity

```text
1/u_sad(N)=1-pi alpha(N;t)/t,
alpha(N;t)=2N+t/(pi N).                                  (11.302.7)
```

Consequently the equation-(124) root threshold and the B15a saddle crossing are the
same threshold, not merely asymptotically related.  Arb certifies

```text
u_sad(37940)>u_0(R_c)>u_0(R_s)>u_sad(37946),             (11.302.8)
```

while, for exactly `N=37941,...,37945`,

```text
u_0(R_s)<u_sad(N)<u_0(R_c).                              (11.302.9)
```

```text
D(N,R_s)-D(N,R_c)
 = integral_[u_0(R_s)]^[u_0(R_c)] f_D(N,u) du.           (11.302.10)
```

This is an exact finite-interval identity for every `N`; for the five modes in

```text
S(R)=C(0,R)+D(0,R)
     +2 sum_(N>=1)(-1)^N {C(N,R)+D(N,R)}.                 (11.302.11)
```

Since the two contours enclose the same poles, Cauchy deformation and the
literal factors in equations (13) and (24) give

```text
R_s A(R_s)-i t S(R_s)/pi
 =R_c A(R_c)-i t S(R_c)/pi.                              (11.302.12)
```

The diagnostic midpoint residual in Section 11.301 therefore defines a

Equation (11.302.10) reduces the crossed `D` contribution to five short real

```text
Phi_s=t/2 log(t/(2pi N^2))-t-pi N^2,                    (11.303.2)

Phi_N(w)-Phi_s
 =t {log(1+q)-q+q^2/[2w_s^2(1+q)^2]}.                  (11.303.3)
```


The primary-source correction in Section 11.305 permits the saved computation

where `Q_src` is the full source hybrid upper contribution and `rho_add` is
the final source addition-rounding residual.  For the 36 endpoint cutoffs
certified in Section 11.299, let `Q_k` be the cumulative source contribution,

```text
e_k=(Q_k-Q_(k-1))-(T_k-T_(k-1)),  k=0,...,35,          (11.306.2)
```

with `Q_(-1)=T_(-1)=0`.  Exact telescoping gives

```text
sum_(k=0)^35 e_k=Q_src-T_upper.                          (11.306.3)
```

```text
E_lower=L_src-L_exact,       R_upper=U_exact-T_upper,    (11.306.4)
```

then the complete finite source-aligned identity is

```text
E_total=Z_src-Z_exact
       =E_lower+sum_(k=0)^35 e_k-R_upper+rho_add.         (11.306.5)
```

Here `pi` is the usual circular constant occurring in the published

## 11.307 Equation-(10) pair current and the global incomplete theta derivative

The source-aligned error in Section 11.306 can be reorganized before any
blockwise approximation.  In paper equation (10), a collection centered at an
even pivot `alpha_E` pairs the odd indices `alpha_E+j` and `alpha_E-j`.  If

```text
u=pi*alpha_E*j*x/2,
```

then the exact algebraic pair is

```text
(alpha_E+j)e^(iu)+(alpha_E-j)e^(-iu)
 =2[alpha_E cos(u)+i*j sin(u)].                           (11.307.1)
```

The common phase `exp(i*pi*(alpha_E^2+j^2)*x/4)` is understood on both sides.
Before equation (51), the paper explicitly drops the `i*j*sin(u)` term and
applies approximation (50).  The retained and omitted pieces together obey

```text
P(alpha_E,j;x)
 =4/(i*pi*x) d/d(alpha_E)
   [e^(i*pi*(alpha_E^2+j^2)*x/4)
    cos(pi*alpha_E*j*x/2)].                              (11.307.2)
```

Thus the omitted term completes a pivot derivative current; it is not an
unrelated additive correction.

The source checkpoint gives an exact combinatorial simplification.  Block zero
contains the 101 direct odd alphas from `159577` through `159777`.  For every
block `k>=1`,

```text
RN1_k=RN1_(k-1)+2(MT_k+1)aenums_k.                       (11.307.3)
```

The even pivots are spaced by `2(MT_k+1)`, and their odd offsets fill the next
interval without overlap.  Consequently all 36 blocks partition exactly

```text
159577,159579,...,5122421,                               (11.307.4)
```

a contiguous roster of `2,481,423` odd alphas.  It consists of 101 direct
terms and 7,034 paired collections, represented by 14,068 Gaussian phase
sums.

Define

```text
Theta_[A,B](x,y)
 =sum_(A<=alpha<=B, alpha odd)
   exp(i*pi*alpha^2*x/4+i*pi*alpha*y/2).                 (11.307.5)
```

Termwise differentiation of this finite sum gives the exact global identity

```text
sum alpha exp(i*pi*alpha^2*x/4)
 =2/(i*pi) d/dy Theta_[A,B](x,y)|_(y=0).                 (11.307.6)
```

Equations (11.307.2) and (11.307.6) preserve both members of every pair and
the entire alpha roster before asymptotic approximation.  They therefore
supply a viable signed coordinate for (11.306.8).

A necessary guard is that a continuous derivative sampled on a step-two
lattice is not automatically a boundary telescope.  For example, with
`G(alpha)=alpha^2` on `{1,3}`, the sum of derivatives is `8`, while the naive
step-two endpoint quotient is `12`.  A finite Poisson, Abel, or
Euler--Maclaurin theorem with explicit endpoints is still required.

## 11.308 Finite-Poisson derivation of the portcullis saddle

For a `C^1` function with piecewise `C^2` derivative on an integer interval,
the symmetric finite-Poisson identity is

```text
sum_(n=0)^L f(n)
 =(f(0)+f(L))/2
  +lim_(M->infinity) sum_(m=-M)^M
     integral_0^L f(u)e^(-2*pi*i*m*u)du.                 (11.308.1)
```

This follows from the Dirichlet-kernel endpoint convention.  Apply it to
`alpha=A+2u` in (11.307.6).  At `y=0`, mode `m` has the exact grouped alpha
integral

```text
J_m=(-1)^m/2 integral_A^B
 alpha e^(i*pi*(x*alpha^2/4-m*alpha))dalpha              (11.308.2)
```

and hence

```text
J_m=(-1)^m/x {[E_m(B)-E_m(A)]/(i*pi)+m F_m},             (11.308.3)
```

where `E_m(alpha)=exp(i*pi*(x*alpha^2/4-m*alpha))` and

```text
F_m=e^(-i*pi*m^2/x) integral_A^B
 exp(i*pi*x*(alpha-2m/x)^2/4)dalpha.                     (11.308.4)
```

The endpoint current and Fresnel integral in (11.308.3) must stay paired mode
by mode; their series need not converge separately.

After insertion into the exact Kummer integral (9), the joint phase is

```text
Phi(alpha,x;m,t)
 =pi*alpha^2*x/4-pi*m*alpha
  +(t/2)log((1-x)/x).                                    (11.308.5)
```

Its stationary equations give

```text
x_m=2*pi*m^2/(t+2*pi*m^2),
alpha_m=2m+t/(pi*m).                                     (11.308.6)
```

The second equation in (11.308.6) is exactly paper equation (124), with
`m=N`.  This derives the occurrence of `pi` from the Kummer quadratic phase
and the Fourier dual frequency.  It is not an inserted geometric constant.

The full Hessian satisfies

```text
det Hess(Phi)=-(2*pi*m^2+t)^3/(8*m^2*t)<0                (11.308.7)
```

for `m,t>0`.  The turning point in the projected map `alpha(N)` is therefore
not a degeneracy of the two-variable saddle.

Solving (11.308.6) for `N` gives

```text
N_+ + N_-=alpha/2,       N_+ N_-=t/(2*pi),               (11.308.8)
```

and the continuous involution `N*=t/(2*pi*N)` satisfies
`x_(N*)=1-x_N`.  It does not generally preserve the integer mode lattice, so
the two reflected branches must be recombined by (11.308.1), not by rounding
the reciprocal partner.

At the central height, 130-digit interval reconstruction gives

```text
N_-(159577) in (39852,39853),
N_+(159577) in (39936,39937),
N_t            in (39894,39895),
N_-(5122421) in (621,622),
N_+(5122421) in (2560588,2560589).                       (11.308.9)
```

The lower interior branch contains `622..39852`.  The lower-alpha endpoint
gap consists of 84 modes: `39853..39894` below `N_t` and `39895..39936` above
it, exactly 42 on each reflected side.  Thus the 39,273-term classical source
upper range `622..39894` is 39,231 interior modes plus 42 endpoint-Fresnel
modes.

The first remaining issue at this stage is an endpoint-uniform
finite-Poisson interchange for the Kummer weight.  Section 11.309 closes that
interchange issue.  Quantitative stationary and nonstationary estimates must
still retain both reflected branches, all 84 turning modes, each grouped
boundary/Fresnel mode, and symmetric tails.  Only after comparison with
`T_upper` may the source cubic truncation and Gaussian evaluator defects be
inserted.

Sections 11.307--11.308 prove exact reductions and finite classifications, not
that interchange theorem, a source-aligned height-uniform Hardy-error bound,
`Lambda<=0`, RH, or a prize-level conclusion.

## 11.309 Height-uniform symmetric-Poisson interchange

Put `alpha=A+2u`, `0<=u<=L=(B-A)/2`, and

```text
f_x(u)=(A+2u)e^(i*pi*x*(A+2u)^2/4),
W_t(x)=e^[i(t/2)log((1-x)/x)]/[x(1-x)]^(1/4).           (11.309.1)
```

Let `I_m(x)=integral_0^L f_x(u)e^(-2*pi*i*m*u)du`.  Two
integrations by parts and the integer identity
`e^(-2*pi*i*m*L)=1` give, with `D=2*pi*i*m`,

```text
I_m=-Delta f_x/D-Delta f_x'/D^2+R_m/D^2.                (11.309.2)
```

Pairing `m` with `-m` before taking absolute values cancels the entire
`Delta f_x/D` current:

```text
I_m+I_(-m)=(-2 Delta f_x'+R_m+R_(-m))/D^2,              (11.309.3)

|I_m+I_(-m)|
 <=[|Delta f_x'|+integral_0^L|f_x''(u)|du]
    /(2*pi^2*m^2).                                      (11.309.4)
```

The exact derivatives are

```text
f_x'=e^(i*pi*x*alpha^2/4)[2+i*pi*x*alpha^2],
f_x''=e^(i*pi*x*alpha^2/4)
      [6i*pi*x*alpha-pi^2*x^2*alpha^3].                 (11.309.5)
```

They imply the pointwise majorant

```text
C_AB(x)=4+pi*x(5B^2-A^2)/2+pi^2*x^2(B^4-A^4)/8.        (11.309.6)
```

Because `|W_t(x)|=[x(1-x)]^(-1/4)`, beta integration and
`sum_(m>M)m^(-2)<=1/M` yield, for every real `t` and `M>=1`,

```text
|K_t-K_(t,M)|<=C_AB/(2*pi^2*M),                         (11.309.7)

C_AB=B(3/4,3/4)
 [4+pi(5B^2-A^2)/4+7pi^2(B^4-A^4)/160].                (11.309.8)
```

Thus the symmetric Poisson limit may be interchanged with the Kummer
integral without an auxiliary endpoint regulator.  The result is uniform in
height on each fixed finite roster.  The source-roster coefficient exceeds
`10^25`, however, so (11.309.7) is a convergence theorem, not a viable
quantitative source-error estimate.  Phase-adapted estimates are still
essential.

For `m>0`, set

```text

     erf(e^(-i*pi/4)sqrt(pi/2)z).                        (11.310.2)
```

Then `F'(z)=e^(i*pi*z^2/2)`, and (11.308.4) is exactly

```text
F_m=e^(-i*pi*m^2/x)sqrt(2/x)[F(z_B)-F(z_A)].            (11.310.3)
```

At the reduced saddle `x_m` from (11.308.6),

```text
z_C*=m sqrt(pi/(t+2*pi*m^2))[C-2m-t/(pi*m)].            (11.310.4)
```

The remaining x phase and its saddle curvature are

```text
psi_m(x)=-pi*m^2/x+(t/2)log((1-x)/x),
psi_m''(x_m)=-(t+2*pi*m^2)^4/(8*pi^2*m^4*t)<0.          (11.310.5)
```

Hence the alpha integral is a smooth Fresnel endpoint transition and the
reduced x saddle is nondegenerate.  These facts do not alone exclude a
characteristic boundary tangent or composite fold in the coupled x/Fresnel
integral.  At `t=10^10`, interval arithmetic certifies for every

```text
z_B*>2480138.8143.                                      (11.310.6)
```

Using `F(+infinity)=(1+i)/2` and the Abel-damped bound
`|F(+infinity)-F(z)|<=2/(pi*z)`, all 84 transition factors obey

```text
|[F(z_B*)-F(z_A*)]-(1+i)/2|<0.044.                      (11.310.7)
```

Thus the 42 source-side endpoint terms are nearly half-saddle Fresnel
contributions, not degenerate saddles.  The exact positive-mode partition is

```text
1..621, 622..39852, 39853..39894, 39895..39936,
39937..2560588, 2560589..infinity,                      (11.310.8)
```

corresponding respectively to the lower nonstationary B-tail, lower

## 11.311 Universal logistic Morse phase and characteristic fold

For a positive Poisson mode, put

```text
w=(1-x)/x,       r=t/(2*pi*m^2),
v=w/r,           x=1/(1+r*v).                           (11.311.1)
```

The reduced phase in (11.310.5) then satisfies the global exact identity

```text
psi_m(x)-psi_m(x_m)=-(t/2)(v-1-log v).                  (11.311.2)
```

It is independent of `m`.  Define the signed Morse coordinate

```text
s=sgn(v-1)sqrt(2(v-1-log v)).                           (11.311.3)
```

This maps `(0,infinity)` monotonically onto the real line and gives

```text
psi_m(x)-psi_m(x_m)=-t*s^2/4,
dv/ds=v*s/(v-1),       (dv/ds)|_(s=0)=1.                (11.311.4)
```

The removable inverse chart is

```text
v(s)=1+s+s^2/3+s^3/36-s^4/270+s^5/4320+O(s^6).         (11.311.5)
```

The alpha current should remain grouped.  With
`q=sqrt(x/2)(alpha-2m/x)`, (11.308.2) becomes

```text
J_m=(-1)^m e^(-i*pi*m^2/x)
 integral_(q_A)^(q_B)
 [m*sqrt(2)x^(-3/2)+q*x^(-1)]e^(i*pi*q^2/2)dq.         (11.311.6)
```

For a full interior saddle, the complete Fresnel and Gaussian mains in
(11.311.6) and (11.311.4) give

```text
2^(5/4)(t/pi)^(1/4)/sqrt(m).                            (11.311.7)
```

The equation-(9) normalization `(pi/(32t))^(1/4)` cancels the first factor
exactly, leaving `1/sqrt(m)`.  Moreover, integer parity gives

```text
(-1)^m e^(i*psi_m(x_m))
 =e^[i{t(log(t/(2*pi))-1)/2-t*log m}].                  (11.311.8)
```

After the source factor `e^(-i*pi/8)`, (11.311.8) is the leading
Riemann--Siegel phase carrier `theta_0(t)-t log m`.  This identifies the
correct complex classical carrier but not yet its real/conjugate assembly or
remainder.

There is a second endpoint scale.  Let

```text
kappa_m(C)=(2/sqrt(t)) partial_s q_C|_(s=0),
Delta_m(C)=1-pi*kappa_m(C)^2/2.                         (11.311.9)
```

When the joint saddle lies on `alpha=C`, direct substitution gives

```text
Delta_m(C)=(2*pi*m^2-t)/(2*pi*m^2+t).                  (11.311.10)
```

At the exact coalescence

```text
m=sqrt(t/(2*pi)),       C=sqrt(8t/pi),
kappa=-sqrt(2/pi),      Delta=0.                        (11.311.11)
```

Thus the full two-dimensional Hessian and reduced x saddle are nondegenerate,
but the boundary tangent is characteristic.  Freezing the Fresnel endpoint
and applying an ordinary one-dimensional Gaussian remainder is not uniform
through the fold.

At `t=10^10`, 130-digit interval reconstruction gives

```text
Delta_m(159577)<0,  39853<=m<=39894,
Delta_m(159577)>0,  39895<=m<=39936,                   (11.311.12)

|Delta_39894(159577)|<6.27e-6,
1/|Delta_39894(159577)|>159000.                         (11.311.13)
```

The characteristic sign change is exactly the certified 42+42 split.  Any
proposed bound dividing by `Delta_m` is nonuniform and already loses more
than five orders of magnitude at the central height.  The next admissible
route is a fold-uniform estimate of the grouped current (11.311.6), or an
equivalent two-variable endpoint normal form, joined to ordinary stationary
phase and integration by parts away from the characteristic chart.

## 11.312 Exact lower-endpoint logit fold and Airy core

Restrict the joint phase to the lower alpha endpoint `alpha=C` and set

```text
u=log((1-x)/x),       x=1/(1+e^u),
eta=pi*C^2/(8t).                                        (11.312.1)
```

After removing the constant `pi*C^2/8-pi*m*C`, the phase is exactly

```text
Phi_C(u)-Phi_C(0)=t[u/2-eta*tanh(u/2)].                 (11.312.2)
```

The mode appears only in the removed constant.  The stationary equation is

```text
sech^2(u/2)=1/eta,                                     (11.312.3)
```

with roots `u_+-=+/-2 acosh(sqrt eta)` when `eta>=1`.  At the fold
`eta=1`,

```text
t[u/2-tanh(u/2)]=t[u^3/24-u^5/240+...].                (11.312.4)
```

Write `mu=eta-1` and scale

```text
u=2z/(t*eta)^(1/3),
lambda=mu*t^(2/3)*eta^(-1/3).                          (11.312.5)
```

The linear and cubic terms then become exactly

```text
t[-mu*u/2+eta*u^3/24]=z^3/3-lambda*z.                 (11.312.6)
```

The real Taylor bound `|tanh^(5)(y)|<=512` gives

```text
|R_phase(z)|
 <=(64/15)t^(-2/3)eta^(-2/3)|z|^5.                    (11.312.7)
```

At `t=10^10`, `C=159577`, 130-digit interval arithmetic certifies

```text
eta=1.0000011009042588...,
lambda=5.1099430394918356... .                         (11.312.8)
```

The two stationary points reproduce the continuous portcullis roots

```text
N_-=39852.3913862312389...,
N_+=39936.1086137687610... .                           (11.312.9)
```

On the natural core `|z|<=4`, (11.312.7) gives

```text
|R_phase|<0.000942<0.001.                              (11.312.10)
```

The Kummer measure is regular in the same chart:

```text
[x(1-x)]^(-1/4)|dx|
 =2^(-3/2)cosh(u/2)^(-3/2)du.                          (11.312.11)
```

There is an essential convergence guard.  Since `C` is odd,

```text
(-1)^m e^(-i*pi*m*C)=1                                (11.312.12)
```

for every integer mode.  The separated lower-boundary current is therefore
mode-independent and cannot be summed over the Poisson lattice.  The Airy
chart must be applied inside the exact grouped boundary/Fresnel current
(11.311.6), where the apparent divergence cancels.

The canonical fold phase is now explicit.  The next obligation is to
transport the full grouped amplitude through `|z|<=4`, bound its variation
and the outer contour tails uniformly in `lambda`, and join it to the ordinary
interior and nonstationary mode ranges.

## 11.313 Weil rank-trace proportion and density-bridge guard

The external 2026-08-10 paper *More than two thirds of the zeros of the
Riemann zeta function lie on the critical line* claims unconditionally

```text
liminf N_0^s(T,2T)/N(T,2T) >= c_*,                    (11.313.1)
c_*=3/2-cot(1/sqrt(2))/sqrt(2)
   =0.672500703679411645734379790803295... .          (11.313.2)
```

The source paper and informal note are preserved locally by hash.  This
programme audits the statement, optimized constant, and central
finite-dimensional assembly, while treating the newly released result as an
external theorem still awaiting broad independent scrutiny.

For Hermitian matrices `P>=0`, `rank(P)<=r`, and `n_+(Q)<=b`, the paper's
rank-trace lemma is

```text
||P+Q||_F^2
 >=c tr(P)-c^2 r/4+2c tr(Q)-c^2 b.                   (11.313.3)
```

At `c=2`, this gives

```text
r>=2tr(P)+4tr(Q)-4b-||P+Q||_F^2.                     (11.313.4)
```

The equality model `P=(c/2)Pi_1`, `Q=c Pi_2` for orthogonal projections is
checked exactly.  Combining (11.313.4) with the paper's zero-side signature,
`tr(A)~N`, `||A||_F^2~4N/3`, and `tr(P)+2b<=N` gives the base constant `2/3`.
The Montgomery-Taylor window then gives (11.313.2).

Put

```text
E(T)=N(T,2T)-N_0^s(T,2T),
delta_*=1-c_*
       =0.327499296320588354265620209196704... .      (11.313.5)
```

If (11.313.1) is accepted, then

```text
limsup E(T)/N(T,2T)<=delta_*.                         (11.313.6)
```

Therefore a defect-amplification contradiction would need an epsilon-positive
unbounded sequence `T_j` on which

```text
N_off(T_j,2T_j)/N(T_j,2T_j)>=delta_*+epsilon.         (11.313.7)
```

If symmetric off-line pairs are counted, the required threshold is
`delta_*/2=0.163749648160294177132810104598352...` pairs per zero.

This is not supplied by any existing cascade.  Since

```text
N(T,2T)~T log(T)/(2 pi),                              (11.313.8)
```

finite, logarithmic, sublinear, and even `O(T)` descendant counts all have
zero relative density.  The fixed-root chain propagates one Jensen root across
shift, the polar cascade raises Jensen degree and multiplicity at one scaled
root, and the cofinal boundary theorem tracks signed contact index.  None of
these quantities is a count of distinct zeta zeros in a dyadic height window.

The alternative heat-dependent Weil-inertia route is also open.  At heat time
zero the explicit formula supplies the prime-side matrix moments used by the
external paper.  The current source machinery supplies no corresponding
trace/Hilbert-Schmidt evolution theorem away from zero, and a naive congruence
transport would preserve inertia and conflict with the collision mechanism.
No such transport is promoted.

The route decision is therefore unchanged: retain (11.313.6) as a strong
external constraint and optional bridge target, but continue the grouped Airy
amplitude, contour tails, interior join, and `T_upper` assembly of Section
11.312.  Reopen the proportion branch only with a genuine order-`T log T`
off-line amplification theorem or a source-controlled heat-dependent
negative-inertia estimate.

The constant (11.313.2) contains no `pi`; it comes from the optimized cosine
window at `theta=1/sqrt(2)`.  The `pi` in (11.313.8) comes from the
Riemann-von Mangoldt density, while the paper's separate `2 pi` Fourier factor
sets its critical Gabor sampling spacing.

## 11.314 Grouped characteristic Airy-boundary normal form

The boundary phase in Section 11.312 is correct, but the remaining grouped
current is not a slowly varying scalar amplitude on the Airy scale. Keep the
endpoint and Fresnel pieces together and sum the finite transition roster
before taking absolute values. Put

```text
eta=pi*C^2/(8t),          beta=(t*eta)^(1/3),
u=2z/beta,                x(z)=[1-tanh(z/beta)]/2,
alpha=C+sigma*y,          sigma=4beta/(pi*C),
d_m=4beta(m-C/4)/C.                                      (11.314.1)
```

Since `C` is odd, the factor `(-1)^m exp(-i*pi*m*C)` is one. Removing the
common constant `pi*C^2/8`, the exact two-variable phase is

```text
Theta_m(z,y)
 =t[z/beta-eta*tanh(z/beta)]
  -d_m*y-beta*y*tanh(z/beta)+x(z)y^2/(2beta).           (11.314.2)
```

The transformed Kummer measure, alpha current, and both Jacobians combine
without approximation to

```text
A(z,y)=sqrt(2)/pi cosh(z/beta)^(-3/2)(1+sigma*y/C).     (11.314.3)
```

For the 84 transition modes `39853<=m<=39936`, all mode dependence is the
exact finite kernel

```text
D_84(y)=sum_m exp(-i*d_m*y)
 =exp[-i(d_0+83h/2)y] sin(84hy/2)/sin(hy/2),
h=4beta/C,                                              (11.314.4)
```

with removable denominator zeros interpreted by continuity. Equation
(11.314.4), not a separated endpoint series, is the cancellation object.

The corresponding cubic-quadratic characteristic model is

```text
Theta_m^0(z,y)
 =z^3/3-lambda*z-(z+d_m)y+y^2/(4beta),
lambda=(eta-1)t/beta.                                   (11.314.5)
```

Its exact phase remainder is

```text
R=R_Airy(z)+y[z-beta*tanh(z/beta)]
  +[x(z)-1/2]y^2/(2beta).                               (11.314.6)
```

The elementary inequalities

```text
|a-tanh(a)|<=|a|^3/3,       |tanh(a)|<=|a|             (11.314.7)
```

together with Section 11.312 give, on `|z|<=4`, `0<=y<=64`,

```text
|R|<0.002117894<0.0022.                                  (11.314.8)
```

On the same rectangle, interval arithmetic certifies

```text
|A/(sqrt(2)/pi)-1|<6.895e-6<1e-5.                       (11.314.9)
```

At `t=10^10`, `C=159577`, the exact scale data are

```text
beta=2154.4354806403688...,
sigma=0.017189898610274817...,
lambda=5.1099430394918356...,
h=0.054003659189992763...,
-2.22765094158720...<=d_m<=2.25465277118220....          (11.314.10)
```

The normal core reaches `1.3788... sqrt(beta)`. This validates the local
normal form but does not dispose of the complement: for some `(z,m)` the
normal alpha saddle lies outside the compact rectangle. The next admissible
step is to bound the finite-kernel canonical integral in (11.314.4)--
(11.314.5), then construct an endpoint/interior partition whose outer piece
captures every displaced normal saddle. A frozen-Fresnel or scalar
slow-amplitude Airy estimate is not uniform and is not admissible.

Every `pi` in (11.314.1)--(11.314.5) is inherited from the original Kummer
quadratic phase `exp(i*pi*x*alpha^2/4)` and the integer Fourier--Poisson
character `exp(-i*pi*m*alpha)`. The factor `sqrt(2)/pi` in (11.314.3) is then
forced by the logit and normal-coordinate Jacobians. No circle, polygon, or
fitted geometric normalization is introduced.

## 11.315 Characteristic canonical-core interval quadrature

The grouped canonical integral from Section 11.314 admits two complementary
one-dimensional representations. Define

```text
I_M(Z,Y)=sum_m integral_(-Z)^Z integral_0^Y
 exp(i[z^3/3-lambda*z-(z+d_m)y+y^2/(4beta)])dy dz.      (11.315.1)
```

Using the Fourier representation of the Airy function and integrating `z`
on the full real line first gives exactly

```text
I_M(infinity,Y)=2pi integral_0^Y Ai(-lambda-y)
 exp(i*y^2/(4beta))D_M(y)dy.                            (11.315.2)
```

Alternatively, complete the square in `y`. If

```text
H_beta(p;Y)=exp(-i*beta*p^2)sqrt(2beta)
 integral_(-sqrt(2beta)p)^((Y-2beta*p)/sqrt(2beta))
 exp(i*q^2/2)dq,                                        (11.315.3)
```

then the finite rectangle is exactly

```text
I_M(Z,Y)=integral_(-Z)^Z exp(i[z^3/3-lambda*z])
 sum_m H_beta(z+d_m;Y)dz.                               (11.315.4)
```

The two leading oscillatory branches of `Ai(-lambda-y)` have normal phase
derivatives controlled by

```text
sqrt(lambda+y)+y/(2beta)-d_m,
sqrt(lambda+y)+d_m-y/(2beta).                           (11.315.5)
```

On `0<=y<=64`, monotonicity reduces the dangerous margins to `y=0`. Interval
arithmetic certifies

```text
sqrt(lambda)-d_max=0.0058655409515...>0,
sqrt(lambda)+d_min=0.0328673705465...>0.                (11.315.6)
```

Thus the discrete 84-mode lattice excludes both near-endpoint stationary
thresholds on this compact normal range. The final integer mode lies close
to, but strictly outside, the continuous threshold.

Thirty-two deterministic interval panels give

```text
I_M(4,64)
 =-46.2734309079314276427...
  +1.41478564696157623630... i.                         (11.315.7)
```

The exact finite-`t` logit phase is still quadratic in `y`, and the exact
amplitude is linear in `y`. Their normal integral is therefore evaluated by
(11.315.3) and its first moment. To prevent interval dependency in
`t[z/beta-eta*tanh(z/beta)]`, use the odd Taylor polynomial for `tanh`
through degree 17. On `|z|<=4`, Cauchy's estimate on `|w|=1` bounds the
resulting full-rectangle integral error by

```text
3.999e-35.                                               (11.315.8)
```

After division by the common physical factor `sqrt(2)/pi`, the exact
finite-`t` rectangle is

```text
-46.2737285575900149052...
+1.41478783597402943204... i.                           (11.315.9)
```

Consequently its correction to (11.315.7) satisfies

```text
|I_exact-I_M|=0.0002976577078334...,
|I_exact-I_M|/|I_exact|=6.4295376876...e-6<6.6e-6.      (11.315.10)
```

This is a cancellation-preserving finite comparison, not the absolute
integral of the pointwise phase-error majorant.

The independent Airy-first evaluation gives

```text
I_M(infinity,64)
 =-43.3329331855623559105...
  +1.42819002920334713304... i.                         (11.315.11)
```

Therefore the canonical `|z|>4`, `0<=y<=64` contribution obeys

```text
|I_M(infinity,64)-I_M(4,64)|/|I_M(4,64)|
 =0.0635171150975...<0.064.                             (11.315.12)
```

The tail is controlled numerically but is not negligible. It must still be
placed on an explicit steepest-descent contour. The separate `y>64`

The `pi` in (11.315.2) is the standard Airy Fourier inversion factor. The

```text
 =[81-a]s/2+(9sqrt(3))s^2/2+s^3/3.                      (11.316.6)
```

## 11.318 Direct R=9 outgoing-ray enclosure

Let `F(z)` denote the complete canonical `z` integrand after retaining the
84-mode kernel inside the `y` integral.  The positive and negative real tails
deform to

```text
z_+(s)=9+exp(i*pi/6)s,
z_-(s)=-9+exp(5i*pi/6)s,       s>=0.                    (11.318.1)
```

The negative real tail has the opposite outward orientation.  Hence

```text
I_ray= exp(i*pi/6) integral_0^infinity F(z_+(s))ds
      -exp(5i*pi/6) integral_0^infinity F(z_-(s))ds.    (11.318.2)
```

For `a=lambda+y`, both rays satisfy

```text
|exp(i phi_a)|
 =exp(-[(81-a)s/2+(9sqrt(3))s^2/2+s^3/3]).             (11.318.3)
```

On the connecting sectors based at `+9` and `-9`, the linear, quadratic,
and cubic imaginary-phase terms are nonnegative, with strict cubic decay
away from the real boundary.  Entirety therefore justifies the two
deformations in (11.318.1).

Put

```text
q(s)=(81-lambda-64)s/2+(9sqrt(3))s^2/2+s^3/3.          (11.318.4)
```

For `s>=2`, convexity and `|D_84(y)|<=84` give the explicit two-ray bound

```text
2*84*64 integral_2^infinity exp(-q(s))ds
 <=2*84*64 exp(-q(2))/q'(2)
 <3.594e-18.                                             (11.318.5)
```

The finite computation combines the full phase before exponentiation.  This
avoids the unstable subtraction of separately exponential Fresnel terms on
the positive ray.  Thirty-two resumable interval panels on `0<=s<=2` give

```text
I_ray,trunc
 =-0.144582281914288298389553059137...
  -0.00391902734872929159093178210949... i.             (11.318.6)
```

Adding (11.318.5) componentwise gives the complete direct ray enclosure.
Its real and imaginary components overlap independently with (11.317.5),
whose midpoint differences are respectively about `3.6e-17` and
`-1.5e-17`.  The independent real-axis subtraction is used only for this
cross-check, not as input to (11.318.6).

## 11.319 Exact y=64 normal-saddle partition

For each transition mode, the complete finite-`t` dependence on the normal
coordinate is

```text
Theta_m(z,y)=constant-(d_m+beta*tanh(z/beta))*y
             +x(z)y^2/(2beta),
x(z)=[1-tanh(z/beta)]/2.                                (11.319.1)
```

Its curvature `x(z)/beta` is positive, and completing the square gives the
unique normal saddle

```text
y_m(z)=beta[d_m+beta*tanh(z/beta)]/x(z).                (11.319.2)
```

At `Y0=64`, define

```text
g_m(z)=d_m+beta*tanh(z/beta)-64x(z)/beta.               (11.319.3)
```

Then `y_m(z)>=64` exactly when `g_m(z)>=0`, while

```text
g_m'(z)=sech(z/beta)^2[1+32/beta^2]>0.                 (11.319.4)
```

Every mode therefore has one crossing.  More generally, `g_m(z)=c` has the
closed solution

```text
z_m(c)=beta*atanh([c-d_m+32/beta]/[beta+32/beta]).      (11.319.5)
```

The normalized Fresnel coordinate at the boundary is

```text
q_m(64,z)=-g_m(z)sqrt(beta/x(z)).                       (11.319.6)
```

Choose the common buffer

```text
delta=0.061063749740668521969601122757....               (11.319.7)
```

It guarantees `|q_m(64,z)|>=4.0062...>4` whenever
`|g_m(z)|>=delta` on `|z|<=9`.  Assign equality to the two outer charts and
define

```text
g_m(z)<=-delta:          nonstationary outer chart,
-delta<g_m(z)<delta:     endpoint/Fresnel chart,
g_m(z)>=delta:           ordinary Morse chart.          (11.319.8)
```

These three sets are disjoint and exhaustive.  Every saddle with `y_m>=64`
belongs either to the boundary band or the Morse chart, while points in the
nonstationary chart have no saddle on the outer `y` interval.

For all 84 modes the full collection of transition bands lies inside

```text
-2.30084845436805...<=z<=2.30355276685094...,           (11.319.9)
```

and each band has width between `0.1221266575...` and
`0.1221267899...`.  The exact crossing differs from its canonical threshold
`64/(2beta)-d_m` by less than `1.466e-5`.

The largest exact normal saddle on `|z|<=9` is

```text
y_m(z)<48698.053,                                        (11.319.10)
```

whereas the transformed upper endpoint is

```text
y_B=(B-C)/sigma=288706996.6214686....                    (11.319.11)
```

The minimum normalized clearance to `y_B` exceeds `4.388e6`; no transition
saddle in the R=9 chart can be assigned accidentally to the upper endpoint.

## 11.320 Exact y=64 affine primitive and local chart envelopes

Fix `(z,m)` and write

```text
k=x(z)/beta,       p=d_m+beta*tanh(z/beta),
y_*=p/k,           c=sigma/C,
E(y)=exp(i[k y^2/2-py]),
H0(L,U)=integral_L^U E(y)dy.                            (11.320.1)
```

Since `E'(y)=i k(y-y_*)E(y)`, direct integration gives

```text
H1(L,U)=y_*H0(L,U)-i[E(U)-E(L)]/k,
K(L,U)=integral_L^U(1+cy)E(y)dy
      =(1+c y_*)H0(L,U)-i(c/k)[E(U)-E(L)].              (11.320.2)
```

The scale identities

```text
pi C^2=8 beta^3,       sigma=C/(2 beta^2)               (11.320.3)
```

imply

```text
y_*=(2m/x-C)/sigma,
C sigma(1+c y_*)=2m sigma/x,
C sigma c/k=2/(pi x).                                  (11.320.4)
```

Consequently the source-normalized affine primitive is exactly

```text
C sigma K(L,U)
 =2m sigma H0(L,U)/x+2[E(U)-E(L)]/(i pi x).             (11.320.5)
```

Thus the source's Fresnel term and endpoint current are the two parts of one
primitive.  In particular,

```text
K(0,y_B)=K(0,64)+K(64,y_B),                             (11.320.6)
```

so the artificial `E(64)` contributions cancel exactly.

On the three charts of (11.319.8), explicit saved-height estimates give

```text
nonstationary: |K(64,y_B)| < 32.766333 < 33,            (11.320.7)
Fresnel band:  |K(64,y_B)| < 561.212600 < 600.          (11.320.8)
```

For the Morse chart, replace only `H0` in (11.320.2) by

```text
H_full=exp(-i p^2/(2k))sqrt(2pi/k)exp(i*pi/4),          (11.320.9)
```

while retaining the endpoint current.  The resulting grouped main and its
two omitted normalized Fresnel tails satisfy, per mode,

```text
|K_Morse,grouped| < 165.750717 < 200,
|K-K_Morse,grouped| < 33.062329 < 34.                  (11.320.10)
```

The bounds in (11.320.7)--(11.320.10) are local per-mode envelopes; they are
not summed over the 84 transition modes.  The occurrences of `pi` in
(11.320.3), (11.320.5), and (11.320.9) come respectively from the exact
Kummer/Fourier-Poisson scaling and the standard Fresnel Gaussian.  No fitted
circle or geometric normalization is inserted.

## 11.321 Moving roster and contiguous Dirichlet blocks

The boundary function has affine mode dependence:

```text
g_m(z)=h(m-C/4)+G(z),
G(z)=beta*tanh(z/beta)-64x(z)/beta,
g_(m+1)(z)-g_m(z)=h>0.                                 (11.321.1)
```

At fixed `z`, the three chart memberships are therefore contiguous integer
blocks with real cutoffs

```text
mu_-(z)=C/4+[-delta-G(z)]/h,
mu_+(z)=C/4+[ delta-G(z)]/h,                            (11.321.2)

m<=mu_-:        nonstationary,
mu_-<m<mu_+:    endpoint/Fresnel,
m>=mu_+:        ordinary Morse.                        (11.321.3)
```

Their real Fresnel width is

```text
mu_+-mu_-=2delta/h=2.2614671174720708...,               (11.321.4)
```

so at most three integer modes lie in the Fresnel block at any one `z`.
The 168 entry and exit events are distinct, their minimum separation exceeds
`0.01412008375`, and they cut `[-9,9]` into 169 open fixed-roster cells.  The
numbers of cells carrying 0, 1, 2, and 3 Fresnel modes are respectively

```text
2, 2, 83, 82.                                           (11.321.5)
```

Equality at `g=-delta` is assigned to the nonstationary chart and equality at
`g=delta` to the Morse chart.  Event points have zero `z` measure, so this
half-open convention is exhaustive without overlap.

For every nonempty consecutive block `a<=m<=b`, the mode phases retain the
exact finite Dirichlet kernel

```text
D_[a,b](y)
 =exp[-i(d_a+d_b)y/2]
  sin((b-a+1)hy/2)/sin(hy/2).                          (11.321.6)
```

At removable denominator zeros, (11.321.6) is interpreted as its original
finite geometric sum.  This gives the cancellation-preserving representation
needed for the large nonstationary and Morse blocks, while no more than three
Fresnel modes need be retained explicitly.

## 11.324 Finite Airy-Fresnel detuning equation

For `Y=64`, define the canonical lower-fold transform


equation

```text

 +(lambda-d^2+i/(2beta))G_Y=R_0(d)+R_Y(d),             (11.324.2)

R_0=-Ai'(-lambda)+i d Ai(-lambda),                    (11.324.3)

R_Y=exp(i[Y^2/(4beta)-dY])
 {Ai'(-lambda-Y)+i[Y/(2beta)-d]Ai(-lambda-Y)}.        (11.324.4)
```

sources are retained.  On all 84 saved detunings,

modes encloses both components of the equation residual around zero.

## 11.329 Fixed-selector turning events and exact handoff

A mode changes turning ownership when its joint saddle reaches the fixed
lower endpoint `C`:

```text
alpha_m=2m+t/(pi m)=C,
tau_m=pi m(C-2m).                                      (11.329.1)
```

The distance below the fixed-selector top is the exact square

```text
pi C^2/8-tau_m=pi(C-4m)^2/8.                          (11.329.2)
```

For `C=159577=4q+1`, `q=39894`, order the events by `n>=0`.  Then

```text
m_(2k)=q-k,              m_(2k+1)=q+k+1,
tau_n=pi C^2/8-pi[n(n+1)/2+1/8],
tau_n-tau_(n+1)=pi(n+1).                              (11.329.3)
```

Thus the event heights are distinct and have minimum spacing `pi`.  Exactly
399 lie in the fixed-selector cell.  Immediately above its lower edge their
modes form the contiguous roster `39695..40093`.  At the saved height,

```text
tau_83>10^10>tau_84,
{m_0,...,m_83}=39853..39936,                           (11.329.4)

tau_83-10^10=57.0578988367820...,
10^10-tau_84=206.835884064761....                      (11.329.5)
```

The next upward event removes mode `39936` from the turning block; the next
downward event inserts mode `39852`.  If `J_r` denotes the same exact finite
Poisson mode integral on both sides, every event obeys the exact ownership
identity

```text
sum_(m in O)J_m+sum_(m in T)J_m
 =sum_(m in O union {r})J_m+sum_(m in T minus {r})J_m. (11.329.6)
```

All 399 handoffs were checked as disjoint finite-set identities.  Equation
(11.329.6) does not equate separately truncated ordinary-Morse and Airy
approximations.

The selector jump is structurally different.  At `C -> C+2`, the old
fixed-`C` turning roster is empty near its upper edge, while the new selector
begins with the 399-mode roster `39696..40094` at the removed lower endpoint
strip `[C,C+2]`.  This is not a one-mode handoff.

## 11.330 Exact selector-strip finite-Poisson reassembly

Write the fixed-`B` odd source roster as

```text
alpha=C+2u,       u=0,...,L,
f_C(u)=(C+2u)exp(i pi x(C+2u)^2/4).                    (11.330.1)
```

Advancing the lower selector to `C+2` shifts the coordinate by one:

```text
f_(C+2)(v)=f_C(v+1),       v=0,...,L-1.               (11.330.2)
```

Thus precisely one source lattice point, `alpha=C`, is removed.  For every
integer Fourier mode, the shift leaves its character unchanged.  The mode
difference is the one-cell strip

```text
S_m(x)=integral_0^1 f_C(u)exp(-2pi i m u)du
 =(-1)^m/2 integral_C^(C+2)
   alpha exp(i pi[x alpha^2/4-m alpha])dalpha.         (11.330.3)
```

The endpoint half-current changes by

```text
H_C(x)=[f_C(0)-f_C(1)]/2.                              (11.330.4)
```

Finite Poisson on `[0,1]` gives

```text
lim_(M->infinity) sum_(m=-M)^M S_m(x)
 =[f_C(0)+f_C(1)]/2,                                   (11.330.5)

H_C+lim_sym sum_m S_m=f_C(0)
 =C exp(i pi x C^2/4).                                 (11.330.6)
```

After multiplication by the Kummer weight and integration in `x`, this is
exactly the single source term removed by `C -> C+2`.  For the saved fixed
upper endpoint, the odd-roster term count drops from `2481423` to `2481422`.

Equation (11.330.6) also supplies a nontruncation guard.  The 399 positive
turning modes in the new endpoint chart are not sufficient for the selector
splice: the complete symmetric mode sum, including zero and negative modes,
and the endpoint half-current are mandatory.

## 11.332 The earlier source transition is an endpoint-scheduling event

At the earlier transition entry from (11.331.4), the pinned implementation
changes its ideal odd roster from

```text
R_-={C,C+2,...,B_-},     C=159577, B_-=5122421,
R_+={C+2,C+4,...,B_+},             B_+=5122423.       (11.332.1)
```

Both rosters contain `2481423` points.  Therefore, for any assigned
single-alpha summand `F_t(alpha)`, finite cancellation gives the exact identity

```text
sum_(alpha in R_+)F_t(alpha)-sum_(alpha in R_-)F_t(alpha)
 =F_t(B_+)-F_t(C).                                      (11.332.2)
```

Let `T_C(t)` denote the transition term inserted by the source.  The complete
idealized scheduling change is consequently

```text
Delta_source=[T_C-F_t(C)]+F_t(B_+).                     (11.332.3)
```

Equation (11.332.3) is a decomposition, not a cancellation theorem.  The
first bracket is the transition-approximation defect; the second term is the
newly scheduled upper endpoint.  At the transition root, interval arithmetic
certifies

```text
N_-(B_-)=621.5561508585892783407562523...,
N_-(B_+)=621.5559080602196631239807351....               (11.332.4)
```

Thus the Riemann-Siegel floor is `621` on both sides, and no RS term absorbs
the added `F_t(B_+)`.

As a diagnostic only, a high-precision repetition of the source-form 64-node
quadrature at the transition root gives

```text

F_t(C)            =-0.0331488605021633922263382127...,
F_t(B_+)          = 0.0007465905980142806096884382...,
Delta_source      = 0.0336430684033743862769475048....    (11.332.5)
```

The 64- and 96-node calculations agree beyond forty decimal places.  This
point computation is not an interval enclosure of the complete compiled
source and is not used as proof.

The primary papers require the same separation.  The 2015 paper describes the
hybrid and transition formulae as approximations, sends part of the transition
zone to direct numerical integration, and identifies numerical transition
correlations that are not proved.  The 2026 paper explicitly states that its
Gaussian-sum hybrid is not exact and again uses numerical integration for part
of the transition range.

For theorem-level height transport, fix

```text
B_fix=5122423.                                           (11.332.6)
```

The fixed chart `{C,C+2,...,B_fix}` has `2481424` points and obeys the exact
bookkeeping identities

```text
source-pre  =fixed-chart-F_t(B_fix),
source-post =fixed-chart+[T_C-F_t(C)].                   (11.332.7)
```

Hence the implementation threshold and moving endpoint belong in a separate
source-approximation ledger.  They do not define the exact `C -> C+2`
selector theorem.  That selector change remains the one-cell symmetric
Poisson identity of Section 11.330 at `t*=pi C^2/8`, with `B_fix` held fixed.

The smallest lower-fold saddle clearance is
`3.1333032536220985e-6`.  More importantly, the first excluded lower mode

```text
lambda(tau_m)=d_m^2,
```

```text
z_C^*(m,t)=(tau_m-t)/sqrt(pi[t+2pi m^2]).               (11.336.3)
```

Consequently every event remains close to the characteristic locus:

```text
                                      <0.004995.        (11.336.6)
```

The nearest event is mode `39894` at `tau=t*-pi/8`.  At the two faces of its

```text
max |z_C^*|<0.004976.                                  (11.336.8)
```

Let `F'(z)=exp(i pi z^2/2)`, `F(0)=0`, and

## 11.337 Exact Fresnel-retaining logistic-Morse transform

For endpoint `D` in `{C,B}`, write

```text
q_D(m,x)=sqrt(x/2)(D-2m/x),
F'(q)=exp(i pi q^2/2),       F(0)=0.                    (11.337.1)
```

Keep the two parts of the finite-Poisson current paired:

```text
P_m(x)=[exp(i pi q_B^2/2)-exp(i pi q_C^2/2)]/(i pi)
       +m sqrt(2/x)[F(q_B)-F(q_C)].                    (11.337.2)
```

The exact completion

```text
pi x D^2/4-pi mD=-pi m^2/x+pi q_D^2/2
```

turns (11.308.3) into

```text
J_m(x)=(-1)^m exp(-i pi m^2/x)P_m(x)/x.                (11.337.3)
```

Now put

```text
r=t/(2pi m^2),       v=(1-x)/(rx),       x=1/(1+rv),
s=sgn(v-1)sqrt(2[v-1-log v]).                          (11.337.4)
```

The phase and Jacobian identities are global:

```text
psi_m(x)-psi_m(x_m)=-t s^2/4,
-dx/ds=r x^2 dv/ds,
dv/ds=vs/(v-1),       (dv/ds)|_(s=0)=1.                (11.337.5)
```

If `K_m` is the Kummer-weighted `x` integral of `J_m`, reversing the
monotone `x(s)` orientation gives the exact representation

```text
K_m=(-1)^m exp(i psi_m(x_m))
 integral_R exp(-i t s^2/4) A_m(s)ds,                 (11.337.6)

A_m(s)=r x(s)(dv/ds)[x(s)(1-x(s))]^(-1/4)P_m(x(s)).   (11.337.7)
```

The universal logistic-Morse phase is now Gaussian, but the endpoint
exponential and Fresnel difference remain paired inside `A_m`; no
full-interior limit has been frozen and no factor `1/Delta_m` appears.

At an event,

```text
x_m=2m/C,       q_C(m,x_m)=0.                          (11.337.8)
```

For mode `39894`, interval evaluation at `tau=t*-pi/8` gives

```text
q_B>2480000,
r x_m[x_m(1-x_m)]^(-1/4)=0.70711121065... .            (11.337.9)
```

The lower endpoint pieces in (11.337.2) are therefore the finite values
`exp(i pi q_C^2/2)=1` and `F(q_C)=0`, even though
`Delta_m=-1/159577` is very small.  This is the required replacement target
for Section 11.336: compare the grouped Airy-Fresnel integral with
(11.337.6) before absolute values while retaining the exact current.

## 11.340 Full-line prototype Airy/logistic join

The apparent `|u|>200` tails contain displaced stationary structure and
should not be bounded separately on the real axis.  Return both charts to
the same physical variables `(z,y)`.  Their exact and canonical phases are

```text
Theta_t(z,y)=t[z/beta-eta tanh(z/beta)]
 -d_m y-beta y tanh(z/beta)+x(z)y^2/(2beta),
x(z)=[1-tanh(z/beta)]/2,                               (11.340.1)

Theta_0(z,y)=z^3/3-lambda z-(z+d_m)y+y^2/(4beta).      (11.340.2)
```

After removing the common `sqrt(2)/pi`, the exact amplitude is

```text
A_t(z,y)=cosh(z/beta)^(-3/2)(1+sigma y/C).             (11.340.3)
```

Thus the complete prototype difference is the single signed integral

```text
Delta I(t)=integral_R integral_0^64
 [A_t(z,y)exp(i Theta_t(z,y))-exp(i Theta_0(z,y))]dy dz.
                                                               (11.340.4)
```

The exact normal-saddle partition places every relevant saddle inside
`|z|<9`.  Lift both tails to `Im z=1`, retaining the vertical connectors at
`z=+/-9`.  On the finite contour, Arb Taylor series are integrated
coefficientwise.  The quadratic normal exponential uses the exact recurrence

```text
c_0=1,       c_1=i b,
c_n=[i b c_(n-1)+2 i a c_(n-2)]/n.                    (11.340.5)
```

Near the removable `b=0` point the complete `y` recurrence is used; elsewhere
`exp(i b y)` is kept exact and only `exp(i a y^2)` is expanded.  Enlarged
Cauchy disks give explicit outer-series tails.  The horizontal segment is
integrated signed through `|Re z|=15`; beyond it, logistic and Gaussian phase
lower bounds give a combined absolute tail below `1.217e-20`.

At the event and both `pi/16` faces, the resulting enclosures prove

```text
|Delta I(t)|<0.000019,
(sqrt(2)/pi)|Delta I(t)|<0.0000086.                   (11.340.6)
```

The three normalized midpoints have magnitudes between `1.6686e-5` and
`1.6764e-5`.  A second calculation with 72 narrower real panels, eight
narrower connector panels, and outer/inner orders `200/240` independently

Every `pi` in (11.339.4)--(11.340.6) is inherited from the Kummer quadratic

For the fixed prototype mode and source endpoint, put

## 11.342 Event-parameter contour and leading-Airy barrier

Order the 399 fixed-selector events as in Section 11.336.  Their exact event
parameter and detuning are

```text
epsilon_n=(4m_n-C)/C=(-1)^(n+1)(2n+1)/C,
d_n=beta epsilon_n,             0<=n<=398.             (11.342.1)
```

For `t=tau_n+h`, `|h|<=pi/16`, the event square and the common-chart height
identity give

```text
t*-tau_n=beta d_n^2,
lambda(tau_n+h)=d_n^2-h/beta,
D_(n,tau_n+h)=exp(i h z/beta)D_(n,tau_n).             (11.342.2)
```

The canonical and exact normal saddles satisfy

```text
z_can^2=d_n^2-h/beta+y,
cosh(z_exact/beta)^2
 =[beta^2+y+y^2/(4beta^2)]/[beta^2-d_n^2+h/beta].     (11.342.3)
```

Across the complete roster `39695<=m<=40093`, interval arithmetic proves

```text
max |d_n|<10.760230,
max |z_can|<13.408305,
max |z_exact|<13.408394.                              (11.342.4)
```

Thus the prototype contour `|Re z|=9` is not atlas-uniform: the outer
saddle lies beyond it for 246 events, from index 153 through 398.  A common
contour with connectors at `Re z=+/-14`, lift `Im z=1`, and signed horizontal
integration through `|Re z|=21` has saddle clearance above `0.5916`.  Every
lifted Cauchy disk has positive factored phase bracket; the minimum is above
`8.75`.  The exact and canonical far-tail exponent margins are above `40.21`
and `260.88`, respectively.

Geometry alone does not propagate the prototype estimate.  Direct signed
integration of the bare Airy comparison at the two extreme detunings gives

```text
n=398, m=39695: |Delta I| in
 [0.0123535125771592,0.0123535125772195],
n=397, m=40093: |Delta I| in
 [0.0127986672601659,0.0127986672610984].              (11.342.5)
```

Both rigorously exceed the prototype target `0.000019`.  Independent
order-200 reconstructions on nonmatching partitions overlap both complex
balls.  The two real components have the same negative sign, while the
imaginary components nearly reverse, so a naive opposite-edge pairing does
not cancel the dominant endpoint defect.

## 11.343 First finite-height normal-form correction

At an event, expand the exact common-chart amplitude and phase in
`beta^-2`.  The exact identity `sigma/C=1/(2beta^2)` and the Taylor series of
`cosh` and `tanh` give

```text

Theta_exact=Theta_0+beta^-2 r_1+O(beta^-4),

a_1=y/2-3z^2/4,
r_1=-2z^5/15+z^3y/3-zy^2/4.                          (11.343.1)
```

Use the signed corrected comparison

```text
exp(i Theta_0)[1+beta^-2(a_1+i r_1)].                 (11.343.2)
```

The normal polynomial is integrated exactly against the canonical quadratic
phase using `H_0,H_1,H_2`.  On the common contour of Section 11.342, rigorous
enclosures at the extreme events give

```text
n=398: |Delta I_1| in
 [2.50669721446e-5,2.50669722057e-5],
n=397: |Delta I_1| in
 [2.54555450745e-5,2.54555460134e-5].                 (11.343.3)
```

Thus the first correction removes more than `99.8%` of the bare defect but
still rigorously exceeds both prototype targets at both extremes.  A denser
order-200 reconstruction independently gives maximum
`2.54555455440e-5` and overlaps both complex balls.  Stopping at
`beta^-2` is therefore an insufficient atlas theorem.

## 11.345 Discrete all-event second-order atlas

The event parameters in (11.342.1) form a finite exact roster, so a proof at

partition its real segment in the translated coordinate

```text
w=z+d_n.                                                   (11.345.1)
```

One rational panel, with center denominator `2048` and center error below
`0.0006`, contains the removable normal point `w=0`.  Only this panel uses the
full inner exponential recurrence.  On all other panels `exp(i b y)` remains
unexpanded and only the quadratic factor is expanded.  The contour and the
integral are unchanged by this event-dependent partition.

At an event center, direct interval evaluation of the phase can lose the
cancellation between `z^3/3`, `-d_n^2 z`, and `-(z+d_n)y`.  On disks meeting
the real axis, integrate vertically from the real phase and retain the
factored derivatives

```text
Theta_0'(z)=(z-d_n)(z+d_n)-y,

Theta_exact'(z)
 =(beta tanh(z/beta)-d_n)(beta tanh(z/beta)+d_n)
```

Together with the positive lifted-contour phase brackets of Section 11.342,

## 11.346 All-event continuous-height transport

Fix an event `0<=n<=398`, its exact center `tau_n`, and the corrected
center integrand `D_(n,tau_n)` from Section 11.345.  The height variable enters
the exact and beta-minus-four corrected common charts through the same linear
factor, while every retained correction polynomial is height independent.
Consequently, for real `h`,

```text
D_(n,tau_n+h)(z)=exp(i h z/beta)D_(n,tau_n)(z).           (11.346.1)
```

This is an identity, not a small-`h` approximation.  Put

```text
h=(pi/16)theta,  |theta|<=1,  kappa=pi/(16 beta),
M_(n,k)=integral_Gamma z^k D_(n,tau_n)(z) dz.             (11.346.2)
```

The `pi` in (11.346.2) comes from the exact `pi/16` event-cell width fixed by
the Fourier--Poisson selector construction.  The `pi` already present in
`beta` comes from `beta^3=pi C^2/8`.  No circle, polygon, fitted period, or
numerically inserted geometric constant is used here.

On the finite common contour, where `|z|<=Z=sqrt(21^2+1)`, expand (11.346.1)
through degree six:

```text
I_n(theta)
 =sum_(k=0)^6 (i kappa theta)^k M_(n,k)/k! + R_(n,7)(theta),

|R_(n,7)(theta)|
 <=A_n exp(kappa Z)(kappa Z)^7/7!,                       (11.346.3)
```

where `A_n` is the rigorously enclosed absolute mass of the corrected
integrand on the finite contour.  The lifted analytic tails from Section
11.345 acquire at most the factor `exp(kappa)`.  Thus (11.346.3), the signed
moments `M_(n,0),...,M_(n,6)`, and the transported tail enclose every point of
the whole cell; no intermediate-height sampling is used.

A deterministic append-only Arb atlas certifies all 399 cells.  Its largest

```text
 < 2.152371e-6,

max_(0<=n<=398, |theta|<=1) (sqrt(2)/pi)|Delta I_2(n,theta)|
 < 9.68907e-7.                                             (11.346.4)
```

Both maxima occur in the production enclosure at event `n=2`; they are below

Equation (11.347.2) is exact combinatorial ownership, not a quantitative

## 11.349 Exact global-Morse Gamma bulk

There is no need to Taylor-expand the ordinary full-line bulk.  In the exact
logistic coordinate, set

```text
P_bulk=m sqrt(2/x)(1+i).
```

The complete Kummer weight and Jacobian reduce algebraically to

```text
A_bulk(s)=m sqrt(2)(1+i)r^(3/4)
          v(s)^(-1/4)dv/ds.                            (11.349.1)
```

After Abel damping and then passage to the boundary value,

```text
I_bulk(t)
 =exp(i t/2) Gamma(3/4+i t/2)
  /(i t/2)^(3/4+i t/2).                                (11.349.2)
```

Divide by `I_G=2sqrt(pi/t)exp(-i*pi/4)` and write `B=I_bulk/I_G`.
At `t=10^10`, rigorous evaluation gives

```text
log|B|=-3.1250000000000000000195...e-22,
arg B=2.0833333333333333333345...e-12,
|B-exp(i(theta-theta_0))|
 <3.126e-22.                                            (11.349.3)
```

The argument in (11.349.3) supplies the saved-height Riemann--Siegel phase
correction.  Summing the remaining amplitude defect over all `39273` target
modes gives

```text
complex aggregate <1.093e-19,
two-real aggregate <2.186e-19,
physical aggregate <4.919e-20.                         (11.349.4)
```

The ordinary full-line bulk is therefore closed at the saved height with
more than `1.7e14` normalized target headroom.  The finite endpoint tails
are not included in (11.349.4).

## 11.350 Exact finite-endpoint tail decomposition

Let `F_D=F(q_D)`, `E_D=exp(i*pi*q_D^2/2)`, and
`a_m=m sqrt(2/x)`.  Since `F(+infinity)=(1+i)/2` and
`F(-infinity)=-(1+i)/2`, every finite current has the exact decomposition

```text
P_m=(E_B-E_A)/(i*pi)+a_m(F_B-F_A)
   =P_bulk+P_A+P_B,                                    (11.350.1)

P_A=-E_A/(i*pi)-a_m[F_A+(1+i)/2],
P_B=+E_B/(i*pi)-a_m[(1+i)/2-F_B].                      (11.350.2)
```

This isolates the only pieces left after Section 11.349.  They cannot be
handled as bare endpoint exponentials.  Quadratic completion gives

```text
-m^2/x+q_D^2/2=xD^2/4-mD.                             (11.350.3)
```

Both source endpoints are odd, hence

```text
(-1)^m exp(-i*pi*mD)=1.                               (11.350.4)
```

The separated endpoint exponential is mode independent and is not an
independently summable Poisson object.  Each expression in (11.350.2) must
remain paired, and the symmetric zero, negative, and outer-positive modes
plus endpoint half-current must be restored before absolute values are
taken.  After parity its outer phase is

```text
Phi_D(x)=pi D^2 x/4+(t/2)log((1-x)/x),
Phi_D'(x)=pi D^2/4-t/[2x(1-x)].                        (11.350.5)
```

Thus the remaining wall is a precise symmetric endpoint-tail reassembly:
the lower `A` characteristic term must splice to the certified fold atlas,
while the upper `B` nonstationary enclosure must be extended to the complete
roster.

## 11.351 Symmetric endpoint-tail reassembly

For `alpha=A+2u`, oddness of `A` identifies the portcullis coefficient with
the ordinary Fourier coefficient `I_m`.  If

```text
D_M=sum_(m=-M)^M exp(-2*pi*i*m*u),
G_T=sum_(m=622)^39894 exp(-2*pi*i*m*u),
C_M=D_M-G_T,                                           (11.351.1)
```

then finite algebra gives

```text
S_M-sum_target B_m
 =H_x+integral f_x C_M
      +sum_target(J_m-B_m).                            (11.351.2)
```

The certified symmetric-Poisson limit applies to (11.351.2).  Moreover,

```text
I_m+I_-m=[-2 Delta f_x'+R_m+R_-m]/(2*pi*i*m)^2,       (11.351.3)
```

so the apparent `1/m` endpoint current cancels only after the complete
positive/negative pairing.  This proves the exact residual normal form, not
its quantitative bound.

```text
 =2 Re[exp(-i*pi/8)integral_0^(1/2)K_alpha].           (11.352.2)
```

This survives the finite roster and the certified symmetric-Poisson limit.
The positive joint saddle satisfies

```text
x_m=2*pi*m^2/(t+2*pi*m^2),
alpha_m=2m+t/(pi*m).                                   (11.352.3)
```

At `t=10^10`, `39894<sqrt(t/(2*pi))<39895`.  Hence the half-domain has one
positive stationary branch: modes `1..39894`; modes `m>=39895` are beyond
the half saddle, and nonpositive modes have no joint alpha saddle.  The old
upper branch is already the conjugate in (11.352.2), not a second family.

## 11.354 Midpoint interpolation guard

At integer roster points, odd-square parity gives the valid direct identity

```text
sum_(u=0)^L f_(1/2)(u)
 =exp(i*pi/8)(L+1)(A+B)/2.                            (11.354.1)
```

Between those points the canonical interpolation remains the quadratic
chirp

```text
f_(1/2)(u)=(A+2u)exp(i*pi(A+2u)^2/8).                 (11.354.2)
```

Consequently

```text
I_m(1/2)=4m(-1)^m
 [F((B-4m)/2)-F((A-4m)/2)],                           (11.354.3)
```

and symmetric pairs do not vanish.  Rigorous witnesses include
`|I_1+I_-1|>8.0077e-10` and
`|I_39894+I_-39894|>69000`.  Discrete midpoint parity is boundary data; it
is not a linear-interpolation or pair-cancellation theorem.

## 11.355 Paired half-domain target residual

Put

```text
K_m=integral_0^(1/2)W_t I_m,
Q_half,M=K_H+K_0+sum_(m=1)^M(K_m+K_-m).               (11.355.1)
```

If `T_target=2 Re sum tau_m` and
`tauhat_m=exp(i*pi/8)tau_m`, the exact residual is

```text
2 Re exp(-i*pi/8){
 K_H+K_0
 +sum_(1..621)(K_m+K_-m)
 +sum_(622..39694)(K_m+K_-m-tauhat_m)
 +sum_(39695..39894)(K_m+K_-m-tauhat_m)
 +sum_(39895..M)(K_m+K_-m)}.                          (11.355.2)
```

Every negative mode and the target occur exactly once.  The target rotation
in (11.355.2) is algebraic allocation under the real projection; it is not a
claim that the full-line Gamma bulk splits into equal modewise halves.

## 11.356 Signed-pair half-Morse transform

The `+m` and `-m` Fresnel coordinates differ, but their outer phase is the
same.  With `P_m^pair=P_m+P_-m`, the exact half-domain transform is

```text
K_m+K_-m=(-1)^m exp(i psi_m(x_m))
 integral_(s_H)^infinity exp(-i*t*s^2/4)A_m^pair(s)ds,

A_m^pair=r*x*(dv/ds)[x(1-x)]^(-1/4)P_m^pair,          (11.356.1)

s_H=sgn(v_H-1)sqrt(2[v_H-1-log v_H]),
v_H=2*pi*m^2/t.                                       (11.356.2)
```

Thus `s_H<0` through mode `39894` and `s_H>0` from mode `39895`.  The
negative partner changes the exact amplitude, not the stationary branch.

## 11.357 Endpoint-driven pair transport

The canonical roster interpolation obeys

```text
partial_u^2 f_x=6i*pi*x f_x+4i*pi*x^2 partial_x f_x. (11.357.1)
```

For `P_m=I_m+I_-m`, Fourier integration gives the exact ODE

```text
4i*pi*x^2 P_m'+(4*pi^2*m^2+6i*pi*x)P_m=2 Delta f_x'. (11.357.2)
```

Since `P_m(0)=0`, its integrating factor yields

```text
P_m(x)=x^(-3/2)e^(-i*pi*m^2/x)/(2i*pi)
 integral_0^x z^(-1/2)e^(i*pi*m^2/z)Delta f_z' dz.    (11.357.3)
```

Consequently

```text
K_m+K_-m=1/(2i*pi) integral_0^(1/2)
 z^(-1/2)e^(i*pi*m^2/z)Delta f_z' G_m(z)dz,           (11.357.4)

G_m(z)=integral_z^(1/2)W_t(x)x^(-3/2)e^(-i*pi*m^2/x)dx.
```

This is an exact endpoint-driven Volterra propagator.  It preserves the
Fresnel/endpoint cancellation rather than splitting bare exponentials.

## 11.358 Incomplete-Gamma Volterra kernel

The substitution `w=(1-x)/x` cancels all remaining rational `x` powers:

```text
G_m(z)=(-1)^m integral_1^((1-z)/z)
 w^(-1/4+i*t/2)e^(-i*pi*m^2*w)dw.                    (11.358.1)
```

This is a path-defined incomplete-Gamma difference.  For `m>=39895`, its
phase is nonstationary on `w>=1`, and monotone integration by parts gives

```text
sup_z |G_m(z)|<=2/[pi*m^2-t/2].                       (11.358.2)
```

At `t=10^10`, rigorous summation by a decreasing-tail integral proves

```text
sum_(m=39895)^infinity sup_z|G_m(z)|
 <0.000103.                                           (11.358.3)
```

The outer kernel is therefore summable.  A raw absolute value on its
endpoint driver remains forbidden and would not close the pair residual.

## 11.359 Separable pair-triangle geometry

Expanding (11.357.4) before taking norms gives, for `D=B,A` and signs
`epsilon_B=1`, `epsilon_A=-1`,

```text
K_m+K_-m=sum_D epsilon_D/(2i*pi)
 integral_(0<z<x<1/2) h_D(z)a(x)
 exp{i[phi_(m,D)(z)+psi_m(x)]}dx dz,                  (11.359.1)

phi_(m,D)=pi*m^2/z+pi*D^2*z/4.                        (11.359.2)
```

The phase is separable and its Hessian diagonal.  Its stationary coordinates
obey

```text
z_D=2m/D,
x_m-z_D=2*pi*m^2(D-alpha_m)/[D(t+2*pi*m^2)].          (11.359.3)
```

Thus `D=alpha_m` is exactly the face crossing `z=x`.  At the saved height,
the B saddle enters at `621|622`, the A saddle enters with opposite sign at
`39852|39853`, and the outer saddle leaves through `x=1/2` at
`39894|39895`.  The B face, A fold, and half-boundary corner are faces of one
exact triangle operator.

## 11.360 Exact bi-Morse face and fold chart

The endpoint phase has a second global Morse coordinate.  Put

```text
z_D=2m/D,  u=z/z_D,
p=sqrt(u)-1/sqrt(u).                                  (11.360.1)
```

Then, globally for `z>0`,

```text
phi_(m,D)(z)=pi*m*D+(pi*m*D/2)p^2.                   (11.360.2)
```

Together with the exact outer coordinate `s`, the standardized variables

```text
P=sqrt(pi*m*D)p,  S=sqrt(t/2)s                       (11.360.3)
```

make the complete phase defect exactly `(P^2-S^2)/2`.  The triangle face is
the exact curve `P<P_D(S)`.  At an endpoint event `D=alpha_m`, its tangent
defect is

```text
[dP_D/dS(0)]^2-1=1-4m/D.                             (11.360.4)
```

This is above `0.999` at the B event but equals `1/159577` at the A event
near mode 39894.  The null face is exactly `m=D/4`, and simultaneous endpoint
criticality gives `t=pi*D^2/8`.  Thus the A characteristic fold and the
half-boundary corner are the same null-face geometry in the critical limit;
the B face is ordinary and noncharacteristic.

## 11.361 Face-trace lattice deghosting

On `z=x`, the two mode phases cancel:

```text
Phi_D(x)=pi*D^2*x/4+(t/2)log((1-x)/x).                (11.361.1)
```

Its stationary roots and corresponding lattice centers are

```text
x_D^pm=[1 pm sqrt(1-8t/(pi*D^2))]/2,
m_D^pm=D*x_D^pm/2.                                    (11.361.2)
```

At the lower face root,

```text
partial_z Phi_(m,D)=pi*D^2[1-(m/m_D^-)^2]/4.          (11.361.3)
```

For `B=5122421`, interval arithmetic gives
`m_B^-=621.556003610237...`; only modes 621 and 622 are adjacent.  Their
normal derivatives have magnitudes above `3.68e10` and `2.94e10`.  The old
near-null tangent at mode 257 is not a face critical point: its exact normal
derivative exceeds `1.70e13` in magnitude.  For A, the lower adjacent pair is
39852/39853 and the reflected root is represented by half-Kummer conjugation.

## 11.362 Exact B crossing as step plus tail

For a positive mode define

```text
q_B=sqrt(x/2)(B-2m/x),  a_m=m sqrt(2/x),
T(r)=integral_r^infinity exp(i*pi*u^2/2)du,
U_B=E_B/(i*pi)-sgn(q_B)a_m T(|q_B|).                  (11.362.1)
```

Oddness of the Fresnel primitive gives

```text
P_B=U_B-1_(q_B<0)P_bulk,                              (11.362.2)

P_bulk+P_A+P_B-1_(m>=622)P_bulk
 =P_A+U_B+[1_(m<=621)-1_(q_B<0)]P_bulk.               (11.362.3)
```

At `q_B=0`, `U_B` jumps by `-P_bulk` and the step term jumps by
`+P_bulk`; their grouped current is continuous.  Away from the crossing,
the leading completed current is mode-independent in phase.  Pairing before
the first normal integration gives

```text
-2(2+i*pi*B^2*x)/[pi^2(B^2*x^2-4m^2)],               (11.362.4)
```

and, for `c=Bx/2`,

```text
sum_(m>=1)1/(B^2*x^2-4m^2)
 =pi*cot(pi*c)/(4*B*x)-1/(2*B^2*x^2).                (11.362.5)
```

Modes 621 and 622 must be removed before the cotangent remainder is bounded.

## 11.363 Abel-theta sum-first triangle

Put `r=1/z-1/x>0`, `tau_epsilon=r+i*epsilon`, and
`Theta(tau)=sum_(m in Z)exp(i*pi*tau*m^2)`.  For `epsilon>0`, summing all
nonzero signed pairs before separating the endpoints gives

```text
S_epsilon=1/(4i*pi) integral_(0<z<x<1/2)
 Delta_g(z)a_t(x)[Theta(tau_epsilon)-1]dx dz.          (11.363.1)
```

The endpoint difference satisfies

```text
|Delta_g(z)|<=(3*pi/2)(B^2+A^2)z^(1/2),              (11.363.2)
```

so the grouped `x=0` majorant is proportional to `x^(-1/4)`.  The paired
`1/m^2` theorem supplies the Abel limit.  Applying
`Theta(tau)=(-i*tau)^(-1/2)Theta(-1/tau)` gives dual phase

```text
Psi_(D,n)=pi*D^2*z/4+(t/2)log((1-x)/x)
           -pi*n^2*x*z/(x-z).                         (11.363.3)
```

Its stationary equations are

```text
alpha_(D,n)=D-2n,
z=x*alpha_(D,n)/D,
x(1-x)=2t/[pi*alpha_(D,n)^2].                         (11.363.4)
```

Thus `n=0..2481422` on the B branch recovers the complete odd source roster
`B,B-2,...,A`.  The transform removes artificial modewise face poles, but it
is involutive: a quantitative gain still requires a uniform modular
face/corner estimate and joint control of the continuation.

## 11.364 Gaussian B window and nonlocal Fresnel remainder

Scale the lower B trace by

```text
xi=sqrt(H_B)(x-x_B^-),  H_B=Phi_B''(x_B^-).           (11.364.1)
```

At the saved height, `2sqrt(H_B)/B=113.763965957559...`.  The crossing
centers for modes 620, 621, 622, and 623 are respectively
`-177.017...`, `-63.253...`, `50.510...`, and `164.274...`.  Hence
`|xi|<=70` contains exactly crossings 621 and 622, while every other
positive mode has `|q_B|>75`.

Three Fresnel integrations by parts give

```text
T(r)=iE/(pi*r)+E/(pi^2*r^3)-3iE/(pi^3*r^5)+R_T,
|R_T|<=30/(pi^4*r^7).                                 (11.364.2)
```

After the exact completed phase and `1/x` factor, the sign-adapted current is

```text
B/[i*pi(Bx-2m)]-m/[2*pi^2(c-m)^3]
 +3i*m*x/[4*pi^3(c-m)^5]+R_ext,m,
|R_ext,m|<=15*m*x^2/[4*pi^4*|c-m|^7].                (11.364.3)
```

The remainder, unlike the three displayed pole-bearing terms, is absolutely
summable.  Interval summation plus a monotone analytic infinite-tail bound
proves, uniformly on the window,

```text
sum_(m>=1, m notin {621,622}) |R_ext,m| < 7.48e-6.    (11.364.4)
```

## 11.365 Pole-subtracted cotangent background

For the first paired boundary current, define

```text
S_all(c)=sum_(m>=1)1/[4(c^2-m^2)]
        =pi*cot(pi*c)/(8c)-1/(8c^2),

                  -1/[4(c^2-622^2)].                 (11.365.1)
```

The two apparent poles are removable.  More generally,

```text
lim_(c->k){S_all(c)-1/[4(c^2-k^2)]}=-3/(16k^2).       (11.365.2)
```

Every retained summand has derivative

```text
-c/[2(c^2-m^2)^2]<0,                                 (11.365.3)
```

so `S_hat` is strictly decreasing throughout the `|xi|<=70` window.  Arb
and an independent direct-series replay prove `|S_hat|<0.000288` there and
locate its unique zero at

```text
c in [621.49827876663,621.49827876665],
xi in (-6.568,-6.566).                                (11.365.4)
```

The analytic current

```text
C_hat(x)=-2(2+i*pi*B^2*x)S_hat(Bx/2)/pi^2            (11.365.5)
```

has magnitude above 88000 at the trace saddle.  Its raw absolute integral
on just `0<=xi<=1` exceeds `0.000302`; this is a guard requiring signed
oscillatory combination with the exact 621/622 currents, not a lower bound
for the full residual.

## 11.366 Discrete B-face joint-gradient gap

After allocating the sharp interior saddle, normalize the two face
directions by

```text
G(x)=Phi_B'(x)/sqrt(H_B),
q_m(x)=(Bx-2m)/sqrt(2x).                              (11.366.1)
```

Both are strictly increasing on `0<x<1/2`.  The minimum of
`max(|G|,|q_m|)` is therefore the unique balance between the trace root and
the mode crossing: `-G=q_m` on the left and `G=-q_m` on the right.  Lattice
monotonicity reduces every positive integer to the adjacent modes 621 and
622.  Arb brackets give

```text
min_x max(|G|,|q_621|)>28.08,
min_x max(|G|,|q_622|)>22.40.                         (11.366.2)
```

Consequently, for every positive integer mode on the B face,

```text
max(|G(x)|,|q_m(x)|)>22.40,
G(x)^2+q_m(x)^2>501.                                 (11.366.3)
```

This is the discrete gain hidden by the continuum tangent model.  It permits
the exact smooth partition

```text
chi_T=G^2/(G^2+q_m^2),
chi_N=q_m^2/(G^2+q_m^2),                              (11.366.4)
```

followed by tangential integration where `G` dominates and Fresnel-normal
integration where `q_m` dominates.  Equation (11.366.3) concerns the face
residual after saddle allocation; it does not erase the ordinary interior
saddle for mode 622.

## 11.367 Exact local quadratic-domain gap

For the two B-local modes use the exact outer and normal coordinates

```text
y=sqrt(t)s/2,
u=q_B(m,x)=sqrt(x/2)(B-2m/x).                         (11.367.1)
```

The complete phase defect is exactly

```text
-y^2+pi*u^2/2,  grad=(-2y,pi*u).                    (11.367.2)
```

There is no phase Taylor remainder.  The mode-621 residual domain lies on
the side `u<=q_621(y)` and the mode-622 residual domain on
`u>=q_622(y)`; both exclude `(0,0)`.  Arb brackets the unique nearest
boundary balances and proves

```text
min max(2|y|,pi|u|)>57.17  for m=621,
min max(2|y|,pi|u|)>45.63  for m=622.                (11.367.3)
```

Thus the only two local integer domains are exactly nonstationary.  The
near-degeneracy of the tangent half-plane is introduced by replacing the
curved boundary with a remote line; it is not present in either exact
domain.

## 11.368 Modular-continuation stationary cancellation

For a matched continuation label

```text
alpha=A-2k=alpha_(B,L+k)=alpha_(A,k),                (11.368.1)
```

the dual `z` saddle is `z_*=x*alpha/D`.  Its reduced phase, Hessian, and
modular coordinate are

```text
psi_alpha=pi*alpha^2*x/4+(t/2)log((1-x)/x),
Psi_zz(z_*)=-pi*D^3/[2(D-alpha)x],
r_*=(D-alpha)/(x*alpha).                             (11.368.2)
```

Multiplying the modular factor, endpoint driver, and leading stationary
scale simplifies exactly to

```text
M_D=4sqrt(x)/D+2i*pi*alpha*x^(3/2).                  (11.368.3)
```

Hence the universal second channel cancels in `M_B-M_A`, leaving only
`4sqrt(x)(1/B-1/A)`.  Moreover Arb and independent rational Machin bounds
prove

```text
A-2<sqrt(8t/pi)<A.                                   (11.368.4)
```

The `k=0` term is therefore the sole face/fold exception;
`1<=k<=79788` has an interior `z` saddle but no real `x` saddle, and every
larger `k` has no interior `z` saddle.  This section concerns the leading
`z`-stationary coefficient only.

## 11.369 Exact Weber completion at fixed continuation label

Put `p=sqrt(x-z)` and `n=(D-alpha)/2`.  The exact monotone coordinate

```text
u_D=Dp/2-nx/p                                       (11.369.1)
```

gives

```text
x(D^2/4+n^2)-D^2p^2/4-n^2x^2/p^2
 =alpha^2x/4-u_D^2,
u_D(sqrt(x))=alpha*sqrt(x)/2.                        (11.369.2)
```

Completing the `p` integral to infinity and using the Weber identities

```text
I_0(a,b)=sqrt(pi)e^(-2sqrt(ab))/(2sqrt(a)),
I_2=-partial_a I_0                                  (11.369.3)
```

gives, in the principal Abel sense,

```text
Full_(D,n)=2i*pi*alpha*x^(3/2)e^(i*pi*alpha^2x/4).   (11.369.4)
```

This is independent of `D`, so every fixed matched B/A completion cancels.
The finite triangle difference is one common-phase Gaussian tail.  A common
dual cutoff cannot yet be sent to infinity by reindexing alone: it leaves
an A-endpoint shift block of exactly `L` terms.

## 11.370 Vanishing of the cutoff-shift defect

For an A-dual mode scale `z=xq`.  Its kernel has the exact form

```text
K_(A,n)(x)=e^(i*pi/4)x integral_0^1 (1-q)^(-1/2)
 [2+i*pi*A^2*xq]e^(i phi_(A,n))dq,                   (11.370.1)

phi_q=pi*x[A^2/4-n^2/(1-q)^2].                       (11.370.2)
```

The retained factor `x` gives the trivial small-`x` bound
`4x+2pi*A^2x^2`.  For `n>=A`, one integration by parts gives

```text
|K_(A,n)(x)|<=[368/(63pi)+(668/315)A^2x]/n^2.       (11.370.3)
```

Splitting at `x=n^(-2)` proves that its weighted mode norm is
`O(n^(-1/2))+O(A^2n^(-2))`.  Since the cutoff defect has the fixed width
`L`, its weighted norm tends to zero.  This licenses the symmetric dual
reindexing at the saved height; the constants are not height uniform.

## 11.371 Source-roster and same-index theta-tail reassembly

The licensed continuation reindexing and fixed-label Weber cancellation give

```text
sum_(n>=1)(B_n-A_n)
 =sum_(n=1)^L Full_(B,n)
  +sum_(n>=1)[Tail_(A,n)-Tail_(B,n)].                (11.371.1)
```

The positive-dual multiplicity and Abel prefactor normalize each completed
term exactly as

```text
[2/(4i*pi)]a_t Full_(B,n)
 =(B-2n)[x(1-x)]^(-1/4)e^(i*pi(B-2n)^2x/4).          (11.371.2)
```

Thus the finite block recovers the equation-(9) source labels
`B-2,B-4,...,A` with no phase or normalization error.  The remaining tails
sum at equal dual index.  With `s=p^2/x>=1` they form one endpoint-grouped
theta integral whose driver difference vanishes at `s=1`; the missing upper
label B remains in the zero/direct/endpoint-half sector.

## 11.372 Double-Weber source reconstruction

Apply Jacobi again to the grouped theta tail and set `p=sqrt(s-1)`.  The
endpoint-D Weber mode is

```text
int_0^infinity [2-i*pi*D^2*x*p^2]
 e^(-i*pi*D^2*x*p^2/4-i*pi*ell^2/(x*p^2))dp

=-2i*pi*ell*e^(-i*pi/4)e^(-i*pi*D*ell)/sqrt(x).     (11.372.1)
```

It is not zero separately.  Because A and B are odd, their values agree for
every integer `ell>=1`; the endpoint difference cancels.  The `ell=0` mode
vanishes by the Abel primitive

```text
d[2p e^(-i*pi*D^2*x*p^2/4)]/dp.                     (11.372.2)
```

In the inherited common Abel prescription, the theta tail therefore
collapses to the dual-zero tail difference.  Adding the dual zero mode gives
one half of the B endpoint minus one half of the A endpoint.  The direct
`-1` cancels the original Poisson zero mode, while
`K_H=[f_x(0)+f_x(L)]/2`; together these terms recover the missing B label.
The complete modular calculation consequently reconstructs exactly

```text
B,B-2,...,A.                                         (11.372.3)
```

This is an involution guard, not an error estimate.  It proves that the
modular continuation, zero mode, direct term, and endpoint halves are one
copy of the source and must not receive independent error budgets.

## 11.376 Exact endpoint residual versus source telemetry

Three source-side quantities must remain distinct.  Write

```text
Q_K = exact finite equation-(9) Kummer roster,
Q_P = published asymptotic/generalized-Gauss hybrid,
Q_S = implemented source hybrid,
T   = exact classical upper main.                    (11.376.1)
```

The saved source discrepancy has the exact decomposition

```text
Q_S-T=(Q_K-T)+(Q_P-Q_K)+(Q_S-Q_P).                   (11.376.2)
```

The symmetric endpoint calculation and the double-Weber involution
reconstruct `Q_K`, not `Q_P` or `Q_S`.  Independently, the paper audit proves
that the exact Kummer integral precedes the asymptotic grouping, that the
`i*j*sin(u)` member of the exact equation-(10) pair is dropped before
equation (51), and that the published hybrid is not exact.  Consequently the
certified central telemetry value

```text
Q_S-T=-0.0069830180084699455319725803829...           (11.376.3)
```

cannot be transferred as either an upper or a lower bound for `Q_K-T`.
For any proposed value `r=Q_K-T`, choosing `Q_P-Q_K=(Q_S-T)-r` and
`Q_S-Q_P=0` preserves (11.376.3); this is an algebraic nonidentification, not
a numerical uncertainty.

The Gamma calculation does close the target-carrier bridge.  If `G` is the
projected exact Gamma bulk, then

```text
Q_K-G=(Q_K-T)-(G-T),
|G-T|<2.186e-19.                                      (11.376.4)
```

Thus replacing the classical carrier by the Gamma bulk changes the exact
Kummer endpoint residual only at the `10^-19` scale.  It does not identify
that residual with source telemetry.  A valid telemetry route must first
bound both `Q_P-Q_K` and the complete global `Q_S-Q_P` in the same
normalization; partial evaluator certificates cannot silently replace them.
