## 11.377 Beta^-4 canonical-fold Airy reduction

The leading Airy representation in Section 11.315 extends exactly through
the complete second-order event normal form.  Put

```text
X=lambda+y,              epsilon=beta^(-2),
A(X)=Ai(-X),             A_X=dA/dX,
D_M(y)=sum_(m in M) exp(-i*d_m*y),                    (11.377.1)
```

where `M` is any finite roster of real detunings.  With `a_1,r_1,a_2,r_2`
as in Sections 11.343--11.344, set

```text
M_4(z,y)=1+epsilon(a_1+i*r_1)
 +epsilon^2(a_2+i*r_2+i*a_1*r_1-r_1^2/2).            (11.377.2)
```

Its largest `z` power is ten.  In the symmetric Abel sense, the Airy Fourier
normalization gives every required moment exactly:

```text
integral_R^Abel z^k exp(i[z^3/3-Xz])dz
 =2*pi*i^k d_X^k A(X),              0<=k<=10.         (11.377.3)
```

This also records the provenance of `pi`: the factor `2*pi` is the inverse
normalization in the Fourier representation of `Ai`, not an inserted
geometric or fitted constant.  Since `A_XX=-X*A`, write

```text
d_X^k A=P_k(X)A+Q_k(X)A_X,
P_0=1, Q_0=0,
P_(k+1)=P_k'-X Q_k,       Q_(k+1)=P_k+Q_k'.           (11.377.4)
```

Exact rational contraction of the ten moments then gives

```text
I_M^[4](beta,lambda,Y)
 =2*pi integral_0^Y exp(i*y^2/(4beta))D_M(y)
   {U(lambda,y,beta)A(lambda+y)
     +V(lambda,y,beta)A_X(lambda+y)}dy,               (11.377.5)

U=1+epsilon U_1+epsilon^2 U_2,
V=  epsilon V_1+epsilon^2 V_2,

U_1=-(13lambda+3y)/60,
V_1=(8lambda^2-4lambda*y+3y^2)/60,

U_2=-(448lambda^5+280lambda^2*y^3+4565lambda^2
       -105lambda*y^4+30lambda*y+63y^5-405y^2)/50400,

V_2=(40lambda^3-20lambda^2*y+lambda*y^2-9y^3+27)/1680.
                                                               (11.377.6)
```

Setting `epsilon=0` recovers (11.315.2).  Thus the complete beta-minus-four
canonical fold model is no longer a two-dimensional comparison problem: it
has precisely two one-dimensional scalar channels, `Ai(-X)` and its
`X` derivative.  The independent checker reconstructs the degree-ten
multiplier from the four normal-form polynomials, uses a separately frozen
Airy-ODE derivative table, and tests that table at three 70-digit points.

The next theorem is now explicit but is not included here: prove a
remainder-controlled two-branch expansion for both Airy channels in every
ordinary corridor, identify its phases and normalization with the
classical/Gamma carrier, retain the exact Airy expression in the fold collar,
and assign the overlaps without omission or duplication.  Section 11.377
does not prove that match, a bound for `Q_K-T`, complete `T_upper`, a
height-uniform theorem, `Lambda<=0`, PF-infinity, RH, or a prize-level result.

## 11.378 Exact positive-X Hankel branch factorization

The two Airy channels in Section 11.377 can be separated without assuming
that `X` is asymptotically large.  For `X>0`, put

```text
xi=2X^(3/2)/3,       A(X)=Ai(-X),       A_X=dA/dX.    (11.378.1)
```

The exact Airy--Bessel connection and Bessel reflection identities give

```text
A(X)=sqrt(X)/(2sqrt(3))
 {e^(i*pi/6) H^(1)_(1/3)(xi)
  +e^(-i*pi/6)H^(2)_(1/3)(xi)},

A_X(X)=-X/(2sqrt(3))
 {e^(-i*pi/6)H^(1)_(2/3)(xi)
  +e^(i*pi/6) H^(2)_(2/3)(xi)}.                      (11.378.2)
```

The `pi/6` phases are forced by reflection at orders `1/3` and `2/3`; they
are not fitted phase shifts.  Since the weights `U,V` in (11.377.5) are real,
define

```text
C_1=1/(2sqrt(3)){
 U sqrt(X)e^(i*pi/6)H^(1)_(1/3)(xi)
 -V X e^(-i*pi/6)H^(1)_(2/3)(xi)},

C_2=1/(2sqrt(3)){
 U sqrt(X)e^(-i*pi/6)H^(2)_(1/3)(xi)
 -V X e^(i*pi/6)H^(2)_(2/3)(xi)}.                    (11.378.3)
```

Then

```text
U A+V A_X=C_1+C_2,             C_2=conj(C_1),         (11.378.4)

W(H^(1)_nu,H^(2)_nu)=-4i/(pi*xi).                    (11.378.5)
```

Thus the two branches are exact and independent for every positive `X`.
Their standard leading forms give the phase contract

```text
C_1 ~[U X^(-1/4)+iV X^(1/4)]/(2sqrt(pi))
      exp(i[xi-pi/4]),

C_2 ~[U X^(-1/4)-iV X^(1/4)]/(2sqrt(pi))
      exp(-i[xi-pi/4]).                               (11.378.6)
```

After restoring `exp(i[y^2/(4beta)-d*y])`, their normal phase derivatives
are

```text
y/(2beta)-d+sqrt(lambda+y),
y/(2beta)-d-sqrt(lambda+y),                           (11.378.7)
```

which are precisely the two cubic-fold ordinary-saddle equations.  Equation
(11.378.6) records phase and leading normalization only; no quantitative
Hankel remainder is claimed there.  Equations (11.378.2)--(11.378.4), by
contrast, are exact and remain valid when `X` is small and positive.

The raw Hankel functions in (11.378.2) diverge at `xi=0`, but their
`sqrt(X)` and `X` prefactors give finite one-sided branch limits.  The written
products are nevertheless undefined at `X=0`; there one must use the regular
Airy basis or separately certify those limits.  Hence a valid splice should
retain the Airy basis in a fold collar and use the branch basis on a
positive-`X` ordinary region.  It must then compare the selected branch with the
endpoint-retaining logistic/Gamma carrier and bound both the branch error and

## 11.379 Hankel carrier selection on all event cells

To separate exact branch algebra from asymptotic approximation, factor the
positive-`X` branches in Section 11.378 as

```text
C_+(X)=exp(i[xi-pi/4])B_+(X),
C_-(X)=exp(-i[xi-pi/4])B_-(X),       xi=2X^(3/2)/3.   (11.379.1)
```

Here `B_+` contains the exact scaled Hankel amplitudes of orders `1/3` and
`2/3`, and `B_-=conj(B_+)` for real data.  Equation (11.379.1) is an exact
factorization, not a replacement of the Hankel functions by their leading
asymptotics.  Restoring `exp(i[y^2/(4beta)-d_m y])`, the extracted carrier
derivatives are

```text

F_-(y)=y/(2beta)-d_m-sqrt(lambda+y).                  (11.379.2)
```

At an event write `t=tau_m+delta`.  Equations (11.336.2) and (11.378.1)
give

```text
lambda=d_m^2-delta/beta.                              (11.379.3)
```

Set `sigma=sign(d_m)`, choosing `C_+` for positive `d_m` and `C_-` for
negative `d_m`.  Exact rationalization gives

```text
F_sigma(0)
 =-d_m+sigma sqrt(lambda)
 =-sigma delta/[beta(sqrt(lambda)+|d_m|)],             (11.379.4)

F_-sigma(0)=-sigma(|d_m|+sqrt(lambda)).                (11.379.5)
```

Thus the selected extracted carrier crosses the lower endpoint precisely at
the event center.  The opposite extracted carrier does not share that
endpoint crossing.

For the 399 events, `|4m-C|` runs through the odd absolute labels from `1`
to `797`.  Since `beta^3=pi C^2/8` and every certified cell has
`|delta|<=pi/16`,

```text
lambda >=(beta/C)^2-pi/(16beta)
        =pi/(16beta)>9e-5.                            (11.379.6)
```

Hence every cell lies strictly in the positive-`X` domain of Section 11.378.
On `0<=y<=64`, interval arithmetic also gives

```text
X<179.783<180<beta^2,
|F_-sigma(0)|>0.023,
|F_sigma(0)|<0.004 at both cell faces.                (11.379.7)
```

Because `X<beta^2`, (11.379.2) shows that the opposite extracted carrier has
fixed derivative sign on the fold strip.  The selected carrier is strictly
monotone there and has at most one carrier saddle.  These are exact carrier
statements; they do not yet control the phase or derivatives hidden in the

integration by parts on the opposite branch or identifying the selected

For each selected mode put


Writing `R=sqrt(2s+mu-1)`, exact substitution into the actions gives


The maximum occurs at `m=40094` and is rigorously nonzero.  Hence its phase

The exact scalar amplitudes and Hessians at the same saddles simplify to

## 11.387 Endpoint-coherent detuning ODE

Let `X=lambda+y`, `epsilon=beta^-2`, and write either corrected selected
Hankel branch as

```text
C_sigma=(U W_sigma+V W_sigma,X)/2,
W_sigma,XX=-X W_sigma.
```

For its finite transform

```text
G_sigma(d)=Integral_0^Y exp(i[y^2/(4beta)-dy])
                         C_sigma(lambda,y)dy,          (11.387.1)
```

two integrations by parts, with neither endpoint discarded, give

```text
G_sigma''/(4beta^2)+i(1+d/beta)G_sigma'
 +(lambda-d^2+i/(2beta))G_sigma
 =R_0,sigma+R_Y,sigma+Q_sigma,                        (11.387.2)

R_0,sigma=C_sigma,y(lambda,0)+id C_sigma(lambda,0),  (11.387.3)

R_Y,sigma=e^(i[Y^2/(4beta)-dY])
 [i(Y/(2beta)-d)C_sigma(lambda,Y)-C_sigma,y(lambda,Y)]. (11.387.4)
```

The beta-minus-four forcing simplifies exactly to

```text
Q_sigma=Integral_0^Y e^(i[y^2/(4beta)-dy])
                    [E_0 W_sigma+E_1 W_sigma,X]/2 dy,

E_0=-epsilon y^2/4
    +epsilon^2(13lambda y^2/240+y^3/80),
E_1=-epsilon^2 y^2(8lambda^2-4lambda y+3y^2)/240.    (11.387.5)
```

Thus both forcing channels vanish quadratically at `y=0`.  Throughout the
selector top corridor and `0<=y<=Y`, interval arithmetic proves

```text
|E_0|<7.31e-4,       |E_1|<1.08e-7.                 (11.387.6)
```

For the 398-term roster in Section 11.385 put `h=4beta/C`, `d_0=-h/4`.
Its detunings are `d_0-hj`, `1<=j<=198`, and `d_0+hj`, `1<=j<=200`.
If `C_-=a+ib` and `C_-,y=a'+ib'`, exact finite summation yields

```text
sum R_0=398a'+(79601/2)h b
        +i[-2b'+(599/2)h a],                          (11.387.7)

sum e^(-i common phase)R_Y
 =-398a'-(79599/2)h b
   +i[2b'-(201/2)h a].                               (11.387.8)
```

Equation (11.387.7) uses the branch values at `y=0`; (11.387.8) uses those
at `y=Y`.  The upper phase is common because the exact selector geometry
gives

```text
hY=2pi,       Y/(2beta)=h/2,
exp(-id_mY)=i                                             (11.387.9)
```

for every selected mode, with `C=1 mod 4`.  The resulting endpoint-source
aggregate magnitudes are below `712.390` and `111.832`, respectively.  They
are two coherent boundary channels, not 398 unrelated errors.  The interior
forcing retains exactly the event-ordered Dirichlet projection (11.385.4),
with `C_sigma` replaced by `(E_0W_sigma+E_1W_sigma,X)/2`.

The large endpoint channels explain why the bare full-saddle finite-integral
diagnostic fails despite good interior one-mode samples.  Section 11.387 does
not prove their cancellation with `g4_lambda(0)`, the endpoint half-current,
or the zero/negative/outer-positive completion.  That composition must occur
before a Green-kernel norm or absolute value is taken.

Every `pi` in (11.387.9) is inherited from `Y=pi C/(2beta)` and
`beta^3=pi C^2/8`; no independent geometric normalization is introduced.

## 11.388 Airy Green kernel and exact event lattice

The detuning operator in Section 11.387 is itself an Airy operator in
disguise.  Put

```text
chi(d)=2beta^2d+beta d^2,
r=beta^2+lambda+2beta d,
G(d)=exp[-i chi(d)]H(r).                              (11.388.1)
```

Direct differentiation gives the exact conjugation

```text
L_beta G=exp[-i chi(d)](H_rr+rH).                     (11.388.2)
```

Hence `L_beta G=S` has transformed source `exp(i chi)S` and Green kernel

```text
K(r,s)=pi[Ai(-r)Bi(-s)-Bi(-r)Ai(-s)],                (11.388.3)
K(s,s)=0,       partial_r K(s,s)=1.                  (11.388.4)
```

For any reference point `r_0`, variation of constants is therefore

```text
H(r)=-partial_s K(r,r_0)H(r_0)+K(r,r_0)H_r(r_0)
 +Integral_(r_0)^r K(r,s)e^[i chi(d(s))]S(d(s))ds.   (11.388.5)
```

The selected detunings form an exact affine lattice:

```text
r_m=beta^2(8m/C-1)+lambda,
Delta_r=8beta^2/C,
r_(q+j)=r_q+j Delta_r,
r_(q-j)=r_q-j Delta_r.                               (11.388.6)
```

Across the top corridor and all 399 selector modes,

```text
4.595460e6<r<4.688074e6,
Delta_r=232.6947988866....                            (11.388.7)
```

DLMF 9.8.20 with its signed first-neglected-term remainder gives
`M(-r)^2<=1/(pi sqrt(r))`.  The determinant and
`M(-r)^2=Ai(-r)^2+Bi(-r)^2` then prove

```text
|K(r,s)|<=pi M(-r)M(-s)<=(rs)^(-1/4)
          <4.664827e-4.                               (11.388.8)
```

The pointwise envelope in (11.388.8) is not summed absolutely over the
lattice.  The exact symmetry in (11.388.6) requires the endpoint sources and
interior forcing from Section 11.387 to be inserted before finite Abel or
phase estimates are taken.

The `pi` in (11.388.3) is the Airy Wronskian normalization.  The lattice
scale inherits `beta^3=pi C^2/8` and the Kummer/Fourier detuning.

## 11.389 Cubic resonance on the Airy event lattice

Let `vartheta(r)=theta(-r)` be the continuous Airy phase from DLMF 9.8,
so that `Ai(-r)=M(-r)sin(vartheta(r))`.  With `m=q+j`, the exact event
lattice in (11.388.6) can be written

```text
u=lambda/beta^2,       0<=u<=1/(2C^2),
r_j=beta^2[1+(8j-2)/C+u],       -198<=j<=200.       (11.389.1)
```

The height bound is exact: `lambda<=pi/(16beta)` and
`beta^3=pi C^2/8` give `u<=1/(2C^2)`.  For the leading phase
`xi(r)=2r^(3/2)/3`, the constant, linear, and quadratic lattice terms
satisfy

```text
pi*j*(C-1+2j)=2pi*j*(2q+j).                         (11.389.2)
```

They are therefore an exact integer multiple of `2pi`.  Put

```text
x_j=(8j-2)/C+u,       x_0=-2/C+u,

P_5(j,u)=pi C^2/12 sum_(k=1)^5 binom(3/2,k)
                         (x_j^k-x_0^k)
          -pi*j*(C-1+2j).                           (11.389.3)
```

At the selector centre this polynomial is exactly

```text
P_5(j,0)=-pi*j*(16j^2-12j+3)/(6C)
 +pi[(8j-2)^4-16]/(512C^2)
 -pi[(8j-2)^5+32]/(1024C^3).                       (11.389.4)
```

Thus the first nonconstant phase after removing the exact resonant integer
is cubic in `j`, not linear or quadratic.  On the full roster and height
corridor, `|x_j|<0.010014`.  Taylor's theorem through degree five, with
`binom(3/2,6)=7/1024`, gives a uniform leading-phase error below
`4.808564e-5`.

DLMF 9.8.22 and the signed first-neglected-term remainder following 9.8.23
give

```text
|vartheta(r)-(pi/4+xi(r))|<=5/(48r^(3/2)).          (11.389.5)
```

The constant `pi/4` cancels between two event phases, and all event
coordinates exceed `4.595460e6`.  Combining the two endpoint corrections
with the binomial error proves

```text
|vartheta(r_j)-vartheta(r_0)
 -2pi*j*(2q+j)-P_5(j,u)|<4.808567e-5.               (11.389.6)
```

For `j=1`, monotonic endpoint enclosure over the complete height interval
gives

```text
-2.297e-5 < vartheta(r_1)-vartheta(r_0)-2pi(2q+1)
           < -1.804e-5.                             (11.389.7)
```

Consequently a generic first-difference Dirichlet denominator is invalid
near event zero: two full asymptotic orders are exactly resonant.  The next
object is the finite cubic-quintic exponential sum generated by
(11.389.3), with the event-pair amplitudes and completed endpoint sources
still attached.  No such sum estimate or grouped Green-operator bound is
asserted here.

Every `pi` in (11.389.1)--(11.389.7) comes either from the exact selector
identity `beta^3=pi C^2/8` or the standard Airy phase normalization; no
fitted frequency or unrelated circle normalization is introduced.

## 11.390 Grouped Airy phase and Green packets

Write the exact event phase from Section 11.389 as

```text
vartheta(r_j)-vartheta(r_0)
 =2pi*j*(2q+j)+P_5(j,u)+delta_j(u),
|delta_j(u)|<4.808567e-5.                            (11.390.1)
```

The integer phase vanishes inside each exponential.  Arb summation at
`u=0` gives

```text
sum_(j=-198)^200 exp(iP_5(j,0))
 =31.7295396359...-0.4287931139...i,
absolute value 31.7324368595....                    (11.390.2)
```

Exhausting all `399*400/2` nonempty contiguous blocks proves

```text
max_(a<=b) |sum_(j=a)^b exp(iP_5(j,0))|
 <52.298192,                                         (11.390.3)
```

with the largest candidate block `-30<=j<=31`.  Exact differentiation of
the polynomial `P_5` over `0<=u<=1/(2C^2)` gives

```text
sum_j sup_u |P_5(j,u)-P_5(j,0)|<0.195889.           (11.390.4)
```

Using `|exp(ix)-exp(iy)|<=|x-y|` in (11.390.1)--(11.390.4) proves, on the
whole top corridor,

```text
|sum_(j=-198)^200 exp(i[vartheta(r_j)-vartheta(r_0)])|
 >31.517362,

sup_(a<=b) |sum_(j=a)^b
 exp(i[vartheta(r_j)-vartheta(r_0)])|<52.513267.     (11.390.5)
```

The first inequality rejects an `O(1)` phase-only collapse.  The second
retains enough cancellation to improve the Green packets.  Indeed,

```text
K(r_j,s)=pi M(-r_j)M(-s)
                sin(vartheta(r_j)-vartheta(s)).      (11.390.6)
```

DLMF 9.8(iii) makes `M(-r_j)` positive and nonincreasing in `j`.  Abel
summation, (11.390.5), and the modulus bound in (11.388.8) therefore give,
for every contiguous active block `I`,

```text
|sum_(j in I)K(r_j,s)|<0.024496527.                 (11.390.7)
```

This replaces the termwise value `0.186126572`, an improvement by a factor
greater than `7.59808`.  The inverse gauge does not disturb this packet.
For `d_m=beta(4m/C-1)`, direct substitution gives

```text
chi(d_m)=2beta^2d_m+beta d_m^2=2pi m^2-beta^3,
exp[-i chi(d_m)]=exp(i beta^3).                      (11.390.8)
```

The gauge phase is therefore exactly common to every integer mode.  The
derivative channel also uses the same event phasor:

```text
partial_s K(r_j,s)=pi M(-r_j)N(-s)
                   sin(varphi(-s)-vartheta(r_j)).    (11.390.9)
```

DLMF 9.8.21 and its signed remainder imply

```text
N(-s)^2<=sqrt(s)/pi [1+7/(32s^3)].                 (11.390.10)
```

Consequently the same Abel argument proves

```text
|sum_(j in I)partial_s K(r_j,s)|<52.775866,         (11.390.11)
```

versus the termwise value `400.995251`, again a factor greater than
`7.59808`.  At fixed `s`, the active indices produced by interchanging the
finite event sum with the variation-of-constants integral are contiguous,
so (11.390.7) applies without reallocating endpoint or complement terms.

Equations (11.390.7) and (11.390.11) have not yet been multiplied by the
initial data or integrated against the coherent endpoint and interior
sources.  Those channels must first be composed with the completed Poisson
remainder.  In particular, the lower bound in (11.390.5) forbids claiming
that the endpoint source disappears by Airy phase cancellation alone.

The `pi` factors inherit the selector identity and Airy Wronskian described
in Sections 11.388--11.389.  The phase, modulus monotonicity, and derivative
modulus bounds are sourced from DLMF 9.8.

Choose event zero as reference and write

```text
r_j=r_0+j Delta_r,
```

```text
H_sigma(r_j)=-partial_s K(r_j,r_0)H_sigma(r_0)
 +K(r_j,r_0)H_sigma,r(r_0)
 +Integral_(r_0)^(r_j)K(r_j,s)F_sigma(s)ds.          (11.392.2)
```

Retaining the leading-defect weights `a_j`, finite Fubini reassembly on the
positive branch is exactly

```text
sum_(j=1)^200 a_j H_+(r_j)
 =-D_+ H_+(r_0)+A_+ H_+,r(r_0)

    [sum_(j:r_j>=s) a_jK(r_j,s)]F_+(s)ds,            (11.392.3)
```

whereas orientation on the negative branch gives

```text
sum_(j=-198)^-1 a_j H_-(r_j)

    [sum_(j:r_j<=s) a_jK(r_j,s)]F_-(s)ds.            (11.392.4)
```

Here `D_sigma=sum a_j partial_sK(r_j,r_0)` and
`A_sigma=sum a_jK(r_j,r_0)`.  The active source blocks are suffixes on the
positive branch and prefixes on the negative branch.  Their exact cell
incidence counts are `20100` and `19701`; a separate rational finite-array
checker verifies both orientation identities.

The inverse gauge remains common on the integer event roster:

```text
sum a_jG_sigma(d_j)=exp(i beta^3)sum a_jH_sigma(r_j). (11.392.5)
```

Thus no modewise phase is introduced after (11.392.3)--(11.392.4).
Sections 11.390--11.391 give the branchwise coefficients

```text
|A_-| and the negative source packet <3.773904e-7,
|A_+| and the positive source packet <3.803312e-7,
|D_-|<0.000813059,
|D_+|<0.000819394.                                  (11.392.6)
```

Equations (11.392.3)--(11.392.6) expose rather than remove the remaining
wall.  The source-kernel coefficients are at the `10^-7` scale, but the
derivative packets multiply branch initial data at the `8.2e-4` scale.
Neither initial value may be discarded.  The event-zero term, the completed

```text
H4+sum G4+C4=g4_lambda(0),                           (11.392.7)
```

and the exact-minus-beta-four source must be expressed in the same

## 11.393 Weighted completion and the partial-sum obligation

Let `L=39696`, `q=39894`, and `U=40094`.  Extend the 398 selected
leading-defect weights to an auxiliary complete beta-minus-four roster by

```text
w_m=a_m (m!=q),             w_q=0.                  (11.393.1)
```

For the unweighted beta-minus-four terms define the prefix and its completed
remainder by

```text
S_k=sum_(m=L)^k G4_m,
R_k=H4+C4+sum_(m=k+1)^U G4_m.                       (11.393.2)
```

The completed projection in (11.392.7) gives, without separating `H4` or
`C4`,

```text
S_k=g4_lambda(0)-R_k.                               (11.393.3)
```

Finite Abel summation is exactly

```text
W_full=sum_(m=L)^U w_mG4_m
 =w_U S_U+sum_(k=L)^(U-1)(w_k-w_(k+1))S_k           (11.393.4)

 =w_L g4_lambda(0)-w_U R_U
  -sum_(k=L)^(U-1)(w_k-w_(k+1))R_k.                 (11.393.5)
```

An independent exact rational 399-mode calculation checks both identities.
Each `R_k` retains the endpoint half-current, the zero/negative/outer-positive
complement, and the untouched upper suffix as one object.  Thus
(11.393.5) neither splits bare endpoint exponentials nor takes termwise
absolute values of the `G4_m`.

Reconstructing all 398 certified weights and inserting `w_q=0` proves

```text
sum_(k=L)^(U-1)|w_(k+1)-w_k|<1.547052e-5,
|w_L|+sum|Delta w|+|w_U|<3.093180e-5.               (11.393.6)
```

Consequently the cancellation-preserving uniform estimate

```text
max(|g4_lambda(0)|,max_(L<=k<=U)|R_k|)<=B_comp
```

would imply

```text
|W_full|<3.093180e-5 B_comp.                        (11.393.7)
```

This is not yet the selected-branch weighted sum.  Since
`G4_m=G_sel,m+G_opp,m`, exact branch algebra requires

```text
W_sel=W_full-W_opp,
W_opp=sum_(m=L)^U w_mG_opp,m.                       (11.393.7a)
```

The completion controls `W_full`; `W_opp` requires a separate grouped
opposite-branch estimate.

The one global completion does not supply this family.  In fact, interval
reconstruction certifies

```text

```

Holding event zero fixed, the formal perturbation
`G4_40093 -> G4_40093+z`, `G4_40094 -> G4_40094-z` preserves the completed
total but changes `W_full` by `(w_40093-w_40094)z`.  Hence the global identity
alone cannot identify or cancel the auxiliary weighted full roster.  This is a logical
non-identifiability statement about that identity, not a claim that the
actual Fourier model admits arbitrary perturbations.

The next theorem targets are therefore a uniform bound for the completed
cutoff family `R_k` and a separate weighted opposite-branch estimate; only
their combination through (11.393.7a) reaches the selected branch.
No new `pi` enters this reduction; all normalization is inherited from
`beta^3=pi C^2/8` and the beta-minus-four projection.

Let `delta J_lambda(s)` denote the reduced exact-minus-beta-minus-four fold

```text
 =integral_0^1 delta g_lambda(s)e^(-2pi i n s)ds.      (11.397.1)
```

Equation (11.397.1) states the common-profile identity that a theorem for
the missing finite-`t` correction would have to prove; it is not silently
assumed for the physical amplitude/Fresnel remainder.  The all-mode collapse

object at `s=0`.  In the raw reduced-fold and canonical Fourier
normalizations it proves only

```text

|delta g_lambda(0)|<1.759e-10.                        (11.397.2)
```

That scalar estimate does not identify a weighted Fourier correction.  For
arbitrary complex `z`, put

```text
phi_z(s)=z[e^(2pi i 198s)-e^(2pi i 199s)].            (11.397.3)
```

Both endpoint values in (11.397.3) vanish.  Adding `phi_z` therefore leaves
the Fourier midpoint, endpoint half-current, completed value, and event-zero

```text
Delta G_40093=z,            Delta G_40094=-z.          (11.397.4)
```

The interval reconstruction of Section 11.393 gives

```text
|w_40093-w_40094|>1.917e-7.                           (11.397.5)
```

Thus (11.397.3) changes the weighted correction by
`z(w_40093-w_40094)` without changing any datum controlled by (11.397.2).
This is a logical insufficiency theorem for the completed-point estimate,
not a claim that the physical exact profile can be perturbed arbitrarily.

It also isolates a compact sufficient replacement.  If the missing physical
correction is first shown to satisfy (11.397.1), define

```text
P_w(s)=sum_(n=-199)^199 w_(39895+n)e^(-2pi i n s),
w_39894=0.                                             (11.397.6)
```

```text
integral_0^1|P_w(s)|ds<3.840283e-5.                   (11.397.7)
```

Consequently one uniform common-profile estimate

```text
sup_(lambda,s)|delta g_lambda(s)|<=epsilon_profile     (11.397.8)
```

would transfer directly as

```text
|sum_m w_m Delta G_m|
 <=integral_0^1|delta g_lambda(s)P_w(s)|ds
 <3.840283e-5 epsilon_profile.                         (11.397.9)
```

Equivalently, a raw-fold estimate
`sup|delta J_lambda|<=epsilon_J` gives the weighted correction below

```text
7.112e-4 epsilon_J.                                  (11.397.10)
```

No coefficientwise finite-integral norm occurs.  The next theorem target is

Keep the common source carrier suppressed and put

```text
t*=beta^3=pi C^2/8,       t=t*-beta lambda,
```

```text

```

Before inserting the mode factor, define the exact reduced fold profile

```text

        -beta Ys tanh(z/beta)+x(z)Y^2s^2/(2beta)})dz. (11.398.3)
```

completed exact strip.  The exact beta-minus-four contraction is

```text

 [U(lambda,Ys,beta)Ai(-lambda-Ys)
  +V(lambda,Ys,beta)d_X Ai(-lambda-Ys)].              (11.398.4)
```

The inverse Airy normalization and `dy=Y ds` force

```text

g_4,lambda(s) =Y/(2pi)e^(-3pi i s/2)J_4(lambda,s),
Y/(2pi)=1/h.                                          (11.398.5)
```

Substitution of (11.398.2) into the exact transformed mode integral proves

```text
G_ex,(39895+n)=integral_0^1 g_ex,lambda(s)e^(-2pi i ns)ds,
G_4,(39895+n) =integral_0^1 g_4,lambda(s)e^(-2pi i ns)ds. (11.398.6)
```

Therefore, with `delta g=g_ex-g_4` and `w_39894=0`, the entire weighted
exact-minus-beta-minus-four coefficient correction is exactly

```text
Delta W=sum_(m=39696)^40094 w_m(G_ex,m-G_4,m)
       =integral_0^1 delta g_lambda(s)P_w(s)ds,
P_w(s)=sum_(n=-199)^199 w_(39895+n)e^(-2pi i ns).     (11.398.7)
```


The whole-kernel theorem of Section 11.395 now yields the exact implication

```text
  ==> |Delta W|<3.840283e-5 epsilon_profile.           (11.398.9)
```

Put

```text

kappa=2beta^3 rho^2,
```


Let `A=Ai(-X)`, `A_X=d_XAi(-X)`, and `X=lambda+y`.  Direct symbolic
reduction of the beta-minus-four profile gives the exact residual


## 11.402 Exact corrected selected-defect splice

For every augmented-roster mode, put

```text
G4_m=G_sel,m+G_opp,m,
```

Without assigning an exact branch decomposition to `G_ex,m`, exact algebra
gives

```text
G_ex,m-G_opp,m=G_sel,m+Delta G_m,
W_corr=sum_m w_m(G_ex,m-G_opp,m)
      =W_sel,4+Delta W_finite-t.                     (11.402.2)
```

Thus the opposite beta-minus-four branch stays inside the completed
remainder while the exact Kummer-ODE correction enters as one whole Fourier
profile.  Combining (11.396.4) and (11.401.10) proves

```text
sup|W_corr|<4.088814e-5.                              (11.402.3)
```

The finite-height correction is less than `2.935e-7` times the selected
bound.  More importantly, all five grouped real parts are negative.
Appending the certified midpoint, height-transport, and exact finite-height
errors in the adverse direction gives the signed theorem

```text
sup_(t*-pi/16<=t<=t*) Re W_corr(t)<-2.233e-5.        (11.402.4)
```

Hence comparing `|W_corr|` with the old scalar headroom discards potentially

in (11.402.4) is favorable: that requires the still-open exact map from the
lower-A source and initial-data coordinates to the final `Q_K-T` or
`T_upper` scalar.

## 11.403 Corrected selected source-projection orientation

Let `J_m(y)` be the raw transformed fold integral after suppressing its common
source carrier.  The canonical Fourier coefficient and the physical
half-domain mode have the exact normalizations

```text
G_m=(1/(2pi)) integral_0^Y J_m(y)dy,
K_m^(half)=(sqrt(2)/pi) integral_0^Y J_m(y)dy
          =2sqrt(2)G_m.                              (11.403.1)
```

The first factor comes from the inverse Airy Fourier normalization; the
second is the amplitude in the exact equation-(9) Kummer normal form.  Thus
no empirical scale is inserted.  Restoring the common carrier and applying
the exact half-domain reflection gives

```text
2 Re[exp(-i*pi/8) exp(i*beta^3) 2sqrt(2)W_corr].     (11.403.2)
```

Here `beta^3=pi*C^2/8`, `C=159577=1 mod 8`, and

```text
(C^2-1)/8=3183102366
```

is even.  Therefore the phase left in (11.403.2) is exactly one, not a
numerically inferred orientation, and

```text
R_corr=4sqrt(2) Re W_corr.                           (11.403.3)
```

Combining (11.403.3) with (11.402.3)--(11.402.4), with outward-rounded Arb
arithmetic, proves uniformly on the ordinary top corridor

```text
R_corr<-1.2633020694e-4<-1.263e-4,
|R_corr|<2.3129817307e-4<2.314e-4.                   (11.403.4)
```

Equation (11.403.4) fixes the physical projection scale and sign of the
weighted corrected selected leading-defect statistic on the augmented
roster.  It neither identifies that statistic with the unweighted selector
strip nor embeds it into the isolated fold-owned paired-residual block.  The common-profile roster is
`39696..40094`, whereas the fold-owned target roster is `39695..39894`, and
the completed selector identity retains zero, negative, and outer-positive
sectors.  The exact 399-to-200 target allocation and the completed-source
embedding must therefore be proved before (11.403.4) is used as a component
of `Q_K-T`.

## 11.404 Fold-owned target allocation and embedding obligation

The half-domain fold block and its two rosters are

```text
F_fold=sum_(r=39695)^39894(K_r+K_-r-tauhat_r),
T={39695,...,39894},
R={39696,...,40094}.                                (11.404.1)
```

Exact event ordering gives the disjoint allocation

```text
A_39894={39894},
A_(39894-j)={39894-j,39894+j},       1<=j<=198,
A_39695={40093,40094}.                              (11.404.2)
```

Thus the 200 target groups cover all 399 augmented modes exactly once: one
event-zero group, 198 reflected pairs, and one selector-exchange edge.  This
is a combinatorial allocation theorem, not an analytic equality between a
group and its target mode.

Let `Z_m` denote an augmented selector contribution after an exact embedding
into paired-residual coordinates has been supplied, and define

```text
E_emb=sum_(r=39695)^39894(K_r+K_-r)
      -sum_(m=39696)^40094 Z_m.                     (11.404.3)
```

For `m!=39894`, restore the suppressed common source carrier and put

```text
c_m=e^(i beta^3)2sqrt(2)a_m(G_ex,m-G_opp,m),
C_corr=sum_(m!=39894)c_m=e^(i beta^3)2sqrt(2)W_corr. (11.404.3a)
```

Pure finite algebra then gives

```text
E_0=Z_39894-tauhat_39894,
A_tar=sum_(r=39695)^39893
 [sum_(m in A_r)(Z_m-c_m)-tauhat_r],

F_fold=E_emb+C_corr+E_0+A_tar.                      (11.404.4)
```

An independent exact-rational reconstruction verifies (11.404.2) and
(11.404.4) on every augmented and target slot.  The common half-domain
projection is

```text
Q_fold=2 Re[exp(-i*pi/8)F_fold].                    (11.404.5)
```

The `pi/8` in (11.404.5) is the exact odd-square half-Kummer reflection
phase; (11.404.2)--(11.404.4) introduce no new `pi` and no fitted constant.
Section 11.403 fixes the scale and negative sign of the projection of
`C_corr`, but it does not prove `E_emb=0`.  The completed selector theorem
retains the zero, negative, outer-positive, and endpoint half-current sectors
as one nonlocal object, while `tauhat_r` is an algebraic allocation rather
than a modewise half-Gamma identity.  Index counting cannot localize either
completion to (11.404.1).  The event-zero gate controls only exact-minus-
beta-minus-four transport and therefore does not bound `E_0`; neither
`A_tar` nor `E_emb` is currently bounded.  The next decisive obligation is
to derive (11.404.3) directly from the paired finite-Poisson current and the
completed one-cell selector identity, preserving every complement sector.

## 11.405 Selector increment in paired fold coordinates

Fix `B=5122423` and advance the lower odd selector from `C=159577` to
`C+2=159579`.  Translation by one source-lattice unit leaves every integer
Fourier character unchanged.  Thus, pointwise in `x` and after the same
half-domain integration,

```text
I_m^(C)-I_m^(C+2)=S_m,
K_m^(C)-K_m^(C+2)=Z_m,
Z_m=integral_0^(1/2)W_t(x)S_m(x)dx.                 (11.405.1)
```

Including the endpoint half-current `Z_H`, the completed symmetric Poisson
identity becomes the exact selector cocycle

```text
P_C=Q_half^(C)-Q_half^(C+2)
   =Z_H+lim_sym sum_m Z_m,                           (11.405.2)
```

where `P_C` is the one removed source term in the same half-domain
normalization.  The endpoint, zero, negative, and outer-positive sectors
remain attached in (11.405.2).

For the fold-owned target state put

```text
F_C=sum_(r=39695)^39894
 [K_r^(C)+K_-r^(C)-tauhat_r].                       (11.405.3)
```

The fixed target carrier cancels in the selector difference, giving

```text
D_fold=F_C-F_(C+2)
      =sum_(r=39695)^39894(Z_r+Z_-r).               (11.405.4)
```

Consequently the one-cell strip is naturally an increment of the paired
residual, not a summand of one fixed selector state.  If

```text
Z_R=sum_(m=39696)^40094 Z_m,
```

then cancellation of the common positive modes `39696..39894` proves

```text
E_raw=D_fold-Z_R
 =Z_39695+sum_(r=39695)^39894 Z_-r
  -sum_(m=39895)^40094 Z_m.                         (11.405.5)
```

Thus the exact Fourier-sector mismatch is one lower edge, all 200 negative
target modes, and 200 outer-positive modes.  The event allocation of Section
11.404 is valid branch bookkeeping, but is not this Fourier-sector
embedding.

The raw mismatch also has the cancellation-safe completed form

```text
C_out=P_C-D_fold,       R_raw=P_C-Z_R,
D_fold-Z_R=R_raw-C_out=E_raw.                        (11.405.6)
```

An independent checker reconstructs (11.405.4)--(11.405.6) from a second
exact rational fixture and from the mode indicator functions.  No sign or
smallness is asserted for `E_raw`.

Crucially, the corrected selected term of Section 11.403 is

```text
C_corr^K=e^(i beta^3)2sqrt(2)W_corr,
W_corr=sum_m a_m(G_ex,m-G_opp,m),                    (11.405.7)
```

The common carrier `e^(i beta^3)` is mandatory in the paired Kummer
coordinate.  Since `exp(i*pi*(C^2-1)/8)=1`, its physical projection is the
signed quantity certified in Section 11.403.  It still carries the
nonconstant leading-defect weights `a_m`; the raw roster `Z_R` is unweighted.
Matching physical units does not identify them.  Thus
(11.405.6) is a selector-increment theorem, not the still-open insertion of
(11.405.7) into the fixed-state source-minus-target residual.  That insertion
must be derived with the opposite branch, target carrier, endpoint half,
zero, negative, and outer-positive sectors all retained.  The physical raw
increment is

```text
Delta Q_fold=2 Re[exp(-i*pi/8)D_fold].               (11.405.8)
```

Here `pi/8` is inherited from exact odd-square Kummer reflection; the
selector cocycle introduces no new `pi` and no fitted constant.

## 11.406 Weighted defect and raw-strip companion decomposition

Restore the common source carrier and put

```text
kappa_C=e^(i beta^3)2sqrt(2),       beta^3=pi*C^2/8,
Z_m=kappa_C G_ex,m.                                  (11.406.1)
```

With the existing convention `a_39894=0`, define on the augmented roster

```text

b_m=kappa_C[(1-a_m)G_ex,m+a_m G_opp,m].              (11.406.2)
```

Direct coefficient algebra gives `Z_m=c_m+b_m`.  Hence

```text
Z_R=C_corr+B_comp,
C_corr=kappa_C W_corr,
D_fold=C_corr+B_comp+E_raw,                           (11.406.3)
P_C=C_corr+B_comp+E_raw+C_out.                       (11.406.4)
```

The event-zero mode is retained exactly: `c_39894=0` and
`b_39894=Z_39894`.  Equation (11.406.4) is the completed one-cell source
identity; it keeps the lower edge, negative target modes, outer-positive
modes, and completed outside sector attached.

Under the paired physical projection,

```text
Delta Q_fold=R_corr+R_joint,
R_corr=2Re[e^(-i*pi/8)C_corr]=4sqrt(2)Re W_corr,
R_joint=2Re[e^(-i*pi/8)(B_comp+E_raw)].              (11.406.5)
```

The second equality uses `exp(i*pi*(C^2-1)/8)=1`.  Section 11.403 therefore
proves `R_corr<-1.263e-4`, but no sign for `Delta Q_fold` follows until the
single cancellation-preserving estimate `R_joint<1.263e-4` is proved.
Separate triangle bounds on `B_comp` and `E_raw` are not licensed because
they are complementary pieces of the same completed selector current.

There is a sharper exact collapse.  Split `C_corr=C_inner+C_outer` at event
zero and set

```text
J_pair=Z_39695+Z_-39695
       +sum_(m=39696)^39894(b_m+Z_-m).               (11.406.6)
```

Then the outer raw modes cancel coefficientwise and

```text
B_comp+E_raw=J_pair-C_outer,
D_fold=C_inner+J_pair,
P_C=C_inner+J_pair+C_out.                            (11.406.7)
```

Thus `C_outer` cancels from the operative fold increment.  The signed bound
for `C_corr=C_inner+C_outer` does not determine the sign of `C_inner`.
The next exact numerical target is the inner/outer split of the grouped
corrected-defect theorem, followed by one paired estimate for `J_pair`.

## 11.408 Two-packet positive barrier for the selector increment

The common-profile coefficient convention is

```text
G_ex,39895+n=integral_0^1 g_ex(s)exp(-2*pi*i*n*s)ds.
```

Consequently the two raw packets in (11.405.4) are not a small local
companion.  Their exact frequency sets are

```text
P_low={-200,...,-1},
P_remote={-79789,...,-79590},

                    +sum_(n in P_remote)G_ex,39895+n].             (11.408.1)
```

Here `kappa_C=exp(i*beta^3)2sqrt(2)`.  Since `C=159577` is odd and
`exp(i*pi*(C^2-1)/8)=1`, the physical selector increment is exactly

```text
Delta Q_fold=4sqrt(2) Re[sum_(n in P_low union P_remote)
                              G_ex,39895+n].                        (11.408.2)
```

This is also a provenance check for every occurrence of `pi` in the packet
calculation: `2*pi*n` is the Fourier phase on the unit interval,
`beta^3=t*=pi*C^2/8` is the fixed Hardy height, and `pi/8` is the inherited
half-Kummer reflection phase.  No geometric or fitted value of `pi` is
inserted.

For the beta-minus-four profile, a 65536-panel ball midpoint rule bounds the
low packet.  A 2048-cell interval atlas for `g`, `g_s`, and `g_ss` supplies
the midpoint remainder.  The remote packet is not sampled: two integrations
by parts reduce all 200 frequencies to endpoint values of `g` and `g_s`,
with an explicit `g_ss sum(2*pi*n)^(-2)` remainder.  Finally, the uniform
exact-minus-beta-minus-four profile bound is multiplied by the rigorous
single-packet Dirichlet `L1` majorant.  This gives, throughout the ordinary
top corridor,

```text

Re(remote exact packet) > -0.0251304103,
exact two-packet profile correction < 4.2172285e-6,
29.5304261718 < Delta Q_fold < 32.0633916103.          (11.408.3)
```

An independent 32768-panel replay preserves the lower barrier `20`.  In

## 11.414 Global extraction of the certified B trace window

The negative window in Section 11.413 must be embedded in the global
fixed-state residual before it can be used.  For `M>=39894`, let

Using `P_B,m=U_B,m-1_(q_B,m<0)P_bulk,m`, every
positive/negative mode pair after the exact target subtraction has the
finite algebraic allocation

```text
I_m+I_-m-tau_m P_bulk,m
 =[U_B,m+P_B,-m+ell_m sigma_m P_bulk,m]
  +[P_A,m+I_-m-P_B,-m
    +(1-ell_m)sigma_m P_bulk,m].                     (11.414.2)
```

This is an identity, not a triangle estimate.  Summing the first bracket
defines `Btr_M`, exactly the trace-current package evaluated in Sections
11.375 and 11.410--11.413.  The local target step and crossing jumps remain
joined.  Every nonlocal term `(1-ell_m)sigma_m P_bulk,m` is retained in the
second bracket.

The certified crossing geometry makes the omitted block completely
explicit on `W`: `sigma_m=+1` for `m<=620`, `sigma_m=-1` for
`623<=m<=39894`, and `sigma_m=0` for `m>=39895`; modes 621 and 622 are the
local crossing modes.  Thus, at a cutoff containing the target range, the
nonlocal bulk-step contribution still in the grouped complement is

```text
sum_(m=1)^620 P_bulk,m - sum_(m=623)^39894 P_bulk,m. (11.414.3)
```

Equation (11.414.3) is bookkeeping, not a separately convergent or small
quantity; it must remain in the common global prescription.

Let

```text
chi_W=1_[x_low,x_high],
xi=sqrt(H_B)(x-x_B),             W={|xi|<=70}.        (11.414.4)
```

At every finite symmetric cutoff,

```text
G_M=chi_W Btr_M+[G_M-chi_W Btr_M].                   (11.414.5)
```

Taking the symmetric Abel limit already justified for `G_M`, and the
certified limit of the B trace window, gives the exact global split

```text
R_end=E_Btr,win+R_group,
E_Btr,win<-1.3198e-4.                                (11.414.6)
```

Here `R_group` contains every omitted nonlocal bulk step from (11.414.2),
the A endpoint current, both B outside-window trace pieces, the
zero/negative/outer-positive completion, and the endpoint half-current.  It

```text
Delta_g(z)=g_B(z)-g_A(z)=O(z^(1/2));                 (11.414.7)
```

the corresponding bare endpoint factors do not separately have that


The stronger estimate `R_group<1.3198e-4` would give `R_end<0`.  These are
sufficient targets, not proved bounds for `R_group`.

## 11.417 Endpoint-safe crossing completion of the exterior B current

The derivative programme stated after (11.415.8) requires one further exact
recombination.  At a common finite cutoff and Abel regulator, put

```text
N_(M,epsilon)
 =sum_(m=1)^M w_(m,epsilon)(1-ell_m)sigma_m P_bulk,m,
Ctr_(M,epsilon)=Btr_(M,epsilon)+N_(M,epsilon).          (11.417.1)
```

Here `tau_m`, `ell_m`, and `sigma_m` are those of (11.414.1)--(11.414.2).
At every nonlocal crossing `q_B,m=0`, `U_B,m` jumps by `-P_bulk,m`, while
the corresponding summand of `N_(M,epsilon)` jumps by `+P_bulk,m` (with the
same Abel weight).  Thus `Btr_(M,epsilon)` alone is not classically
differentiable across the released exterior.  In particular, modes 620 and
623 lie in the fully-on left and right exterior supports, respectively; the
obstruction is present already at finite cutoff.

The jump cancellation is algebraically complete.  Since

```text
P_B,m=U_B,m-1_(q_B,m<0)P_bulk,m,
```

one has mode by mode

```text
U_B,m+P_B,-m+sigma_m P_bulk,m
 =P_B,m+P_B,-m+(1-tau_m)P_bulk,m.                      (11.417.2)
```

The right side is smooth for `x>0`.  Hence every finite
`Ctr_(M,epsilon)` is smooth through all B crossings.  With the cutoff from
Section 11.415 define

```text
R_B,comp(M,epsilon)=eta_delta E_W Ctr_(M,epsilon),
R_join,comp(M,epsilon)
 =G_(M,epsilon)-chi_W Btr_(M,epsilon)-R_B,comp(M,epsilon).
                                                               (11.417.3)
```

Then exactly

```text
G_(M,epsilon)=chi_W Btr_(M,epsilon)
               +R_B,comp(M,epsilon)+R_join,comp(M,epsilon),

R_join,comp=R_join-eta_delta E_W N_(M,epsilon).         (11.417.4)
```

Because `eta_delta=0` for `x<=delta`, this transfer changes nothing at the
Abel corner.  The `Delta_g` endpoint cancellation, zero and negative modes,
outer completion, and endpoint half-current remain under the inherited common
prescription.  Because `E_W=0` on the certified window, the bound
`E_Btr,win<-1.3198e-4` is also unchanged.  The released current is now
crossing-complete before any derivative or absolute value is taken.

## 11.418 Exact derivative transport for the completed B current

The crossing-completed coefficient admits a closed derivative system.  After
odd-endpoint parity and extraction of the common B phase, put, for
`s in {+1,-1}`,

```text
a=m sqrt(2/x),                    b=B sqrt(x/2),
a_s=s a,                          q_s=b-s a,
rho=1/(i*pi),

Y_+^tau=e^(-i*pi*q_+^2/2)[P_B,++(1-tau_m)P_bulk,+],
Y_-    =e^(-i*pi*q_-^2/2)P_B,-.                         (11.418.1)
```

Let

```text
K_s=1/(2x)+i*pi*q_s q_s'.                               (11.418.2)
```

The Fresnel identity `F'(q)=exp(i*pi*q^2/2)` gives exactly

```text
Y_s'=a_s q_s'+(rho-Y_s)K_s,                             (11.418.3)

q_s' =(b+s a)/(2x),
q_s''=(-b-3s a)/(4x^2),
K_s' =-1/(2x^2)+i*pi[(q_s')^2+q_s q_s''].               (11.418.4)
```

The added non-target completion is the homogeneous solution

```text
V_+=(1-tau_m)a(1+i)e^(-i*pi*q_+^2/2),
V_+'=-K_+V_+.                                           (11.418.5)
```

It therefore changes the value of `Y_+` but not the form of (11.418.3).
Differentiating once more gives

```text
Y_s''=a_s(q_s''-q_s'/(2x))-Y_s'K_s+(rho-Y_s)K_s'.       (11.418.6)
```

For the complete phase-stripped pair

```text
C_m=(Y_+^tau+Y_-)/x,

C_m'=(Y_+'+Y_-')/x-(Y_++Y_-)/x^2,

C_m''=(Y_+''+Y_-'')/x-2(Y_+'+Y_-')/x^2
       +2(Y_++Y_-)/x^3.                                 (11.418.7)
```

The remaining Kummer amplitude `w=[x(1-x)]^(-1/4)` satisfies

```text
w'/w =(2x-1)/[4x(1-x)],
w''/w=(12x^2-12x+5)/[16x^2(1-x)^2].                    (11.418.8)
```

Equations (11.418.3)--(11.418.8) give exact first and second derivatives of
the finite common-regulator sum before norms.  In the normalized coordinate,
`partial_xi=H_B^(-1/2)partial_x` and
`partial_xixi=H_B^(-1)partial_xx`.  No numerical differentiation of a
Fresnel difference and no distributional crossing term is needed.

## 11.426 Hyperbolic flat-face projector kernel

In the exact bi-Morse coordinates, replace the curved face temporarily by

```text
Phi(P,S)=(P^2-S^2)/2,       P<a+rho S,
c=rho^2-1.                                             (11.426.1)
```

For `c!=0`, positive Gaussian damping followed by its Abel boundary value
gives the normalized profile

```text
F_c'(a)=exp(i sgn(c)pi/4)exp[-i a^2/(2c)]
        /sqrt(2pi|c|),
F_c(a)=1/2+integral_0^a F_c'(r)dr.                    (11.426.2)
```

The full-plane Gaussian fixes `F_c(-infinity)=0` and
`F_c(+infinity)=1`.  As `c` tends to zero, (11.426.2) tends
distributionally to the sharp projector step.  Thus a noncharacteristic
straight face is exactly a Fresnel smoothing; at a null face, curvature is
the next nonvanishing datum.

The earlier B tangent profile is the same kernel under

```text
P=sqrt(pi)q,       S=sqrt(2)y,
a=sqrt(pi)q_B*,    rho=kappa_B sqrt(pi/2),
c=-Delta_B.                                            (11.426.3)
```

Its complementary scalar profile is exactly the certified `U_0`; the
affine `q`-density current `U_1` is a separate mandatory amplitude term.  A
near-zero B slope at mode `257` is not a fold: its face lies more than
`1.8e6` canonical widths from the saddle.  A joint fold requires both

```text
a=0 and c=0
 iff alpha_m=D and m=D/4
 iff t=pi D^2/8.                                       (11.426.4)
```

At the A occupancy edge, the scaled detunings for modes `39852` and `39853`
have absolute value below `0.08`; at `39894|39895`, `c` changes sign.  Hence
the A face and half-boundary corner realize the near codimension-two geometry
that must retain curved-face terms and match the fold atlas.

## 11.427 Hyperbolic wedge and half-boundary corner kernel

The half-domain is not represented by the flat-face profile alone.  It adds
the coupled boundary `S>h`, giving the canonical Abel wedge

```text
C_rho(a,h)=(2pi)^(-1) Abel-integral_(S>h) exp(-iS^2/2)

c=rho^2-1.                                             (11.427.1)
```

```text

 =exp[-ia^2/(2c)]/[2sqrt(pi|c|)]

T_eps(u)=integral_u^infinity exp(i eps pi v^2/2)dv,

partial_h C_rho(a,h)
 =-exp(-ih^2/2)/(2pi)
   integral_(-infinity)^(a+rho h)exp(iP^2/2)dP,

partial_a partial_h C_rho
 =-exp(i[(a+rho h)^2-h^2]/2)/(2pi).                  (11.427.3)
```

The limiting identities

```text
lim_(h to -infinity) C_rho(a,h)=F_(rho^2-1)(a),
lim_(h to +infinity) C_rho(a,h)=0                   (11.427.4)
```

show that Section 11.426 is the remote-half-boundary limit of this same
kernel.  In the exact logistic Morse coordinate,

```text
h=sqrt(t/2)s(v_H),       v_H=2pi m^2/t,
s(v)=sgn(v-1)sqrt(2[v-1-log v]).                     (11.427.5)
```

## 11.428 Exact affine-wedge remainder identity

Including both bi-Morse Jacobians, the endpoint-`D` triangle has the exact
form

```text
eps_D exp(i Phi_D,m) W0_D,m (2pi)^(-1)
 int_(S>h) int_(P<P_D(S)) A_D,m(P,S)
 exp(i(P^2-S^2)/2)dP dS,                              (11.428.1)

W0_D,m=4(pi Dm-i)r^(3/4)/(D sqrt(pi t)),
r=t/(2pi m^2).                                        (11.428.2)
```

The normalized transformed amplitude separates globally:

```text
A_D,m(P,S)=E_D,m(u(P))O(v(S)),
E_D,m(u)=2u(pi Dm u-i)/[(u+1)(pi Dm-i)],
O(v)=v^(3/4)s/(v-1).                                  (11.428.3)
```

Both factors equal one at the joint saddle.  Retain the complete affine
tangent

```text
A_aff(P,S)=1+lambda_P P+mu_S S,
lambda_P=(3pi Dm-i)/[2(pi Dm-i)sqrt(pi mD)],
mu_S=(5/12)sqrt(2/t).                                 (11.428.4)
```

This keeps both the mandatory endpoint-density current and the first outer
logistic correction.  Its canonical wedge moment is still exact:

```text
C_aff=C+i mu_S partial_h C
        -i(lambda_P+mu_S rho)partial_a C.             (11.428.5)
```

With `P_lin(S)=a+rho S`, the exact defect splits before norms as

```text
R_exact-aff=R_amp+R_face,                              (11.428.6)

R_amp=(2pi)^(-1) int_(S>h) int_(P<P_D(S))
      [A_D,m(P,S)-A_aff(P,S)]exp(i(P^2-S^2)/2)dP dS,

R_face=(2pi)^(-1) int_(S>h) int_(P_lin(S))^(P_D(S))
       A_aff(P,S)exp(i(P^2-S^2)/2)dP dS.              (11.428.7)
```

The inner face integral is oriented, so crossing of the curved face and its
tangent introduces no sign ambiguity.  The phase remainder is identically
zero.  At the six saved-height transition modes, interval arithmetic gives

```text
|P_D''(0)|<7e-6,       Re(lambda_P)<2e-5,
|Im(lambda_P)|<1e-14,  mu_S<6e-6.                    (11.428.8)
```

## 11.429 Null-coordinate unfolding of the A wedge

The parameter `c=rho^2-1` is a poor coordinate at the A null face.  Put

```text
R=P+S,       delta=1+rho.                              (11.429.1)
```

Then

```text
(P^2-S^2)/2=R^2/2-RS,
P<a+rho S  iff  R<a+delta S,
r0=a+delta h.                                         (11.429.2)
```

Swapping the half-plane integrations and evaluating the `S` integral gives,
for `delta<0`,

```text
C=(2pi i)^(-1) int_(-infinity)^r0 exp(iR^2/2)
 [exp(-iRh)-exp(-iR(R-a)/delta)]dR/R.                 (11.429.3)
```

The numerator is removable at `R=0`.  For `delta>0`, the common Abel value is

```text
C=1/2+(2pi i)^(-1)PV{
 int_(-infinity)^r0 exp(iR^2/2-iRh)dR/R
 +int_r0^infinity exp(iR^2/2-iR(R-a)/delta)dR/R}.     (11.429.4)
```

At `delta=0`, this becomes

```text
C=H(a)/2+(2pi i)^(-1)PV
 int_(-infinity)^a exp(iR^2/2-iRh)dR/R.               (11.429.5)
```

Thus the half-jump remains explicit and no factor `1/sqrt(|c|)` is used.
The continuous half-boundary mode and dynamic null endpoint are

```text
nu=sqrt(t/(2pi)),       D_t=4nu=sqrt(8t/pi).           (11.429.6)
```

The exact codimension-two unfolding for endpoint `D` is

```text
eta_D=sqrt(pi)(D-D_t)/2
     =4(pi D^2/8-t)/[sqrt(pi)(D+D_t)].                 (11.429.7)
```

For the saved `A`, `eta_A` lies in `(0.07784,0.07785)`.  Modes `39894` and
`39895` straddle `delta=0`, but their tangent `r0` values differ from this
same `eta_A` by less than `1e-10` and `1e-9`, respectively.  At the continuous
null point, `rho=-1`, `P_A''(0)=-2/(3sqrt(pi)A)`, and the face phase has
cubic coefficient `1/(3A sqrt(pi))`.  The Airy cubic is therefore forced by
the exact paired-triangle geometry.

## 11.431 Exact A carrier and paired-projector orientation

The stationary phase of the endpoint-`D` triangle is

```text
Phi_D,m=pi*m*D-pi*m^2-t/2+(t/2)log[t/(2pi*m^2)].     (11.431.1)
```

For an odd endpoint `D=2d+1`, the integer
`m(D-m)=2md+m(1-m)` is even.  Hence both odd endpoints reduce to the same
classical carrier,

```text
exp(i Phi_D,m)
 =exp(i{t[log(t/(2pi))-1]/2-t log m}),

exp(-i*pi/8)exp(i Phi_D,m)
 =exp(i[theta_0-t log m]),
theta_0=t[log(t/(2pi))-1]/2-pi/8.                    (11.431.2)
```

The affine A endpoint and its equation-(9) projection are therefore

```text
K_A,m^aff=-exp(i Phi_A,m)W0_A,m C_aff,A,m,
q_A,m^aff=2(pi/(32t))^(1/4)
 Re[exp(-i*pi/8)K_A,m^aff].                          (11.431.3)
```

The sign in (11.431.3) is the geometric endpoint orientation
`epsilon_A=-1`.  It is not created by the target projector.  Indeed,

```text
I_m+I_-m-chi_T(m)P_m
 =(1-chi_T(m))P_m+P_-m+Q_m+Q_-m.                    (11.431.4)
```

Thus the paired endpoint coefficient remains `+1` across `39894|39895`;
only the positive full-line bulk coefficient changes from zero to one.
Restoring the common carrier gives

```text
q_A,39894^aff=-0.0058473814010481522425...,
q_A,39895^aff=-0.0018925895733072011429...,

sum q_A,m^aff=-0.0077399709743553533855...,
sum(q_A,m^aff-q_A,m^scalar)=-6.3099857276746194e-6. (11.431.5)
```

The two tangent corners reinforce, but their sum is a carrier component,
not an error estimate.  It must remain grouped with the rest of the A
roster, the full-line projector jump, and both exact remainders.

Let `chi_E` and `chi_T` be the exact and tangent A-domain indicators, and

tangent exterior.  The cancellation-safe affine decomposition is instead

```text
Phi_A,face(x)=pi A^2 x/4+(t/2)log((1-x)/x).           (11.434.5)
```

Its unique half-domain stationary point is

```text
x_*=(1-kappa)/2=0.49947538036472974128....            (11.434.6)
```

At `y_0=0.0037`, this genuine exact-face saddle lies in the exterior for

## 11.436 Exterior affine/amplitude nonseparability at x=0

The affine/exact-minus-affine identity of Section 11.428 is exact at every
common finite exterior cutoff.  Its two terms do not possess separate
improper limits at `x=0`.

Let `H_aff(P_A,S)` be the inner `P` integral of
`1+lambda_P P+mu_S S`.  The lower Fresnel expansion and exact face limits
give

```text
exp(-iP_A^2/2)H_aff(P_A,S) -> i(mu_S-lambda_P),       (11.436.1)
sqrt(x)P_A -> -m sqrt(2pi),
sqrt(x)S   ->  m sqrt(2pi),
x^(3/2)S_x-> -m sqrt(pi/2).                           (11.436.2)
```

For all modes `39853..39936`, interval arithmetic proves

```text
4.7084937318005548e-6
 < Re(lambda_P-mu_S)
 <4.7195271486251214e-6,
|Im(lambda_P)|<3.6e-16.                               (11.436.3)
```

Consequently each affine exterior current has the common-phase asymptotic

```text
J_A,m^aff(x)=L_m x^(-3/2)exp(i Phi_A,face(x))+O(x^-1),
Phi_A,face(x)=pi A^2 x/4+(t/2)log((1-x)/x).           (11.436.4)
```

Required all-mode grouping does not cancel the leading coefficient:

```text
Re sum_m L_m=+2.22817223099254296e-10,
Im sum_m L_m=-8.91263383468451327182...,
|sum_m L_m| = 8.91263383468451327183....              (11.436.5)
```

Since `exp(i Phi_A,face(x))=x^(-it/2)(1+O(x))`, the cutoff
primitive has a nonzero `epsilon^(-1/2-it/2)` leading term.  The standalone
affine exterior therefore has no improper limit.  The exterior
exact-minus-affine amplitude has the opposite leading term and likewise has
no standalone limit.

The full endpoint factor restores convergence.  With `K=pi A m`,

```text
E(P)=-2iK/(K-i)P^(-2)+O(P^-4),
exp(-iP^2/2) integral_(-infinity)^P E(q)exp(iq^2/2)dq
 =-2K/(K-i)P^(-3)+O(P^-5).                           (11.436.6)
```

Together with
`x^(1/4)O(v(x))->sqrt(2)r^(-1/4)`, this makes the full exact current
`O(x^-1/4)`, hence absolutely integrable at zero.  The admissible exterior
object is therefore

```text
C_A,ext^exact=lim_(epsilon->0)
 [C_A,ext^aff(epsilon)+R_A,ext^amp(epsilon)],         (11.436.7)
```

with one common cutoff, or equivalently the full exact endpoint factor
integrated directly.  The affine/amplitude split remains valid on the
compact local box used in Section 11.435.

Pi provenance: every `pi` in (11.436.1)--(11.436.7) comes from the exact
equation-(9) bi-Morse map, the original triangle face, and the endpoint
normalization.  No fitted constant is introduced.

## 11.437 Full exact A-exterior common-phase reduction

Return to the original exact triangle before splitting its endpoint
amplitude.  Put

```text
F_m(z)=pi m^2/z+pi A^2 z/4,
h_A(z)=z^(-1/2)(2+i pi A^2 z),
H_m(x)=integral_0^x h_A(z)exp(iF_m(z))dz.             (11.437.1)
```

For

```text
alpha=exp(-i pi/4)sqrt(pi)A/2,
beta =exp(-i pi/4)sqrt(pi)m,
X=sqrt(x),   w_+/-=beta/X +/- alpha X,               (11.437.2)
```

differentiating the exact inverse-Gaussian erfc primitive gives

```text
H_m(x)=4sqrt(x)exp(iF_m(x))
 -2sqrt(pi)beta(-1)^(mA)[erfc(w_-)+erfc(w_+)].        (11.437.3)
```

The phase-stripped tail `B_m=exp(-iF_m)H_m` satisfies the exact ODE

```text
B_m'+iF_m'B_m=h_A.                                   (11.437.4)
```

No exterior cutoff reaches the endpoint saddle.  Therefore

```text
b_0=h_A/(iF_m'),
b_(j+1)=-b_j'/(iF_m')                                (11.437.5)
```

is an exact finite integration-by-parts hierarchy with one explicit
oscillatory remainder.  At all 84 cutoff points the maximum successive term
moduli are

```text

0.0112281897550515...,
4.93533309645e-7,
3.61552323726e-11.                                   (11.437.6)
```

The endpoint phase cancels the mode-dependent outer phase exactly.  Thus the
full convergent exterior is reduced to

```text
C_A,ext^exact=-1/(2pi i) sum_(m=39853)^39936
 integral_0^(x0_m) x^(-7/4)(1-x)^(-1/4)B_m(x)
 exp(i Phi_A(x))dx,                                  (11.437.7)

Phi_A(x)=pi A^2 x/4+(t/2)log((1-x)/x),
x0_m={1+[t/(2pi m^2)](1+0.0037)}^(-1).               (11.437.8)
```

The unique stationary point remains
`x_*=0.4994753803647297412765...`.  In the exact signed Morse coordinate

```text
w0_m=sgn(x0_m-x_*)
 sqrt(2[Phi_A(x0_m)-Phi_A(x_*)]),                    (11.437.9)
```

the endpoint roster runs from `-10.5508889686027...` to
`1.09533403228579...`; `w0_m>0` exactly for modes `39927..39936`.

A nonrigorous 180-node-per-mode pilot, using three endpoint terms and five

```text
-0.00240161895424093,
-0.00240156220182666,
-0.00240153356655061,
-0.00240153381358943.                                (11.437.10)
```

Equation (11.437.10) is route-selection telemetry only.  It is not an

## 11.439 Rational common-phase contour value

Use the logistic coordinate

```text
q=log((1-x)/x),   x=(1+exp(q))^(-1).                 (11.439.1)
```

After the four-term replacement of Section 11.438, (11.437.7) becomes

```text
I_4=sum_m integral_(q0_m)^infinity
 G_m(q)exp(i[Phi(q)-Phi_*])dq,

G_m(q)=-exp(3q/4)(b_0+b_1+b_2+b_3)/(2pi i).         (11.439.2)
```

The factor `exp(3q/4)` is exactly the transformed Jacobian-weight product,
because
`x^(-7/4)(1-x)^(-1/4)x(1-x)=exp(3q/4)`.  In particular, the
leading rational endpoint term makes `G_m(q)=O(exp(-3q/4))`.

Take the exact rational splice and contour height

```text
q_L=0.0083,   eta=0.001.                             (11.439.3)
```

The largest mode cutoff is below `q_L`.  Every endpoint pole

```text
q_p,m=log((A-2m)/(2m))
```

lies at least `0.003692070973...` to the left of its cutoff, and the first
logistic singularity has imaginary part `pi`.  Hence the rectangle
`Re q>=q_L`, `0<=Im q<=eta` is analytic for all 84 modes.

The compact part is split at every exact cutoff, so the active roster is
constant on each band and is summed before integration.  On a panel of half
width `h`, an order-`N` Arb Taylor polynomial is integrated exactly.  If `M`
bounds the integrand on the complex disk of radius `R=2h`, Cauchy's estimate
gives the omitted-panel error

```text
E_panel<=2Mh (h/R)^N/[(N+1)(1-h/R)].                 (11.439.4)
```

The implementation fails closed unless the python-flint series cap equals
the advertised order.  With 376 order-36 compact panels and 100 vertical
panels, the total compact Cauchy allowance is
`5.301902692153e-11` in the relative canonical coordinate.

For the far interval, contour closure gives

```text
integral_(q_L)^infinity f(q)dq
 =i integral_0^eta f(q_L+iy)dy
  +integral_(q_L)^infinity f(s+i eta)ds.             (11.439.5)
```

Writing `R=exp(s)`, monotonicity of
`R/(1+2R cos(eta)+R^2)` proves on the horizontal ray

```text
Im(Phi(s+i eta)-Phi_*)>=80.1904463374521...,
integral_(q_L)^infinity |f(s+i eta)|ds
 <=1.370521721782e-31.                               (11.439.6)
```

The rational amplitude majorant in (11.439.6) retains all powers from
`b_0,...,b_3` and all 84 endpoint denominators.  It uses no sampled decay.

Restoring the common carrier, paper rotation, and equation-(9) normalization
then yields

```text
 =-0.0024015340184814209578429561 +/- 3.38e-13,

full exact A exterior
 =-0.0024015340184814209578429561 +/- 3.40e-13.       (11.439.7)
```

## 11.440 Compact exact-minus-affine A amplitude

On the compact exact A domain, the transformed amplitude still factors as

```text
A_exact(P,S)=E(P)O(S),
E=2u(pi A m u-i)/[(u+1)(pi A m-i)],
O=v^(3/4)sigma/(v-1).                                (11.440.1)
```

For `x=1/[1+r_m(1+y)]` and the exact face `P_A(y)`, put

```text
C_E=2sqrt(2)i(pi A m-i)/(sqrt(pi)A).
```

The exact identities

```text
C_E E(P_A)dP_A/dx=x^(-1/2)(2+i pi A^2x),
P_A^2/2=pi m^2/x+pi A^2x/4-pi A m                 (11.440.2)
```

and oddness of `A=159577` turn the inverse-Gaussian primitive of Section
11.437 into the exact lower endpoint current

```text
I_E(P_A)=integral_(-infinity)^P_A E(P)exp(iP^2/2)dP
        =(-1)^m H_m(x)/C_E.                           (11.440.3)
```

Hence the two-dimensional nonlinear defect reduces without approximation to

```text
R_A,m^amp=(2pi)^(-1) integral_(y_half)^0.0037
 exp(-iS(y)^2/2)[O(S(y))I_E(P_A(y))
                 -I_aff(P_A(y),S(y))]S'(y)dy.         (11.440.4)
```

Direct interval evaluation of the raw `erfc` formula on complex disks is
poorly conditioned near its Stokes cancellation.  The rigorous callback
therefore evaluates each current at the disk centre and encloses its
variation by the disk radius times the supremum of its exact elementary ODE
derivative.  This changes only the enclosure, not the analytic function.

Restoring the endpoint orientation, common carrier, paper rotation, and
equation-(9) normalization, deterministic summation gives

```text
target-side compact nonlinear=+2.5696412105123670e-9

outer-side compact nonlinear =+8.492655050997492e-9

sum of modewise moduli       = 1.1426783870400915e-8
                               +/- 2.19e-14.          (11.440.5)
```

## 11.442 Global `R_Dir` ownership after the A extraction

Write `Q_m=A_m+B_m` for the two endpoint atoms and retain `P_m` for the
full-line bulk atom.  At every common finite cutoff `M>=39936`, the exact
positive/negative pair identity is

```text
I_m+I_-m-chi_T(m)P_m
 =(1-chi_T(m))P_m+P_-m+A_m+A_-m+B_m+B_-m.          (11.442.1)
```

The positive labels partition without overlap into

```text
1..621, 622..39852, 39853..39894,
39895..39936, 39937..M,

621+39231+42+42+(M-39936)=M.                       (11.442.2)
```

The certified A object removes `A_m+A_-m` on all 84 modes
`39853..39936` and removes the positive full-line atom only when
`m=39895..39936`.  In particular, it removes no `P_-m` and no B endpoint
atom.  At finite regulator its coefficient transfer is therefore

```text
A_(M,epsilon)
 =sum_(m=39853)^39936 w_m
   [A_m+A_-m+(1-chi_T(m))P_m].                     (11.442.3)
```

The B trace window is already extracted from `R_Dir`; its only local bulk
steps occur at modes 621 and 622.  The analytic completed-B outer block
starts at mode 5122421.  Hence neither overlaps (11.442.3).  The finite
completed-B block is a representation of the common Dirichlet/Abel
residual, not a third numerical contribution; (11.442.3) reassigns its
positive bulk atoms `39895..39936` exactly.  Consequently

```text
R_KGamma=E_Btr,win+E_outer+A_transition+R_after_A,
```

## 11.443 Finite-regulator equivalence for `R_after_A`

Let `T={622,...,39894}`, `w_m=exp(-pi epsilon m^2)`, and use one common
finite regulator with

```text
M>=B=5122421,       epsilon>0.                         (11.443.1)
```

The stronger cutoff is required because the A deletion alone is present for
`M>=39936`, whereas the separately extracted analytic B exterior
`O_(M,epsilon)=eta_delta E_W Ctr_>=B,M,epsilon` is defined in the same finite
identity only for `M>=B`.  The common projector kernel is

```text
Delta_(M,epsilon)(x)
 =H_x+integral_0^L f_x(u)[D_(M,epsilon)-G_(T,epsilon)]du
   +sum_(m in T)w_m(A_m+B_m).                         (11.443.2)
```

Delete the certified A transition algebraically before any norm:

```text
mathcal A_(M,epsilon)
 =sum_(m=39853)^39936 w_m
   [A_m+A_-m+(1-chi_T(m))P_m],                       (11.443.3)

mathfrak R_A,(M,epsilon)
 =Delta_(M,epsilon)-chi_W Btr_(M,epsilon)
   -O_(M,epsilon)-mathcal A_(M,epsilon).              (11.443.4)
```

Expanding the Fourier kernel, using `I_m=P_m+A_m+B_m`, pairing `+m` and
`-m` with the even Abel weight, and then subtracting (11.443.3) gives the
equivalent mask

```text
mode range       post-A joined summand
1..621           P_m+P_-m+A_m+A_-m+B_m+B_-m
622..39852       P_-m+A_m+A_-m+B_m+B_-m
39853..39894     P_-m+B_m+B_-m
39895..39936     P_-m+B_m+B_-m
39937..M         P_m+P_-m+A_m+A_-m+B_m+B_-m.         (11.443.5)
```

Together with `H_x+I_0`, `-chi_W Btr`, and `-O`, (11.443.5) is exactly
(11.443.4).  The two A-window rows have the same surviving vector for
different reasons: the target projector had already removed `P_m` below the
target edge, while (11.443.3) removes it above that edge.  No `P_-m` or B
endpoint atom is deleted.

For the inherited physical functional

```text
mathcal P_t[F]=2(pi/(32t))^(1/4)
 Re[e^(-i*pi/8) integral_0^1 W_t(x)F(x)dx],           (11.443.6)
```

the remaining object is precisely

```text
R_after_A
 =lim_(epsilon down 0) lim_(M to infinity)
   mathcal P_t[mathfrak R_A,(M,epsilon)],             (11.443.7)

R_KGamma=E_Btr,win+E_outer+A_transition+R_after_A.    (11.443.8)
```

The symmetric cutoff limit is taken first at fixed positive `epsilon`; the

## 11.444 Two-edge modular transform of the target notch

After the `M->infinity` passage at fixed `epsilon>0` licensed by Section
11.443, put

```text
T={622,...,39894},       c=621.5,       d=39894.5,
q_epsilon(y)=exp(-pi epsilon y^2),
h_epsilon(y)=q_epsilon(y)[1_(y<c)+1_(y>d)].           (11.444.1)
```

The half-integer edges make the integer samples of `h_epsilon` exactly the
target complement.  Poisson summation for this integrable bounded-variation
function gives, in the inherited symmetric prescription,

```text
C_epsilon(u)
 =sum_(m in Z)[1-chi_T(m)]q_epsilon(m)e^(-2pi i m u)
 =sum_(k in Z)hat h_epsilon(k+u),                     (11.444.2)

hat h_epsilon(xi)
 =e^(-pi xi^2/epsilon)/(2sqrt(epsilon))
  {erfc[-sqrt(pi epsilon)c-i sqrt(pi/epsilon)xi]
   +erfc[ sqrt(pi epsilon)d+i sqrt(pi/epsilon)xi]}.   (11.444.3)
```

For `j=0,1`, define

```text
b_j(xi)
 =[q_epsilon^(j)(d)e^(-2pi i xi d)
   -q_epsilon^(j)(c)e^(-2pi i xi c)]
   /(2pi i xi)^(j+1),                                (11.444.4)

E_j(u)=q_epsilon^(j)(d)e^(-2pi i u d)
       -q_epsilon^(j)(c)e^(-2pi i u c).
```

Because both edge phases at integer `k` equal `(-1)^k`, the standard
Mittag-Leffler sums yield

```text
sum_k b_0(k+u)= E_0(u)/(2i sin(pi u)),
sum_k b_1(k+u)=-E_1(u)cos(pi u)/(4sin(pi u)^2).       (11.444.5)
```

Three integrations by parts on the two exterior intervals, before taking an
absolute value, give for `rho_2=hat h-b_0-b_1`

```text
|rho_2(xi)|
 <=[|q_epsilon''(c)|+|q_epsilon''(d)|+20pi epsilon]
    /(2pi|xi|)^3,                                    (11.444.6)

integral_R |q_epsilon'''(y)|dy<=20pi epsilon.         (11.444.7)
```

Thus, away from integer `u`,

```text
C_epsilon(u)
 =E_0(u)/(2i sin(pi u))
  -E_1(u)cos(pi u)/(4sin(pi u)^2)
  +sum_(k in Z)rho_2(k+u),                           (11.444.8)
```

with continuous extension of the complete expression at the integer lattice.
The closed pieces are not separately stable there, so the licensed evaluator
uses the direct Gaussian sum near integers and (11.444.8) away from them.
For `|k|<=64`, `0.1<=u<=0.9`, and `epsilon=10^-10`, the certified omitted
dual tail is below `7e-15`.  A separate floating pilot checks nine direct/dual
rows down to that regulator: the largest direct cutoff is `328014`, the dual
cutoff remains `64`, and the largest discrepancy is below `4.19e-11`.  Those
samples select the route and are not used to prove (11.444.1)--(11.444.8).

## 11.445 Pole-free centred-cell recombination and one-cell fold

Retain `hat h_epsilon`, `E_0`, `E_1`, and `rho_2` from Section 11.444.  For

```text
g_0(s)=[csc(pi s)-1/(pi s)]/(2i),

```

Both apparent singularities are removable.  With `z=pi s`,

```text
g_0(s)=(1/(2i))[z/6+7z^3/360+31z^5/15120+...],

g_0(0)=0,                 g_1(0)=1/24.                (11.445.2)
```

The `k=0` identity

```text
rho_2(s)=hat h_epsilon(s)-b_0(s)-b_1(s)
```

must be recombined with the two closed boundary currents before evaluation.
It gives the single pole-free formula

```text
C_epsilon(s)
 =hat h_epsilon(s)+E_0(s)g_0(s)+E_1(s)g_1(s)
  +sum_(k in Z, k!=0)rho_2(k+s),       |s|<=1/2,      (11.445.3)

C_epsilon(0)
 =hat h_epsilon(0)+E_1(0)/24+sum_(k!=0)rho_2(k).      (11.445.4)
```

Thus no direct high-cutoff switch is required at the integer lattice.  If

```text
K3=|q_epsilon''(c)|+|q_epsilon''(d)|+20pi epsilon,
```

then the cubic estimate in Section 11.444 and `|k+s|>=|k|-1/2` imply,
uniformly on the closed centred cell,

```text
sum_(|k|>K)|rho_2(k+s)|
 <=K3/[(2pi)^3(K-1/2)^2].                            (11.445.5)
```

For `K=64`, the certified right sides are below `6.549e-11`, `6.888e-13`,
and `6.910e-15` at `epsilon=10^-6`, `10^-8`, and `10^-10`, respectively.

Now let

```text
A=159577,       B=5122421,       L=(B-A)/2=2481422,

Theta_L(x,s)
 =sum_(n=0)^(L-1)e^[i*pi*x*(A+2n+2s)^2/4],

F_x(s)
 =sum_(n=0)^(L-1)(A+2n+2s)e^[i*pi*x*(A+2n+2s)^2/4]
 =(i*pi*x)^(-1)partial_s Theta_L(x,s),       x>0.     (11.445.6)
```

The direct finite sum defines `F_x` continuously at `x=0`.  Since
`C_epsilon` is one-periodic, partitioning `[0,L]` into its `L` unit cells and

```text
integral_0^L f_x(u)C_epsilon(u)du
 =integral_0^1 F_x(s)C_epsilon(s)ds.                  (11.445.7)
```

For evaluation on the right side, use the centred representative `r=s` for
`0<=s<=1/2` and `r=s-1` for `1/2<s<=1`.  The finite roster shifts from

```text
Theta_L(x,1)-Theta_L(x,0)
 =e^(i*pi*x*B^2/4)-e^(i*pi*x*A^2/4).                 (11.445.8)
```

## 11.446 Periodic two-jet extraction of the folded current

Write `e_D(x)=exp(i*pi*x*D^2/4)` for `D` in `{A,B}` and put

```text
D_x=e_B(x)-e_A(x),
E_x=D_x/(i*pi*x),               E_0=(B^2-A^2)/4,
K_x=B e_B(x)-A e_A(x),         K_0=B-A=2L.             (11.446.1)
```

The endpoint quotient is entire at zero and has the stable form

```text
E_x=((B^2-A^2)/4)e^[i*pi*x*(A^2+B^2)/8]
    sinc[pi*x*(B^2-A^2)/8],                            (11.446.2)
```

where `sinc(z)=sin(z)/z`.  For `x>0`, define

```text
Psi_x(s)
 =[Theta_L(x,s)-Theta_L(x,0)-s D_x]/(i*pi*x),

Phi_x(s)=Psi_x(s)-(K_x/2)(s^2-s).                     (11.446.3)
```

The exact finite-roster sums give the extensions

```text
Psi_0(s)=L(s^2-s),                Phi_0(s)=0.           (11.446.4)
```

The value and first-derivative jumps have both been removed:

```text
Phi_x(0)=Phi_x(1)=0,
partial_s Phi_x(0)=partial_s Phi_x(1).                 (11.446.5)
```

For `T={622,...,39894}`, let

```text
H_T(epsilon)=sum_(m in T)e^(-pi*epsilon*m^2)/m.
```

At every finite cutoff `M>=39894`, the symmetric Fourier pairs cancel and
the positive target notch is the only survivor in the quadratic bridge:

```text
integral_0^1 (s^2-s)C_(M,epsilon)'(s)ds
 =i H_T(epsilon)/pi.                                   (11.446.6)
```

Since `integral_0^1 C_(M,epsilon)=1`, integration by parts using
(11.446.5) gives the exact joined identity

```text
integral_0^1 F_x(s)C_(M,epsilon)(s)ds
 =E_x-i K_x H_T(epsilon)/(2pi)
  -integral_0^1 Phi_x(s)C_(M,epsilon)'(s)ds.           (11.446.7)
```

Certified summation gives

```text
H_T(0)=4.16185772996900304025207600348705...,
H_T(0)/pi=1.32476046033956276831194354001237....       (11.446.8)
```

For `hat Phi_x(m)=integral_0^1 Phi_x(s)e^(-2*pi*i*m*s)ds`, three
integrations by parts yield

```text
|hat Phi_x(m)|<=K_Phi(x)/(2*pi*|m|)^3,
K_Phi(x)=|Delta Phi_x''|+integral_0^1|Phi_x'''(s)|ds,

sum_(|m|>K)2*pi*|m|*|hat Phi_x(m)|
 <=K_Phi(x)/(2*pi^2*K).                                (11.446.9)
```

Thus the differentiated leakage is absolutely convergent after the two
endpoint jets are removed, including at zero Abel regulator.  The raw
derivative majorant proves convergence only and is not asserted to meet the

## 11.447 Two-jet reassembly of the common projector kernel

For every nonzero integer `m`, (11.446.3)--(11.446.5) give

```text
I_m=2*pi*i*m*hat Phi_x(m)+i K_x/(2*pi*m),
I_0=E_x.                                                (11.447.1)
```

The second term in (11.447.1) contributes
`-i K_x H_T(epsilon)/(2pi)` to the notched source.  On each positive target
mode, however, the exact endpoint atoms obey

```text
A_m+B_m=I_m-P_m,                                       (11.447.2)
```

where `P_m` is the full-line Gamma bulk.  Their first-jet contribution is
`+i K_x H_T(epsilon)/(2pi)`.  The two harmonic currents therefore cancel
coefficientwise before any norm, while the target Fourier coefficients of
`Phi_x` are restored.

Consequently, for `w_m=exp(-pi*epsilon*m^2)` and every common `M>=B`, the
complete Gamma-normalized kernel is exactly

```text
Delta_(M,epsilon)(x)
 =H_x+E_x
  +2*pi*i*sum_(m=1)^M m*w_m
      [hat Phi_x(m)-hat Phi_x(-m)]
  -sum_(m=622)^39894 w_m P_m(x).                       (11.447.3)
```

The harmonic current from Section 11.446 is therefore not an independent
error term and must not be counted after (11.447.3).  Equation (11.446.9)
makes the symmetric series in (11.447.3) absolutely convergent.  Since the
source roster is finite, `K_Phi(x)` is continuous on `0<=x<=1`; its maximum
is finite, so the convergence is uniform on the Kummer interval.  This
licenses the zero-regulator pair representation structurally, although the
resulting raw constant is not quantitatively useful.

The post-A object remains, with no ownership change,

```text
mathfrak R_A=Delta-chi_W Btr-O-mathcal A.               (11.447.4)
```

## 11.448 All-order signed-pair endpoint jets and turning-ratio guard

For `D_m=2*pi*i*m`, repeated integration by parts at any even order `2r`
and pairing before taking absolute values gives

```text
I_m+I_-m
 =-2 sum_(k=0)^(r-1) Delta f_x^(2k+1)/D_m^(2k+2)
  +[R_(m,2r)+R_(-m,2r)]/D_m^(2r),                    (11.448.1)

R_(+/-m,2r)
 =integral_0^L f_x^(2r)(u)e^(-/+2*pi*i*m*u)du.       (11.448.2)
```

Thus all even endpoint derivatives cancel from the signed pair.  The
elementary remainder estimate is

```text
|remainder|<=2 integral_0^L |f_x^(2r)(u)|du
                    /(2*pi*m)^(2r).                  (11.448.3)
```

With `y=A+2u` and `q=i*pi*x`, the exact derivative polynomials obey

```text
p_0(y)=y,
p_(n+1)(y)=2p_n'(y)+q*y*p_n(y),
f_x^(n)(u)=p_n(y)e^(q*y^2/4),
p_n(y)=q^n y^(n+1)+lower powers.                     (11.448.4)
```

Consequently the ratio between successive highest odd-jet monomials from
endpoint `D` is exactly

```text
rho_D(x,m)^2=[x*D/(2m)]^2.                           (11.448.5)
```

This is the normal turning coordinate.  It equals one at `x=2m/D`, so the
raw endpoint hierarchy cannot be uniformly descending through an endpoint
crossing.  The saved integers make both relevant obstructions exact:

```text
B/(4*39894)=5122421/159576>32,
A/(4*39894)=159577/159576>1,
A/(4*39895)=159577/159580<1,
x_(B,622)=1244/5122421,       rho_B(x_(B,622),622)=1. (11.448.6)
```

Hence every target mode is on the non-descending side of both raw endpoint
top-monomial hierarchies at `x=1/2`, while the A half-boundary lies between
modes 39894 and 39895.  An 80-digit order-seven scout reproduces the predicted
unit B ratio at its crossing, the unit A ratio at its half-boundary, and the
large unremoved B growth; those rows are route-selection telemetry only.

## 11.449 Post-A extended-notch normal form

Let

```text
T={622,...,39894},

U={622,...,39936}=T union W_A.                       (11.449.1)
```

The 84-mode A window has 42 modes inside `T` and 42 outside.  Consequently

```text
chi_T+chi_A(1-chi_T)=chi_U.                          (11.449.2)
```

At every inherited common cutoff and positive regulator, subtracting the
certified A transition before any norm therefore gives

```text
Delta_(M,epsilon)-mathcal A_(M,epsilon)
 =H_x+sum_(m=-M)^M w_m I_m
  -sum_(m=622)^39936 w_m P_m
  -sum_(m=39853)^39936 w_m(A_m+A_-m).                (11.449.3)
```

The former six-row positive-bulk mask is one contiguous extended notch.
Equivalently, with `G_U` its positive Fourier projector,

```text
Delta-mathcal A
 =H_x+integral_0^L f_x(u)[D_(M,epsilon)-G_(U,epsilon)]du
  +sum_(m in U)w_m(A_m+B_m)
  -sum_(m in W_A)w_m(A_m+A_-m).                      (11.449.4)
```

The endpoint roster reduces to two rows:

```text
622..39852:    A_m+B_m,
39853..39936:  B_m-A_-m.                             (11.449.5)
```

The one-cell fold and two-jet reassembly give the equivalent form

```text
H_x+E_x
 +2*pi*i sum_(m=1)^M m*w_m[hat Phi_x(m)-hat Phi_x(-m)]
 -sum_(m=622)^39936 w_m P_m
 -sum_(m=39853)^39936 w_m(A_m+A_-m).                 (11.449.6)
```

The B extractions retain their ownership:

```text
mathfrak R_A=(Delta-mathcal A)-chi_W Btr-O.           (11.449.7)
```

For the extended notch, the two half-integer edges are `621.5` and
`39936.5`.  The two-edge modular and pole-free centred-cell formulas from
Sections 11.444--11.445 therefore apply with the upper edge replaced by
`d_A=39936.5`; both edge phases remain `(-1)^k` on integer dual cells.

Since `A/4=39894.25` and `q_A(m,1/2)=(A-4m)/2`, exactly


## 11.450 Post-A extended-notch pole-free kernel

Retain the exact post-A notch

```text
U={622,...,39936},       c=621.5,       d_A=39936.5,
```

```text

```

Consequently the fixed-regulator complement has the exact Poisson form

```text

 =sum_(m in Z)[1-chi_U(m)]q_epsilon(m)e^(-2*pi*i*m*s)
 =sum_(k in Z)hat h_A,epsilon(k+s),                  (11.450.3)

hat h_A,epsilon(xi)
 =e^(-pi*xi^2/epsilon)/(2sqrt(epsilon))
  {erfc[-sqrt(pi*epsilon)c-i sqrt(pi/epsilon)xi]
   +erfc[ sqrt(pi*epsilon)d_A+i sqrt(pi/epsilon)xi]}. (11.450.4)
```

For `j=0,1`, set

```text
b_A,j(xi)
 =[q_epsilon^(j)(d_A)e^(-2*pi*i*xi*d_A)
   -q_epsilon^(j)(c)e^(-2*pi*i*xi*c)]
   /(2*pi*i*xi)^(j+1),

E_A,j(s)=q_epsilon^(j)(d_A)e^(-2*pi*i*s*d_A)
         -q_epsilon^(j)(c)e^(-2*pi*i*s*c).           (11.450.5)
```

Writing `rho_A,2=hat h_A,epsilon-b_A,0-b_A,1`, the `k=0` term cancels the
apparent boundary-current poles before evaluation.  On the whole centred

```text

 =hat h_A,epsilon(s)+E_A,0(s)g_0(s)+E_A,1(s)g_1(s)
  +sum_(k in Z,k!=0)rho_A,2(k+s),       |s|<=1/2,

g_0(s)=[csc(pi*s)-1/(pi*s)]/(2i),
g_1(s)={1/(pi*s)^2-cos(pi*s)/sin(pi*s)^2}/4,
g_0(0)=0,       g_1(0)=1/24.                        (11.450.6)
```

Three integrations by parts on the two exterior intervals give

```text
|rho_A,2(xi)|<=K3_A/(2*pi*|xi|)^3,
K3_A=|q_epsilon''(c)|+|q_epsilon''(d_A)|+20*pi*epsilon,

sum_(|k|>K)|rho_A,2(k+s)|
```
